label: 1000 Genomes
counts: individuals from 26 populations with reconstructed genomes (final phase 3)
quote: Here we report completion of the project, having reconstructed the genomes of 2,504 individuals from 26 populations using a combination of low-coverage whole-genome sequencing, deep exome sequencing, and dense microarray genotyping.
note: Phase 3 completion paper, the project's final report; earlier phases were smaller.

label: AddNeuroMed Cohort
counts: individuals enrolled at baseline
quote: The AddNeuroMed study was established in 2006 and enrolled 781 individuals at baseline.
note: From a comparison of six data sets, not AddNeuroMed's own design paper. The example study (PMID:21116278) says 281 AddNeuroMed subjects were selected and genotyped (94 AD, 96 MCI, 91 controls), an analysed subset. The design paper (Lovestone et al. 2007, J Nutr Health Aging, PMID:17653500) was not read.

label: Adenoma Prevention with Celecoxib trial
counts: subjects randomised to placebo or celecoxib
quote: The trial randomized 2,035 subjects to receive either placebo, celecoxib 200 mg twice daily, or celecoxib 400 mg twice daily.
note: The full text gives the arms: placebo 679, celecoxib 200 mg 685, celecoxib 400 mg 671; 933 patients took part in the 5-year extension.

label: Advanced Study of Aortic Pathology
counts: patients in the original ASAP study population (operated 2007-2013)
quote: Analysis of the clinical outcomes (aortic events and survival) was performed in 566 of the original 600 patients.
note: PMID:40207537 describes the ASAP population as patients operated between January 17, 2007 and February 14, 2013; its abstract speaks of 570 patients. The definition source PMID:38508639 counts ASAP together with its follow-on DAVAACA study: 1180 operated patients included (28 June 2017), 1034 analysed. The original ASAP design paper was not read; it would settle the enrolled number.

label: Africa Wits-INDEPTH partnership for Genomics studies
counts: participants enrolled in Wave 1 (baseline)
quote: During Wave 1 (2013–17), 12 032 participants were enrolled.
note: Cohort profile. Wave 2 (2018-22) collected data on 7804 participants (7225 recalled and 579 new participants recruited at Dikgale/DIMAMO); no source states the total ever enrolled, so the baseline count is given.

label: Arthritis Research UK Osteoarthritis Genetics
counts: arcOGEN osteoarthritis cases in the GWAS (controls came from other UK studies)
quote: We undertook a large genome-wide association study (GWAS) in 7410 unrelated and retrospectively and prospectively selected patients with severe osteoarthritis in the arcOGEN study, 80% of whom had undergone total joint replacement, and 11 009 unrelated controls from the UK.
note: The 11 009 controls were publicly available data from WTCCC2, ALSPAC, T1DGC and People of the British Isles, not recruited by arcOGEN, so participants counts the cases only; no source states a case-plus-control total. The example study (PMID:34450027) likewise calls arcOGEN 'a collection of 7410 unrelated, UK-based individuals of European ancestry with knee and/or hip osteoarthritis'. A further 2409 arcOGEN cases were used for de-novo replication.

label: Asian Cancer Project
counts: cases and controls contributed to the BCAC COGS genotyping (analysed subset)
quote: Asian Cancer Project (ACP) Thailand 636 423 92 53
note: Only source is a row of Table 1 of PMID:24943594 (columns Controls, Cases, ER+, ER−), i.e. the ACP samples in the BCAC COGS analysis, not the study's own enrolment; no sentence states a total. Europe PMC finds no ACP design paper (only this and PMID:24548884). The study's own description (e.g. BCAC supplementary Table S1) would settle the enrolled number.

label: Aspirin for Asymptomatic Atherosclerosis Study
counts: participants randomly assigned to aspirin or placebo
quote: The 3350 remaining were randomly assigned to aspirin or placebo.
note: The main trial report (PMID:20197530) abstract says the trial involved 28,980 men and women screened by ABI and 'Of those, 3350 with a low ABI' (the Europe PMC abstract text is truncated after that); the screened population was 28 980, the randomised trial cohort 3350.

label: AtheroExpress
counts: patients included in the biobank (stated as a lower bound, 'over 3,500')
quote: The current number of included AE patients is over 3,500, some 2,400 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy, almost 700 “femoral” patients had surgery, and well over 70 other types of arteries were operated on.
note: The website states 'over 3,500' without a date, so 3500 is a lower bound. The example study (PMID:33784435) used a subset of 144 plaques. The design paper (PMID:15678794) describes the original design only; a recent cohort profile would give the exact current number.

label: Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study
counts: Black and White participants recruited from the 4 communities
quote: The ARIC is a population-based epidemiologic study among a total of 15,792 Black and White participants recruited from 4 communities (17).
note: The design paper (PMID:2646917) gives the planned size: '4,000 adults aged 45-64 years will be examined twice' in each of four communities. The achieved number is taken from the example study, since no cohort profile was read.

label: Atopic Dermatitis Research Network
counts: participants with atopic dermatitis enrolled in the ADRN registry at 9 academic centres
quote: Participants with AD (N = 2862) whose disease was categorized as mild (11.6%), moderate (58.0%), or severe (30.4%) based on Rajka-Langeland scoring were enrolled.
note: Network-level registry paper (abstract read via Europe PMC). The network's website says only that it 'will be enrolling large numbers of people with AD'; the example study (PMID:34536413) pools ADRN with TOPMed and CAAPA (N=21,901 overall) without an ADRN-only count in the text read. The registry may count only AD participants; non-atopic controls enrolled in individual ADRN studies are not included.

label: Australia Cancer Study
note: Read the definition source PMID:18086758 (full text via Europe PMC PDF): it says only that recruitment of cases 'through the New South Wales and Victorian Cancer Registries was conducted in parallel under a separately funded study: the Australian Cancer Study', and gives AOCS-level numbers without an ACS-specific count. The example study PMID:20852632 (PMC3020231) names the Australian Cancer Study (Ovarian Cancer) as an author group only. An ACS ovarian-cancer design paper or OCAC study table (usually AUS = AOCS+ACS combined) would settle it.

label: Australian Ovarian Cancer Study
counts: women with invasive or borderline ovarian tumours among 2,456 consenting cases (2002-2006); controls enrolled
quote: Between 2002 and 2006, a total of 2,456 women with suspected epithelial ovarian cancer from all Australian states consented to take part in the study, of whom 1859 had invasive or borderline ovarian tumours.
note: Controls from the same page: 'Detailed epidemiological data have been collected from cases and demographically matched control women (1,065 enrolled), allowing us to refine information about known environmental risk factors, and understand how environmental and genetic risk for ovarian cancer may intersect and guide prevention strategies.' No source states a case-plus-control total, so participants is null. The definition source PMID:18086758 gives different figures (cases: 'Of those invited to participate, 2,714 (85%) agreed to take part'; controls: '1,614 (47%) agreed to take part'; '87% of eligible cases (n = 1717) and 85% of controls (n = 1287) provided a sample of blood'), possibly including cases recruited through the parallel Australian Cancer Study. The AOCS cohort page reports 2,157 case and 1,064 control questionnaires.

label: Australian Twin Registry
counts: twin members of Twins Research Australia (the renamed Australian Twin Registry), current website
quote: We are non-profit with our research made possible through the incredible volunteer efforts of our 75,000 twin members Australia-wide.
note: The registry profile (PMID:23200298) counts pairs, not people: 'Since the late 1970s the ATR has enrolled more than 40,000 twin pairs of all zygosities' and 'Our twin membership is comprised of more than 40,000 twin pairs and HOM.' The website's rounded count of individual members is given because the profile states no count of individuals; the website figure is undated.

label: Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children
counts: live-born index children in the enrolled sample (from 15 247 enrolled pregnancies, by age 18)
quote: The ‘Children of the 90s’ ‘enrolled sample’ consists of 14 775 (75.7% of the 19 600 eligible live births) live-born children from the 15 247 pregnancies (15 458 foetuses) where an individual, either the mother/primary caregiver or the child, has provided data.
note: Index-offspring cohort profile. 14 541 pregnancies were recruited antenatally in 1990–92, rising to 15 247 enrolled pregnancies by age 18; 14 701 children were alive at one year. Mothers and partners are counted separately in companion profiles, which were not read; later profile updates (after 2012) may give slightly larger numbers.

label: Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster trials
counts: children treated in the five consecutive ALL-BFM trials 1981-2000 (pooled long-term analysis)
quote: Between 1981 and 2000, 6609 children (<18 years of age) were treated in five consecutive trials of the Berlin-Frankfurt-Münster (BFM) study group for childhood acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
note: The pooled report covers only the trials ALL-BFM 81 to 95; earlier (1970s) and later trials (e.g. AIEOP-BFM ALL 2000 onwards) are not counted, so the number understates all BFM trials together. Abstract read; the full text is subscription-only.

label: Bladder Cancer Prognosis Programme
counts: patients enrolled December 2005-October 2011 on cystoscopic findings suggestive of bladder cancer
quote: Briefly, during the enrolment period (December 2005–October 2011), a total of 1,550 male and female patients (age ≥18 years) were enrolled based on abnormal cystoscopic findings suggestive of bladder cancer.
note: Sources disagree slightly: PMID:30903352 says 'During the recruitment period (2005–2011), 1536 participants were enrolled', of whom 326 did not have primary bladder cancer. The design paper (PMID:19751260) gives an interim 771 patients recruited since December 2005. Enrolment was on suspicion of bladder cancer, so the enrolled number includes people later found not to have it.

label: Brazilian Cohort
counts: babies whose exomes were sequenced
quote: Here we provide a catalogue of variants called after sequencing the exomes of 45 babies from Rio Grande do Nord in Brazil.
note: The full text says 'The sample comprised 45 babies (26 males ...; 19 females ...), 44 with confirmed Zika-associated congenital microcephaly and one baby with familial congenital microcephaly.'

label: Breast Cancer Association Consortium
counts: invasive breast cancer cases from 34 member studies pooled in the 2011 risk-factor and tumour-subtype analysis
quote: We pooled tumor marker and epidemiological risk factor data from 35568 invasive breast cancer case patients from 34 studies participating in the Breast Cancer Association Consortium.
note: Taken from the definition source, whose pooled analysis the definition describes; the case-control part used 12 population-based studies without a total stated in the abstract. BCAC's later genome-wide analyses are much larger: PMID:29059683 reports 'a genome-wide association study of breast cancer in 122,977 cases and 105,974 controls of European ancestry and 14,068 cases and 13,104 controls of East Asian ancestry' (no single total stated, and it includes data beyond BCAC). PMID:24943594 reports the BCAC COGS component as 53 835 cases and 50 156 controls.

label: Bruneck study
counts: women and men examined at the 1990 baseline (of 1,000 invited)
quote: A total of 933 women and men participated in the baseline examination in 1990 (participation rate, 93.3%); 703 of 764 individuals being alive in 2000 participated in the 2000 re‐evaluation (participation rate, 92.0%).
note: The study website (definition source) gives only the invited sample: 'a sex- and age-stratified random sample of all inhabitants of Bruneck (n=1,000) was invited to participate in the study.' The example study (PMID:22199011) used n=786 Bruneck participants. The baseline number comes from a later Bruneck paper rather than a cohort profile; other Bruneck papers may report a slightly different baseline count.

label: Cancer and Leukemia Group B
note: Cooperative trials group (now part of the Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology); no source read states a total enrolment across its trials or a number of member institutions/trials. Read: abstract of PMID:16740784 (full text on aacrjournals.org returned 403, not cached); PMC3886682 (CALGB 50-year history) gives only per-trial numbers (e.g. 1572 randomised in CALGB 8541) and 'hundreds of members'; example PMID:34528705 pools 1,520 patients from CALGB 80303, 40503, 80405 and ICON7 (a GWAS subset, not the group). A group-wide accrual statement from the history paper's full text or the Alliance website would settle it.

label: Cancer Genome Atlas
counts: patients whose tumours TCGA characterised across 33 cancer types (TCGA-CDR, whole program)
quote: By the end of this 10-year project, TCGA network investigators had characterized the molecular landscape of tumors from 11,160 patients across 33 cancer types and defined their many molecular subtypes.
note: From the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource paper (PMID:29625055, Cell 2018), fetched from PMC. Its abstract says 'more than 11,000 human tumors across 33 different cancer types'. The NCI program page (https://www.cancer.gov/ccg/research/genome-sequencing/tcga) says 'over 20,000 primary cancer and matched normal samples spanning 33 cancer types', which counts samples, not people. Example PMID:32585557 is closed (only abstract cached) and was not used.

label: Cancer Prevention Study
counts: American men and women enrolled in CPS-II in 1982
quote: The Cancer Prevention Study II (CPS-II), which began in 1982, is a prospective mortality study of approximately 1.2 million American men and women.
note: The ACS CPS-II page states approximately 1.2 million (recorded as 1200000). The same page: the CPS-II Nutrition Survey subcohort obtained updated information for 184,194 men and women in 1992-1993, and blood samples from 40,000 and cheek cells from 70,000 Nutrition cohort participants. Example PMID:37783704 used 1712 CPSII participants (a validation subset).

label: Cancer Prostate in Sweden
counts: prostate cancer cases and controls recruited 2001-2003
quote: The CAPS (Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden) study represents a large Swedish population- based cancer study, comprising 3,161 cases and 2,149 controls, recruited between 2001 and 2003.
note: Cases and controls from the supplementary note of the 2014 PRACTICAL meta-analysis (doi:10.1038/ng.3094); no source read states the total, so participants is left null. The example study's supplement (PMID:23535732, ng.2560 MOESM4) says 'a population-based prostate cancer case-control study with 3,030 cases and 1,960 controls who donated blood samples during 2001-2003'. The definition source PMID:15087412 (abstract only) analysed 1383 cases and 780 controls; PMC4422072 describes 2,618 cases and 1,728 controls; PMC3435290 calls CAPS1 'over 1,400 cases and 700 controls'. A CAPS design paper stating the total recruited would settle participants.

label: Candesartan in Heart failure Assessment of Reduction in Mortality and morbidity
counts: patients randomised across the three CHARM trials (CHARM-Overall)
quote: Overall, 7601 patients (7599 with data) were randomly assigned candesartan (n=3803, titrated to 32 mg once daily) or matching placebo (n=3796), and followed up for at least 2 years.
note: Quote from the abstract of the CHARM-Overall results paper (Lancet 2003), read via the Europe PMC API. The design paper PMID:10496201 planned 6,500 patients ('CHARM is intended to randomize 6,500 patients'). The example PMID:35736394 says the primary endpoint occurred in 2460 of 7599 patients in the overall programme and genotyped 2727 patients of European ancestry.

label: Cardio-metabolic Genome Epidemiology Network
note: No source read states a pooled number of participants or a number of member studies for the CAGE Network. The definition source (PMID:26648100, PMC4673465) describes it only qualitatively and gives member cohorts' sizes (Amagasaki Study 5,743 individuals; Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort 12,959 subjects). Other cached papers give only analysed subsets or member cohorts (CAGE GWAS 1,547 Japanese in the AGEN-BP meta-analysis; CAGE 988 in the kidney-trait GWAS, ng.2352; CAGE-KING 3,975). The example PMID:34059833 does not describe CAGE's size. A CAGE Network overview stating its total enrolment would settle it.

label: Cardiogenics Study
counts: participants recruited in five centres (MI patients and controls)
quote: This initiative recruited 918 participants (459 patients with myocardial infarction and 459 normal controls) in five centres: Cambridge (UK), Leicester (UK), Lübeck (Germany), Regensburg (Germany), and Paris (France).
note: From the definition source PMID:22325189 (Lancet 2012, Y chromosome), which cites the Cardiogenics design reference; the same paper says 1533 samples (849 monocytes, 684 macrophages) were available for RNA analysis. The example PMID:21965548 analysed monocyte transcriptomes 'from 395 healthy blood donors and 363 patients with premature MI assembled by the Cardiogenics consortium', which does not match the 459/459 split, so the Cardiogenics design paper would confirm the figure.

label: CARDIoGRAMplusC4D
counts: CAD cases and controls in the 2015 1000 Genomes-based meta-analysis (approximate)
quote: Leveraging phased haplotypes from the 1000 Genomes Project, we report a GWAS meta-analysis of ∼185,000 CAD cases and controls, interrogating 6.7 million common (minor allele frequency (MAF) > 0.05) and 2.7 million low-frequency (0.005 < MAF < 0.05) variants.
note: Flagship analysis taken as the 2015 1000 Genomes-based CARDIoGRAMplusC4D meta-analysis (Nikpay et al., PMID:26343387), the GWAS the definition source (PMID:38060277) uses: 'In total, the GWAS includes 60,801 CAD cases, 123,504 control samples, and 9.4 million variants.' The cases and controls come from its full text (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC4589895/fullTextXML): 'We assembled 60,801 cases and 123,504 controls from 48 studies for a GWAS meta-analysis of CAD; 34,997 (57.5%) of the cases and 49,512 (40.1%) of the controls had been previously included in our Metabochip-based CAD meta-analysis (Supplementary Fig. 1)3.' The abstract's ∼185,000 is approximate. The earlier 2013 Metabochip meta-analysis (example PMID:23202125) analysed 63,746 CAD cases and 130,681 controls, and the 2022 analysis (Aragam et al.) is described as 'over a million participants' in a reference title only.

label: Carolina Head and Neck Cancer Epidemiology
counts: interviewed head and neck cancer cases and controls, 2002-2006
quote: Interview data were available for 1,389 cases and 1,396 controls.
note: From the definition source PMID:20049634 (oral health and head and neck cancer in CHANCE). No source read states the total; the same paper's analysed set is 'The final dataset included 2,650 subjects, with 1,289 cases and 1,361 controls (93 and 97% of eligible cases and controls, respectively).' (after excluding lip cancers, proxy interviews, other race and missing data). A pooled-consortium table lists CHANCE with 940 and 1,087 (genotyped subset). The example PMID:34642315 gives no CHANCE size. A CHANCE design paper stating the total enrolled would settle participants.

label: CARTaGENE cohort (CHU Sainte-Justine, Quebec, Canada)
counts: men and women aged 40-69 recruited in phases A and B (over 43 000)
quote: CARTaGENE recruited over 43 000 men and women aged 40-69 in two phases (A and B).
note: From the abstract of the 2024 CARTaGENE Cohort Nutrition Study profile (read via the Europe PMC API), the most recent profile found; it adds 'In phase A, a total of 19 784 men and women were enrolled between 2009 and 2010.' The 2013 cohort profile (definition source PMID:23071140, abstract only) says 'Over 20,000 participants consented to visiting 1 of 12 assessment sites', i.e. phase A. The example PMID:38970920 used 20,010 CARTaGENE controls and genotype data for 25,653 subjects.

label: Center for Autism Research and Treatment
note: UCLA CART is a research and clinical centre whose participants are recruited study by study; no source read states a number of participants for the centre as a whole. Read: the mission page (definition source), the CART history page (https://teams.semel.ucla.edu/autism/our-history), which mentions only the related Autism Center of Excellence network reaching 'over 500 families with autism' (a separate network study), and the example PMID:22318914, which recruited 19 ASD participants through CART. Probably no single enrolment figure exists.

label: Center on Antisocial Drug Dependence
note: CADD is a research centre with several samples (the example's supplement names the Colorado longitudinal twin sample and community twin sample); no source read states a total number of participants. Numbers seen are analysed subsets only: 'n = 601 for the Colorado based CADD study' in the example PMID:35534559 (height/BMI meta-analysis); CADD N 853 in the cannabis-use GWAS (PMC4872459); CADD cases and controls in the PGC alcohol dependence (PMC6430207) and cannabis use disorder (PMC7674631) tables. The definition source (IBG 50-year history page) gives no size. A CADD design paper (e.g. its Colorado Twin Registry or clinical-sample description) stating total enrolment would settle it.

label: Centre dEtude du Polymorphisme Humain
note: The term is the CEPH foundation; its reference family panel (whose Utah trios form the HapMap/1000 Genomes CEU population used by the example PMID:26432245) is counted only in families. The CEPH site (https://www.fjd-ceph.org/familles-de-r%C3%A9f%C3%A9rence-du-ceph) says 'une collection de 40 familles de référence (puis 61)' (10 French, 48 Utah Mormon, 1 Amish, 2 Venezuelan families, averaging more than eight children), 30 CEU trios for HapMap, and selections of 91 trios and 192 unrelated individuals; no number of individuals for the whole panel. The home page also lists the separate HGDP-CEPH panel of 1063 cell lines from 1048 individuals in 52 populations. A statement of the number of individuals in the 61 reference families would settle it.

label: Chicago Asthma Genetics
note: No source read states how many people the Chicago Asthma Genetics study enrolled. The definition source PMID:21798578 (PMC3548570) describes recruitment criteria and analyses 79 Chicago cases with childhood-onset asthma; the example PMID:23146381 names CAG only within the combined STAMPEED/EVE samples. The EVE asthma meta-analysis (PMC3445408, fetched from PMC) and the EVE sex-interaction study (PMC4159149) report CAG only pooled with CSGA and SARP (e.g. 843 European American and 644 African American asthma cases for CAG/CSGA/SARP). A CAG design description (the study's reference 36 in PMC3548570) stating enrolment would settle it.

label: Children, Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm, Epidemiology
counts: children enrolled at 3-4 months of age, 1994-1996
quote: In November 1996, this number was reached (4,093).
note: From the abstract of the BAMSE design paper (definition source); the preceding sentence gives the target: 'To reach sufficient power, 4,000 children had to be included.' The same abstract says 97.7% of the original 4,093 children remained at the time. No later cohort profile was found in Europe PMC. The example PMID:29496485 (MeDALL EWAS) gives only analysed subsets across cohorts.

label: Cholesterol and Atherosclerosis Pharmacogenetics
counts: African-American and white adults enrolled who completed the 6-week simvastatin trial
quote: We enrolled 944 African-American and white men and women who completed an open-label, 6-week pharmacogenetics trial of 40 mg of simvastatin.
note: From the abstract of the CAP design/phenotype paper (definition source). The example PMID:20339536 (PMC2842298) agrees: 'The Cholesterol and Pharmacogenetics (CAP) trial involved 944 healthy volunteers, 609 of whom were Caucasian'; it genotyped 304 CAP participants in stage I.

label: Cilento study
counts: participants recruited in Campora, Gioi and Cardile, 2003-2008
quote: The sample for this study was based on the initial cohort of 2,137 participants, which were recruited in the Genetic Park of Cilento and Vallo di Diano Project between 2003 and 2008.
note: From the definition source PMID:30858532 (exome sequencing of 247 individuals; 1,617 genotyped on Illumina arrays). The example PMID:34413389 analysed 2068 individuals from the three villages (1600 in the discovery sample), which exceeds this 2003-2008 figure, so recruitment may have continued; a later Cilento design description would confirm the current total.

label: COIN
counts: patients randomised to the three COIN arms, 2005-2008
quote: Between March 9, 2005, and May 9, 2008, 2445 patients were randomly allocated to treatment groups at 111 centres in the UK and Ireland, with 1630 patients assigned to the comparison of continuous versus intermittent treatment.
note: From the COIN intermittent-versus-continuous results paper (PMID:21641867, Lancet Oncol 2011), full text fetched from Europe PMC; the arm A vs B paper (PMID:21641636, PMC3159415) gives the same total. The definition source PMID:26889974 covers only arms A and C: 'A total of 1630 patients were assigned to the continuous (N=815) or intermittent (N=815) arms.' The example PMID:35467766 studied 2671 patients from COIN and COIN-B together.

label: COIN-B
counts: patients enrolled (randomised) in COIN-B, of 401 registered
quote: We registered 401 patients, 226 of whom were enrolled.
note: From the COIN-B results paper (definition source PMID:24703531); results are reported for the 169 with KRAS wild-type tumours. The example PMID:35467766 states 'COIN‐B patients were randomised 1:1 to receive intermittent chemotherapy and cetuximab (n = 112) or intermittent chemotherapy and continuous cetuximab (n = 114)', consistent with 226 randomised; 401 is the number registered (screened for KRAS status).

label: Colorectal Cancer Study of Austria
counts: participants recruited since 2003 (more than 13,000; cases, adenomas and colonoscopy-negative controls)
quote: In the ongoing CRC study of Austria (CORSA), more than 13,000 Caucasian participants have been recruited within the province-wide screening project “Burgenland Prevention Trial of Colorectal Disease with Immunological Testing” (B-PREDICT) since 200313 .
note: From the supplementary text of the example PMID:30510241 (Huyghe et al., Nat Genet 2019); the '13' after 2003 is a reference number in the extracted text. It gives no split into cases and controls. The earlier definition source PMID:22495810 (abstract only): 'The study population of our ongoing colorectal cancer study of Austria (CORSA) comprised 3,842 Caucasian participants.', of whom 3,264 were genotyped (142 CRC cases, 492 high-risk polyps, 837 low-risk polyps, 1,793 polyp-free controls).

label: Consortium for the Longitudinal Evaluation of African Americans with Early Rheumatoid Arthritis
counts: member counts only: 2 member registries (CLEAR I, CLEAR II)
quote: At the time of this interim analysis, a total of 357 and 418 patients had been enrolled in CLEAR I and II, respectively; baseline radiographic were available in 294 for CLEAR I and 167 for CLEAR II and are included in these analyses.
note: No source read states a pooled total for the consortium; it reports its two member registries separately: CLEAR I (early RA, 2000-2005) 357 and CLEAR II (cross-sectional, from 2006, still enrolling; ~600 planned) 418 at the 2010 interim analysis. A later paper (PMID:35468261, PMC9592673) says 'The CLEAR I study recruited 354 self-identified African American patients diagnosed with RA within two years of disease duration between 2000 and 2006'. The example study (PMID:35925860) used 'a GWAS of AAs with RA (916 RA cases and 1370 controls) as part of the Consortium for the Longitudinal Evaluation of AA with RA (CLEAR)registry'. A current registry total from the consortium would settle it.

label: Consortium of Minority Population Genome-Wide Association Studies of Stroke
counts: cases and controls of African ancestry in the 2020 COMPASS meta-analysis of 13 cohorts
quote: The COMPASS (Consortium of Minority Population Genome-Wide Association Studies of Stroke) has conducted a genome-wide association meta-analysis of stroke in >22 000 individuals of African ancestry (3734 cases, 18 317 controls) from 13 cohorts.
note: The 2020 meta-analysis (abstract read from Europe PMC) states the total only as '>22 000', so participants is left null; cases and controls are as stated. The earlier 2015 analysis (definition source PMID:26089329) states 'we conducted meta-analyses of GWAS in 14,746 African-Americans (1,365 ischemic and 1,592 total stroke cases) from COMPASS' in the abstract and 'COMPASS comprises 14,745 African-Americans including 1,365 ischemic and 1,592 total stroke cases' in the results. If a single figure is wanted, the 2015 14,746 is the only exact stated total.

label: Cooperative Health Research in the Region of Augsburg
counts: participants of the four baseline surveys S1-S4 (1984-2001)
quote: In total, 17.602 participants were randomly selected from population registries in the study region.
needs: PMID:16032513 (Gesundheitswesen 2005, Thieme bot challenge; only the abstract, which gives no number, could be read)
note: The KORA website says the cohort 'consists of four cross-sectional baseline surveys from 1984 – 2001'; the figure is written with a German thousands separator (17.602 = 17,602). The AMI registry is not included in this count. The example study (PMID:28240269) gives member-survey numbers: 'KORA F4 is the follow-up study of the KORA S4 survey conducted in 1999–2001 (4,261 participants)' and 'The KORA F4 study is a population-based cohort of 3,080 subjects living in southern Germany'.

label: Copenhagen Hospital Biobank
counts: patients in the biobank (approximate)
quote: At present, the biobank counts ~425,000 patients (Table 4).
needs: PMID:33169150 (Data Resource Profile, Int J Epidemiol 2021; subscription, not readable)
note: Taken from a 2023 review of Danish biobanks (Europe PMC full text of PMC9960719), since the CHB's own data resource profile is closed. Other figures: the CHB-CVDC cohort profile (PMID:36070241, 2021) says 'Presently, CHB contains samples from more than 450 000 individuals.' and 'CHB is continuously growing with ~40 000 samples/year.'; the same review says genome-wide genotype data are available for '∼330,000 patients (January 2022)'. The approximate figure is recorded as stated; the profile paper would settle the enrolled count.

label: CROATIA-Korcula Study
counts: adult volunteers recruited 2007-2014 (entire cohort)
quote: This study describes whole genome sequencing (TruSeq Nano, Illumina) run on a HiSeqX  platform at 30X coverage on 200 individuals best capturing the genetic variation of the entire cohort (N= 2701); they were selected using ANCHAP, an identity by descent inference tool (PMID 23361219).
note: The EGA study abstract (definition source) gives the whole cohort as N= 2701 (the quote keeps the source's double space after 'HiSeqX'). The example study (PMID:35332118) says the cohort 'includes samples of blood DNA, plasma and serum, anthropometric and physical measurements, information related to general health, medical history, lifestyle and diet for ~3000 residents of the Croatian island of Korčula' and analysed 948-951 samples.

label: Danish Glostrup Cohort
counts: men and women aged 60 evaluated (stated separately)
quote: We have evaluated 325 men and 370 women of 60 years, participating in the Danish Glostrup study.
needs: PMID:12871360 full text (J Thromb Haemost 2003; publisher pages not readable, only the abstract)
note: The only source read (the abstract of the definition and example paper) states men and women separately and no total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The full text or a design paper of the Glostrup 60-year-old examination would settle the total enrolled.

label: Diabetes Genetics in Pakistan
counts: DGP participants genotyped in this study (type 2 diabetes cases and normoglycaemic controls)
quote: All subjects (UKADS, n = 1274; DGP, n = 1988; total, n = 3262) were genotyped for the 16 SNPs using the KASPar method (KBioscience, Hoddesdon, UK).
note: Cases and controls from the same paper (Europe PMC full text PMC3176767): 'the Diabetes Genetics in Pakistan study (DGP; 821 participants with type 2 diabetes, 1167 without) [3]'. This is the DGP sample used in the 2011 analysis; the collection's own design paper (the paper's reference 3) was not read and may give a larger enrolled number.

label: Diabetes in Mexico Study
counts: DMS type 2 diabetes cases and controls in the SIGMA T2D dataset, before QC (table row)
quote: Diabetes in Mexico Study (DMS) Mexico City, Mexico Prospective Cohort Controls 472 (505) 25.8% 52.5 ± 7.7 – 28.0 ± 4.4 5.0 ± 0.4 T2D Cases 690 (762)
note: The only numbers read are a row of Table 1 of the SIGMA paper (PMID:24390345), whose caption says it gives 'numbers of cases and controls (including numbers before quality control (QC) checks)': 505 controls and 762 cases before QC, 472 and 690 after. No sentence states a DMS total, so participants is left null. This is the subset contributed to SIGMA; a DMS design paper would settle the enrolled number.

label: Diabetes Prevention Program
counts: participants randomised
quote: We randomly assigned 3234 nondiabetic persons with elevated fasting and post-load plasma glucose concentrations to placebo, metformin (850 mg twice daily), or a lifestyle-modification program with the goals of at least a 7 percent weight loss and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week.
note: Achieved randomised number from the main DPP results paper (NEJM 2002; abstract read from Europe PMC); the abstract does not give the year randomisation ended. The design paper (PMID:10189543) gives the planned size: 'the randomization goal of the DPP is 2,834 participants, which was increased to 3,000 participants (1,000 per group)', and says 'The 585 participants randomized to this drug were unmasked' for the discontinued troglitazone arm. The example study (PMID:35621206) used N=1612 DPP/DPPOS participants.

label: Diabetes Reduction Assessment with Ramipril and Rosiglitazone Medication
counts: participants randomised
quote: During this period a total of 191 clinical sites in 21 countries screened 24,872 individuals and randomised 5269 participants using a variety of recruitment strategies (Table 2).
note: From the DREAM design and recruitment paper (definition source PMID:15322749, publisher full text). The abstract says 'A total of 24,872 individuals in 21 countries were screened over 2 years and are eligible for follow-up. Of these, 5269 were randomised'; the screened non-randomised individuals form EpiDREAM. 1427 participants were in the STARR carotid substudy.

label: Diabetes Research on Patient Stratification
counts: member counts only: 2 member cohorts (cohort 1 prediabetes risk, cohort 2 diabetes)
quote: After excluding participants who did not meet the inclusion criteria or whose data failed quality control, a total of 2127 participants at risk of diabetes and 789 participants with type 2 diabetes were retained in cohort 1 and cohort 2, respectively.
note: The DIRECT descriptive-characteristics paper (Europe PMC full text PMC6677872) reports its two cohorts separately (2127 and 789) and states no pooled total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The design paper (PMID:24695864) gives targets only: 'Prediabetic participants (target sample size 2,200–2,700) and patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes (target sample size ~1,000)'. The 2019 paper also says 'A total of 3032 samples and 517,958 markers across the two studies passed quality control procedures' (genotyped samples, not participants).

label: Dortmund Health Study
counts: participants recruited 2003-2004
quote: From 2003 to 2004 overall 2,291 participants were recruited into the study, 1,312 attended the study centre and the others participated by answering a mailed questionnaire.
note: From the study's own design paper (Bundesgesundheitsblatt 2012; English abstract). The German text adds that a random sample of 3820 people aged 25-74 was drawn from the Dortmund residents' registry and invited.

label: Duke Cognition Cohort
counts: DCC participants in the COGENT meta-analysis (analysed subset, table row)
quote: DCC Duke Cognition Cohort USA 1193 27.1 11.6 18 77 558 0.47
note: The only number read is the DCC row of Table 1 ('Demographic characteristics of the consortium') of the COGENT paper (PMID:28093568): N 1193, age 18-77, 558 male. The paper's supplementary methods (mp2016244x1.docx) describe DCC recruitment ('Participants were recruited to be members of the DCC to study the genetics of normal variation in cognitive performance') without a count. This is the number analysed in COGENT; no design paper or website stating the cohort's enrolment was found.

label: DUNDEE
note: No source read states how many patients came from the Dundee site. The EGA study EGAS00001004410 (definition source) and its publication (PMID:33741650, PMC7610896) give only whole-study figures for the Scottish HGSOC study, across Edinburgh, Glasgow, Dundee and Aberdeen: 'the previously unpublished primary tumours from Scottish High Grade Serous Ovarian Cancer (SHGSOC) study (N=81)', and EGA datasets of 81 and 34 matched tumour-normal WGS pairs. A per-site breakdown (for example a supplementary sample table giving the collection site) would settle it; counting rows of such a table was not attempted.

label: Durban Diabetes Study
counts: participants recruited to date (interim, recruitment ongoing)
quote: Of the 1204 participants recruited to date, 28.3% (341) are men compared with 48.2% found in the general population census data.
note: From the DDS cohort profile (BMJ Open 2017, Europe PMC full text PMC5732575), an interim count: 'to date, 1300 individuals have been invited join the study, of whom 96 refused participation, with a resulting response of 92.6% (n = 1204)'. The planned size is 10 000 ('the target sample size is 10 000 participants'). The example study (PMID:35546142) used 'Durban Diabetes study (DDS) (N = 1117)'. A later report of achieved recruitment would supersede this.

label: Dutch and Belgian Lung Cancer Screening Trial
counts: participants randomised by 18 October 2005 (two recruitment rounds)
quote: Until October 18, 2005 11,103 (first recruitment round) and 4,325 (second recruitment round) (total = 15,428) participants have been randomised.
note: From the NELSON design paper (definition source; abstract read from Europe PMC), which also says '17,300-27,900 participants are needed'. The main results paper (NEJM 2020, PMID:31995683, abstract read) states men and women separately and no total: 'A total of 13,195 men (primary analysis) and 2594 women (subgroup analyses) between the ages of 50 and 74 were randomly assigned'; these separate figures may reflect the final randomised population, but no source read gives their total, so the 2005 stated total is recorded.

label: Dutch Microbiome Project
counts: Lifelines participants with sequenced faecal metagenomes
quote: The Dutch Microbiome Project (DMP) data includes raw data generated by shotgun metagenomic sequencing of faecal samples of 8,208 Dutch individuals, processed microbiome data analysed using Biobakery2 tools (including taxonomy, pathway, virulence factors and antibiotic resistance gene profiles), and basic phenotypes (age and sex, BMI).
note: From the EGA study (definition source; released 2021). The example study (PMID:35115690) analysed a subset: 'we performed a genome-wide association study of 207 taxa and 205 pathways representing microbial composition and function in 7,738 participants of the Dutch Microbiome Project'.

label: Edinburgh Stroke Study
counts: stroke patients assessed April 2002 - May 2005
quote: We assessed 1,408 patients, of whom 844 (60%) had blood drawn for markers of inflammation.
note: From the definition source (PLoS Med 2009, Europe PMC full text PMC2730573), whose abstract counts only the biomarker subset: 'We recruited 844 patients; mortality data were available in 844 (100%) and functional outcome in 750 (89%).' Other ESS papers give other denominators: PMID:25299053 (PMC4192583) 'Of 1257 patients (671 outpatients and 586 inpatients), 1051 (84%) had record of doctor’s predictions', and PMID:35287300 (PMC8915237) included '812 patients with first-ever ischaemic stroke'. No ESS protocol or profile giving the overall recruited number was read (the paper cites www.dcn.ed.ac.uk/ess/protocol).

label: ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48
counts: patients randomised
quote: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years).
note: Achieved size from the main results paper (NEJM 2013; abstract read from Europe PMC). The design paper (definition source PMID:20934556) gave the planned size: 'Approximately 20,500 subjects will be randomized to edoxaban high exposure (60 mg daily, adjusted for drug clearance), edoxaban low exposure (30 mg daily, adjusted for drug clearance), or warfarin titrated to an international normalized ratio of 2.0 to 3.0.'

label: EPIGEN
counts: genotyped individuals from the three member cohorts in the flagship 2015 analysis
quote: A population-based genome-wide analysis of 6,487 individuals was performed in the context of worldwide genomic diversity to elucidate how ancestry, kinship, and inbreeding interact in three populations with different histories from the Northeast (African ancestry: 50%), Southeast, and South (both with European ancestry >70%) of Brazil.
note: Pooled number of the EPIGEN-Brazil flagship paper (definition and example source). Member cohorts as stated in its full text (PMC4507185): SCAALA '(1,309 individuals)', Bambuí '(1,442 individuals who were 82% of the residents older than 60 y old at the baseline year)', and the 1982 Pelotas Birth Cohort '(3,736 individuals; 99% of all births in the city at the baseline year)'. These are the EPIGEN-genotyped subsets of the member cohorts, not their full sizes.

label: Erasmus Rucphen Family Study
counts: participants examined June 2002 to February 2005
quote: Data collection started in June 2002 and was finished in February 2005 (n=2065).
note: From the NIAGADS cohort page (the definition source). The example study (PMID:26068415) gives no ERF-specific count. The ERF design papers were not read; they could confirm the number of participants.

label: Estonian Biobank
counts: individuals enrolled in the open cohort (stated as more than 212 000)
quote: Because the Estonian Biobank is an open cohort, the sample size has now expanded to >212 000 individuals since the publication of the previous cohort profile,1 covering ∼20% of the adult population in Estonia.
note: The number is a lower bound ('>212 000') from the 2024 Cohort Profile Update of the EstBB mental health survey (PMID:38381979). The 2015 cohort profile (PMID:24518929, definition source) says 'The current number of participants-close to 52000--represents a large proportion, 5%, of the Estonian adult population'. The example study (PMID:36922633) gives only analysed cases and controls (30,194 cases, 94,694 controls).

label: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer
counts: participants recruited in 23 centres, 10 countries
quote: The study currently includes 519 978 participants (366 521 women and 153 457 men, mostly aged 35-70 years) in 23 centres located in 10 European countries, to be followed for cancer incidence and cause-specific mortality for several decades.
note: From the EPIC study populations and data collection paper (definition source), abstract. 366 521 women and 153 457 men.

label: European Prospective Investigation of Cancer-Norfolk
counts: people who consented and completed the baseline health questionnaire, 1993-1997
quote: Of these, 30 445 consented to take part and completed a health questionnaire.
note: From the EPIC-Norfolk 3 cohort profile (PMID:23771720); 77 630 individuals from 35 general practices were invited. The same paper says 'EPIC-Norfolk examined 25 639 men and women resident in East Anglia (aged 40–79 years), between 1993 and 1997' (attendees of the first health check). The study website (definition source) says 'Over 30,000 people living in Norwich and surrounding towns and rural areas were recruited into the EPIC-Norfolk study between 1993 and 1997.' The example study (PMID:34836419) used 5841 EPIC-Norfolk participants.

label: EuroTARGET project
counts: patients with metastatic renal cell cancer included (prospective plus previous studies)
quote: In total, 1,210 patients with mRCC were included.
note: From the EuroTARGET cohort description paper (definition source), abstract; this total includes 462 patients with mRCC from previous studies. Of these, 920 received a tyrosine kinase inhibitor first-line with at least 6 months of outcome assessment, and germline chip data were generated for 811.

label: Extremely Low Gestational Age Newborns
counts: infants born before 28 weeks enrolled at 14 sites
quote: We enrolled 1506 ELGANs born before 28 weeks gestation at 14 sites; 1201 (80%) survived to 2 years corrected age.
note: From the ELGAN Study design paper (definition source), abstract; 1201 survived to 2 years corrected age. The full text says the study 'achieved large numbers (close to 1500)'.

label: Fatty Acid Sensor Study
counts: healthy subjects recruited September 2009 to December 2011
quote: A total of 254 healthy Canadian Caucasian subjects living in the Quebec City metropolitan area were recruited into the FAS study from September 2009 to December 2011 using announcements in local newspapers, as well as electronic messages sent to students and employees of Université Laval (Quebec).
note: From PMID:30624603 (definition source and example study), full text. The same paper says 'A total of 210 participants completed the intervention' and the analysed sample was 208 participants (abstract: 'A total of 208 participants of the Fatty Acid Sensor (FAS) Study received 5 g fish oil/d').

label: Finnish Twin Cohort Study
counts: no pooled number; member cohorts only (older twin cohort, FinnTwin16, FinnTwin12)
note: The sources read report only member-cohort counts, no pooled total. The 2013 update (PMID:23298696, definition source) says of FinnTwin12 'We have enrolled 5,600 twins and their families ascertained from nation-wide birth cohorts born 1983–1987' and of FinnTwin16 'The cohort has over 3,000 twin pairs'; for the older cohort it gives only the 2011 wave ('to 11,738 twins born 1945–1957'). The abstract of 'Twin studies in Finland 2006' (PMID:17254406) says 'In 1974, the older twins were identified, with a total of 13,888 like-sexed pairs of known zygosity.' That makes three member cohorts. The 2019 older-cohort and FinnTwin16 profile papers (PMID:31462340, PMID:31796134) were not read in full and might give each cohort's achieved size.

label: FINRISK
counts: no pooled participant number found; the profile gives invitees (101 451 across nine surveys, 1972-2012)
note: The cohort profile (PMID:29165699, definition source) has no abstract and is not open access; academic.oup.com refuses curl (403). Read only through WebFetch, which passes the page through a model, so these spans are not recorded as verbatim evidence: 'Altogether, the FINRISK Study has now had nine cross-sectional surveys including a total of 101 451 invitees (Table 1).' It also gives participation rates (91% of men and 94% of women in 1972; 57% and 67% in 2012) but no total of participants. The WebFetch output also claimed a sentence 'The cohort formed by the participants include 101 451 men and women aged 25 to 74 years', which conflicts with 101 451 being the invitees. PMC2465683 (non-participation paper, read through WebFetch) says 'The total sample size for all surveys in the age range 25–74 years was 54 453, out of which 45 902 (84%) participated' for 1972–92 only. The example study (PMID:35748965) gives no counts. Reading the profile's Table 1 directly would settle the number of participants.

label: Flemish Gut Flora Project
counts: participants providing stool samples (stated as more than 5000)
quote: We collect and examine stool samples from more than 5000 participants.
note: A lower bound from the VIB project page. A 2015 conference abstract (PMC4582441) calls FGFP 'a large-scale (n>5000) microbiome research project'. The 2016 Science paper (PMID:27126039) abstract analysed 'the Belgian Flemish Gut Flora Project (FGFP; discovery cohort; N = 1106)'. The definition source and example study (PMID:34957435) used a 2018 release with 'genotype (Illumina Human CoreExome array) and bowel data for 2,027 individuals' and n = 2,001 in the meta-analysis. No design paper giving an exact achieved enrolment was found.

label: Gabriel Advanced Survey
counts: children in the phase I screening survey
quote: In a first-screening phase, a comprehensive population-based survey was conducted to assess the prevalence of exposure to farming environments and of asthma and atopic diseases (n = 103,219).
note: From the GABRIEL Advanced Surveys design paper (definition source), abstract. Phase II: 'a stratified random sample of phase 1 participants (n = 15,255)'; phase III in Bavaria: n = 895. PMID:22534534 gives the Alpine arm only (79,888 phase I children; 8,419 in phase II) and PMID:23621318 the Polish arm only (23 331 families in phase I).

label: GCAT Genomes for Life
counts: volunteers recruited 2014-2018
quote: The GCAT cohort comprises 20,000 volunteers, recruited between 2014 and 2018, from Catalan general population, aged between 40 and 65 years old at the time of recruitment, and 59.16% women.
note: From a 2024 GCAT multiomic paper (PMID:39449064), a round figure. The 2018 cohort profile (PMID:29593016, definition source and example study) gives the planned size ('At the end of 2017, the GCAT Study will have recruited 20 000 participants aged 40-65 years') and says the laboratory 'currently contains around 270 000 2D tubes from blood aliquots from 18 659 participants'; its Table 5 lists baseline characteristics by sex (7471 men, 10 918 women, 62 missing). A later cohort profile update, if one exists, would give the exact achieved count.

label: GENESIS
counts: participants included 2007-2013 (stated as over 6000)
quote: This is a large study including over 6000 participants, and the biological, clinical and epidemiological data collected are detailed and complete.
note: From the GENESIS resource paper (PMID:26758370, definition source). The paper's own group counts are: 'A total of 1721 index cases, 826 affected sisters, 599 unaffected sisters and 1419 controls were included.' Cases here are the index cases and controls the unrelated controls; affected sisters (826) are further cases and unaffected sisters (599) further controls. The 'over 6000 participants' in the discussion is larger than those four groups and may count other relatives (the paper says parents and brothers were also contacted), so it is recorded with low confidence; no total of the four groups is stated.

label: Genetic Analysis of Multiple Sclerosis
counts: cases and controls after QC in the 2011 IMSGC/WTCCC2 GWAS; no total stated
quote: We introduced a number of novel quality control (QC) methods for processing these datasets (see Supplementary Information), which ultimately provided reliable information from 9772 cases and 17376 controls (see Figure 1A).
note: The EGA study EGAS00000000101 (definition source) cites no paper; its description (cases from many parts of the world on the Illumina 660 chip with Swedish controls, WTCCC2 common UK controls and controls from other published studies) matches the IMSGC/WTCCC2 GWAS (PMID:21833088), which says 'We genotyped the cases (9772) and some Swedish controls (527) using the Illumina Human 660-Quad platform, and the UK controls (5175, the WTCCC2 common control set12,13) using the Illumina 1.2M platform.' The controls include published-study controls not generated by this study. Neither source states a total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null. The EGA dataset EGAD00000000120 ('WTCCC2 project Multiple Sclerosis (MS) samples') lists 11375 samples in its metadata. The example study (PMID:31604244) gives no count for this collection.

label: Genetic Consortium for Anorexia Nervosa
counts: AN cases and matched controls in the 2014 GCAN/WTCCC3 discovery GWAS; no total stated
quote: We performed a GWAS in 2907 cases with AN from 14 countries (15 sites) and 14 860 ancestrally matched controls as part of the Genetic Consortium for AN (GCAN) and the Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 3 (WTCCC3).
note: From the consortium's flagship GWAS (example study), abstract; cases came from 14 countries (15 sites). The same abstract says 'The final global meta-analysis across discovery and replication data sets comprised 5551 AN cases and 21 080 controls.' The EGA study EGAS00001000913 (definition source) says 'we have amassed the largest anorexia nervosa (AN)sample in the world (~4,000)' and proposes exome-chip genotyping of '3,000 female cases and 3,000 archived matched controls'. No total of cases plus controls is stated, so participants is left null.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of Asthma in Costa Rica
counts: consented subjects in the dbGaP/TOPMed release (pedigrees and trios)
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 4283
note: From the dbGaP study page (definition source), phs000988.v6.p1; this counts subjects consented for the shared data, not necessarily everyone recruited. The same page says of the trio arm '1,200 asthmatic children and their parents (3,600 individuals) were ascertained and enrolled in this study in the Central Valley of Costa Rica', and that at least 15 extended pedigrees were enrolled. The example study (PMID:33888571) was not needed for the number.

label: Genetic Overlap between Metabolic and Psychiatric traits
counts: patients' DNA samples in the GOMAP collection (cases only)
quote: The GOMAP (Genetic Overlap between Metabolic and Psychiatric disorders) study comprises a collection of 2,747 DNA samples from four different patient categories: T2D patients, SCZ patients, individuals with both SCZ and T2D (referred to from here on as SCZplusT2D), and individuals with a different psychiatric diagnosis (this last group is not used in further analyses reported here) (Table 1).
note: From PMID:30470734 (definition source), full text. GOMAP is described there as 'a cases-only sample collection'; the population controls (n = 1,125: TEENAGE n = 413 and ARGO n = 712) come from other Greek cohorts and are not counted here. After QC: 'A total of 2,582 samples passed QC' (SCZ n = 924; T2D n = 822; T2D/SCZ n = 505; other diagnosis n = 331).

label: Genetic Prostate cancer risk stratification for targeted screening
counts: men who entered the PROFILE pilot study, December 2010 to January 2013
quote: The enrollment was closed in January 2013 when 115 men had entered the study and 100 had agreed to undergo PB (Table 1).
note: From the PROFILE feasibility (pilot) study (PMID:27151655, definition source and example study), full text: 897 men were invited, 285 replied, 115 entered and 100 underwent biopsy (abstract: 'A total of 100 men aged 40-69 years with a FH of PrCa underwent PB'). The paper says 'A larger prospective study powered to detect statistical associations is in progress'; the COHO term is defined from the pilot, and the later full PROFILE study's size was not read.

label: Genetic Research in Isolated Populations
counts: no pooled number; the programme's source population, not its participants, is stated
note: The definition source (epib.nl) no longer resolves; its 2014 archived copy describes the programme but gives only the size of the source population ('Using municipal records and genealogical databases of this isolated population of 20,000 residents, we were able to link most of the patients of each disorder to a common ancestor.'), not a number of participants, and names no fixed set of member studies. The example study (PMID:22570627) uses 'an independent series of 104 glaucoma cases from an isolated population (Genetic Research in an Isolated Population [GRIP] study)'. Its family-based arm, the Erasmus Rucphen Family study (COHO:0000063), has its own count (n=2065). A GRIP overview paper listing its disease-specific patient series would settle a pooled number.

label: Genetics of diabetes Audit and Research
counts: participants recruited 1998-2015 (T2D patients and healthy controls)
quote: This gives a current total GoDARTS cohort of 18 306 participants, 10 149 of whom have T2D ( ∼ 44.8% of the DARTS study, representing the diabetic population in Tayside) and 8157 of whom were healthy controls at baseline.
note: From the GoDARTS cohort profile (PMID:29025058, definition source), full text. Phases: GoDARTS1 recruited 2763 patients with T2D (1998-2004); GoDARTS2 'A total of 16 146 people were recruited in this phase, including 7989 patients with T2D and 8157 matched healthy controls'; GoDARTS3 recruited 1342 patients with T2D (2009-2015), with overlaps between phases.

label: Genetics of Healthy Aging
counts: participants (nonagenarian siblings and younger controls) whose samples reached the central DNA extraction centre, recruitment 2004-2008
quote: The central DNA extraction centre in Helsinki received a total of 11392 samples belonging to 7918 participants from the recruitment centres.
note: Design paper (PMID:21871552) gives the enrolled groups separately but no stated overall total: "Thus, a total of 5319 old siblings from 2535 GEHA families with at least 2 old siblings were enrolled in the GEHA project." and "A total of 2548 younger control persons consented to participate in the study and were interviewed." (recorded as cases/controls; the old siblings are the long-lived group, not disease cases). Also: 5418 old participants from 2634 families were visited and interviewed; 2249 complete trios formed. The 7918 figure is the only stated count of all participants; it is the number with samples at the DNA centre, not strictly the enrolled number.

label: GenomeAsia 100K project
counts: high-coverage genomes in the GenomeAsia Phase 2 dataset after QC and relative removal
quote: After standard quality control filters and the removal of one individual from each first-degree relative pair, we obtained a set of 6442 high-coverage genomes (average 25×) for downstream analyses (Supplementary Data 1).
note: The GAsP2 dataset (PMID:37291107) combines newly sequenced samples with previously published genomes, so 6442 is the dataset size rather than people recruited by the project alone; it states "Of these, 5734 genomes were of South Asian ancestry (5118 of which were sequenced for this study)" and "WGS data from 4806 individuals recruited from the healthcare delivery systems of Pakistan, India and Bangladesh, combined with WGS from 927 individuals from isolated South Asian populations". The pilot phase (PMID:31802016) reported "a whole-genome sequencing reference dataset from 1,739 individuals of 219 population groups and 64 countries across Asia". The project's target of 100,000 genomes is a plan, not an achieved size.

label: German Multiple Myeloma Study Group
counts: patients recruited across GMMG trials (stated as more than 5300)
quote: > 5300 IN GMMG-STUDIEN REKRUTIERTE PATIENTEN
note: Cohort aggregation; the group's website gives a pooled lower bound ("> 5300" patients recruited in GMMG trials) rather than an exact count, fetched 2026-09-25. The same page states the flagship ongoing trial reached its recruitment target: "Die GMMG-HD8/DSMM XIX-Studie hat am 26.02.2025 das Rekrutierungsende mit 514 Patienten erreicht". The page does not list the number of member trials. Example study PMID:39103364 not used for the pooled figure.

label: Ghana Prostate Study
counts: prostate cancer cases and population controls, 2004-2012 (no stated overall total)
quote: The Ghana Prostate Study is a case-control study of PCa that was conducted from 2004 to 2012 in 749 cases and 964 controls.
note: Cases and controls are stated but no source read gives their total, so participants is left null. Quote read from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:30530485 (search API). Definition source PMID:32350862 gives the components: "There were 1,049 men sampled between 2004–2006, of which 1,037 were ultimately enrolled (a response rate of 98.8%)." (population screening, 73 cases and 964 controls) and "an additional 676 prostate cancer patients were recruited from the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital in 2008–2012"; its analysis used 566 cases and 964 controls. The cohort's own total number of men would settle it.

label: Glaucoma Inheritance Study in Tasmania
counts: probands and family members examined
quote: Of 2062 participants examined, 1700 were classified as POAG.
note: From the abstract of the study's design paper (Europe PMC). Of these, 1700 had POAG; "A total of 1014 participants (59.6%) belonged to families in which other members were affected". The 467 TEST participants were an external reference group, not GIST participants. The example study (PMID:30267046) pools GIST with ANZRAG (3071 glaucoma cases in total) and gives no GIST-only count.

label: Greece Hellenic Isolated Cohorts
counts: analysed subset: whole-genome-sequenced samples from MANOLIS and Pomak combined
quote: We use whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to capture the entire allele frequency spectrum in 2,893 samples from two Greek population-based cohorts, MANOLIS and Pomak.
note: Cohort aggregation of two cohorts; no source read states the total number recruited into HELIC, so this is the analysed WGS subset from the definition source (PMID:34857772). Other figures: the same paper sequenced "1482 MANOLIS samples and 1642 Pomak samples"; PMID:37778719 used "3,005 individuals from the HELIC founder populations cohort"; PMID:25373335 genotyped 2,296 samples from the two isolates; PMID:27989266 studied MANOLIS adults (n 1553). The HELIC project page cited by the paper now redirects to the Helmholtz Munich home page. A HELIC cohort profile or www.helic.org stating recruitment would settle it.

label: Health and Retirement Study
counts: individuals over age 50 surveyed since 1992 (stated as more than 37 000), in 23 000 households
quote: The Health and Retirement Study (HRS) is a nationally representative longitudinal survey of more than 37 000 individuals over age 50 in 23 000 households in the USA.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:24671021, 2014); the figure is a lower bound ("more than"). The profile's Table 1 gives per-entry-cohort baseline sizes (e.g. the original 1992 HRS cohort: 12 652 interviewed of 15 497 eligible). The HRS website (hrs.isr.umich.edu) returned no readable content to a script, so no more recent total was read.

label: Health2000 Study
counts: nationally representative sample of persons aged 30 or over drawn and invited, 2000-2001
quote: In Health 2000 Survey, conducted in Finland in 2000–2001, a nationally representative sample of 8,028 persons aged 30 years or over was drawn from the population register and invited to take part in a two-phased study.
note: 8028 is the invited sample, not the number who took part. The same paper (PMID:26672964) states: "Of these 7,087 (89%) responded to the interview and 6,354 reported for physical examinations". PMID:34396808 also states "used two-stage cluster sampling to identify 8028 persons aged at least 30 years". The definition source (sisuproject.fi/cohorts) is behind a JavaScript challenge and is not cached, so it was not read; the survey's separate sample of 18-29-year-olds was not found in any source read. The Health 2000 methodology report (THL) would settle the participant count.

label: Heart Protection Study
counts: UK adults aged 40-80 randomised, 1994-1997
quote: 20,536 UK adults (aged 40-80 years) with coronary disease, other occlusive arterial disease, or diabetes were randomly allocated to receive 40 mg simvastatin daily (average compliance: 85%) or matching placebo (average non-study statin use: 17%).
note: Quote read from the Europe PMC abstract of the main simvastatin results paper (Lancet 2002); the vitamin results paper PMID:12114037 states the same 20,536. The definition source (PMID:10329064) gives the randomised numbers by sex: "Between July 1994 and May 1997, 15 454 men and 5082 women were randomized, with 9515 aged over 65 years at entry."

label: Hoorn Diabetes Care System
counts: people with type 2 diabetes enrolled with at least one annual examination, 1998-2015
quote: In 2015, 12 673 individuals with T2D and at least one annual examination at the DCS centre had been enrolled in the study, of which 2497 had died during follow-up.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:28588112). A dynamic cohort still enrolling, so later counts will be larger; 1413 participants were lost to follow-up and about 5500 have biobank samples.

label: Hospital Discharge Register Sweden
counts: no stated number of persons
note: Nationwide register of inpatient discharges. The definition source (PMID:21658213, full text read) gives the volume of records, not people: "Each year, there are about 1.5 million hospital discharges in the IPR (Figure 4), with the majority of these taking place in somatic care." No source read states how many distinct persons the register covers. A National Board of Health and Welfare statistic on unique individuals in the register would settle it; the example study (PMID:32117730) was not needed, since it would describe only the subset it used.

label: Human Genetics Initiative
counts: participants with clinical data and biomaterials available in the NIMH repository (approximately), 2016
quote: Currently, clinical data and biomaterials from approximately 120,000 participants are available, with more than 200,000 to be available soon.
note: Cohort aggregation; pooled count for the NIMH Repository and Genomics Resource that holds the Human Genetics Initiative collections, from the May 2016 council minutes (definition source). The same minutes elsewhere say the repository has "more than 200,000 well-characterized, high-quality patient and control samples" (samples, not participants). The number of member collections is not stated there.

label: Hunter Community Study
counts: men and women aged 55-85 recruited in the first phase
quote: The first phase of this study sampled 3253 people representing a response rate of 44.5%.
note: From the study's dataset record (definition source, issued 2011). The example study (PMID:27030319) says "Over 7,500 people were randomly selected from the compulsory electoral roll of Newcastle, Australia, and invited to participate" and used a genotyped subset of n = 313.

label: Icelandic Cancer Registry
counts: no stated number of persons; cancer diagnoses only
note: The definition source's abstract (read via Europe PMC) counts diagnoses, not people: "Data from the ICR for the period 1955-2009 (41 994 cancer diagnoses) were used, applying established quantitative and semi-quantitative methods." A person may have more than one diagnosis, so this is not recorded as participants. Its full text (Acta Oncologica, tandfonline) is closed and blocked (403) and not cached. The example study (PMID:39886913) gives only its 2020-2022 subset (522 colorectal and 106 endometrial cases). A registry statistic on the number of individuals registered would settle it.

label: Identification of Men with a genetic predisposition to ProstAte Cancer
counts: men aged 40-69 recruited 2005-2015 (BRCA1/2 carriers and non-carrier controls)
quote: Between 2005 and 2015, 3063 participants aged 40-69 yr (median 54 yr) were recruited from 65 centres in 20 countries in two cohorts: (1) BRCA1/BRCA2 PGV carriers (915 BRCA1, 901 BRCA2); and (2) age-matched noncarriers for a familial PGV (727 BRCA1 and 520 BRCA2 noncarriers).
note: Quote read from the Europe PMC abstract of the five-round results paper (2026), the most recent report of the whole study. Earlier: the definition source (PMID:20840664) "In total, 300 men were recruited" (preliminary, first 300); the example study (PMID:24484606) "We recruited 2481 men (791 BRCA1 carriers, 531 BRCA1 controls; 731 BRCA2 carriers, 428 BRCA2 controls)" to February 2013. Carriers and non-carriers are the study's groups (not a disease case-control design), so cases/controls are left null; group sizes are in the quote.

label: IIBDGC genotyped CD study
counts: analysed subset: genotyped Crohn's disease cases of known smoking status
quote: We used 55 immunochip-wide data sets that included 19,735 IBD cases (10,856 CD cases and 8879 UC cases) of known smoking status.
note: The definition source and example (PMID:28506689) is a case-only analysis; 10,856 is the CD subset with known smoking status from IIBDGC centres with at least 10 samples per smoking category, not every genotyped CD patient in the consortium. Controls (n=8143 genotyped at ten centres) are not part of this cohort. No source read states the total number of genotyped CD patients; the IIBDGC Immunochip papers (e.g. PMID:26192919) would give a larger whole-collection figure.

label: Indiana Sisters Study
counts: healthy premenopausal white (European-American) sisters studied; excludes the extended and African-American samples
quote: Healthy premenopausal white sisters (age 33.1+/-7.2, n=1692) and healthy white brothers (age 33.6+/-10.9, n=715) were studied.
note: No design paper or website stating the whole cohort's size was found; each figure read is a sample used in one analysis. Quote read from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:18755304 (the brothers are a separate sample, not part of this cohort). Other figures: PMID:17909879 "1,688 European American, premenopausal sisters, 512 African American premenopausal sisters"; PMID:20164292 "1524 premenopausal EA women aged 20-45 yr from 762 sibships and 669 AA premenopausal women aged 20-44 yr from 383 sibships"; the definition source (PMID:23074152) Table 1 lists Indiana Sisters Study 1504 (discovery) and Indiana Sisters Extended Study 802 European American and 1090 African American (replication). A profile giving total enrolment across the core and extended samples would settle it.

label: INfancia y Medio Ambiente Project
counts: total N of the base study (mother-child pairs recruited in the seven cohorts, 1997-2008)
quote: INMA 21471022 http://www.proyectoinma.org/ Population-based birth cohort Spain 1997–2008 3768 >90% European
note: Cohort aggregation. The quote is the INMA row of Table 1 of the PACE Consortium cohort profile (PMID:29025028), whose column is headed "Total N of base study". The INMA website (definition source) gives only per-cohort sizes: Ribera d'Ebre (n=102), Menorca (n=492), Granada (n=668), Valencia (n=787), Sabadell (n=622), Asturias (n=485) and Gipuzkoa (n=612), i.e. seven member cohorts; no total is stated there. A 2025 scoping review (PMC12570564) lists INMA with 3,944 and 3,768 in columns not identified here. The INMA cohort profile (PMID:21471022, IJE) is closed to scripts (403) and has no abstract; it would give the design's own total. The example study (PMID:30850646) used 1061 INMA individuals as controls.

label: International Cancer Genome Consortium-Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
counts: CLL cases in the project's comprehensive genomic evaluation (excludes 54 patients with monoclonal B-lymphocytosis)
quote: Here we describe a comprehensive evaluation of the genomic landscape of 452 CLL cases and 54 patients with monoclonal B-lymphocytosis, a precursor disorder.
note: Quote read from the Europe PMC abstract of the ICGC-CLL genome project's main 2015 paper (Nature). The EGA study (definition source, EGAS00000000092) states the plan "to generating a comprehensive catalogue of genetic alterations in 500 independent tumours" (a target, not an achieved size). The example study (PMID:21642962) sequenced four whole genomes and validated in "363 patients with CLL".

label: International Headache Genetics Consortium
counts: migraine cases and controls in the 2016 IHGC meta-analysis of 22 GWA studies (as rounded in the title)
quote: Meta-analysis of 375,000 individuals identifies 38 susceptibility loci for migraine.
note: Cohort aggregation; the definition source's own figure is rounded in its title. Its abstract gives the exact groups: "To identify new susceptibility loci, we carried out a genetic study of migraine on 59,674 affected subjects and 316,078 controls from 22 GWA studies." (collected from six tertiary headache clinics and 27 population-based cohorts). A later IHGC analysis (PMID:35115687, 2022) is larger: "we performed a genome-wide association study of 102,084 migraine cases and 771,257 controls", with no stated total, so the 2016 figure is recorded; a reviewer may prefer the 2022 cases and controls.

label: International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium
counts: cases and controls passing QC in the 2011 IMSGC/WTCCC2 GWAS discovery analysis
quote: We introduced a number of novel quality control (QC) methods for processing these datasets (see Supplementary Information), which ultimately provided reliable information from 9772 cases and 17376 controls (see Figure 1A).
note: Consortium; flagship analysis is the 2011 Nature GWAS (definition source), whose abstract says 9772 cases of European descent from 23 research groups in 15 countries. No sentence read states the combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The replication analysis added 4218 cases and 7296 controls. The example study (PMID:22570697) used only 931 IMSGC cases from dbGaP. Later IMSGC meta-analyses (e.g. 2019) were not read here; the consortium's most recent flagship would give a larger number.

label: International Schizophrenia Consortium
counts: European cases and controls in the 2009 ISC GWAS after QC
quote: We performed a genome-wide association study of 3,322 European individuals with schizophrenia and 3,587 controls.
note: Consortium; flagship analysis is the 2009 Nature GWAS (definition source and example study). No sentence states the combined total, so participants is null rather than summed. The supplement gives the raw dataset before QC as 3,798 cases and 3,998 controls; the combined sample with the companion MGS and SGENE studies was 8,014 cases and 19,080 controls.

label: Italian Network on Genetic Isolates Studies
counts: individuals of the INGI cohorts in the 2019 GWAS meta-analysis (analysed subset)
quote: GWAS analyses using the different imputation panels comprised a total of 3292 individuals (Supplementary Table 8).
note: Consortium of isolate cohorts (Val Borbera, Friuli Venezia Giulia, Carlantino). The definition source reports whole-genome sequencing of 947 samples, of which 926 passed QC, and a GWAS meta-analysis of 3292 individuals; neither is the full enrolment of the member cohorts, and the Supplementary Notes give only village census sizes. The size of each member cohort's recruitment (from the INGI cohort profile papers or website) would settle a whole-consortium number.

label: Leeds Melanoma Cohort
counts: melanoma patients recruited 2000-2012
quote: 2183 patients were recruited to the Leeds Melanoma Cohort (LMC) between 2000 and 2012 (Newton-Bishop et al., 2015).
note: Quote from the PMC full text (PMC6983339) of the definition source. Vitamin D levels were available for 1780 subjects; 574 patients had died at median follow-up 6.7 years. The cohort's profile (Newton-Bishop et al. 2015) was not read.

label: Leiden Longevity Study
counts: long-lived proband siblings, their offspring and the offspring's spouses
quote: In total, 944 long-lived proband siblings with a mean age of 94 years (range, 89–104), 1671 offspring (61 years, 39–81) and 744 spouses thereof (60 years, 36–79) were included.
note: The quote (PMID:24425829, open access) gives the three enrolled groups separately (944 long-lived siblings, 1671 offspring, 744 spouses) but no total, so participants is left null rather than summed. Other LLS papers agree: 421 families (PMC6132126, PMC7051926), 'In total, 944 longevous F1 participants ... were included' (PMC6132126), and 'The total study population, excluding the nonagenarian siblings, consisted of 2415 participants (1671 offspring; 744 partners)' (PMC3047139). One paper mentions 'the LLS study as a whole ( N = 1986)' without explanation (PMC9550250). The definition source PMID:16251894 is closed (abstract only on disk). The example study (PMID:26068415) gives only the pooled 7,478 of its seven-cohort meta-analysis. Families were recruited 'between 2003 and 2006' (PMC7051926).

label: LifeLines
counts: participants with baseline data, recruited 2006-2013
quote: Baseline data were collected for 167 729 participants, aged from 6 months to 93 years.
note: From the cohort profile abstract (definition source): recruitment between 2006 and 2013 in the northern Netherlands; genome-wide genetic data for 15 638 participants.

label: Living Biobank
counts: individuals with array genotypes analysed in 2017 (analysed subset)
quote: Using genotypes across 435,314 SNPs, we compared the ancestry backgrounds of 2,452 individuals in the Singapore Living Biobank with 268 individuals previously reported by the Singapore Genome Variation Project (SGVP) [ 54 ].
note: From the paper the EGA study (EGAS00001002619, definition source) cites, PMC5636172. The EGA study itself holds a subset of 762 closely related individuals (263 Chinese, 499 Malays). The example study (PMID:32936915) abstract gives 983 Malay Living Biobank participants on GWAS array; its full text is not on disk. No source read states the biobank's total enrolment; a Living Biobank design paper or the programme's website would settle it.

label: Los Angeles component of The Womens Contraceptive and Reproductive Experiences Study
counts: African American cases and controls in the AABC GWAS scan (analysed subset)
quote: Cases in Los Angeles County were diagnosed from July 1, 1994 through April 30, 1998, and controls were sampled by random-digit dialing (RDD) from the same population and time period; 380 African American cases and 224 African American controls were included in Stage 1 of the scan.
note: Only the African American subset genotyped for the AABC consortium is reported in any source read; the same 380/224 appears in PMC3749077 and PMC5445618, and after QC 254 cases and 204 controls of African ancestry were used in a 2024 Nature Genetics supplement. The definition source (PMID:18628424) reports 1457 cases and 1455 controls aged 55-64 across all five Women's CARE sites, not the Los Angeles component. The example study (PMID:42098873) gives no CARE-specific count in its text. The Los Angeles site's full enrolment (White and African American women) would need the Women's CARE design paper (Marchbanks et al.) or a Los Angeles-specific report; no total was stated, so participants is null.

label: Lothian Birth Cohorts
