counts: member counts only: 2 member cohorts (LBC1921 550 recruited 1999-2001; LBC1936 1091 recruited 2004-2007)
quote: Between 2004 and 2007, 1091 members of SMS1947 were recruited to Wave 1 of the LBC1936 study, at a mean age of 70 years.
note: Aggregation of two cohorts; the 2018 profile update (definition source, PMC6124629) reports each member separately and gives no combined total, so participants is null rather than summed. The companion sentence for the other member is 'Between 1999 and 2001, 550 of the SMS1932 were recruited to Wave 1 of the LBC1921 study, at a mean age of 79 years.' The example study (PMID:21826061) pools LBC1921 and LBC1936 with three other CAGES cohorts (3511 individuals), not a LBC-only figure.

label: Lund Stroke Register
counts: patients with first-ever stroke found in the register's first year of screening (2001-2002)
quote: A total of 456 patients with first-ever stroke (n = 412 prospective screening methods, n = 17 primary care, n = 12 hospital registers, n = 10 death register, n = 2 autopsy registers, n = 3 other).
note: From the definition source's abstract (full text not on disk); it covers only the one-year screening. The register is ongoing since 1 March 2001 (MEGASTROKE supplement, s41588-018-0058-3), so its current size is larger; no source read states it. PMID:24803595 says 416 patients were included in the register between 1 March 2001 and 28 February 2002. PMC3783404 used LSR and Malmö Diet and Cancer together (3145 patients, 1793 controls), not LSR alone. The example study (PMID:30796134) gives no LSR count in its text. A recent LSR description or the register's website would settle the total.

label: Marseille Thrombosis Association Study
counts: unrelated venous thrombosis patients recruited 1994-2005
quote: MARTHA patients (n = 1,592) are unrelated VT patients, mainly of French origin, consecutively recruited at the Thrombophilia center of La Timone hospital (Marseille, France) between January 1994 and October 2005.
note: From the definition source's full text (PMC3181335). The GWAS genotyped 1,542 cases (after QC), with controls from the Three-City Study, not MARTHA. The example study (PMID:39424413) agrees that MARTHA 'consists of 1 592 patients with VT' and used a subsample of 1011.

label: Mexican Biobank
counts: individuals genotyped from 898 localities in all 32 states
quote: To fill this gap, the Mexican Biobank project genotyped 6,057 individuals from 898 rural and urban localities across all 32 states in Mexico at a resolution of 1.8 million genome-wide markers with linked complex trait and disease information creating a valuable nationwide genotype–phenotype database.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMC10600006). The paper says the samples were selected for genomic characterization from people recruited by the National Institute of Public Health, enriched for Indigenous-language speakers and rural localities; the size of the source survey was not read here. Subsets used in analyses range from 5,436 to 5,833.

label: MIRAGE
counts: no whole-study enrolment found; only analysed subsets in tables
note: No sentence read states how many people the MIRAGE Study enrolled. The definition source (PMID:22159054, PMC3356921) gives MIRAGE only in Table 1: 267 African American cases and 292 controls (total 559) and 609 white cases and 875 controls (total 1484), analysed subsets. Other papers give further analysed subsets: 'For this study, we used 1262 subjects (509 cases and 753 controls)16 from the MIRAGE Caucasian data set.' (PMC3365264); a 2010 meta-analysis table lists MIRAGE Caucasian 560 cases/790 controls and African American 180 cases/200 controls (PMC3048805); an NSAID analysis queried 756 probands and 1020 relatives (PMC546007). MIRAGE enrolled AD cases and unaffected sibling controls at 17 clinical centres in the United States, Canada, Germany and Greece. The MIRAGE design paper (reference 27 of the definition source, reference 15 of PMC3048805) would settle the enrolment.

label: Molecular Genetics of Schizophrenia Collaboration
counts: European-ancestry cases and controls in the primary 2009 MGS GWAS (African American sample separate)
quote: Because the frequencies of tag SNPs and disease susceptibility alleles can vary across populations, we carried out a primary analysis of the larger MGS European-ancestry sample (2,681 cases, 2,653 controls) and then additional analyses of the African American sample (1,286 cases, 973 controls) and of both of these samples combined, to test the hypothesis that there are alleles that influence susceptibility in both populations.
note: Collaboration; flagship analysis is the 2009 Nature GWAS (definition source, PMC2775422). The same sentence gives the African American sample as 1,286 cases and 973 controls. No sentence states a combined total, so participants is null rather than summed. The supplement gives post-QC sample totals of 5334 European-ancestry and 2259 African American (Table S5, a table), and 'In total, 3,364 EA and 1,301 AA control subjects were recruited'. The meta-analysis with ISC and SGENE covered 8,008 cases and 19,077 controls.

label: MOnica Risk, Genetics, Archiving and Monograph
counts: persons free of cardiovascular disease at baseline in the 2009 MORGAM stroke analysis (43 cohorts, 18 populations)
quote: In 93 695 persons aged 19 to 77 years and free of major cardiovascular disease at baseline, total observation years were 1 234 252 and the number of stroke events analyzed was 3142.
note: Project pooling European cohorts; the number is the definition source's analysed population (abstract; full text not on disk). The example study (PMID:22848412, PMC3405046) says 'The MORGAM project comprises >128,000 men and women from 57 European (mainly white Caucasian) cohorts', a lower bound for the whole project, not recorded because it is not an exact count. The MORGAM design paper would give the exact whole-project number.

label: Monitoring of Trends and Determinants in Cardiovascular Disease
counts: surveillance project; only the population covered and the number of centres are stated
quote: Thirty-nine collaborating centres from 26 countries of Europe, North America, and the Western Pacific collaborate in this project, using a standardized protocol and covering a population of approximately 10 million men and women aged 35-64.
note: MONICA monitored event rates in whole populations and ran risk-factor sample surveys; the 'approximately 10 million' is the population under surveillance, not enrolled participants, so participants is null. The project website (https://www.thl.fi/monica/) says 'There were total of 32 MONICA Collaborating Centres in 21 countries.' and 'The total population age 25-64 years monitored was ten million men and women.' The example study (PMID:22162987) uses only the MONICA/KORA Augsburg surveys. The pooled number of risk-factor survey participants (MONICA Monograph or data books) would give a participant count.

label: Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis
counts: men and women aged 45-84 recruited 2000-2002
quote: Between 2000 and 2002, MESA recruited 6,814 men and women 45 to 84 years of age from Forsyth County, North Carolina; New York City; Baltimore;
note: The design paper (definition source, PMID:12397006, abstract only on disk) gives the planned 'population-based sample of 6,500 men and women aged 45-84 years'. The achieved 6,814 is stated in many cohort descriptions read here (e.g. PMC9395431 'MESA included 6814 participants between the ages of 45–84 years recruited at six clinical centers', PMC9576575, PMC6050158). The example study (PMID:34732054) gives no MESA total in its text.

label: Multicenter Family Study
counts: genotyped individuals from 631 pedigrees in the 2012 family GWAS
quote: The family sample included 2,461 individuals from 631 pedigrees (581 in the primary European-ancestry analyses).
note: Aggregation of seven family collections; the number is the pooled sample of its flagship GWAS (definition source abstract, also in PMC6927206). It counts genotyped individuals; the collections may have ascertained more family members than were genotyped. The example study (PMID:23974872) was not needed.

label: Multiethnic Cohort Study of Diet and Health
counts: men and women aged 45-75 enrolled 1993-1996
quote: The cohort consists of 215,251 adult men and women (age 45-75 years at baseline) living in Hawaii and in California (primarily Los Angeles County) with the following ethnic distribution: African-American (16.3%), Latino (22.0%), Japanese-American (26.4%), Native Hawaiian (6.5%), White (22.9%), and other ancestry (5.8%).
note: From the cohort design paper (definition source; abstract, and full text PMC4482109, which also says 'the total number of subjects who comprised the cohort was 215,251'). Its Table gives 96,810 men and 118,441 women.

label: Multiple Environmental and Genetic Assessment of Risk Factors for Venous Thrombosis
counts: participating patients with first venous thrombosis, 1999-2004 (controls in two groups, no stated total)
quote: Of the remaining 6257 patients, 5184 participated (83%).
note: From the definition source's full text (PMC2726929). Controls were recruited in two groups stated separately in the same paragraph: partners ('Of the remaining 3734 partners, 3039 participated (81.4%).') and random-digit-dialling controls ('Of the remaining 4346 individuals, 3000 participated (69%).'). No sentence states the total of controls or of all participants, so controls and participants are null rather than summed. The oral-contraceptive analysis itself included 1524 patients and 1760 controls. The example study (PMID:39424413) says MEGA comprises 1289 patients with VT, apparently the genotyped subset.

label: National Study of Colorectal Cancer Genetics
counts: cases and spouse/partner controls entered by 2007
quote: To date, blood samples and completed questionnaires have been collected from 8722 cases and 2185 controls.
note: Design paper (PMID:17895893, 2007) gives 8722 cases and 2185 controls but states no total, so participants is left null. Collection was ongoing, with a target of 20,000 cases; the example GWAS (PMID:19011631) used NSCCG subsets (2,873 cases in phase 2; 3,286 cases and 3,017 controls in replication, ascertained post 2005). A later NSCCG profile giving the final size would settle the achieved number.

label: Netherlands Twin Registry
counts: twins and family members with longitudinal data (lower bound)
quote: NTR collects longitudinal data from over 200,000 participants, including twins (40%) and their family.
note: Website (dated July 2024) says 'over 200,000'; recorded as 200000, a lower bound. The 2019 profile paper (PMID:31666148, abstract) says 'Since the early 1980s, the NTR has enrolled around 120,000 twins and a roughly equal number of their relatives', giving no total. The example study (PMID:26068415) used a metabolomics subsample.

label: New England-based Case-Control Study of Ovarian Cancer
counts: cases and controls enrolled across the four phases, 1984-2008
quote: From the four study phases, 2,465 eligible women with ovarian cancer consented for participation and were subsequently enrolled as cases.
note: Controls from the same source (PMID:33634849): 'Across the four study phases, 2,339 eligible women (55% of those eligible through lists and 72% of those eligible through random digit dialing) consented for participation and were enrolled as controls.' No total is stated, so participants is null. The analytic sample was 2,323 epithelial cases and 2,339 controls. This is an analysis paper, not the design paper (references 19 and 31 there), which might state a total.

label: Gastroparesis Clinical Research Consortium cohort
counts: participants enrolled in the GpCRC studies (approximate)
quote: We have enrolled approximately 1400 participants to date, with both delayed and normal emptying, in an approximately 3:1 ratio.
note: From the consortium's narrative review (PMID:35688353, 2022/2023), 'approximately 1400' recorded as 1400; it includes patients with normal gastric emptying as well as gastroparesis. The same review reports 981 patients enrolled over 12 years in one prospective analysis. The definition source and example GWAS (PMID:37688361) used 478 GpCRC gastroparesis patients as cases (analysed subset).

label: Nijmegen Biomedical Study
counts: NBS-1 questionnaire responders, 2002
quote: The first phase of NBS was started in 2002: 22 451 inhabitants of the municipality of Nijmegen were invited, of whom 9350 filled out the questionnaire and 6468 donated a blood sample.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:28082374). 22,451 invited, 9350 took part by returning the questionnaire, 6468 of them also gave blood; later phases re-approached NBS-1 participants. A pilot (2001-02) had 342 respondents.

label: Northern Ireland Cohort for Longitudinal Study of Ageing
counts: Wave 1 participants aged 50 and over, 2013-2016
quote: 8283 participants aged ≥50 years and living in private residential accommodation were recruited, from a randomized, stratified sample of Northern Ireland addresses, to the Wave 1 cohort between December 2013 and March 2016.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:37011634). The same paper says 'A total of 195 who were aged <50 years chose to participate, resulting in a total of 8478 participants in NICOLA Wave 1.' (partners under 50); 8283 is the age-eligible panel matching the definition. Wave 2 (2017-2019) retained 6152.

label: Northern Sweden Population Health Study
counts: NSPHS participants in the 2013 allergy study (may be the analysed subset)
quote: The study was conducted in Karesuando and Soppero in Northern Sweden as part of the Northern Sweden Population Health Study (n=1,068).
note: Definition source (PMID:23986895, abstract). Its full text gives the two collection rounds as approximate figures: 'The study was performed in 2 periods, with 750 participants mainly from the Karesuando area in 2006, and 350 participants from the Soppero and Vittangi area in 2009.' The example study (PMID:28832569) says SNP-array data were available for 1033 NSPHS individuals. A design paper giving the total enrolled would settle whether 1,068 is the whole cohort.

label: Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort study
counts: children only (lower bound); parents counted separately
quote: The cohort includes more than 114 000 children, 95 000 mothers and 75 000 fathers.
note: Cohort profile update (PMID:27063603, abstract): children born 1999-2009, 'more than 114 000 children, 95 000 mothers and 75 000 fathers'; no combined total is stated, so the number recorded counts children only. The institute's website (https://www.fhi.no/en/ch/studies/moba/) says the same: 'Over 114,000 children, 95,000 mothers, and 75,000 fathers are participating.' The example GWAS (PMID:35315439) analysed 28,681 children, 27,088 mothers and 26,239 fathers. The update's full text (OUP PDF) returned 403.

label: Orkney Complex Disease Study
counts: participants aged 16-100 recruited 2005-2011
quote: 2078 participants aged 16-100 years were recruited between 2005 and 2011, most having three or four grandparents from Orkney, the remainder with two Orcadian grandparents.
note: From the study's website (the definition source). The same page says the Viking Genes cohorts together (ORCADES, Viking Health Study - Shetland, Viking II & III) have over 10,000 volunteers; that figure is not ORCADES alone.

label: Outcome Reduction With Initial Glargine Intervention Trial
counts: randomised participants
quote: A total of 12,612 (mean age 64, 35% women) people in 40 countries were randomized during a 2-year period ending December 2005.
note: Design and baseline paper of the ORIGIN trial (abstract).

label: Ovarian Cancer Association Consortium
counts: OCAC cases and controls in the 2017 histotype GWAS
quote: Genetic association analyses were performed using genotype data from 25,509 population-based EOC cases and 40,941 controls from OCAC and meta-analysis of these data with 19,036 BRCA1 and 12,412 BRCA2 mutation carriers from CIMBA, of whom 2,933 and 954, respectively, were affected with EOC.
note: Flagship OCAC GWAS (PMID:28346442, 2017); no combined total is stated, so participants is null. The CIMBA carriers are a separate consortium. The definition source (https://sph.umich.edu/mocog/about.html) returned a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read; the example study (PMID:27697780, OncoArray design paper) gives no OCAC participant count. OCAC's own website, if readable, might state a pooled total or member-study count.

label: Oxford Biobank
counts: participants recruited by 2017
quote: The 7640 participants recruited so far in the OBB have a wide range of phenotypes that allow studying specific disease characteristics in relation to both their genotype and their phenotype.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:29040543). Its summary gives '∼8000 healthy participants'; Table 1 has 3324 men and 4316 women. Recruitment was ongoing at publication.

label: PanCareLIFE
counts: no pooled total stated
note: The design paper's abstract (PMID:30273888; full text closed) gives only per-study numbers: 'For our fertility studies, more than 6000 survivors have completed questionnaires, more than 1500 provided serum samples and more than 400 case-control triads have been identified.', 'More than 2000 survivors have contributed audiograms for the ototoxicity study.' and a planned SF-36 study in 'more than 10,000 survivors'. It names '17 partner institutions from eight European countries, with additional 11 data providers from five other countries' rather than a count of member cohorts. The example GWAS (PMID:38729340) used 743 female survivors. The project website (pancarelife.eu) gives no numbers. The full text might give a pooled total.

label: Parkinson Environment and Gene
counts: cases and controls in a 2025 analysis (analysed subset)
quote: PEG included 1367 participants (634 PD cases and 733 controls) (Table 1) with a mean (SD) age of 66.7 (11.2) years (623 [45.6%] female and 744 [54.4%] male; 27 [2.0%] African American, 64 [4.7%] American Indian or Alaska Native, 37 [2.7%] Asian, 263 [19.2%] Latino, and 976 [71.4%] White).
note: Definition source and example study (PMID:40094665): PEG1 (2000-2007) and PEG2 (2010-2017) participants with genetic, demographic and pesticide data; this may be fewer than all enrolled. A 2025 PEG paper (PMID:40510182, PMC12159956) gives enrolled patients only: 'A total of 357 participants in PEG1 and 470 in PEG2 were eligible and enrolled after the baseline exams.' No source read gives the total enrolled cases and controls; a PEG design paper would settle it.

label: People of the British Isles
counts: samples (people) collected in the whole PoBI project
quote: In total 4,371 samples were collected as part of the PoBI project.
note: From the 2015 fine-scale structure paper (PMID:25810005, PMC4632200), which analysed 2,039 of them. The definition source (PMID:21829225, 2011) said 'So far, some 4000 samples have been collected'; the example study (PMID:22961001) used 2,578 PoBI controls.

label: Physical Activity and Nutrition in Children Study
counts: children at baseline, 2007-2009
quote: A total of 504 children aged 7–9 years participated in the baseline examinations in 2007–2009 and underwent extensive phenotypic assessments and blood sampling for biomarker analyses.
note: Study website (definition source). Follow-ups: 438 children at 2 years (2009-2011), 277 adolescents at 8 years (2015-2017); a 16-year follow-up ran in 2024-2026.

label: Population-based Colonoscopy study
counts: general-population participants who underwent the research colonoscopy
quote: In the Swedish population-based colonoscopy (PopCol) study, 745 individuals from the general population underwent a colonoscopy of which 130 had diverticulosis, and none had diverticulitis.
note: Abstract of a 2025 PopCol paper, read through the Europe PMC API. The wider questionnaire sample is described inconsistently: 'The PopCol study recruited a random sample of 3556 adults; 745 underwent colonoscopy.' (PMID:31601615) versus 'invited a random sample of 3556 adults to participate, of which 745 underwent colonoscopy' (PMID:36987880); PMID:25947550 describes 1,244 randomly sampled adults interviewed. The definition source and example study (PMID:34957435) used 247 genotyped PopCol participants. The PopCol design paper (Scand J Gastroenterol, not read) would settle whether 3556 is the number invited or the number who took part.

label: Precocious Coronary Artery Disease Study
counts: CAD cases and controls in the case-control cohort (2014 genotyping)
quote: The LPA null allele (rs41272114) was genotyped in the PROCARDIS (Precocious Coronary Artery Disease) case-control cohort (4073 CAD cases and 4225 controls).
note: Abstract read through the Europe PMC API; it gives no combined total, so participants is null. PROCARDIS numbers vary by analysis: 'The PROCARDIS study recruited 2,658 affected sibling pairs (ASPs) with onset of CAD before age 66 y from four European countries to map susceptibility loci for CAD.' (PMID:16710446, 2006); 'PROCARDIS, a CHD case control study (n = 7,998)' (PMID:25781951); 5765 CAD cases (PMID:23279374). The definition source (PMID:29713486) measured cytokines on 1000 cases and 1000 controls. A PROCARDIS design paper giving total recruitment would settle it.

label: Pressioni Arteriose Monitorate E Loro Associazionie
counts: adults aged 25-74 with office, home and ambulatory BP (baseline)
quote: Office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory BP values were obtained in 2051 subjects between 25 and 74 years of age who were representative of the general population of Monza (Milan, Italy).
note: Definition source and example study (PMID:15809377, 2005 follow-up paper, abstract only). It may count only those with all three BP measurements rather than everyone sampled; the original PAMELA design paper (not read) would settle the number enrolled.

label: Prospective Investigation of the Vasculature in Uppsala Seniors
counts: 70-year-olds recruited at baseline
quote: Of 2025 invited, 1016 participants were recruited.
note: Definition source and example study (PMID:34523676), describing PIVUS in its methods. The PIVUS design paper (its reference 41, not read) would give the baseline years.

label: Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension
counts: cases and controls genotyped on the Immunochip (after QC, as used in the 2012 meta-analysis)
note: Supplementary Table 1 of PMID:23143594 (columns Study, Cases (N), Controls (N), Total, lambdaGC). The main text states 'the Psoriasis Association Genetics Extension (PAGE: 3,580 cases and 5,902 controls)'. Supplementary Table 2 breaks this down by country (USA, Canada, Estonia, Germany). PAGE has no separate design paper; this is the only source.

label: Psychiatric GWAS Consortium
counts: cases and controls (controls include trio pseudocontrols) across the five disorders in the 2013 cross-disorder analysis
quote: The final dataset consisted of 33 332 cases and 27 888 controls (including pseudocontrols formed from non-transmitted alleles) distributed among the five disorder groups: autism spectrum disorders (4788 trio cases, 4788 trio pseudocontrols, 161 cases, 526 controls), attention deficit-hyperactivity disorder (1947 trio cases, 1947 trio pseudocontrols, 840 cases, 688 controls), bipolar disorder (6990 cases, 4820 controls), major depressive disorder (9227 cases, 7383 controls), and schizophrenia (9379 cases, 7736 controls).
note: Cross-Disorder Group of the PGC, Lancet 2013 (PMID:23453885), the consortium's analysis spanning all five disorders it was founded for; no total of participants is stated, and the controls include pseudocontrols from trios, so participants is left null. The definition source (PMID:20955924, Neuron 2010) describes the consortium but gives no sample size. The example study (PMID:21926972, PGC bipolar disorder working group) states 'In the combined analysis of all 63,766 subjects (11,974 cases and 51,792 controls)' and a primary GWAS of 7,481 cases and 9,250 controls; those are one working group's analysis.

label: Research on Adolescent Development and Relationships
counts: only member counts reported: 2 member cohorts (RADAR Young N = 497, RADAR Old N = 233 target adolescents)
quote: RADAR consists of two cohorts: RADAR Young ( N = 497, 283 boys), 12 years old at Time 1 (2005) and RADAR Old ( N = 233, 107 boys), 12 years old at Time 1 (2001).
note: PMID:32823179 (introduction to four Dutch cohorts, 2020) reports the two member cohorts separately and no pooled total, so participants is null and the aggregation has 2 member cohorts. The definition source PMID:40153111 says instead 'For the RADAR-Old study, families were recruited from a larger longitudinal cohort study, resulting in a sample of 306 adolescents', and that a combined same-aged three-wave dataset of both cohorts 'consisted of 993 adolescents' (a derived analysis dataset). The example study PMID:26997371 used 255 RADAR-Y adolescents. The RADAR-Young and RADAR-Old cohort profiles (DANS data documentation) would settle the member sizes.

label: Rotterdam Study
counts: participants aged 40 and over across the four sub-cohorts (RS-I to RS-IV)
quote: The study currently includes 17,931 participants (overall response rate 65%), aged 40 years and over, who are examined in-person every 3 to 5 years in a dedicated research facility, and who are followed-up continuously through automated linkage with health care providers, both regionally and nationally.
note: From the abstract (Europe PMC) of the 2024 design update. The definition source PMID:32367290 (2020 design update) states 'By the end of 2008, the Rotterdam Study therefore comprised 14,926 subjects aged 45 years or over' (RS-I 7983, RS-II 3011, RS-III 3932), with a fourth cohort of persons aged 40 and over recruited since 2016 but not counted there.

label: Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean asthma study
counts: individuals in 271 families
quote: The collection includes 1394 individuals distributed in 271 families.
note: From the abstract of the collection's 2014 profile paper (Genes & Immunity). The example study PMID:23066387 (2012) states 'A total of 1,428 individuals from 254 nuclear families were included the study' (a count by nuclear family, 254 probands); the profile paper's 1394 in 271 families is taken as the collection's own count.

label: Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke
counts: consecutive ischaemic stroke cases aged 18-69 and age- and sex-matched controls
quote: Six hundred consecutive white participants with ischemic stroke (18 to 69 years) and 600 age- and sex-matched controls were examined for vascular risk factors and family history of stroke and myocardial infarction (MI).
note: From the abstract of the 2005 SAHLSIS family-history paper (Stroke), the earliest design description found; later abstracts repeat 'The Sahlgrenska Academy Study on Ischemic Stroke comprises 600 cases and 600 matched population controls' (PMID:18331453, PMID:17272741). No source read states the combined total, so participants is left null. The definition source PMID:36418382 analysed a longitudinal subset of 209 cases and 209 controls; the example study PMID:29378355 used '600 cases with ischaemic stroke at ages 18 to 69 years and 600 controls matched for age and sex'.

label: SardiNIA Study of Aging
counts: participants aged 14-102 recruited at baseline from four towns
quote: We recruited a cohort of 6,148 participants, aged 14-102 y, from four clustered towns in Sardinia.
note: From the abstract of the 2006 baseline heritability paper (PLoS Genet), the cohort's founding description. The project website (definition source, https://sardinia.nia.nih.gov/) states 'In a first survey, the project team recruited over 6,100 subjects from a catchment area including four towns in east-central Sardinia'. The example study PMID:32929287 analysed a subset of 3,757 Sardinians with immune cell traits.

label: Scania Diabetes Registry
counts: individuals with diabetes in the registry (catalogue metadata field)
quote: Number of individuals/objects: 7400
note: From the Swedish National Data Service catalogue entry (the definition source), whose description also says 'The Scania Diabetes Registry contains over 7000 diabetes patients recruited at hospitals in Scania, Sweden as from 1996.' The entry does not date the count; recruitment is ongoing. The example study PMID:34601942 (GoLEAD/SUMMIT peripheral artery disease GWAS) gives no count for the registry in the text read.

label: Shanghai Study
counts: gallbladder carcinoma patients with sequenced tumour-normal pairs
quote: Here, we report our identification of somatic mutations of GBCs in 57 tumor-normal pairs by use of a combination of exome sequencing and ultra-deep sequencing of cancer-related genes.
note: The EGA study description (the definition source) counts tumour-normal pairs, one per patient. Its two datasets hold exome data for 32 pairs (EGAD00001000901) and targeted sequencing for 51 pairs (EGAD00001000902). No example paper is recorded; the corresponding publication (the 2014 gallbladder carcinoma exome study from Xinhua Hospital) would confirm the patient count.

label: Short Course Oncology Treatment trial
counts: patients randomised, March 2008 to November 2013
quote: 6088 patients underwent randomisation between March 27, 2008, and Nov 29, 2013.
note: From the abstract of the SCOT primary results paper (Lancet Oncol 2018), the definition source and example study. The same abstract says '3044 patients were assigned to 3 month group and 3044 were assigned to 6 month group', and that after withdrawals of consent 3035 and 3030 remained for the intention-to-treat analyses.

label: Simons Simplex Collection
counts: simplex families (2,600), not individual participants; enrolment ended 2011
quote: The SSC achieved its primary goal to establish a permanent repository of genetic samples from 2,600 simplex families, each of which has one child affected with an autism spectrum disorder, and unaffected parents and siblings.
note: Every source read counts families, not people, so participants is null: the SFARI resource page says 2,600 simplex families (and 'Active enrollment of participants ended in 2011'); the definition source page says 'data drawn from 2,700 families'; the 2010 design paper PMID:20955926 abstract says 'More than 2000 families have been evaluated to date'; the example study PMID:25534755 genotyped '2576 families'; PMID:24565360 analysed '2,418 probands with autism'. A SFARI Base count of individuals (probands, parents, siblings) would settle the number of participants.

label: Singapore Chinese Study
counts: age- and sex-matched cases and controls genotyped (1,000 cases, 1,000 controls)
quote: Mucosa specimens from 1,000 sporadic Chinese CRC patients (defined as age 50 or more at date of operation and without dominant family history of FAP and HNPCC) archived over the past ten years were selected as cases for the study.Blood samples from 1,000 age- and gender-matched healthy donors from the Singapore Chinese Health Study (SCHS) (n = 931) [10] and the SGH Health Screening Unit (n = 69) constituted the controls of the study.
note: Total from the abstract of the definition source PMID:22879968: 'in 2,000 age- and gender-matched Singapore Chinese (SCH) cases and controls'; cases and controls from the methods sentence quoted (run together with the next sentence in the source text). Table 1 of the same paper gives 991 cases and 993 controls after QC. The example study PMID:24448986 lists 'Singapore Chinese Study (SCH, n = 2,000)'.

label: SORCE
counts: patients randomised, July 2007 to April 2013
quote: 1711 patients were randomised into the SORCE trial.
note: From the trial unit's page (the definition source), which also says 'Patients were randomised to the trial between July 2007 and April 2013.' The example study PMID:23184150 (renal cell carcinoma GWAS) used 856 cases from the TRANSORCE collection within SORCE, a subset.

label: Spit for Science
counts: students enrolled across five entering cohorts (2011, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2017)
quote: The project began in fall 2011, and new cohorts were recruited in 2012, 2013, 2014, and 2017 ( N = 12,358).
note: From PMID:35186215 (2022, COVID-19 and college students). PMC12098791 (2025) describes 'a prospective longitudinal study of over 12,000 college students'. The definition source PMID:24639683 (2014) covers only the first cohort: 'Nearly 70% of the incoming freshman class (N = 2715) completed on-line surveys'. The example study PMID:30482948 (PGC alcohol dependence meta-analysis) gives no Spit for Science total in the text read.

label: Sweden Bipolar Disorder Cohort
counts: individuals with bipolar disorder recruited across two waves (2009-2013 and 2017-2022); controls not counted
quote: Across the two waves, SWEBIC recruited 8580 individuals diagnosed with bipolar disorder, 89 percent from BipoläR.
note: From the abstract of the 2025 SWEBIC description paper (Swedish Bipolar Collection). The same abstract adds 'Including individuals from other cohort studies, the total number of DNA samples from individuals with bipolar disorder in SWEBIC exceeds 10,000.' No control count for SWEBIC as a whole was found; the definition source PMID:28072414 (ICCBD GWAS) says 'SWEBIC controls are from the Swedish Schizophrenia Consortium' and after QC analysed 1378 + 923 SWEBIC cases and 3716 + 2215 SWEBIC controls on two genotyping platforms.

label: Swedish Twin Registry
counts: twins the registry currently holds data on (stated as 'more than 160,000')
quote: The registry currently holds data on more than 160,000 twins, with ongoing ascertainment at 9 months and 9 years with follow-ups at ages 15, 18, and 24.
note: From the abstract of the 2026 description of the registry under new Swedish legislation, the most recent profile; the figure is a lower bound. The 2019 infrastructure paper PMID:31747977 states 'The Swedish Twin Registry functions as research infrastructure containing information on 216,258 twins born between 1886 and 2015, of whom 86,199 pairs have zygosity determined'; the difference is not explained in the abstracts read (the 2026 full text would say whether records were removed under the new law). The definition source PMID:12270000 (2002) abstract gives no count. The example study PMID:34982741 cross-matched 63,010 STR twins and analysed 1,130.

label: Taiwan Type 2 Diabetes Study
counts: type 2 diabetes cases and normal controls across the two GWAS stages
quote: There were a total of 2,798 cases and 2,367 normal controls (995 cases and 894 controls in stage 1, 1,803 cases and 1,473 controls in stage 2).
note: From the definition source PMID:20174558 (PLoS Genet 2010, two-stage T2D GWAS in Han Chinese in Taiwan). No combined total of participants is stated, so participants is null. The example study PMID:24001895 (AGEN blood pressure meta-analysis) lists 'Taiwan Type 2 Diabetes Study 1,000' in its table of study characteristics, a subset.

label: TEENs of Attica: Genes and Environment
counts: adolescent students recruited 2008-2010
quote: A random sample of 857 adolescent students (Table S1) attending public secondary schools located in the wider Athens area of Attica in Greece were recruited in the study from 2008 to 2010.
note: From the example study PMID:23347264 (Ann Hum Genet 2013); its abstract says the genetic analysis used '707 (55.9% females) adolescents of Greek origin', the genotyped subset after QC. The EGA study EGAS00001000996 (definition source) gives 24 participating schools but no participant count.

label: The English Longitudinal Study of Ageing
counts: core members aged 50-100 at wave 1 (2002)
quote: The original sample consisted of 11 391 members ranging in age from 50 to 100 years.
note: From the abstract of the ELSA cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2013), the definition source. The full text adds 'The total sample of 12099 consisted of 11391 core members, 636 partners aged <50 years and 72 new partners aged 550 years' (the last figure as extracted from the PDF, presumably >=50). Refreshment samples added in later waves are not counted here; a later ELSA profile or the study website would give the cumulative number.

label: The Fenland Study
counts: participants recruited at baseline (phase 1), 2005-2015
quote: The Fenland Study recruited 12,435 participants born between 1950 and 1975, via general practices from 3 centres (Cambridge, Ely, and Wisbech) in Cambridgeshire, UK, between 2005 and 2015.
note: From PMID:41939009 (2026, planetary health diet and adiposity), a Fenland analysis paper describing the cohort. The definition source (participant information sheet, 2019) says 'Approximately 12,500 people from across Cambridgeshire took part in the first phase of the Fenland Study'. The example study PMID:35446786 (uromodulin GWAS) gives no Fenland total in the text read. The Fenland cohort profile would be the preferred source.

label: The Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren
note: The term is defined as the Helmholtz Association, a research organisation, not a participant collection; its about-us page (https://www.helmholtz.de/en/about-us/) gives only staff ('more than 48,000 employees work together in 18 centers'), which is not a participant count. The example study (PMID:35915169) uses the 'Helmholtz-Gemeinschaft Deutscher Forschungszentren Lung Cancer GWAS (GERMAN)' as one of 12 discovery studies but gives its size only in Supplementary table 1/25, whose cached copies are empty. The German lung cancer GWAS's own sample size (from its design paper or the supplementary tables) would give a number for that dataset.

label: The MANOLIS cohort
counts: adults recruited in the Mylopotamos villages
quote: Adults (n 1553).
note: Quote is the 'Subjects' line of the abstract (Europe PMC) of the MANOLIS cohort description paper, which states 'We carried out de novo recruitment of a population-based cohort (MANOLIS study)'. Other numbers seen: MANOLIS n=1,476 in the GWAS meta-analysis and 250 whole-genome sequenced (PMID:28548082); 1457 samples after WGS QC and proteomics in 1407 samples (PMID:33303764, example study); these are analysed subsets.

label: The Netherlands AAA GWAS dataset
counts: AAA cases (Utrecht, 8 Dutch centres, 2007-2009) and Nijmegen controls in the Dutch GWAS
quote: We performed a GWAS using 452 Icelandic and 840 Dutch individuals with AAA, and 27,712 Icelandic and 2,791 Dutch controls, genotyped with the Illumina HumanHap370 or HumanHap610 SNP chips.
note: Quote is from the dataset's original GWAS (PMID:20622881, author manuscript on PMC), cited as the source of the dataset by the definition paper. No source states the total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null. The definition paper's supplement (PMID:27899403, Online Table I, Europe PMC supplementaryFiles res-120-341-s002.pdf) gives the same 840 cases and 2,791 controls and says 'As controls, we included 2,791 Dutch subjects who were recruited as part of the Nijmegen Biomedical Study (n=1,832) and the Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study (n=1,278)'; the AAA sample set 'was recruited in 2007-2009 from 8 centres in The Netherlands'.

label: The Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma
counts: unique myeloma patient donors (approximate)
quote: This biobank represents one of the largest collections of samples from patients with Multiple Myeloma with approximately 3000 unique donors.
note: The biobank's page on Biobank Norway (live site refused TLS from here, so read via the Internet Archive capture of January 2026); the introduction page says it was established in 1991 in Mid-Norway and became a national biobank receiving samples from 30 hospitals in 2005. The definition/example paper (PMID:27363682) used only 157 MM patients from the Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma in the Swedish/Norwegian GWAS (analysed subset). Year is the capture date, not a stated count date.

label: The Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study
counts: first-ever acute MI cases and controls in nine urban centres (approximate)
quote: Our primary analyses involved a subset of participants from the Pakistan Risk of Myocardial Infarction Study (PROMIS), a case-control study of first-ever acute myocardial infarction (MI) in nine urban centres in Pakistan consisting of approximately 16,700 cases and 18,600 controls.
note: No source read states the total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null. The design paper (PMID:19404752) reports 'By March 2009, PROMIS had recruited over 5,000 cases of first-ever confirmed acute myocardial infarction (MI) and over 5,000 matched controls aged 30-80 years' and a target of 'about 20,000 cases and about 20,000 controls'; the example study (PMC8431908, full text) gives the later achieved size above and analysed 5662 PROMIS controls (analysed subset). A later PROMIS profile stating the total recruited would settle participants.

label: Second Manifestations of ARTerial disease study
counts: patients included since September 1996
quote: By May 2022, a total of 14 830 patients have been included ( figure 3 ).
note: From the 2023 UCC-SMART cohort profile (PMID:36806141), whose abstract also says 'Since September 1996, a total of 14 830 patients have been included.' The 1999 design paper (PMID:10608355) planned 'At least 1000 patients, aged 18 to 80 years'; the example study (PMID:26390057) gives no SMART count in text.

label: The Hellenic study of Interactions between Single nucleotide polymorphisms and Eating in Atherosclerosis Susceptibility
counts: consecutively enrolled adult CAD patients and adult controls
quote: We consecutively enrolled 1221 adult patients with coronary artery disease and 1344 adult controls.
note: Quote is the 'Subjects' line of the abstract (Europe PMC) of the THISEAS overview paper (Public Health Nutr 2016); its full text was not retrievable from Europe PMC, and no source read states the total, so participants is left null. The definition/example paper (PMID:38929788) analysed a genotyped subset: 'The sample under study comprised 924 Greek individuals (390 cases with CAD and 534 controls) from the THISEAS study.'

label: Treating to New Targets
counts: patients randomised to atorvastatin 10 or 80 mg
quote: A total of 10,001 patients with clinically evident CHD and LDL cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) were randomly assigned to double-blind therapy and received either 10 mg or 80 mg of atorvastatin per day.
note: From the abstract (Europe PMC) of the TNT main results paper, the definition source. Only the abstract is cached; no other count needed.

label: Twins Early Development Study
counts: twin PAIRS recruited (not individuals); 'over 16,000'
quote: The Twins Early Development Study (TEDS) is a longitudinal twin study that recruited over 16,000 twin pairs born between 1994 and 1996 in England and Wales through national birth records.
note: The number is in twin pairs and is a lower bound ('over'); no source read states the number of individual twins. Same profile paper (PMID:31544730) also says '16,810 families expressed interest in taking part', 'over 13,000 families participating in the first wave of data collection when twins were around 18 months old', 'more than 8,000 twin pairs continue to take part', DNA from 12,500 individuals and genotypes for 10,346 individuals.

label: Type 1 Diabetes Genetics Consortium
counts: subjects recruited by the T1DGC whose DNA the 2024 study used (families, cases, controls)
quote: We obtained DNA samples from 13 412 subjects recruited by the T1DGC (Supplementary Table 1).
note: Aggregation: no pooled participant total is stated in the design paper (PMID:20603248), which says the initial goal was 2500 affected sibling pair families, that 'T1DGC achieved its original ASP recruitment goal', that 'A total of 214 clinics in 34 countries participated in recruitment', and whose Table 1 lists 2855 completed ASP families overall as of 4 July 2009 plus trios, cases and controls by network (a table, not a sentence; no overall people count). The number used is from the example study (PMID:38453145), which may be the whole set of T1DGC samples available to it rather than everyone recruited.

label: UK Adult Twin Register
counts: registered volunteer twins, including mixed, single and triplets
quote: The registry comprises over 14,000 volunteer twins (14,838 including mixed, single and triplets); it is predominantly female (82%) and middle-aged (mean age 59).
note: From the abstract (Europe PMC) of the 2019 registry update 'TwinsUK: The UK Adult Twin Registry Update', which also says 'over 1800 parents and siblings of twins are registered volunteers' (not counted). Earlier figures: 'about 12000 volunteer twins' in the 2013 cohort profile (PMID:22253318, the definition source; also 'about 12 000 twins' in its full text) and 'approximately 10,000' in 2006 (PMID:17254428).

label: UK Biobank
counts: participants recruited and assessed 2006-2010 (round figure)
quote: Recruitment of 500,000 participants and the collection of an unprecedented wealth of baseline data and samples were completed in 2010.
note: From the UK Biobank design paper (PMID:25826379), which also says 'The 500,000 participants were assessed between 2006 and 2010 in 22 assessment centres throughout the UK'. Bycroft et al. 2018 (PMID:30305743) says 'approximately 500,000 individuals'. The figure is a round number; UK Biobank's data showcase would give the exact recruited count (not read here). The example study (PMID:30104761) gives no cohort count in text.

label: UK Brain Expression Consortium
counts: neuropathologically normal post-mortem brain donors (Edinburgh and Sun Health banks combined)
quote: Central nervous system (CNS) tissues originating from 134 control individuals was collected by the Medical Research Council (MRC) Sudden Death Brain and Tissue Bank, Edinburgh, UK (Millar et al. 2007), and the Sun Health Research Institute (SHRI) an affiliate of Sun Health Corporation, USA (Beach et al. 2008).
note: The consortium's own Materials & Methods page (definition source), section 'Collection and dissection of post-mortem human brain tissue'; the count is the pooled donors across its two brain banks, with up to 10 regions each. The example study (PMID:32098967) used a subset: '180 brain samples originating from 117 individuals of European descent'.

label: UK Childhood Cancer Study
counts: children with cancer and unaffected control children studied
quote: Altogether 3,838 children with cancer, including 1,736 with leukaemia, and 7,629 unaffected children have been studied.
note: From the abstract of the UKCCS design paper (definition source); its full text (PMC2374433) adds 'Altogether the study included 1461 children with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, 2377 children with other types of cancer and 7629 control children'. No sentence states the total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null. Eligible: 4433 cases and 11 987 controls (flow chart).

label: UK Household Longitudinal Study
note: No source read states the number of individuals in the study; the sources give households. The Catalogue of Mental Health Measures (https://www.cataloguementalhealth.ac.uk/?content=study&studyid=UKHLS) gives 'Sample size at recruitment 5,500 households (Wave 1 BHPS) 39,802 households (Wave 1 Understanding Society)' and '19,734 households (2023-2025 - Wave 15)', and says 'From Wave 2, over 6,000 participants from the BHPS sample joined the UKHLS.'; BRIN (https://www.brin.ac.uk/understanding-society/) says 'Wave 1, Year 1 of the general population sample had participation from 14,103 households (59% response) and 22,265 adults (86% response)' (first year of wave 1 only); PMC10114108 says 'around 40 000 households'; the UKDS user guide (https://doc.ukdataservice.ac.uk/doc/6614/mrdoc/pdf/6614_main_survey_user_guide.pdf) gives only weight-specific person counts. The definition source (Understanding Society working paper 2023-06) and the Wave 1 technical report returned 403 from understandingsociety.ac.uk; the technical report mirror at doc.ukdataservice.ac.uk gives individual outcomes only as percentages. The Understanding Society user guide or a cohort profile giving individuals enumerated/interviewed at wave 1 would settle it. The example study (PMID:35507331) used 9,965 UKHLS genotyped controls (analysed subset).

label: UK Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium
counts: British CD and UC patients recruited to the consortium's studies ('nearly')
quote: Together we have recruited nearly 15000 British patients with CD and UC to our studies.
note: The consortium's own website; the page gives no date for the figure. Other numbers: the definition source (Crohn's & Colitis UK project page, 2011) says 'They wanted to collect 5000 DNA samples from IBD patients from across the UK' (a target); the example study (PMID:28067908) generated 'low-coverage whole genome sequences for 4,686 IBD cases' from the UKIBDGC and had GWAS data on 4,474 CD, 4,173 UC and 592 IBD-unclassified cases (analysed subsets). The separate UK IBD BioResource is a distinct resource and not counted.

label: Viking Health Study
counts: participants recruited 2013-2015
quote: The 2105 participants were recruited between 2013 and 2015, 95% of them having at least three grandparents from Shetland.
note: From PMID:31765389 (Increased ultra-rare variant load in an isolated Scottish population), which elsewhere says 'A total of 2,122 participants of the VIKING Health Study–Shetland [33] were genotyped ... and 2,011 passed all quality control thresholds' (inconsistent with 2105, hence medium). PMC6662790 (PMID:31358886) says 'Over 2,000 volunteers from the archipelago of Shetland were recruited to the Viking Health Study Shetland in 2013–2015'. The example study (PMID:40883583) mentions 'the whole 2005 individuals in the VIKING1 cohort' (for the GRM) and used a 200-person proteomics subset; the definition source (EGA EGAS00001003872) describes whole-genome sequencing of 500 individuals. The cohort's own design paper (reference 33 of PMID:31765389) was not read.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium
counts: cases of 7 diseases and shared controls retained after QC in the 2007 WTCCC1 GWAS
quote: We excluded 809 samples after checks for contamination, false identity, non-Caucasian ancestry and relatedness (see Methods and Supplementary Table 4); 16,179 individuals remained in the study.
note: Aggregation: the flagship analysis is the 2007 WTCCC1 study (PMID:17554300, definition source). Same text: 'All 17,000 samples were genotyped' and 'With data on 2,938 controls and 16,179 individuals in total' (source of controls); no sentence states the post-QC case total (title gives the round '14,000 cases of seven common diseases and 3,000 shared controls'), so cases is left null. The consortium also ran a Gambian tuberculosis GWAS (1,500 cases, 1,500 controls) and a non-synonymous SNP study, not counted here; later WTCCC2 collections are not counted.

label: Basquecolon cohort
counts: colon cancer cases biobanked 2009-2019 at Donostia University Hospital and blood-donor controls
quote: Basque-colon cohort included 873 participants with colon cancer, biobanked between 2009- 2019. Participants were diagnosed and/or treated according to usual clinical practice in the Donostia University Hospital, San Sebastian, Spain, including follow-up to this date. Controls (n = 945) came from the blood donor biobank of the same geographical area.
note: From the Supplementary Information of the definition/example paper (PMID:37783704). No sentence states the total; Table 1 of the main text (PMC10545678) has the row 'BCC non-Hispanic White 1818 873 (48.0%)', i.e. 1818 participants in a table cell, not a sentence, so participants is left null. This is the validation sample as used in the PRS study; no separate Basque-colon design paper was read.

label: INTERVAL study
counts: whole blood donors recruited and randomised 2012-2014
quote: 45 263 whole blood donors (22 466 men, 22 797 women) were recruited between June 11, 2012, and June 15, 2014.
note: From the abstract (Europe PMC, 'Findings' section) of the INTERVAL main results paper (Lancet 2017); it adds 'Data were analysed for 45 042 (99·5%) participants.' The protocol (PMID:25230735, definition source) planned 50,000 trial participants; the example study (PMID:36357675) describes INTERVAL as comprising 'up to 50,000 participants' and used 8,455 INTERVAL samples (analysed subset).

label: CONVERGE
counts: Han Chinese women recruited (cases and controls)
quote: The CONVERGE (China, Oxford and Virginia Commonwealth University Experimental Research on Genetic Epidemiology) consortium recruited 11,670 Han Chinese women through a collaboration involving 58 hospitals in China.
note: No case/control split of the 11,670 recruited is stated. After QC the GWAS analysed 10,640 samples: 'After applying stringent quality controls (Supplemental Methods), we obtained 10,640 samples (5,303 cases of MDD, 5,337 controls)'. Design target was 6,000 cases and 6,000 controls. The 2017 Scientific Data paper (PMID:28195579, abstract) also says the project 'sequenced 11,670 female Han Chinese'.

label: Gene-Environmental Interaction and phenotype study
counts: individuals genotyped at the time of the 2022 study
quote: At the time of this study, a total of 10,349 individuals had been genotyped using the Affymetrix Axiom KORV 1.0–96 Array (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Santa Clara, CA, USA) by DNA Link, Inc.
note: GENIE is the genotyped biobank subcohort of the H-PEACE health check-up cohort; no source read gives a total enrolment figure. PMID:35121771 analysed 9742 after QC. A 2025 paper (PMC12228804) says 'Of the 10,342 people whose GWAS information was first analysed, 8,790 were aged 40 years or older.' Other papers split the genotyped set differently: PMC10847124 'Among them, 7999 and 2349 participants from the H-PEACE and GENIE cohorts, respectively, were genotyped'; PMC11928451 'The GENIE cohort comprised 7999 participants who visited Seoul National University Hospital Gangnam Center in 2014'. The cohort description cited as ref 10 of PMID:35121771 would settle the enrolled total.

label: China Atherosclerosis Study
counts: CAD cases and controls retained after QC in the discovery GWAS
quote: After these quality control procedures, 5,008 samples and 613,724 autosomal SNPs were retained for subsequent analyses.
note: The case and control numbers are from the same text: 'CAS consisted of 1,010 cases of CAD and 3,998 controls.' Before QC: 'For CAS in the discovery stage, a total of 1,034 cases of CAD and 4,245 controls were genotyped' (no total stated for that set, so the post-QC total is recorded). Controls were drawn from the InterASIA survey; cases from Fuwai Hospital. The example study (PMID:34887591) gives no CAS count.

label: Diabetes Prediction and Prevention
counts: newborn infants screened for HLA risk by June 2006
quote: By June 6, 2006, 104,111 consecutive newborn infants had been screened, and 8,026 children with genetic risk continued in the follow up.
note: Same sentence gives 8,026 genetically at-risk children in follow-up. Screening continued after 2006, so this is an interim count; no later whole-cohort figure was found in the sources read. A 2024 DIPP paper (PMC10884602) covers only a subset: 'Of the 6080 participants enrolled for the follow-up, the food record data were available from 5626 children' (children born 1996-2004 in Oulu and Tampere). A recent DIPP cohort profile would settle the current total.

label: Functional genomic diagnostic tools for coronary artery disease
counts: patients undergoing angiography recruited 2007-2010 (initial cohort)
quote: The initial cohort consists of 7710 individuals.
note: Same paper (PMID:33766035): 'Out of the 2643 subjects, we identified 1734 patients as cases and 757 subjects as controls making a total study population of 2491.' That is the analysed case-control subset with GWAS data, not the whole cohort.

label: German Chronic Kidney Disease Study
counts: adults with CKD enrolled 2010-2012
quote: The GCKD study is an ongoing prospective observational study that enrolled 5,217 adult persons with CKD between 2010 and 2012.
note: The design paper (PMID:21862458, abstract) gives the planned size: 'It aims to enrol a total of 5000 patients with CKD of various aetiologies'. The example study (PMID:37277652) analysed metabolites from 5,023 participants.

label: German Longevity Study
counts: long-lived individuals (cases) and younger controls in the 2022 GSA-genotyped sample
quote: The examined sample comprised 1351 German LLI (≥94 years, including 643 centenarians) and 4680 German younger controls.
note: No source read states a total, so participants is left null; cases and controls are as stated. The controls were 'recruited as part of the FoCus cohort [41] and as blood donors'. The 2025 exome study (PMID:40232348) says 'Our study population was comprised of 1265 unrelated German LLI and 4195 geographically matched younger controls.' (1245 and 4105 after QC). Neither paper gives a whole-collection total; the German longevity collection's own description would settle it.

label: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events
counts: patients with suspected ACS enrolled 1999-2007
quote: Between 1999 and 2007, 70,395 patients with a suspected acute coronary syndrome were enrolled.
note: Read in the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:25554379 (2015, GRACE follow-up). The design paper (PMID:11174331, abstract only) gives the aim: 'A goal of this study is to study approximately 10,000 patients with ACS on an annual basis.' Other GRACE abstracts give smaller analysed sets for the same period (e.g. PMID:22608950 '63,118 patients enrolled from April 1999 to December 2007'). The example study (PMID:20231156) used the GRACE Genetics substudy: 'Overall, 3473 patients were enrolled in the GRACE Genetics Study.' GRACE continued as GRACE2; a final registry total from its own publications would settle whether the figure is higher.

label: TwinGene Study
counts: twins who gave blood samples 2004-2008
quote: TwinGene is a subcohort study within the Swedish Twin Registry, which collected blood sample from 12,648 older Swedish twins in 2004–2008
note: From PMID:37184129 (2023), citing the Swedish Twin Registry biobank paper (PMID:23137839, not open access; its abstract gives no TwinGene count). Analysed subsets elsewhere: example study PMID:34431594 'Swedish TwinGene participants (n = 10,616, 41-87 years)'; PMC6015288 'study base of 10 682 twins from TwinGene cohort'. The definition source PMID:35410261 pools TwinGene with other STR substudies and gives no TwinGene count.

label: Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men
counts: men aged 50 examined at baseline 1970-1974
quote: In the Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men study, 2322 men, all aged 50 years, were assessed for CVD risk factors and then followed for four decades regarding incident CVDs.
note: Read in the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:34518286; PMID:33635119 likewise says 'ULSAM (Uppsala Longitudinal Study of Adult Men; 2322 men aged 50 years)'. The definition source PMID:25919442 (abstract) gives the analysed set: 'Swedish men investigated in 1970-74 (aged 48.6-51.1) and followed up for four decades (N=2,293)', with 472 reinvestigated in 2008-09. PMC6450581 gives an approximate 'This cohort of 2300 middle-aged men'.

label: Baltimore Longitudinal Study of Ageing
counts: volunteers since 1958 (stated as 'more than 3,200', a lower bound)
quote: This is thanks to its more than 3,200 volunteers who made the lifelong commitment to be part of the research.
note: The NIA page (last updated July 27, 2018) gives only a lower bound, recorded as stated. The example study (PMID:40111762) repeats it: 'including >3200 participants'. An exact cumulative enrolment count from a BLSA design paper or NIA data documentation would settle it.

label: Motor Neuron Disease Biobank study
counts: DNA samples in the bank at end of collection (patients, family members and controls)
quote: In October 2012, at the end of the collection period, the UK MND DNA Bank comprised 3159 high quality DNA samples.
note: From the bank's design paper PMID:26170009 (2015). The count is of DNA samples, not explicitly of distinct people. Same text: 'Of these, 1344 samples were taken from individuals diagnosed with sporadic MND', 'There were 133 familial MND samples within the collection and a further 500 samples taken from family members', and 'The remaining 1085 samples were taken from controls.' Not a simple case-control split, so cases is left null. The definition source PMID:20801717 genotyped 'genotypes were obtained from 663 individuals in the UK MND DNA bank' (599 after QC).

label: Singapore Diabetic Cohort Study
counts: adults with type 2 diabetes recruited 2004-2010
quote: A total of 14 033 adult participants with type 2 diabetes were recruited from multiple public sector polyclinics and hospital outpatient clinics in Singapore between November 2004 and November 2010.
note: Cohort profile PMID:32474429 (2020). Recruited in two phases: 'In phase 1, 5324 participants were recruited' and 'An additional set of 8709 participants were recruited'. 'The first round of follow-up was conducted for 4131 participants between 2012 and 2016'.

label: Ely Study
counts: non-diabetic adults aged 40-69 at baseline analysed for 1990-2000 incidence (analysed subset)
quote: Population-based longitudinal study (1990-2000) with clinical, anthropometric and biochemical measurements, including an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), in 1040 non-diabetic adults aged 40-69 years at baseline.
note: Read in the Europe PMC abstract of the definition source PMID:17257284; this may be the analysed subset with follow-up rather than everyone who attended baseline. No source read states how many attended the 1990-1992 baseline. PMC3814419 (PMID:22283392) gives the invitation frame: 'In 1990–1992, one third ( n = 1705), selected randomly, received an invitation for screening' and a further 1705 invited ten years later; of 3390 eligible then, 1442 attended. Genetic papers use larger pooled Ely samples (e.g. PMC2518506 'MRC Ely (n = 1,709)'). The Ely study's baseline description (e.g. its 1990s design paper) would settle the attended baseline count.

label: Genetic Asthma Susceptibility to Indoor Pollution in Peru
counts: children aged 9-19 enrolled in the case-control study (with and without asthma)
quote: Of 1177 children enrolled, 884 (413 with asthma, 471 without asthma) had serum available for analysis of 25(OH)D levels.
note: From PMID:28588900 (2017), authored with the GASP Study Investigators, describing the parent unmatched case-control study of July 2012 to March 2014 in Pampas and Villa El Salvador. Cases and controls are given only per site ('we had a final enrollment of 258 and 248 children with asthma, and 374 and 297 without asthma, in Pampas and Villa, respectively'), so they are not recorded as totals. Enrolment goal: 'our goal was to enroll 700 asthma cases and 700 controls.' The definition source PMID:33713768 genotyped a subset: 'A total of 436 Peruvian children (aged 9-19 years) with asthma and 291 without asthma were genotyped'.

label: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative
counts: untreated PD (cases) and healthy controls enrolled in the original de novo cohort; plus 64 SWEDD
quote: A total of 423 untreated PD, 196 Healthy Control (HC) and 64 SWEDD (scans without evidence of dopaminergic deficit) subjects were enrolled at 24 sites.
note: Design paper PMID:30564614 (2018). No overall total is stated, so participants is left null; the three groups are 423 PD, 196 HC and 64 SWEDD. Same paper: 'A total of 811 subjects (570 PD and 241 HC) were screened for participation in PPMI.' PPMI later added prodromal and genetic cohorts and expanded enrolment (PPMI 2.0), which this definition and count do not cover; the PPMI website's current enrolment figures would give the larger total. The example study (PMID:36370000) gives only analysed numbers.

label: Psychosis Endophenotype Consortium
counts: pooled participants (patients, unaffected relatives, controls) in the 2013 psychosis GWAS before exclusions
quote: Before any exclusion, the full data set included 6935 participants with 1820 patients, 1224 of their unaffected relatives, and 3891 healthy control subjects.
note: Flagship analysis of the consortium, PMID:23871474. Besides cases and controls, 1224 unaffected relatives are included in the total. After QC: 'After quality control, the full sample included 4835 participants of which 1239, 857, and 2739 were patients, their unaffected relatives, and healthy control subjects, respectively.'

label: Study of Health in Pomerania
counts: adults examined at the SHIP-START-0 and SHIP-TREND-0 baselines combined
quote: In total, 8,727 individuals underwent baseline investigations in SHIP-START (n = 4308) and SHIP-TREND (n = 4420).
note: From PMID:39085387 (2024). The next sentence reads 'One participant from SHIP-START withdrew consent subsequently.'; the total is recorded as stated. PMC12347048 (PMID:40807204) gives the same member baselines, START-0 (1997–2001) n = 4308 and SHIP-TREND-0 (2008–2012) n = 4420. The definition source, the 2022 Cohort Profile Update (PMID:35348705, doi:10.1093/ije/dyac034), is subscription-only (publisher returned 403) and was not read; it would confirm the figures.

label: The Cooperative Health Research in South Tyrol
counts: adults recruited at baseline 2011-2018
quote: The Cooperative Health Research In South Tyrol (CHRIS) study completed the baseline recruitment of 13,393 adults from the Venosta/Vinschgau rural district in 2018, collecting extensive phenotypic and biomarker data, metabolomic data, densely imputed genotype and whole-exome sequencing data.
note: Read in the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:34637685 (CHRIS COVID-19 protocol, 2021). The design paper PMID:26541195 (2015) gave the target ('The aim is to recruit at least 10,000 participants') and an interim first data release of 4979 participants recruited until 15 July 2014. The example study PMID:34827661 used data release 3.0 with 10,518 participants.

label: The Health Effects of Arsenic Longitudinal Study
counts: adults aged 18-75 enrolled 2000-2002 (original cohort)
quote: From 12 050 residents who met our eligibility criteria from an enumerated total of 65 876 in the study area, 11 746 (97% response rate) men and women (4801 married couples and 2144 married individuals whose spouses did not participate) were enrolled in the HEALS cohort.
note: Definition source PMID:20646756 (Lancet 2010); the abstract likewise says physicians 'clinically assessed 11 746 population-based participants (aged 18-75 years) from Araihazar, Bangladesh'. HEALS was later expanded with further recruitment after 2002; that expansion is not covered by this count, and was not checked in this session.

label: 100,000 Genomes Project
counts: NHS patients with rare disease or cancer whose genomes were sequenced (approximate)
quote: Genomics England's very first initiative – sequencing 100,000 genomes from around 85,000 NHS patients affected by rare disease or cancer – is leading to groundbreaking insights and continued findings into the role genomics can play in healthcare.
note: Genomics England's project page gives 'around 85,000' patients for 100,000 genomes; the same page says the 100,000th genome was sequenced in 2018. The definition source (EGAS00001004364) describes only the NIHR BioResource pilot: 'WGS data for 13,037 participants, of whom 9,802 had a rare disease'. The supplement of Nature s41586-022-04576-6 used 46,770 unrelated 100KGP participants as controls (a subset). No exact enrolled count found in the text read.

label: 1958 British Birth Cohort
counts: individuals born in England, Scotland and Wales in one week of March 1958 (original birth cohort)
quote: In brief, participants were drawn up from 17 638 individuals born in England, Scotland and Wales within 1 week of March 1958.
note: From a hearing-loss GWAS (PMC4572074) describing the B58C; the same paper says 9377 members were revisited for the 2002-2004 biomedical follow-up and 6099 were genotyped (the DNA collection used as controls; the definition source EGAS00000000038 has 2604 T1DGC control samples). The WTCCC paper (nature05911) says 'an original sample of over 17,000 births'. The cohort profile (Power & Elliott 2006, PMID:16155052) is closed and the CLS website blocked the request; either would confirm the birth-cohort count.

label: 300BCG
counts: healthy adult volunteers vaccinated with BCG, 2017-2018
quote: Of the 325 individuals vaccinated, 18 participants were vaccinated in the evening and 307 were vaccinated in the morning.
note: From a 300BCG substudy paper (PMID:32692732): 'A total of 327 healthy volunteers were assessed, of which 2 did not meet inclusion criteria.' The same paper's methods say 'In the 300BCG study, 321 healthy (male and female) adult volunteers of Western European ancestry were included from April 2017 until June 2018'; the paper does not reconcile 321 with 325. The definition source (EGAS50000000090) profiles 323 individuals; PMC10851559 describes the cohort as '325 (142 males and 183 females) healthy individuals'. 325 is the number vaccinated in the flow description.

label: AACR Project GENIE
counts: patients with sequenced tumours in the public registry release 20.0 (stated as 'more than')
quote: AACR Project GENIE® 20.0-public was released in July 2026 and contains more than 289,000 sequenced samples from more than 242,000 patients, making the AACR Project GENIE® Registry among the largest fully public cancer clinico-genomic datasets available.
note: A lower bound ('more than 242,000 patients') for the latest public release; the count grows with each release. The definition source (EGAS00001006707) analysed 121,771 patients from GENIE and Foundation Medicine combined, not GENIE alone. The BioPharma Collaborative aims to annotate approximately 20,000 of the registry's patients. The flagship 2017 paper (PMID:28572459) was not read.

label: AC-ANGIOPREDICT Phase II trial
counts: patients enrolled in the phase II trial (actual enrolment, ClinicalTrials.gov)
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":76,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT01822444 (completion 2017-02) gives an actual enrolment of 76. The trial's cfDNA paper (PMC11137102, PMID:38811554) says 'The AC-ANGIOPREDICT cohort contained 74 patients.' (samples collected April 2013 to February 2015); the definition source's EGA dataset has 139 samples from the trial. The main trial publication was not read.

label: Adjuvant Lapatinib and/or Trastuzumab Treatment Optimisation trial
counts: women with HER2-positive early breast cancer randomised, June 2007 to July 2011
quote: Between June 2007 and July 2011, 8,381 patients from 945 sites in 44 countries were randomly assigned.
note: Primary results paper of the ALTTO trial (JCO 2016), read on PMC (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4872016/). The definition source (EGAS50000000525) profiled 386 trastuzumab-treated tumours, a subset.

label: African Collaborative Center for Microbiome and Genomics Research
counts: women enrolled in the ACCME HPV and cervical cancer cohort, February 2014 to July 2016
quote: From commencement of enrolment in February 2014 to July 2016, 11 500 women had been enrolled in the ACCME cohort.
note: Cohort profile (IJE 2017), read from the cached PMC page https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5837640/. Enrolment was ongoing at the time; 5349 participants had had the 12-month follow-up visit. A pilot of 1000 women tested the data collection tools and is not part of the count. No later count read.

label: African Genome Resource
counts: Africans with low-depth whole-genome sequence in the African Diversity Reference Panel (approximate)
quote: Whole genome DNAseq data at 4x-8x depth from approximately 3,000 Africans of 14 distinct ethnicities, which is the largest and most diverse set of haplotypes for the continent.
note: From the resource's EGA study description (the definition source), which also gives 'approximately 3000 whole genome sequences, 600 transcriptomes'; the transcriptome donors (6 populations) are not counted separately and may overlap. The EGA study is pending release; no publication describing the finished resource was read.

label: African Genome Variation Project
counts: individuals from 18 ethno-linguistic groups with dense genotypes (whole-genome sequenced individuals given separately)
quote: The African Genome Variation Project represents dense genotypes from 1,481 individuals and whole-genome sequences from 320 individuals across sub-Saharan Africa.
note: AGVP design paper (Nature 2015), abstract. 320 further individuals (seven groups) have low-coverage whole genomes; the paper does not state how far the two sets overlap, so no total is given and the genotyped number is recorded.

label: African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research
counts: no pooled participant count stated; member studies: four (as one paper describes the APCDR cohort)
quote: The APCDR cohort comprises four studies: the Ugandan Genome Resource (UGR), the Durban Diabetes Study (DDS), the Durban Case–Control Study (DCC), and the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study (AADM).
note: APCDR is a research partnership, not a single pooled study, and no source read states its total number of participants. Numbers seen: the Uganda Genome Resource Cell paper (PMID:31675503, PMC7202134), which thanks APCDR 'for providing a network', meta-analysed 'up to 14,126 individuals from across the African continent'; a white-blood-cell GWAS (PMC8674726) meta-analysed '17,802 participants from the African Partnership for Chronic Disease Research (APCDR) and African ancestry individuals from the Blood Cell Consortium (BCX2)', of whom 2,741 were APCDR (table). The definition source (EGAS00001001917) describes the African Genome Resource (~3,000 genomes). A consortium overview or website stating the pooled size would settle it.

label: ALLG ALL06
counts: patients aged 15-39 with newly diagnosed Ph-negative ALL enrolled in the ALL06 trial, 2012-2018
quote: ALLG-ALL06 was a prospective, single-arm phase 2 study that enrolled 82 patients aged 15 to 39 years, with newly diagnosed Philadelphia-negative ALL.
note: From the genomic substudy paper (Blood Neoplasia 2025, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12182849/), which also says '82 patients were treated between 2012 and 2018 (complete cohort)'. The genomic study cohort, which the COHO definition describes, was 57 patients (40 B-ALL, 17 T-ALL); the EGA dataset has RNA-seq from 45. The primary ALL06 trial report (its ref. 19) was not read.

label: Alpe-DPD study
counts: cancer patients included in the prospective Alpe-DPD study
quote: In total, 1181 were included in the Alpe-DPD study, of which 1103 were evaluable (Fig. 2 ).
note: From the Alpe-DPD GWAS paper (Genome Med 2024, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11325793/), which also has 'All patients ( N  = 1181 of which 1103 were evaluable)'. 986 were exon sequenced and 942 in the GWAS; the EGA dataset has 1146 samples. The original Alpe-DPD trial report (the paper's ref. 5) was not read.

label: APCDR Diabetes Case Control Study
counts: individuals of Zulu descent with type 2 diabetes recruited at a tertiary hospital in Durban
quote: The Diabetes Case Control study is a study of individuals with diabetes recruited from a tertiary hospital in Durban (n = 1,542).
note: From the STAR Methods of the Uganda Genome Resource paper (Cell 2019, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7202134/), which also lists 'the Diabetes Case control study (n = 1,542)' among the meta-analysed cohorts. The collection consists of cases only; no controls are counted for it there (the population-based Durban Diabetes Study, n = 1,204, is a separate study). The EGA study (EGAS00001002584) is pending release and gives no number.

label: Atlas of Blood Cancer Genomes
counts: no pooled count read; one member cohort (BPDCN) has 88 patients
quote: To address this gap, we performed integrated DNA and RNA sequencing on 88 BPDCN patients representing the largest and most ancestrally diverse cohort described to date (~77% European, ~16% Asian, ~7% African).
note: The quote gives only the BPDCN member cohort from the definition source, not the whole project, so participants is left null. A web search snippet of the ABCG project's 2021 ASH abstract (Blood 138 Suppl 1:2213) mentions samples from 10,481 patients contributed by 25 institutions, but the abstract (ASH, ScienceDirect) and a 2024 AACR abstract returned 403 and could not be read, so that number is not recorded. Reading either abstract would settle it.

label: Australian childhood AML cohort
counts: not stated separately for the Australian cohort in text read
note: The definition source (EGA study EGAS00001006276) gives only 'the combined childhood AML cohort (n=72)', which pools the Australian cohort with TARGET cases, and its one dataset holds 'whole exome sequencing of 24 paediatric AML samples at diagnosis' without saying these are all the Australian patients. The paper (Blood 2021;138:2293-2298, PMID:34521114) is closed and has no abstract in PubMed; its methods would give the Australian cohort's size.

label: BEACON eczema drug trial
counts: adults needing systemic eczema treatment in the BEACON randomised trial (the trial's stated size; may be the planned target)
quote: BEACON is a UK-wide randomised, controlled, 12-month assessor-blind trial in 536 adults who require systemic treatment for their eczema.
note: The trial website's FAQ says 'The trial will involve around 536 adults with moderate to severe eczema who need a systemic treatment', so 536 looks like the planned sample size, not the achieved enrolment. The COHO term (from EGA study EGAS00001007976, pending release, no numbers) covers the patients profiled in the BEACONomics mechanistic substudy, whose size was not found. A results paper or the trial registry's actual enrolment would settle it.

label: Beat AML
counts: AML patients in the harmonised cumulative Beat AML cohort (942 specimens)
quote: Here, we present a dataset that has been harmonized with our initial report to yield a cumulative cohort of 805 patients (942 specimens).
note: Abstract of the Beat AML follow-up (Cancer Cell 2022, read from the Europe PMC record). The initial report and definition source (PMID:30333627) had 'a cohort of 672 tumour specimens collected from 562 patients'; of these 531 were exome sequenced, 411 RNA sequenced and 363 drug tested.

label: Belgian Approach of Local Laboratory Extensive Tumor Testing
counts: patients with advanced cancers enrolled from 12 Belgian hospitals
quote: This multi-center study enrolled 872 patients from 12 Belgian hospitals.
note: Abstract of the BALLETT main results paper (NPJ Precis Oncol 2025, read from Europe PMC). Its preprint abstract also says 814 were sequenced; the economic evaluation (PMID:41379447) says 814 patients enrolled between May 2021 and October 2023 participated, so the year is taken from that enrolment period. The planned size was 936 (EGA definition source and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05058937 estimated enrolment).

label: BELLINI trial
counts: patients treated in stage I of cohorts A, B and C (safety population)
quote: Treatment-related AEs of any grade occurred in 41 of 46 patients (89%).
note: From the BELLINI results paper (Nat Med 2024, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11564107/). Cohorts A, B and C had 15 evaluable patients each; 'A total of 44 patients received both ICI doses and 2 patients only received one dose'.
