The trial was still recruiting for stage II expansion: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03815890 gives an estimated enrolment of 80. The EGA definition source has WES of 30 patients (cohorts A and B) and scRNA-seq of 29.

label: Blood First Assay Screening Trial
counts: total enrolment across the treatment cohorts not stated in text read; patients screened given in the quote
quote: Between 11 January 2018 and 9 December 2020, 5,220 patients were screened of whom 92 were identified to have ROS1 -positive, advanced/metastatic NSCLC by liquid biopsies, giving a prevalence of ROS1 fusions of 1.8%.
note: From the BFAST Cohort D paper (Nat Med 2024, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11271410/). 5,220 patients were blood-screened by December 2020, but that is screening, not enrolment in a treatment cohort, so participants is left null. Cohort D (the definition source EGAS50000000105) enrolled 55 patients; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03178552 (active, not recruiting) gives an estimated enrolment of 1000. A final report giving the trial's actual enrolment across cohorts A-F would settle it; the ALK cohort paper (PMID:34311110) was not read.

label: Born in Bradford
counts: women recruited in pregnancy 2007-2011
quote: Born in Bradford (BiB) is a multi-ethnic birth cohort in Bradford, UK, which recruited 12 453 women with 13 776 pregnancies and 3448 of their partners between 2007 and 2011.
note: From the 2024 Cohort Profile Update (PMID:38552669). The cohort also counts 13 776 pregnancies and 3448 partners; the definition source (EGA EGAS00001005273) says BiB 'recruited 13,858 babies between 2007 and 2011'. The women recruited are given as the enrolled number; the babies (13,858, EGA) would be the alternative unit. The 2013 cohort profile (PMID:23064411) is closed and was not read. The 2016-2023 Growing Up follow-up recruited 5318 mothers, 9805 children and 838 partners.

label: CALGB 40601
counts: patients randomised in the phase III trial
quote: Among 305 randomly assigned patients (THL, n = 118; TH, n = 120; TL, n = 67), the pCR rate was 56% (95% CI, 47% to 65%) with THL and 46% (95% CI, 37% to 55%) with TH (P = .13)
note: Primary trial report (Carey et al. 2016, abstract read via Europe PMC). The example study (PMID:37923752) also says '305 eligible patients ... were randomized' and that 264 of them had baseline RNA sequencing.

label: Cambridge Biorepository for Translational Medicine
note: Read the definition source (EGA EGAS00001008228, no donor count, no dataset sample count) and the CBTM website overview and home pages (https://www.cbtm.group.cam.ac.uk/aboutus, /), which give no number of donors. A web search snippet attributes 'more than 50 deceased human donors' to the Human Cell Atlas White Paper (arXiv 1810.05192), not read here and only a lower bound. A CBTM profile paper or a statement of total donors on its website would settle it.

label: Canadian Airways Research Group
counts: patients with iSGS (cases) and controls enrolled to 1 August 2023
quote: We prospectively enrolled 126 patients with iSGS, 104 controls, and 13 patients with traumatic SGS.
note: From the CARE group study cited by the definition source (PMID:40048847, EBioMedicine 2025). The paper states the three groups separately (126 idiopathic SGS, 104 controls, 13 traumatic SGS) but no total, so participants is left null. Subsets: 75 iSGS and 70 controls had exome sequencing.

label: Canadian Prostate Cancer Genome Network
note: The definition source (EGA EGAS00001000900) gives only the plan: 'Over 5 years, CPC-GENE will sequence the genomes of 350 intermediate risk prostate cancers'. The flagship paper (PMID:28068672, abstract read; closed, no PMC copy) says 'we analysed 200 whole-genome sequences and 277 additional whole-exome sequences from localized, non-indolent prostate tumours' but gives no total of patients. EGA dataset names mention a '666PG' study. A statement of the total number of men in the CPC-GENE cohort (e.g. in PMID:28068672 full text or later CPC-GENE papers) would settle it.

label: Cancer Genomics of the Kidney
counts: ccRCC patients with targeted sequencing, multinational CAGEKID cohort
quote: In this multinational study, comprising final data from a total of 943 patients, we have examined the role of targeted gene sequencing to improve individual risk stratification.
note: From Vasudev et al. 2023 (PMID:36815791), a publication listed on the definition source (EGA EGAS00001000083), which calls its patients 'the CAGEKID cohort' (943 patients; Discovery n = 469, Validation n = 474). The original CAGEKID whole-genome study (Scelo et al. 2014, PMID:25351205, closed; abstract read) gives no number in its abstract; EGA datasets hold 95 blood/tumour DNA pairs and 708 samples. The 943 is the targeted-sequencing validation cohort, not necessarily the whole-genome discovery set; the 2014 full text would settle the size of the original constitutional/tumour pair collection.

label: Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands cohort
counts: coeliac disease patients (cases) and controls with faecal samples
quote: The Celiac Disease Northern Netherlands cohort (CeDNN, currently unpublished) comprises 128 CeD patients and 106 controls who provided fecal samples at project onset, with complete metadata including age and sex.
note: From the study cited on the definition source (Slager et al. 2025, PMID:40289251), which says the cohort is otherwise unpublished. No total is stated, so participants is null. The EGA dataset (EGAD50000001397) describes samples 'from 130 (mostly treated...) celiac disease patients and 106 controls'. The count may be only those with faecal samples and complete metadata; a CeDNN design paper would settle the whole cohort's size.

label: CENet Cohort
counts: analysed subset: whole-genome sequenced patients (cases) and controls
quote: We used WGS from 377 controls and 247 patients, 123 GGE, 112 NAFE and 12 mixed patients ( Table 1 ).
note: From Girard et al. 2023 (PMID:37756314), the publication on the definition source (EGA EGAS00001007507). These are the whole-genome sequenced subset (patients recruited 2002-2014; controls are unaffected parents of DEE trios from CHU Ste-Justine and SickKids), not the whole CENet cohort, and no total is stated. The EGA study holds 108 patients. CNV papers (PMID:35678011, PMID:29649218) describe CENet families but were not found to give a whole-cohort count; a CENet design paper would settle it.

label: CHILD Cohort Study
counts: pregnant women recruited (with 3542 eligible offspring)
quote: The Canadian Healthy Infant Longitudinal Development (CHILD) birth cohort study recruited 3624 pregnant women, most partners and 3542 eligible offspring.
note: From the CHILD design paper (Subbarao et al. 2015, Thorax; abstract read via Europe PMC). The exposure-assessment paper (PMID:25805254) confirms 'Between 2008 and 2012, the CHILD study enrolled 3624 pregnant mothers'. The offspring count is 3542; partners are not counted. The definition source (EGA EGAS00001006725) holds whole genomes of 200 trio families.

label: City of Hope triple negative breast cancer cohort
counts: women with TNBC in the COH phase II neoadjuvant trial cohort
quote: This cohort comprises 42 female patients with pathologically confirmed diagnosis of locally advanced and inflammatory TNBC, who were enrolled in a phase II trial testing the safety and efficacy of carboplatin and NAB-paclitaxel in the neoadjuvant setting ( NCT01525966 , ( 17 )) at the City of Hope Comprehensive Cancer Center.
note: From Menghi et al. 2022 (PMID:35857626), the publication on the definition source (EGA EGAS00001006085, whose WGS dataset also holds 42 tumours). The underlying phase II trial (NCT01525966, ref. 17 of the paper) may have enrolled more patients; this is the genomically profiled cohort the term describes.

label: CLUSTER consortium
counts: individuals in harmonised data of 4 member studies
quote: A total of 7013 records (from 5435 individuals) were identified; of which 2882 (41%, corresponding to 1304 individuals) represented the same child across >1 study.
note: From a 2022 conference abstract of the consortium (Rheumatol Adv Pract, PMC9515876) on harmonising four member studies (CAPS, CHARMS, BCRD and BSPAR-ETN). After removing duplicates the harmonised datasets hold 2899 methotrexate and 2401 TNF-inhibitor patients. The definition source's paper (PMID:40681434, abstract read) used a discovery cohort (n = 97) and two validation cohorts (n = 26 and n = 47). The consortium also includes trials not counted here; a CLUSTER overview paper giving its pooled size would settle it.

label: COMPARE study
counts: blood donors consented to COMPARE (stages 1 and 2)
quote: A total of 29 029 participants were consented to participate in the COMPARE study (17 861 in Stage 1 and 11 168 in Stage 2), of whom 21 840 (75.2%) provided data for the current analysis (Figure 1 ).
note: From the COMPARE main results paper (PMID:33341984, Transfus Med 2021). The definition source (EGA EGAS00001003748) says 'The COMPARE study enrolled 29,066 British blood between donors between February 2016 and March 2017', and that 4,796 of them consented to the NIHR BioResource and were genotyped; the paper's 29 029 consented participants is preferred. 21 840 were analysed.

label: COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative
counts: cases and controls in the 2021 reported-infection meta-analysis (44 studies)
quote: Finally, seven loci reached genome-wide significance in the analysis using data for all available 49,562 reported cases of SARS-CoV-2 infection and 1,770,206 controls, using data from a total of 44 studies (Fig. 2a, bottom).
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:34237774, Nature 2021). No combined total is stated, so participants is null. Overall the paper says the initiative 'combined genetic data from 49,562 cases and 2 million controls across 46 distinct studies'; the critical-illness analysis used 6,179 cases and 1,483,780 controls (16 studies) and the hospitalised analysis 13,641 cases and 2,070,709 controls (29 studies). Later HGI releases are larger and were not read.

label: CRCbiome
counts: FIT-positive screening participants who consented
quote: Those with a positive FIT test (>15 microgram Hb/g feces) were invited to participate in the CRCbiome study ( N = 2700), and 1640 consented.
note: From Birkeland et al. 2026 (PMID:42642381, Nat Commun), a publication on the definition source (EGA EGAS50000000170), giving the achieved recruitment (2700 invited, 1640 consented; 1034 in the final analysed population). The 2021 design paper (PMID:34407780) gave interim figures ('So far, 2426 have been invited and 1413 (58%) have agreed to participate') and expected 'about 1600'.

label: DERMATLAS
note: Only planned sizes were found: the Sanger news item (31 Mar 2021) says the project 'will analyse 70 skin tumour subtypes ... and collect up to 50 cases for each type', and the HRA research summary says 'We will analyse around 50 cases per skin tumour type'; neither gives a total, and the definition source (EGA EGAS00001008193, pending release) gives none. Individual DERMATLAS papers (e.g. sebaceous tumours, Nat Commun 2025) report per-subtype cohorts; a statement of the total number of cases sequenced would settle it.

label: Diagnosis and Management of Febrile Illness using RNA Personalised Molecular Signature Diagnosis
note: Only lower bounds were found. The EU CORDIS periodic report (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/848196/reporting) says 'Since January 2020, the DIAMONDS consortium has recruited over 13000 patients and 2000 control subjects.' and 'DIAMONDS included over 1500 patients affected by COVID-19 and multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C).' The project website says 'thousands of patients ... will be recruited'. The definition source (EGA EGAS00001007409) holds 46 samples from the MIS-C signature study (PMID:37255317). A final recruitment total from the DIAMONDS consortium would settle it; 13000 could be recorded as a lower bound.

label: DKTK MASTER
counts: patients enrolled and analysed (first MASTER report)
quote: We analyzed the molecular profiles and clinical outcomes of 1,310 patients (rare cancers, 75.5%) enrolled in a prospective observational study by the German Cancer Consortium that applies whole-genome/exome and RNA sequencing to inform the care of adults with incurable cancers.
note: From the MASTER programme's main report (Horak et al. 2021, Cancer Discov; abstract read via Europe PMC); a 2025 paper (PMC11724059) calls these 'the first 1310 patients sequenced in the MASTER program', so enrolment has since grown, but no later total was found. The example study (PMID:35763870, pazopanib in sarcoma) analysed 109 patients with WGS/WES data.

label: Donor InSight III study
counts: donors who took part in DIS-III (2015-2016)
quote: In total 3046 (50%) participants provided blood samples and/or questionnaire information for DIS‐III of whom 2868 (47%) participants provided informed consent.
note: From the Donor InSight cohort profile (Timmer et al. 2019, Vox Sang, PMID:30590867), which also says 'A second follow‐up (DIS‐III, n = 3046) ... was completed in 2015‐2016'; 6140 were invited, 2868 gave informed consent and 2552 provided blood and the general questionnaire. The EGA dataset description (EGAD00001005026, on EGAS00001003748) likewise says Donor InSight III 'recruited 3,046 Dutch blood donors between 2015 and 2016'.

label: East London Genes and Health
counts: volunteers recruited to Stage 1, April 2015 to mid-June 2019
quote: Between April 2015 and mid-June 2019, ELGH recruited 38 899 volunteers to Stage 1.
note: From the ELGH cohort profile (Finer et al. 2020, IJE, PMID:31504546), which gives a target of 100 000. Recruitment has continued: the Genes & Health home page (https://www.genesandhealth.org/, read 2026-09-25) shows 'Our volunteers so far' 78,534 against a target of 125,000, but as a counter under a heading rather than a sentence, so it is not used. The definition source (EGA EGAS00001001888) says '~12,000 have been collected' at an earlier date. A current profile update would settle the achieved size.

label: Egyptian Collaborative Cardiac Genomics Project
counts: healthy volunteers recruited Dec 2015 to June 2018 (initial cohort)
quote: Here, we report data from an initial cohort of 391 volunteers recruited from December 2015 to June 2018 via national advertisement (brochures, flyers, and public events) and assessed at the Aswan Heart Centre (AHC).
note: From the ECCO-GEN cohort paper (Aguib et al. 2020, NPJ Genom Med, PMID:33110626), which says the project 'is recruiting 1000 Egyptian healthy volunteers' (target). A 2023 HCM study (PMC10733735, Eur Heart J) used 'Egyptian healthy volunteers ( n = 400) ... recruited from across the country as part of the ECCO-GEN', and 514 HCM patients from the same project. The final achieved size of the healthy volunteer cohort is not stated.

label: EMC-DC-IL10R study
counts: RNA-seq study sample (moDC and PBMC sets); no total stated
note: The study paper (PMID:31417161, PMC6752724, deposited as EGAS00001003741) gives only per-experiment counts and no total: moDC RNA-seq 'Monocyte-derived dendritic cells from healthy controls (n=3), IBD patients (n=3) and an IL10RA -deficient patient (PT)'; PBMC RNA-seq 'We generated RNA-seq data of PBMCs from 6 healthy individuals, 11 patients with CD, and 9 patients with UC.' Table 1 lists paediatric IBD cohorts I, II and III of 3, 38 and 20 patients. Whether the sets overlap is not stated, so no total is recorded; the EGA page gives no sample count.

label: Emirati Genome Program
counts: samples collected from Emirati citizens by April 2025
quote: The latest figures of 815,000 samples, announced at Abu Dhabi Global Health Week, mark a significant rise on the 600,000 which had been collected as of June last year.
note: Whole-programme figure from a news report (The National, 17 April 2025), counting samples collected, not necessarily genomes sequenced; 600,000 had been collected by June 2024. The Emirates Genome Council site says the programme 'aims to collect one million genetic samples from citizens nation-wide'. The EGA study EGAS50000001071 (the source of the COHO definition) characterises the analysed subset: 'a cohort of 43,608 Emirati genomes sequenced as part of the Emirati Genome Program (EGP)'. The medRxiv preprint on the 43,608 (10.1101/2025.09.12.25334546) returned 403 and could not be read; a peer-reviewed programme profile would settle the enrolled number.

label: Entebbe Mother and Baby study
counts: live-born children enrolled in the birth cohort, 2003-2006
quote: They were then followed to delivery and 2345 resulting liveborn children, born between 17 April 2003 and 19 April 2006, were enrolled into the EMaBS birth cohort.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:42648772, BMJ Open 2026). The birth cohort (the COHO term's children) is 2345; their mothers were also enrolled: 'A total of 2507 women were enrolled and randomised to receive either albendazole (400 mg) or matching placebo, and praziquantel (40 mg/kg) or matching placebo, in a 2×2 factorial design.' The EGA study EGAS00001003283 planned to genotype 1,500 of the children.

label: EORTC-SPECTA RP1759
counts: AYA patients with high-grade glioma or other high-risk CNS tumours recruited
quote: 50 AYAs aged 12-29 with newly diagnosed or recurrent HGG and other high risk central nervous system (CNS) tumours were prospectively recruited to the EORTC SPECTA platform study and underwent whole exome sequencing, RNA sequencing and methylation profiling, with central pathological review.
note: Abstract of PMID:40393126 (the SPECTA-AYA high-grade glioma paper; full text closed). The EGA study EGAS50000000985 says the pilot 'aimed to recruit 50 AYA patients' and its dataset holds 'tumor samples from 50 patients with newly diagnosed or relapsed high-grade gliomas'. Of the 50, 46 were locally diagnosed HGGs and 4 other recurrent CNS tumours.

label: ESTAMPA
counts: women aged 30-64 with valid screening results, 2012-2021
quote: From December 2012 to December 2021, 42,502 women aged 30–64 years had valid screening tests results in the ESTAMPA study.
note: From the ESTAMPA analysis in Lancet Reg Health Am 2023 (PMID:37766799), one of the two papers the EGA study EGAS00001007730 links. The same paper describes the study as 'including more than 42,000 participants' across 12 centres in nine countries, and its analysis included 30,606 women after excluding 10,962 from one centre. The number of women with valid results, not all women enrolled; the sequenced EGA subset is not stated.

label: Estonian Microbiome Cohort
counts: Estonian Biobank participants who gave stool, oral and plasma samples
quote: As part of the Estonian Biobank, we established the Estonian Microbiome Cohort which includes stool, oral and plasma samples from 2,509 participants and is supplemented with multi-omic measurements, questionnaires, and regular linkages to national electronic health records.
note: EGA study description (from the mSystems 2025 paper). A sub-cohort of 'over 300 individuals' gave a second stool sample after a median 4.4 years (328 samples in dataset EGAD50000001686).

label: Etude des Déterminants pré et postnatals précoces du développement et de la santé de l'Enfant
counts: pregnant women recruited 2003-2006 in Nancy and Poitiers
quote: Briefly, the study included 2002 pregnant women recruited from 2003 to 2006 in two French university hospitals (Poitiers and Nancy), before 24 weeks of amenorrhoea.
note: From the methods of an EDEN analysis paper (PMID:38786654, 2024), not the cohort profile (Heude et al., IJE 2016, PMID:26283636, doi 10.1093/ije/dyv151), which is closed and has no abstract; the profile would confirm the number and give the births. The HELIX cohort profile (PMC6144482) tabulates 1900 births for EDEN's entire cohort. The MeDALL EGA dataset EGAD00010001455 holds 1347 samples across four cohorts.

label: EuroEPINOMICS
counts: no pooled participant count for the programme
note: A research networking programme whose sub-projects each report their own samples; no source read gives a pooled number of participants or of member sites. In the example study (PMID:25262651, AJHG 2014) EuroEPINOMICS-RES contributed 19 of 356 trios: 'Three epileptic encephalopathy cohorts were evaluated in this study: (1) Epilepsy Phenome/Genome Project (EPGP) cohort 1 (n = 264 trios) used in the previously published paper,2 (2) new EPGP cohort 2 (n = 73 trios), and (3) EuroEPINOMICS-RES cohort (n = 19 trios).' Its NLES probands 'were enrolled by clinical sites in 18 different European countries.' The EGA study EGAS00001000048 (shared with the International Headache Genetics Consortium) has datasets of 97 and 327 samples. A programme overview (European Science Foundation report) would settle a total.

label: European BestAgeing Study
counts: participants enrolled at 11 European centres 2013-2017 (cases and controls with miRNA profiles)
quote: Two thousand fifty seven participants were enrolled from 11 major centers across Europe from 2013 to 2017.
note: BMC Med 2025 (PMID:41310616). Cases and controls from the same paper: 'We assessed genome-wide miRNA expression profiles in a total of 1209 cardiovascular patients and 848 controls in a uniform, standardized fashion'. The results section gives a larger figure: 'A total of 2378 participants were included in the study and miRNAs were assessed by standardized assays in as much as 2057 patients (Fig. 1 ).' So 2057 may be the profiled set of 2378 included; medium confidence for that reason.

label: Extended Cohort for E-health, Environment and DNA
counts: participants recruited to 4 December 2018 (first recruitment wave)
quote: In total, 10 156 participants have been recruited to 4 December 2018.
note: Cohort profile (IJE 2019, PMID:31062032). The 2021 COVID-19 focus paper (PMC11635928) repeats 'The first wave of EXCEED recruitment (November 2013-December 2018) recruited 10,156 participants aged 30–69 years' and describes the cohort as 'N>11,000' (no exact figure), with 10,102 recruited before 28 May 2020. The EGA page says 'approximately 10,000 participants' and its genotype datasets hold 5216 samples.

label: Genome Database of Latvian Population
counts: biobank participants since 2006 (stated as 'over')
quote: Since its start in 2006, the LGDB is comprised of biosamples and associated phenotypic and clinical information from over 31,504 participants, constituting approximately 1.5% of the Latvian population.
note: Design paper (J Epidemiol 2018, PMID:29576601); the figure is phrased 'over 31,504', so the current total is larger and a later source would update it. The WGS paper linked from the EGA study (PMID:37895026) analysed 502 of the 887 LGDB participants with WGS data in July 2022; a 2024 T2D PGS paper used 3990 genotyped LGDB samples.

label: Genome Diversity in Africa Project
counts: individuals whole-genome sequenced at high depth (analysed subset of the project so far)
quote: Currently, 25 individuals from 24 ethnolinguistic groups have been whole-genome sequenced at high depth totalling 585 individuals.
note: From a later GDAP EGA study (EGAS00001003602, dataset EGAD00001006965 released 2021), which adds 'An additional 41 individuals have been sequenced with 10X Genomics libraries' and plans 600 more. Planned size, from the EGA study behind the definition (EGAS00001000929) and the HRA summary: 'up to 2000' / 'up to 2,000 whole genomes across Africa (up to 150 individuals from each ethno-linguistic group)'. The count of people sampled (DNA drawn from existing African studies) is not stated; a GDAP publication would settle the achieved size.

label: Genome Research at Fundació ACE
counts: unrelated individuals genotyped in GR@ACE stage I (AD cases and controls)
quote: The GR@ACE study comprises 7,409 unrelated individuals. 4,120 AD cases were diagnosed at Fundació ACE Memory Clinic (Barcelona, Spain). 3,289 Controls were obtained from three collections (Fundació ACE, Barcelona; DNA National Biobank, Salamanca and HU Valme, Seville).
note: EGA study description of GR@ACE Stage I; its three datasets each hold 7409 samples. Later GR@ACE/DEGESCO papers pool further samples, but this is the cohort's own stage I count.

label: Genomic Advances in Sepsis
counts: adult sepsis patients recruited 2005-2018 (stated as '>1,400', a lower bound)
quote: The UK Genomic Advances in Sepsis (GAinS) study has recruited a cohort of >1,400 patients with sepsis due to community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and fecal peritonitis (FP), admitted to adult intensive care units (ICUs) across the United Kingdom.
note: From the eQTL paper that the EGA study EGAS00001007786 cites (Cell Genom 2024, PMID:38897207); the figure is a lower bound, and no source read gives the exact number recruited. The same paper: 'We recruited adult patients (>18 years old) to the UK Genomic Advances in Sepsis (GAinS) study ( NCT00121196 ) from 34 intensive care units (ICUs) between 16/11/2005 and 30/05/2018' (the EGA page says 35 hospitals), with genotypes on 1,168 and expression data on 1,043 patients. A GAinS design paper or the trial registration would give the exact total.

label: German Cancer Consortium
counts: patients in the flagship DKTK MASTER analysis (2021)
quote: We analyzed the molecular profiles and clinical outcomes of 1,310 patients (rare cancers, 75.5%) enrolled in a prospective observational study by the German Cancer Consortium that applies whole-genome/exome and RNA sequencing to inform the care of adults with incurable cancers.
note: Aggregation of German cancer centres; the number is the flagship DKTK MASTER analysis (Cancer Discov 2021, PMID:34112699, abstract), not everyone in all DKTK programmes, and MASTER has enrolled more since. The example study (PMID:35763870) analysed 109 pazopanib-treated sarcoma patients from DKTK MASTER, with further MASTER sets of 43 and 97. No source read gives the number of partner sites.

label: German MI cohort
counts: not stated for this collection
note: The only source naming this collection, the Cardiogenics re-sequencing EGA study, says only 'The experiment will use the early onset patients from the German MI cohort and the UK BHF CAD/MI cohort both of which have strong family history', with pools of 25 individuals (8 miRNA pools, 80 gene pools) and 10 exomes, and gives no size for the German cohort. It is probably drawn from the German Myocardial Infarction Family Studies (GerMIFS; the CARDIoGRAM design paper PMC3070269 tabulates GerMIFS I at 884 cases / 1604 controls and lists further GerMIFS panels), but which panel(s) Cardiogenics used is not stated, so no number is recorded. A Cardiogenics re-sequencing publication naming its German case source would settle it.

label: GMMG-BIRMA trial
counts: RRMM patients with BRAF V600E enrolled in the phase II trial
quote: Twelve RRMM patients with a median of five prior lines of therapy were enrolled.
note: EGA study description (the trial's abstract). Genomic data cover subsets: WGS triplets from 6 patients and RNA-seq of 11 samples.

label: Gutenberg Health Study
counts: participants aged 35-74 at baseline
quote: The Gutenberg Health Study (GHS) is a population-based, prospective, observational cohort study in Germany that includes 15,010 participants between 35 and 74 years of age.
note: Abstract of a GHS analysis paper (PMID:34424371); the same total is given in another cached source (supplement of Fan et al., Commun Biol 2020: 'with a total of 15,010 participants and follow-up after five years'). The design paper (Wild et al., Bundesgesundheitsblatt 2012) was not read. The EGA study (FXI meta-analysis) gives no GHS count.

label: Haematological Malignancy Research Network
counts: patients newly diagnosed 2004-2019 in the patient cohort (approximate)
quote: Providing generalizable information on clinically meaningful cancer subtypes ( Figure 1 ), ∼38 000 patients newly diagnosed in 2004–2019 with a haematological malignancy or related disorder have entered HMRN’s patient cohort, with a further 2500 new diagnoses being added each year.
note: Cohort Profile Update (IJE 2022, PMID:35134983), the most recent profile. A later HMRN paper on patient involvement (PMC12821308, 2026) says the cohort 'currently holds data on around 55,000 patients; increasing by ~ 2500 annually'. The EGA page gives about 2,400 new diagnoses a year and its DLBCL study covers 928 patients diagnosed 2005-2012. Approximate figures; the cohort grows each year.

label: Health, Alcohol and Psychosocial factors In Eastern Europe study
counts: people recruited at baseline in the four country cohorts
quote: Altogether 36,106 individuals were recruited at baseline, of whom 24,944 met the inclusion criteria (Fig. 1 ).
note: From a four-cohort HAPIEE analysis (Sci Rep 2022, PMID:35902678) covering the Czech, Polish, Russian and Lithuanian cohorts; it dates the baseline to 2002–2005. The design paper (BMC Public Health 2006, PMID:17049075) predates Lithuania's baseline: 'The planned sample size was 10,000 persons in each country; the actual study size 28,947 individuals (Table 1 ).' (Russia 9,363, Poland 10,728, Czech Republic 8,856), with a total planned size of 36,500 and 7,000 planned for Kaunas. The EGA study covers DNA methylation in the Siberian (Novosibirsk) branch only; no cohort profile giving the four-country total was read.

label: Healthy Life in an Urban Setting
counts: participants in the baseline examination (HELIUS-1)
quote: Between 2011 and 2015, 24 780 individuals (aged 18–70 years) participated in the baseline examination that consisted of a questionnaire, physical examination, and collection of biological material.
note: From the 2025 Cohort Profile Update (read as Europe PMC full text PMC12145211). The same paper says the baseline number was adjusted from n = 24 789 because some participants attended twice, and that 11 035 took part in the first follow-up (HELIUS-2, 2019-2022). The definition source (EGA EGAS50000000795) says 'over 25,000 participants' and covers a 476-participant metagenomics subset. The 2017 profile (PMID:29247091) was not read.

label: ICGC Gastric Cancer China project
counts: gastric cancer cases in the ICGC GACA-CN project
quote: There are 340 cases belongs to ICGC GACA-CN project.
note: The EGA study (pending release) is the only source read; no project paper or ICGC portal page was found to confirm the number of donors.

label: ICGC Gynecological Carcinosarcoma project
counts: carcinosarcomas (tumours) to be characterised
quote: The aim of ICGC GCS program is to genomically characterize C and S components of 20 tumors, from endometrium or ovary, through an integrative analysis of whole genome sequencing, RNA sequencing and methylome array.
note: The number counts tumours, stated as the programme's aim; the EGA study title also says '20 carcinosarcomas'. One tumour per patient is not stated. No project paper was read.

label: ICGC India Project
counts: treatment-naive gingivobuccal cancer patients, discovery set
quote: With informed consent, blood and tumour tissues were collected at the time of surgical excision, from 50 treatment-naive OSCC-GB patients (discovery set) who underwent a comprehensive staging, curative resection, post-operative radiotherapy±chemotherapy and follow-up at ACTREC.
note: The EGA study (EGAS00001000249) likewise says paired DNA samples from the blood and tumour of 'fifty patients' were analysed. The same paper adds '60 independent OSCC-GB patients (confirmation set)' recruited similarly and analysed by targeted resequencing; no source states a combined total, so the discovery set whose exomes are in EGA is recorded.

label: ICGC Liver Cancer China project
counts: HCC patients' tumour/normal pairs sequenced
quote: Whole genome shotgun sequencing (WGS) and the landscaple of somatic mutations in 88 paired samples from HCC patients including tumors and matched adjacent normal tissues using Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform were performed.
note: The number counts matched tumour/normal pairs; one pair per patient is implied but not stated. The EGA study is the only source read; no project paper was found.

label: ICGC MMML-Seq
counts: lymphoma genomes with matched normals analysed (adult cohort plus Burkitt lymphomas), analysed subset
quote: We identified 4538 clusters of very high mutation density (termed kataegis clusters) [27, 28] in 219 lymphoma genomes (consisting of 179 genomes from this study plus 39 pediatric BLs [17] and one adult BL, Supplementary Table S2), using a definition of a maximal intermutation distance of 1000 bp and a minimum of five mutations per cluster.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC8257491 (the ICGC MMML-Seq whole-genome paper on germinal-centre B-cell lymphomas). The same paper says 'We performed whole genome sequencing of 181 pre-treatment lymphoma samples from adult patients, and 179 matching nontumor tissues'. No source read gives a total enrolment for the whole MMML-Seq project; the example paper (PMID:24139898, X-chromosome hypermutation) gives B-cell lymphoma n = 29 only. A project overview or ICGC portal donor count would settle it.

label: ICGC Oesophageal Adenocarcinoma project
counts: patients with whole-genome sequenced Barrett's, primary OAC or metastatic samples (OCCAMS/ICGC), as surveyed in 2023
quote: To this end, we survey a cohort of 997 patients across different stages of OAC progression, from pre-malignant to advanced disease (Fig. 1, Supplementary Tables 1, 2).
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC10349863. The same paper says the cohort 'comprising 161 Barrett, 777 OACs and 59 metastatic samples' was collected through OCCAMS and whole-genome sequenced as part of the ICGC, and that 409 primary tumours are at the ICGC Data Portal under ESAD-UK. The EGA study page (EGAS00001000725) lists earlier datasets of '303 cases (620 samples)' and '409 cases (832 samples)' from the ICGC ESAD-UK project, '496 OCCAMS ... cases', and the 2019 paper on 551 oesophageal adenocarcinomas; the 2023 figure is the most recent. The paper counts the 997 as patients although it describes them as samples elsewhere; a per-patient total from a project profile would settle it.

label: ICGC Pancreatic Cancer project
counts: pancreatic cancer samples whole-genome sequenced
quote: Pancreatic Cancer whole genome sequencing of 112 samples
note: The EGA study (pending release) is the only source read; it counts samples, not patients, and does not say which ICGC pancreatic project (for example PACA-CN) it belongs to or whether samples are tumour-normal pairs. A project paper or ICGC portal donor count would settle it.

label: ICGC PedBrain Tumor Project
counts: pilocytic astrocytoma patients whole-genome sequenced (one tumour type only), analysed subset
quote: To investigate the full range of genetic alterations in pilocytic astrocytoma, we performed whole-genome sequencing of tumor and blood DNA from 96 patients (Supplementary Table 1).
note: The example paper covers only the pilocytic astrocytoma arm of the PedBrain Tumor Project; the X-hypermutation paper read for MMML-Seq (PMID:24139898) mentions '113 primary medulloblastoma samples collected within the International Cancer Genome Consortium (ICGC) PedBrain Tumor Project'. No source read gives a project-wide total across tumour types, and the project website (pedbraintumor.org) no longer resolves. A project overview or ICGC portal donor count (PBCA-DE) would settle it.

label: ICGC Prostate Cancer UK project
counts: prostate cancer-normal pairs whole-genome sequenced, analysed subset
quote: For the 112 cancer-normal pairs in our cohort, we identified 392,753 SNVs, 54,952 indels and 10,921 chromosomal rearrangements (Fig. 1).
note: Example paper (Nature Genetics 2018; read as PMC6372064 via cached.py). Its discussion also says 'The analysis of whole genome sequence data from 112 prostate cancers'. The EGA study (EGAS00001000262) says the study 'was funded with the ambition of collecting Whole Genome DNA sequence data from 250 prostate cancers' (a planned size). No source read states the achieved total for the whole CRUK-ICGC prostate project; later project papers or the ICGC portal (PRAD-UK) would settle it.

label: ICR MOPOPGEN UK exome control series
counts: UK 1958 Birth Cohort controls whose exomes were deposited as EGAS00001001667
quote: WES data on the 1,006 CRC cases and 648 controls have been deposited at the European Genome-phenome Archive, which is hosted by the European Bioinformatics Institute, accession numbers EGAS00001001666 and EGAS00001001667, respectively.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC4917884. The paper's control set was larger: 'The controls comprised 1,644 healthy individuals from the UK 1958BC21—974 from the ICR1000 data set (EGAD00001001021)22 and an additional 670 individuals', with 1,609 controls after QC; the 648 deposited under this EGA study are the series recorded here. The EGA study page itself gives no number.

label: IMI-RHAPSODY
counts: diabetes patients in the 12 cohorts federated by RHAPSODY (stated as 'over 68000')
quote: Started in 2016, within the RHAPSODY project, we federated 12 patient cohorts totalling over 68000 diabetes patients.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC10951062. The number is a lower bound ('over 68000'). The consortium's clinical-clustering analysis used 'Data from 15,940 individuals with type 2 diabetes from three cohorts, DCS (Netherlands), GoDARTS (Scotland) and ANDIS (Sweden)' (PMID:34110439, PMC8382625), and the multi-omics subgrouping used 1,134 patients from DCS and GoDARTS. The EGA study gives no number. The 68000 figure counts the federated database rather than any single flagship analysis.

label: IMMUcan
counts: cancer patients across five cancer types profiled by the consortium (stated as 'more than 2,500')
quote: Here, we present two such workflows for multiplexed immunofluorescence and imaging mass cytometry of cancer tissues, which are applied to a total of roughly 10,000 samples from more than 2,500 patients over 6 years.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC12539258 (IMMUcan multi-modal imaging paper). The number is a lower bound. The same paper says the consortium 'acquires molecular and cellular profiles of over 2,500 patients across five cancer types up to 2026' (breast, renal cell, head and neck squamous, colorectal and non-small cell lung cancer). The EGA study (EGAS50000001533) gives no consortium total. It reports no per-cohort member counts.

label: IMMUcan SCCHN1 cohort
counts: R/M SCCHN patients with WES passing QC in the IMMUcan SCCHN cohorts, analysed subset
quote: After quality control, a total of 253 patients with WES datasets were included, of which 223 had RNA-seq.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC13320198 (EORTC/IMMUCAN SCCHN landscape paper, one of the two publications the EGA study EGAS50000001533 cites). The paper speaks of 'the IMMUCAN SCCHN cohorts' in the plural and does not name SCCHN1, so it may include patients outside it. The other cited paper (PMC13044521, anti-PD-1 progression) analysed 153 patients (74 anti-PD-1-resistant, 79 anti-PD-1-naive). The EGA WES dataset EGAD50000002205 lists 499 samples (tumour and germline) and the RNA dataset EGAD50000002206 lists 202. Patients were enrolled via EORTC-SPECTA (NCT02834884) or EORTC-HNCG-1559 (NCT03088059). An IMMUcan description of SCCHN1 enrolment would settle it.

label: ImmunAID
counts: patients with systemic autoinflammatory disorders and healthy controls enrolled at 30 centres
quote: 450 patients with different systemic autoinflammatory disorders (SAID) and healthy controls were enrolled from 30 clinical centers throughout Europe and Turkey, to assure a broad inclusion of SAID subtypes and a sufficient number of individuals for rare diseases.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC13201634, which names EGAS50000001393 as its data. The sentence groups patients and healthy controls without splitting them. Other ImmunAID papers analysed subsets: 372 patients with active SAID (PMC13507625) and 'a unique prospective cohort of 273 patients with SAID' (PMID:40341183). The EGA study's non-genomic datasets list up to 447 patients (mass spectrometry). A consortium design paper would settle the total enrolment.

label: Initiative for Molecular Profiling and Advanced Cancer Therapy 2
counts: patients with advanced metastatic cancer enrolled in IMPACT2 (Parts A and B)
quote: Of 829 patients with advanced metastatic cancer enrolled in the IMPACT2 study, 692 completed molecular testing.
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC13265806; the 2026 concordance paper (PMID:41730847, PMC12929784) also says 'Overall, 829 patients were enrolled in the IMPACT2 study', of whom 438 entered Part B from April 2019 to October 2023. Randomised numbers are small and partial: 'In Part A, 69 (21.8%) of 317 patients were randomized' and in Part B '32 (20.4%) of 157 patients were offered randomization; 16 accepted' (PMID:36302890). The preliminary-results paper that the EGA study EGAS00001004964 names (PMID:33742104) reports 391 patients enrolled May 2014 to April 2017, 320 with detectable aberrations. The enrolled count is recorded because the COHO term is the profiled cohort, not only the randomised patients.

label: International Cancer Genome Consortium
counts: cancer donors (tumour and matched normal genomes) in the 2020 PCAWG flagship analysis, ICGC and TCGA
quote: Here we report the integrative analysis of 2,658 whole-cancer genomes and their matching normal tissues across 38 tumour types from the Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes (PCAWG) Consortium of the International Cancer Genome Consortium (ICGC) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA).
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC7025898 (PCAWG flagship paper). The same paper says 'We collected genome data from 2,834 donors (Extended Data Table 1), of which 176 were excluded after quality assurance', and 2,583 donors were white-listed. The EGA definition source (EGAS00001001651) says PCAWG covers 'more than 2,800 cancer whole genomes'. The count is for the flagship analysis, not the total of all ICGC member projects, which no source read states; the number of member projects was not found either.

label: International Genetics of Parkinson Disease Progression Consortium
counts: Parkinson's disease patients represented in the 24 IGPP cohorts pooled in the 2026 meta-analysis
quote: Out of the total of 8099 patients represented in the 24 cohorts, 7745 participants had the genetic and covariate data available for inclusion in the downstream analyses (Supplementary Fig. 1).
note: Read as Europe PMC full text PMC13424109 (15-year meta-analysis of 24 cohorts), the most recent consortium analysis; 7745 of the 8099 patients were analysed. The same paper describes Phase 1 (the genome-wide survival study whose summary results are EGA EGAS00001005110, PMID:33958783): 'we analyzed the genetic drivers associated with progression from PD to dementia in 3821 PD patients over 31,053 longitudinal visits and 15 longitudinal cohorts'. The Phase 1 paper's own full text could not be fetched (Europe PMC returned an error).

label: International HapMap Project
counts: reference individuals from 11 populations genotyped in HapMap 3
quote: To inform the design and interpretation of such studies, we genotyped 1.6 million common single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 1,184 reference individuals from 11 global populations, and sequenced ten 100-kilobase regions in 692 of these individuals.
note: Abstract of the HapMap 3 paper (read via cached.py, Europe PMC abstract and PDF); HapMap 3 includes all Phase I and II samples. The Phase II paper (PMID:17943122) genotyped '270 individuals from four geographically diverse populations'. The definition source (EGA EGAS00001002548) concerns 139 Maasai individuals from the collection and gives no total.

label: InterPregGen
counts: maternal cases and controls in the 2020 maternal preeclampsia GWAS meta-analysis (Europe and Central Asia); no total stated
quote: Preeclamptic women from Europe and Central Asia (9515 cases and 157,719 controls)
note: From the Figure 1 caption of the example paper (Europe PMC full text PMC7688949). No source read states the combined total, so participants is left null. The same caption gives the offspring meta-analysis as 'Offspring of preeclamptic pregnancies from Europe and Central Asia (6775 cases and 375,372 controls)'; a follow-up set had 2635 cases and 6379 controls (Table 1 header). The EGA study (EGAS00001001266) says the consortium grew out of the WTCCC3 GWAS 'comparing ~2000 UK PE mothers with ~6000 common UK controls'.

label: Korean Genome Project
counts: Korean whole genomes in the Korea4K phase of the project
quote: Here, we present the second phase of the Korean Genome Project (KGP) with 4,157 sets of whole genome data, Korea4K.
note: Korea4K (PMID:38626723) is the project's second phase; 2,685 of the 4,157 have 107 clinical traits, 2,848 were newly sequenced participants, and Korea1K had 1,094 genomes. The whole Korean Genome Project may have enrolled more people than the Korea4K release; a project-level enrolment figure was not found in the sources read.

label: LifeLines-DEEP
counts: LifeLines participants enrolled in LifeLines DEEP, April-August 2013
quote: Initially, 1539 participants were included in the LifeLines DEEP study.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:26319774). 78 of the 1539 dropped out; additional blood was collected from 1387, exhaled air from 1425 and faeces from 1248. The EGA study page gives approximately 1,500.

label: Lifelines-NEXT
counts: pregnant Lifelines participants included 2016-2023 (mothers; partners and children also followed)
quote: From 2016 to 2023, we included 1450 pregnant Lifelines participants in Lifelines NEXT and intensively followed them, their partners and their children up to at least 1 year after birth.
note: The design paper (PMID:32100173) and the EGA page give the planned size: 'Lifelines NEXT aims to include 1500 pregnant women.' The achieved number is from a 2024 Nature Communications virome paper (PMID:38431663); it counts pregnant mothers only, not the infants or partners also followed, so the total of individuals is larger and no source read states it.

label: Liverpool Preterm Birth Biomarker Study
counts: women with singleton pregnancies recruited at Liverpool Women's Hospital
quote: Whole blood samples were obtained from women with singleton pregnancies (N=567) recruited at the Liverpool Women’s Hospital at 16 and 20 weeks of gestation.
note: The study paper (PMID:35046466, PMC8770724) does not state the total in its text (it is in Figure 1); it gives analysed outcome groups: 'PPROM (≤ 34 weeks gestation, n = 53), high-risk term (HTERM, ≥ 37 weeks, n = 126) or low-risk (no history of SPTB/PPROM) term (LTERM, ≥ 39 weeks, n = 188)'. The SPTB group size is not stated in the text read, so cases and controls are left null.

label: Low coverage Kuusamo whole genome sequencing study
note: The EGA study (EGAS00001000143, deprecated, never released, no datasets or PMIDs in the EGA metadata API) gives no sample count. A 2017 SISu paper (PMID:28145424, PMC5346294) says 'Amongst the sequenced Finnish individuals, 371 belonged to the Kuusamo sub-isolate within Finland', but those were unrelated FINRISK/Health 2000 Finns sequenced at ~4.6x, not clearly the 1x Kuusamo study, so the number is not recorded. PMID:32519380 mentions a Kuusamo WGS subset in the HRC without a count. The number of Kuusamo samples sequenced at 1x would settle it (e.g. the Sanger sequencing project or HRC documentation).

label: Lung Cancer Diagnostic Study
counts: individuals at risk of lung cancer examined consecutively at Bispebjerg Hospital over seven months
quote: We examined patient blood samples from a prospective observational trial of 365 individuals examined consecutively at Bispebjerg Hospital in Copenhagen, Denmark (LUCAS cohort) during a seven-month period.
note: PMID:34417454. The EGA study EGAS00001005340 breaks the 365 down: 'including 129 individuals ultimately diagnosed with lung cancer and 236 individuals determined to not have lung cancer'. A prospective diagnostic cohort, not a case-control design, so cases/controls are left null. The external validation cohort (385 non-cancer, 46 cancer) is a separate group.

label: lungNENomics
counts: patients with a lung neuroendocrine tumour in the lungNENomics series (pathological review)
quote: The lungNENomics series is a multicentre, international, retrospective cohort of 259 patients diagnosed with an LNET, whose clinical data are summarised in Table 1 .
note: ESMO Open 2024 (PMID:38878324). The 2026 dataset preprint (PPR1209274, doi 10.64898/2026.05.12.724489, Europe PMC abstract) describing the multi-omic data deposited at EGA says '201 participants, for a total of  n = 294 tumours'; the 2026 Mol Cancer paper (PMID:42649496) analyses '319 fresh frozen lung NETs', 'primarily sourced from the lungNENomics network', so that tumour count is not only lungNENomics patients. The EGA datasets give WGS for 72 and RNA-seq for 179 individuals. The 259 is the whole reviewed series; the multi-omic subset is 201.

label: Maastricht IBS studies
counts: IBS cases and controls from Maastricht UMC+ with faecal metagenomes
quote: an IBS case–control cohort with 313 participants from Maastricht University Medical Center + (MUMC + ) 37 – 39 .
note: Vich Vila et al. 2020 (PMID:31953381), which deposited the MIBS metagenomes in EGA (EGAD00001002668, 336 samples); 305 passed its sequencing-depth filter. The split of the 313 into cases and controls is not stated in that text. Other MIBS figures: the 2016 biomarker paper (PMID:27263852) 'a cohort of 196 clinical IBS patients and 160 HC without GI symptoms'; the 2022 paper (PMID:35446234) 'Fecal samples were available for 314 individuals (181 IBS patients, 133 HCs).' The 313 is taken because it describes the metagenomic collection this term covers; no source read gives a single total for the whole MIBS cohort (NCT00775060).

label: Malaria Genomic Epidemiology Network
counts: severe malaria cases and population controls in the 2019 genome-wide association analysis
quote: A total of 17,056 samples had PCs and assigned case/control status, and were included in association analyses.
note: MalariaGEN 2019 Nat Commun GWAS (PMID:31844061), from 11 countries; the title rounds it to 17,000. The same paper describes the underlying case-control study as 'records for over 16,000 individuals admitted to a hospital with severe symptoms of P. falciparum malaria, and 22,000 population controls', Sequenom genotyping of 37,571 individuals ('including 15,866 SM cases, 19,845 controls and samples collected as parents'), and a data release of 40,631 individuals. The case/control split of the 17,056 is not stated in the text, so cases and controls are null. The network's low-coverage WGS reference set (EGAS00001000629) is a separate, smaller effort (100 per Gambian ethnic group in the pilot, 400 in Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Ghana and Tanzania).

label: Malaysian Breast Cancer cohort
counts: female breast cancer patients in the MyBrCa tumour cohort (recruited 2012-2018)
quote: The MyBrCa tumour cohort comprises of 934 female breast cancer patients of self-reported Malaysian nationality who were sequentially recruited from two Malaysian hospitals, Subang Jaya Medical Centre and Universiti Malaya Medical Centre.
note: Breast Cancer Res 2024 (PMID:38649964). The 2020 Nat Commun paper (PMID:33353943) reported 'In all, 661 tissue samples were collected from breast cancer patients recruited as part of the MyBrCa study at the Subang Jaya Medical Centre'. The EGA study EGAS00001006518 covers a 35-tumour TNBC validation set plus 94 TNBC discovery samples. The tumour cohort is drawn from the larger MyBrCa Genetics case-control study, whose total was not looked for here because the term is defined as the tumour-sequenced hospital cohort.

label: Malmö Diet and Cancer Study
counts: Malmö residents born 1923-1950 who attended baseline screening 1991-1996
quote: All residents in Malmö, Sweden born between 1923 and 1950 without exclusions were invited to an initial screening 1991–1996 and 30,446 participated [ 25 ].
note: Also 'MDCS is a population-based prospective study comprising 30,446 participants' (PMID:36275419, PMC9535608). A 2026 paper (PMID:42590020) gives 30,466 examined at baseline, 'of whom 28,098 provided complete dietary, questionnaire, and anthropometric data'; 30,446 is the figure used by most sources read. The EGA study EGAS00001000936 is a stroke case-control analysis using MDC among other samples.

label: Mechanisms of the Development of Allergy
counts: participants of the 14 member birth cohorts in the MeDALL knowledge base (approximate)
quote: The MeDALL knowledge base integrates historical and newly collected data from around 44 000 participants on 398 clinical and phenotypic attributes (harmonized from 7495 individual cohort variables) and 160 different follow‐ups at 25 different time points between pregnancy and age 20.
note: MeDALL summary paper, Allergy 2016 (PMID:26970340); the number is stated as 'around 44 000'. The same paper describes 'a large network of 14 ongoing birth cohorts'. A 2017 analysis of 10 MeDALL cohorts (PMID:28845428) used 'a total sample of 26 663 children'. The EGA study EGAS00001002169 is the MeDALL epigenetics study of 4 cohorts (INMA, EDEN, BAMSE, PIAMA; dataset of 1347 samples). The 2014 comorbidity paper (PMID:24503268) is closed and was not read.

label: Medical Genome Reference Bank
counts: healthy older individuals from ASPREE and the 45 and Up Study selected for whole-genome sequencing
quote: The MGRB is comprised of 4000 healthy, older individuals, mostly of European descent, recruited from two Australian community-based cohorts.
note: Rationale and cohort paper, Eur J Hum Genet 2019 (PMID:30353151). The 2020 Nat Commun paper (PMID:31974348) says 'The MGRB consists of over 4000 individuals from the ASPREE study 12 , and Sax Institute’s 45 and Up Study' and that 'After exclusion of 356 samples that failed quality control and relatedness checks, 2570 samples remained, forming the first release of the MGRB cohort genomic data'. EGA holds datasets of 2570 and 1440 sequenced samples. The 4000 is the round target/cohort size; the exact final number sequenced was not found stated.

label: MESOMICS
counts: malignant pleural mesothelioma patients with multi-omic data
quote: In the context of the MESOMICS project, we have performed the most comprehensive molecular characterization of MPM to date, with the underlying dataset made of the largest whole-genome sequencing series yet reported, together with transcriptome sequencing and methylation arrays for 120 MPM patients.
note: GigaScience data note (PMID:36705549). The Nat Genet paper (PMID:36928603) likewise analyses 'a novel cohort of 120 MPM tumors'. Other counts: methylation arrays 'for 135 MPM samples from 122 patients'; the EGA study EGAS00001004812 says 123 samples. The 120 is the multi-omic series; the methylation count shows a few more patients were profiled on one platform only.

label: Milieu Intérieur
counts: healthy donors aged 20-69 recruited 2012-2013, stratified by sex and decade
quote: To identify the determinants of immune variability, the Milieu Intérieur (MI) population cohort study 14 was established in 2012–2013, consisting of 1000 well-defined healthy donors equally stratified by age and sex (100 male and 100 female donors in each decade of life between 20 and 69 years old).
note: Agrees with the design paper abstract (PMID:25562703): 'a 1000-person healthy population-based study (stratified according to sex and age)', and with the EGA dataset text. The 10-year follow-up (PMID:42173848) 'successfully recruited 415 of the original 1000 donors'; 863 of the 1,000 gave stool for 16S profiling (EGA).

label: MITO16A/MaNGO-OV2 trial
counts: patients with ovarian cancer enrolled in the phase IV trial
quote: Among 398 patients enrolled in the MITO‐16A/MaNGO‐OV2 study, the following patients were excluded from the final p53 IHC evaluation: 13 patients because the samples were not available for research; 12 patients who underwent neo‐adjuvant chemotherapy and could not provide treatment‐naïve tissue; 15 because of inadequate tumor sample; 42 because the samples had inadequate morphology for TMA; 5 because tumor samples were exhausted after nucleic acid extraction.
note: TP53 translational paper (PMID:39415516); the same paper also says 'Three hundred ninety‐eight patients were enrolled in the MITO16A/MaNGO OV‐2 study.' PMID:41249601 also gives the whole trial population as n = 398. The ctDNA paper linked from the EGA study (PMID:41747586) says 'Among 389 patients enrolled' in its text but n = 398 in its Table 1, so 389 looks like a transposition. The primary trial report was not read.

label: Molecular Phenotyping to Accelerate Genomic Epidemiology
counts: only member-study counts reported
note: No source read gives a pooled MolPAGE participant number; the papers report the sub-studies separately. MolOBB: 'we analysed ABD, GLU and WB samples from 29 MetS cases and 44 controls from the MolOBB study' and 'In a separate dataset (MolTWIN) of 154 healthy twins' (Min et al. 2012, PMID:22383892, PMC3285582); 'the MolOBB case/control study for MetSyn ... involves 20 cases (10 male, 10 female) and 20 controls' (Drong et al. 2013, PMID:23431366); '70 human subjects in the MolOBB study (41 healthy controls and 29 metabolic syndrome cases' (PMID:22102887). The EGA study EGAS00000000102 names two sub-studies (MolOBB, MolTWIN) and holds 170 genotyped case and control samples. No sentence read states the number of member studies, so it is not recorded as a number. A MolPAGE project report giving total recruitment would settle it.

label: Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium
counts: primary breast tumour specimens from UK and Canadian tumour banks (stated as 'over 2,000'; one tumour per patient not stated)
quote: We assembled a collection of over 2,000 clinically annotated primary fresh-frozen breast cancer specimens from tumour banks in the UK and Canada ( Supplementary Tables 1 – 3 ).
note: Curtis et al. 2012 (PMID:22522925). The number is a lower bound ('over 2,000') and counts tumours. The same paper analyses 'a discovery set of 997 primary tumours and a validation set of 995 tumours from METABRIC'; no sentence read gives their total. A 2016 follow-up (PMID:27161491) sequenced '2,433 primary breast tumours that have copy number aberration (CNA), gene expression and long-term clinical follow-up data', but the text read does not say all are METABRIC, so it is not used.

label: MRCE family panel
counts: individuals from 320 British families in the MRCE panel, genotyped
quote: The second sample (MRCE) of 950 individuals from 320 families of British descent was genotyped using the Illumina Sentrix HumanHap300 Genotyping BeadChip.
note: Liang et al. 2013 Genome Res (PMID:23345460). Of these, the eQTL study used 'expression data on 550 additional individuals from the MRCE family panel' (also on the EGA page, which the COHO definition follows); the EGA MRCE genotype dataset has 543 samples. The same paper says the MRCE families were 'ascertained through a child with asthma ... (the MRCA panel) ... or eczema using the Illumina bead array platform (the MRCE panel)', i.e. MRCE families came through a child with eczema, whereas the COHO definition says 'asthma families'; worth checking in the definition. The original panel paper (Morar et al. 2007) was not read.

label: MultiMuTHER
counts: TwinsUK women with longitudinal whole-blood expression and metabolite profiles
quote: We profiled longitudinal whole-blood gene expression and metabolite levels in 335 females over 8 years.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of the Science 2026 paper (doi 10.1126/science.aed6452). The EGA study EGAS50000000144 agrees: 'The MultiMuTHER study is a longitudinal study of 335 subjects seen at three or more clinical visits per participant.' (960 RNA-seq samples).

label: Multiple Tissue Human Expression Resource
counts: female TwinsUK twins recruited to MuTHER
quote: In total of 856 female twins (154 monozygotic (MZ) twin pairs, 232 dizygotic (DZ) twin pairs and 84 singletons) aged 38.7-84.6 years were recruited from the TwinsUK resource 17and adipose (subcutaneous fat) and skin tissue biopsies as well as peripheral blood samples (for generation of lymphoblastoid cell lines or LCLs) were collected for subsequent genome-wide expression profiling.
note: MuTHER design paper (Grundberg et al. 2012, PMID:22941192). Post-QC expression profiles for 825 (adipose, LCL) and 705 (skin) individuals; the 2011 pilot (PMID:21304890) used 156 LCL, 160 skin and 166 fat samples; the EGA definition source (EGAS00001001569) is a WGBS subset of 43 female twins.

label: Nala GSI GSAv3 PGx Study
counts: no participants: 73 reference cell lines
quote: Here, we present the results of accuracy and precision assessments, involving a total of 73 cell lines.
note: A pre-clinical validation study on reference cell lines (GIAB, GeT-RM, 1000 Genomes), not on recruited people, so no participant count exists; the EGA dataset EGAD00010002645 lists 74 samples. Publication: Front Pharmacol 2024;15:1349203.

label: NCI China cohort
note: The EGA study (pending release, no datasets or publication listed) describes the cohort but gives no number of participants; a web search found no publication of the NanoSeq study of this cohort. A publication of the Sanger/NCI/IARC buccal-cell NanoSeq work, or the EGA dataset once released, would settle it.

label: NCI Taiwan cohort
note: The EGA study (pending release, no datasets or publication listed) describes the cohort but gives no number of participants; no publication of the Taiwan buccal-cell NanoSeq study was found. A publication or the released EGA dataset would settle it.

label: NeoALTTO
counts: patients randomised in the NeoALTTO trial
quote: The NeoALTTO phase III trial randomized 455 HER2-positive early-stage BC patients to receive neoadjuvant trastuzumab (T), lapatinib (L) or T + L1,3,4.
note: From the EGA study's paper (Rediti et al. 2023, PMID:37923752), which also says baseline frozen biopsies were available for 423 of the 455 patients and that its RNA sequencing cohort was N = 254. The trial's primary report (Baselga et al. 2012, Lancet) was not read.

label: NIHR BioResource
counts: volunteers in the recallable resource ("over", a lower bound)
quote: The NIHR BioResource is a recallable resource of over 250,000 volunteers, with and without health conditions who have agreed to take part in health-related research.
note: Stated in the supplement of a 2025 osteoarthritis GWAS (Nature, doi 10.1038/s41586-025-08771-z), not by the BioResource itself; the BioResource website (bioresource.nihr.ac.uk) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read, though search snippets suggest it now claims over 300,000. A consent text on gladstudy.org.uk says over 200,000. The EGA definition source (EGAS00001004870) is a 13,489-sample blood-donor genotype dataset; the Genes and Cognition sub-cohort profiled 21,051; the rare-disease pilot enrolled 9,742.

label: Pan-Cancer Analysis of Whole Genomes
counts: cancer donors (white- and grey-listed) in the 2020 PCAWG marker paper
quote: Across the 2,658 white- and grey-listed donors, whole-genome sequencing data were available from 2,605 primary tumours and 173 metastases or local recurrences.
note: PCAWG marker paper (PMID:32025007). Genome data were collected from 2,834 donors at the autumn 2014 data freeze, of which 176 were excluded after quality assurance; 2,583 were white-listed (optimal quality). The EGA study says 'more than 2,800 cancer whole genomes'. Member projects (ICGC/TCGA) are not counted separately.

label: PANDA trial
counts: patients included in the phase 2 PANDA trial
quote: A total of 21 patients were included, of whom 20 patients underwent surgery and were evaluable for the secondary pathologic response and survival endpoints, while 19 were evaluable for exploratory translational analyses.
note: The EGA study reproduces the abstract of the trial paper (Verschoor et al., Nat Med 2024;30:519-530); the EGA datasets hold RNA and exome data from 20 patients.

label: PELICAN
counts: men who died of metastatic prostate cancer 1995-2004 and consented to rapid autopsy (PELICAN33)
quote: We analyzed deep longitudinal clinical, neuroendocrine expression, and autopsy data of 33 men who died from mPC between 1995 and 2004 (PELICAN33), and related findings to mPC biomarkers reported in the literature.
note: The core rapid-autopsy cohort. The EGA study (EGAS00001006959) describes a PELICAN45 RNA-seq set that adds non-androgen-deprived metastases from 'an additional 12 men' to the PELICAN33 participants, but no source read states a PELICAN45 total; Wedge et al. 2018 studied 20 men from PELICAN. Whether the label should cover PELICAN45 decides between the two.

label: PETAL trial
counts: DLBCL patients in the PETAL trial's intention-to-treat population
quote: Of 609 DLBCL belonging to the intention-to-treat population of the PETAL trial, 546 (89.7%) were iPET-negative and 63 (10.3%) were iPET-positive 2 .

label: PHOENIX trial
counts: patients randomised in the PHOENIX trial
quote: A total of 838 patients were randomly assigned to ibrutinib plus R-CHOP (n = 419) or placebo plus R-CHOP (n = 419).
note: Primary trial report (Younes et al., J Clin Oncol 2019). The EGA study says 773 biopsies were sequenced (189 China, 584 non-China); a 2023 follow-up (PMID:36696540) analysed RNA-seq for 766 patients; a Chinese subgroup analysis (PMID:36467814) covers 200 patients enrolled in China.

label: Polish glioma cohort
counts: glioma patients/samples analysed (analysed set, not all Polish)
quote: Most of the patients from our cohort suffered from glioblastoma (132/182).
note: From the bioRxiv preprint of the EGA study's work, which also says 'In the analysis we used 182 II, III and IV grade glioma samples' and that samples GL162-GL182 came from the Canadian Human Tissue Bank, so not all 182 are Polish patients; no Polish-only count is stated. The published version (Int J Cancer 2023, doi 10.1002/ijc.34631, closed) says 180 gliomas, 135 of them IDH-wild-type GBM. The EGA dataset lists 207 glioma samples with matched blood for 48.

label: Posthumous Evaluation of Advanced Cancer Environment
note: No source read states how many patients PEACE (NCT03004755) has enrolled. The ClinicalTrials.gov record gives an estimated (planned) enrollment of 500 as a structured field, not a sentence (status unknown, last updated 2024-05-10). Analysed subsets: 14 ICI-treated melanoma patients (EGAS00001007081, Spain et al. 2023); 24 NSCLC patients, of 49 co-enrolled in TRACERx and PEACE (PMC13190308, 2026). label: PRedicting Outcomes For Crohn's disease using a moLecular biomarker

quote: Between Dec 29, 2017, and Jan 5, 2022, 386 patients (mean age 33·6 years [SD 13·2]; 179 [46%] female, 207 [54%] male) were randomised: 193 to the top-down group and 193 to the accelerated step-up group.
note: Primary trial report (Noor et al., Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2024). Primary outcome data were available for 379 participants. The EGA metagenomics study (EGAS00001007958) gives no number of stool samples or participants.

label: Pregnancy Outcome Prediction study
counts: nulliparous women with a viable singleton pregnancy, recruited 2008-2012
quote: The study included 4512 women with a viable singleton pregnancy; study participants provided written informed consent and were recruited between January 2008 and July 2012.
note: Stated by the POP study team in the EGA study description (the definition source). The POPs cohort-profile paper was not read; the EGA placental datasets are small subsets (e.g. 64 female and 67 male placentas).

label: Premature Atherosclerosis Study pedigrees
note: No source read states how many pedigrees or individuals make up the exome-sequenced PAS pedigree collection; the EGA dataset EGAD00001000017 lists 18 samples without saying they are individuals. The parent case cohort is larger: 'Premature Atherosclerosis (PAS) Cohort: this cohort comprises 935 patients with early symptomatic atherosclerosis before the age of 51 years.' (PMC4039470, a single-pedigree KERA study whose linkage used 12 family members). A paper describing the whole pedigree collection would settle it.

label: PrevANZ trial
counts: people with a clinically isolated syndrome enrolled in PrevANZ
quote: Between 2013 and 2021, we enrolled 204 participants.
note: Primary trial report (Brain 2024). 199 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis; the transcriptome sub-study (PMID:38479439, the EGA study's work) included datasets from 55 participants.

label: Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy
counts: newborns at the start of the birth cohort (recruited 1996-1997)
quote: The study started with 3,963 newborns.
note: From the PIAMA recruitment paragraph in the supplement of an atopic dermatitis GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Commun 2023): 10,232 pregnant women were screened, 7,862 invited and 4,146 gave consent. The cohort profile (Wijga et al., Int J Epidemiol 2014, PMID:23315435) is closed and was not read. The EGA nasal RNA-seq dataset (EGAS00001006240) holds 186 adolescents.

label: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre acute myeloid leukemia patient cohort
counts: AML patient samples RNA-sequenced (analysed subset of the Leukemia Tissue Bank)
quote: The PMCC AML RNAseq dataset consists of 81 AML patient samples (clinical data in Supplemental Table 11 of manuscript), processed in two batches.
note: The term is defined as this 81-patient RNA-seq cohort (Xie et al., Blood Cancer Discov 2021), so the number is the cohort as defined; five patients were included in both batches and the EGA dataset lists 85 samples. The Princess Margaret Leukemia Tissue Bank itself holds many more patients, but no source read states its size.

label: Radar cohort
counts: offspring of former German radar operators (children, not counting parents)
quote: We recruited 110 offspring of former German radar operators, who were likely to have been exposed to IR (Radar cohort, exposure = 0-353 mGy), and reanalyzed sequencing data of 130 offspring of Chernobyl cleanup workers (CRU, exposure = 0-4080 mGy) from Yeager, et al.
note: Brand et al., Sci Rep 2025. The EGA study says 'We sequenced the whole genome of 110 children from 70 families (Radar cohort)'; the number of sequenced parents is not stated in anything read, so parents are not counted. The EGA dataset lists 103 samples.

label: Research on Obesity and Diabetes among African Migrants
counts: Ghanaian participants who completed the RODAM baseline assessment (2012-2015)
quote: Participants All the participants in the RODAM cross-sectional study that completed the baseline assessment (n=5114) were eligible for the follow-up of which 2165 participants (n=638 from rural-Ghana, n=608 from urban-Ghana, and n=919 Ghanaian migrants in Amsterdam, the Netherlands) were included in the RODAM-Pros cohort study.
note: From the 2022 RODAM-Pros cohort profile (PMC9756160); baseline completed in 2015. Of these, 2165 were followed up in RODAM-Pros (plus 1047 Ghanaian and 2098 Dutch HELIUS participants added in Amsterdam). The 2014 design paper (PMID:24657884) planned 6250 (five subgroups of 1250). The EGA dataset holds 16S data for 1211 participants.

label: ROBUST trial
counts: patients with ABC-DLBCL randomised (285 per arm)
quote: Results A total of 570 patients with ABC-DLBCL (n = 285 per arm) were stratified by International Prognostic Index score, age, and bulky disease, and randomly assigned to R2-CHOP or placebo/R-CHOP.
note: Primary results paper (PMC8078325): enrolment February 2015 to August 2017; 2,109 patients were screened centrally. The EGA dataset EGAD50000000482 holds RNA-seq profiles of 1040 patients from the trial (screened patients, not all randomised).

label: SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Response in Cancer trial
counts: patients with haematological malignancies enrolled April-June 2021 (healthy controls not counted)
quote: Results Hematological patients show severe impairment of anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies after COVID-19 vaccination The CORSA trial ( NCT04345315 ) enrolled 77 hematological patients from April to June 2021 who received at least one dose of vaccine (73 patients received Comirnaty and 4 received Spikevax).
note: CORSA trial results paper (PMID:42245663, Front Immunol 2026). The healthy controls were a separate reference population: "We compared the antibody response of patients to the reference population of 150 sex-matched (1:2) HC working at the Cancer Center where patients were enrolled and who received the BTN162b2 vaccine from January to March 2021, according to the Italian guidelines." No source states a combined total, so participants gives the enrolled patients only. The EGA study covers a random subset of 10 lymphoma patients and 7 healthy controls.

label: Schizophrenia Exome Sequencing Meta-analysis consortium
counts: schizophrenia cases and controls in the 2022 exome meta-analysis (no total stated)
quote: Here, we generated, aggregated, harmonized variant identification, and meta-analyzed the exome sequences of 24,248 individuals with schizophrenia and 97,322 controls from seven continental populations.
note: Flagship SCHEMA analysis (PMID:35396579). The 97,322 controls include 46,885 gnomAD external controls with summary counts only: "We aggregated exome sequence data consisting of 24,248 individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia and 50,437 individuals without a known psychiatric diagnosis, recruited in eleven global collections"; de novo mutations from 3,402 trios were also meta-analysed. No source read states a combined participant total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The SCHEMA website is a results browser giving no count.

label: Severe Childhood Onset Obesity Project
counts: British individuals of European ancestry with severe childhood-onset obesity (approximate)
quote: The Severe Childhood Onset Obesity Project (SCOOP) cohort (Wheeler et al., 2013), includes ∼4800 British individuals of European ancestry with childhood onset obesity (BMI standard deviation score (SDS) > 3; onset of obesity before the age of 10 years).
note: Approximate figure from the 2020 exome study (PMID:32492392), the most recent statement of the whole cohort's size found. The EGA study EGAS00001000922 describes an earlier GWAS of 1,509 SCOOP cases and 5,380 population controls and a plan to genotype an additional 3,500 SCOOP samples; the EGA STILTS study says '>5,000 UK Caucasian subjects with severe early onsetobesity (SCOOP)'. Other cached documents describe a SCOOP-UK sample of 1,038 (or 1,028) participants, a subset used in one consortium. The Wheeler et al. 2013 GWAS (PMID:23563609) was not read.

label: SG10K Pilot
counts: Singapore Chinese, Malays and Indians whole-genome sequenced
quote: By whole-genome sequencing of 4,810 Singapore Chinese, Malays, and Indians, we found 98.3 million SNPs and small insertions or deletions, over half of which are novel.
note: Abstract of the SG10K pilot paper (Cell 2019); the EGA study EGAS00001003875 and dataset EGAD00001005337 give the same 4,810 individuals. Full text is closed but the abstract suffices.

label: STRAT-PARK
counts: participants included by March 2023 (recruitment ongoing)
quote: By March 2023, 252 participants were included, comprising 204 cases and 48 controls.
note: From the abstract of the 2024 STRAT-PARK cohort paper (Prog Neurobiol; full text closed). Recruitment is ongoing: the same abstract gives a target of 2000 individuals with PD and controls from Norway and Canada and a rate of about 150 participants per year, so the current size is larger. Later papers read (PMC13578105, PMC13347526, PMC12034802) give only analysed subsets (e.g. 61 PD and 31 controls with platelet samples).

label: STREP GENE
counts: invasive GAS cases genotyped and analysed after quality control
quote: Results and Discussion After quality control, we included 43 cases of European ancestry aged less than 65 years without comorbidity ( Supplementary Table 1 ).
note: From the only STREP GENE paper found (PMID:31462703). This is the analysed set after quality control, which excluded some recruited cases (seven at QC and six earlier for age or comorbidity); no source states how many were recruited in total, and no count is given by recruitment route. The 1,540 controls in the case-control analysis were healthy children from Oxford Vaccine Group studies, not STREP GENE participants. The EGA dataset EGAD00001004558 likewise holds genotypes of 43 cases.

label: Stroke Investigative Research and Education Network
counts: 1:1 matched stroke cases and stroke-free controls analysed in a 2026 SIREN report
quote: To ensure accurate comparisons and minimize confounding, stroke cases were matched with stroke-free controls at a 1:1 ratio on key demographic factors known to confound stroke epidemiology, including age (± 5 years), sex, and ethnicity, for a total of 7368 participants (3684 cases and 3684 controls) in this study.
note: Largest and most recent count found (PMID:41917906, 2026), but it is the matched analysed set; no SIREN profile paper states the whole enrolment. Its abstract calls these '7,368 case-control pairs', inconsistent with the full text. Other counts: the 2015 phenomics protocol (PMID:26304844) planned 3,000 cases and 3,000 controls; the 2018 Lancet Glob Health case-control paper (PMID:29496511) enrolled 2118 case-control pairs from Aug 2014 to June 2017; a 2025 paper (PMID:40599698) reports 'A total of 7104 subjects (3553 stroke cases and 3551 stroke-free controls'; the 2024 GWAS (PMID:38317187) genotyped 3434 (1691 ischemic stroke cases, 1743 controls), matching the 3421 samples in the EGA datasets.

label: Study Into Lean and Thin Subjects
counts: UK thin healthy adults in the cohort (approximate)
quote: We were able to take advantage of the UK National Health Service (NHS) research infrastructure to recruit from primary care ( Methods ) using body mass index (BMI: weight in kg/height in metres 2 ) criteria and personal review of individual case files to identify a cohort of approximately 2000 UK European descent thin adults (Study Into Lean and Thin Subjects, STILTS cohort; mean BMI = 17.6 kg/m 2 ) who are well, without medical conditions or eating disorders ( Methods ).
note: From the 2019 STILTS GWAS paper (PMID:30677029), the only paper describing the cohort. Its methods also say 25,000 eligible individuals were invited and 'approximately 12% (2,900) replied consenting to take part'; genotype data were obtained for 1,622 STILTS individuals and 1,471 remained after QC. The EGA study EGAS00001000923 says 1,600 people with thinness had been recruited (earlier statement).

note: SweGen design paper (Eur J Hum Genet 2017, PMC5765326): 942 unrelated individuals were selected from the Swedish Twin Registry PCA (the rest from the Northern Sweden Population Health Study); the samples were chosen from a Twin Registry cohort of over 10 000 genotyped individuals.

note: From the 2024 Sys4MS prediction paper (PMID:38133801), which also recruited 98 healthy controls; no source read states the combined total. By centre: Barcelona n = 93, Genova n = 110, Berlin n = 96, Oslo n = 121; 278 patients had 2-year follow-up. EGA descriptions differ: clinical data for 419 patients (EGAD00001010867) and '350 patients with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) and 9 controls' in the genotype dataset (EGAD00010002505).
