note: Pooled number from TARGET's flagship pan-cancer paper (Nature 2018). It counts tumour cases across six histotypes, one per patient; the paper does not state TARGET's total enrolment across all its projects. The NCI TARGET pages fetched (ocg.cancer.gov/programs/target, cancer.gov/ccg/research/genome-sequencing/target) give no case count.

note: From the 2025 TransplantLines cohort profile (PMC12374880); recruitment is ongoing. The EGA gut-microbiome dataset EGAD00001008907 holds 1177 samples, a subset.

note: Quote read from the Europe PMC record (PPR853079) of the medRxiv preprint doi:10.1101/2024.05.14.24307227; it counts samples, not stated as participants. The EGA phase-1 sequencing study covers 182 controls, 97 cases, 17 latent infections and 3 suspect cases.

label: Tumor Profiler
counts: no overall total stated; counts by indication only
note: No source read gives the whole study's enrolment. (PMID:40425842); ovarian, 'For TuPro in ovarian cancer, we enrolled a total of 62 female patients between December 2018 and March 2021 in three Swiss hospitals' (PMID:42443179, PMC13486661); AML, 'Our cohort included 21 patients in total' (PMID:39477946, PMC11525670, relapsed/refractory AML only). These are not summed. The 2021 design paper (PMID:33482122, Cancer Cell, closed; its abstract gives no number) or the study website would settle the total. label: Type 2 Diabetes Genetic Exploration by Next-generation sequencing in multi-Ethnic Samples

note: Flagship analysis (Fuchsberger et al., Nature 2016, PMID:27398621). The joint set includes GoT2D exomes; T2D-GENES itself generated 'exome sequence data from 10,437 T2D cases and controls of diverse ancestry'. The EGA study EGAS00001001460 states 'We preformed exome sequencing in 6,546 T2D cases and 6,457 control individuals of multiethnic origin' (before QC, no total given). The paper's follow-up exome-array stage added 28,305 cases and 51,549 controls of European ancestry.

counts: individuals in the open population cohort (stated as 'over 22,000', a lower bound)

note: From a 2023 GPC paper (PMID:37775773). The COHO definition's 'about 6,400' is the Uganda Genome Resource sample drawn from the GPC; the EGA study EGAS00001000545 describes 'a population-based study of 6,400 individuals from a geographically defined rural community in South-West Uganda' (4,778 genotyped, up to 1,978 sequenced). If the term is meant as that genomic subset, 6400 is the number.

counts: subjects collected (affected and unaffected siblings), 1998-2003
quote: In total, we collected 6,285 subjects.
note: From the 2005 BHF Family Heart Study genome-wide linkage paper (PMID:16380912), whose methods describe recruitment; the count includes unaffected siblings. The other definition sources (PMID:21966275, PMID:22325189) use BHF-FHS subsets only.

quote: Here we report several new replicated associations in our scan of nsSNPs in 1500 shared controls and 1000 individuals from each of 4 different diseases: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS), Autoimmune Thyroid Disease/Graves’ Disease (AITD), Breast Cancer (BC) and Multiple Sclerosis (MS).

label: Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center
counts: Knight-ADRC participants recruited during the last 30 years
quote: Out of the 6,625 Knight-ADRC participants (Table 1) recruited during the last 30 years, 2,746 of them are classified at the last assessment as AD (with 29 of them being Autosomal Dominant AD), 2,369 are considered cognitively unimpaired, and 1,510 are considered to suffer from other dementias (1,285 AD Related Dementias (ADRD), 153 FTD, and 72 DLB - Table 1.
note: Knight-ADRC resource paper (PMID:38997326, Sci Data 2024), the definition source. The same paper also says cognitive assessments were performed on 'more than 6,625 participants', that the GHTO core holds samples from 6,625 participants, and that omic data exist for 5,283 participants (as of October 2023). Year is the paper's publication year.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
counts: subjects enrolled at baseline in ADNI-1 (229 cognitively normal, 398 MCI, 192 AD)
quote: A total of 819 subjects (229 cognitively normal, 398 with MCI, and 192 with AD) were enrolled at baseline and followed for 12 months using standard cognitive and functional measures typical of clinical trials.
note: The number is the first phase (ADNI-1) only; ADNI has since added participants in ADNI GO, ADNI-2, ADNI-3 and ADNI4. The ADNI About page gives only per-phase planned numbers (e.g. 200 EMCI in ADNI GO, 550 newly enrolled in ADNI-2), and the ADNI4 digital-study paper (PMC11485063) plans an in-clinic cohort of up to 1500 including rollovers; no source read states a cumulative total across phases. The example study (PMID:35086473) analysed 1,576 subjects, and QT-PAD holds 1,737 ADNI participants.

label: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network
counts: participants enrolled as of 15 May 2012
quote: 255 DIAN participants were enrolled as of May 15, 2012, the largest international cohort of ADAD individuals in the world.
note: An interim count from the design paper, which adds that enrolment was ongoing and anticipated to reach 400. The DIAN website's Observational Study description (https://dian.wustl.edu/observational-study/description/) now targets 'Up to 850 participants', a planned size. The example study (PMID:42127933) included 472 participants from DIAN, an analysed subset that shows the cohort has grown past 255. A recent DIAN cohort profile would settle the achieved size.

label: Barcelona-1
counts: subjects at baseline (approximate)
quote: Barcelona -1 is a longitudinal observational study consisting of ~300 subjects at baseline carried out in the Memory and Disorder unit at the University Hospital Mutua de Terrassa, Terrassa, Barcelona, Spain.
note: An approximate figure from a multi-cohort proteomics paper (PMID:35871346), not a Barcelona-1 design paper. The example study (PMID:39528825) analysed CSF proteomics for 198 Barcelona-1 individuals, a subset.

label: Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Networks Engineering Task
counts: coronary artery disease patients genotyped and RNA-sequenced
quote: We genotyped and RNA-sequenced vascular and metabolic tissues from 600 coronary artery disease patients in the Stockholm-Tartu Atherosclerosis Reverse Networks Engineering Task study (STARNET).
note: The design paper (PMID:27540175) counts the 600 CAD patients only; it does not state in the text read how many non-CAD comparison patients were enrolled (its Table S1, not read, may). The example study (PMID:41456820) profiled a subset of 284 patients: CABG patients (n = 200) and controls eligible for other open-heart surgeries (n = 84).

label: Million Veteran Program
counts: Veterans who have joined since 2011
quote: Since launching in 2011, 1 million Veterans have joined MVP.
note: A round figure from the VA research website; the MVP participant site (https://www.mvp.va.gov/pwa/) says 'Over one million Veterans are part of our program'. The design paper (PMID:26441289) reports 397,104 veterans enrolled as of August 3, 2015. The example study (PMID:39024449) analysed 635,969 participants (Genomics Release 4) and says MVP 'enrolled its one-millionth Veteran in 2023'.

label: Chinese Imaging Genetics study
counts: participants recruited to date (more than 7000)
quote: To date, we have recruited more than 7000 participants, becoming the largest and most integrative Chinese neuroimaging genetics cohort.
note: A lower bound from the design paper (PMID:31827248), which aimed to recruit 10,000 participants in 30 research centres; its cohort description is based on 5819 participants who had passed quality assessment, of whom 4885 had been genotyped. The recruitment was ongoing, so the final size may be larger.

label: African American Study of Kidney Disease and Hypertension
counts: African American adults randomized in the AASK Trial
quote: Of 1,094 persons enrolled in the AASK Trial (June 1995 to September 2001; mean age, 55 years; 61% men), 691 enrolled in the AASK Cohort Study (April 2002 to present), 299 died or reached dialysis therapy or transplantation, and 104 declined to participate in the AASK Cohort Study.
note: The trial paper (PMID:12819322) also says 1094 patients were randomized between June 1995 and September 1998 at 21 clinical centers. Of these, 691 went on to the AASK Cohort Study; the term covers trial and cohort phases, so the trial's randomized total is given.

label: Amsterdam Dementia Cohort
counts: memory-clinic patients in the cohort (almost 7000)
quote: This patients population comprises the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort, which currently consists of almost 7000 individuals.
note: Approximate figure from the Alzheimer Center Amsterdam website; the same page gives the cohort's distribution 'per January 1st 2019', which is taken as the year. The cohort profile (PMID:29562540) says 'all patients forming the Amsterdam Dementia Cohort number almost 6,000 individuals', with pie charts based on 5,960 patients in September 2017, and a biobank with material from over 4,000 individuals. The example study (PMID:40021830) used 487 ADC samples.

label: Protein Aggregation and Neurotransmitter Deficits Study
note: No source read states the size of the PAND study. The Campbell Research Lab study page gives no numbers, and the example study (PMID:42054495) was available only as its abstract. A PD-subtype replication paper (PMID:38838453, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11590651/) analysed a subset: 'The replication sample included 87 PAND participants and 13 PIB participants (total N =100)', PD participants with baseline visits 2016-2020 only. The example study's supplement or a PAND design description would settle it.

label: Protein and Imaging Biomarkers of Parkinson Disease Study
note: No source read states the size of the PIB study. The Campbell Research Lab study page gives no numbers, and the example study (PMID:42054495) was available only as its abstract. A PD-subtype replication paper (PMID:38838453, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11590651/) says 'The original subtyping analysis [17] included 162 PD participants from the PIB study who completed baseline evaluations between the years 2006 and 2015' plus 13 more PIB participants in its replication sample; these are analysed PD subsets without the healthy controls. The example study's supplement or a PIB design description would settle it.

label: BioBank Japan
counts: patients (collaborators) with 51 diseases in the first and second cohorts

note: The quote is one span of the cached page text, in which the phase heading runs into the sentence ('dataWe'); the sentence itself begins 'We promoted utilization'. Same page: first cohort of 200,000 patients (300,000 cases) with 47 diseases, second cohort of 67,000 new collaborators (100,000 cases), and 'approximately 270,000 collaborating patients' from 2003 to 2017. The first-cohort profile (PMID:28189464) says 200,000 participants were registered, with baseline data for 199,982.

note: From a later AGES-Reykjavik paper (PMID:37641038), not the design paper; another (PMC13021594) says 'By 2006, 5,764 surviving members were re-examined'. note: No source read states how many participants the Stanford ADRC cohort has. The ADRC home page, its Clinical Core page and its Summer 2026 newsletter give no count. An NACC data summary or a Stanford ADRC cohort description would settle it.

label: PopGen Biobank
counts: no whole-biobank count found (patients plus population controls)
note: The design paper (PMID:16490960, Community Genet 2006) is closed; its abstract gives no numbers and the publisher page did not load. The PopGen website (https://www.popgen.de/, the Kiel Institute of Epidemiology page) lists disease collections but no counts. Only the population control cohort is counted anywhere read: the abstract of PMID:22736164 (closed) says "Between 2005 and 2007, 1,317 study participants (age: 19-77 years, 55% men) were recruited into the PopGen control cohort, 747 via the local population registry and 570 as blood donors." The example study (PMID:35348614) used 1081 PopGen controls. A PopGen overview giving total patients and controls recruited would settle it.

label: Diabetic Nephropathy Cohort
counts: outpatients with type 2 diabetes recruited 2004-2015
quote: DN cohort recruited 2080 outpatient participants with T2D from the diabetes centre (Chinese N = 1309, Malay = 411, Asian Indian = 360) in a regional hospital between March 2004 and December 2015 with the primary aim to study the development and progression of DN and the secondary aim to study the major cardiovascular diseases (CVD) in T2D patients.
note: From the definition source (2019), which describes the cohort but is not its own profile paper. The example study (PMID:39621102, 2024) includes 'the Diabetic Nephropathy (DN) cohort (n=4069)' and says 4069 DN samples were genotyped, which suggests the cohort has grown since; its own profile paper (the 2024 paper's reference 26) was not read.

label: Singapore Study of Macro-Angiopathy and Micro-Vascular Reactivity in Type 2 Diabetes
counts: patients with type 2 diabetes recruited at baseline (2011-2014)
quote: A total of 2258 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) were recruited at baseline.
note: The same paper says 'Of the 2258 patients recruited at baseline, 1660 were followed up in the second wave and 842 remained in the third wave.' An earlier paper (PMID:31146758) gives 2057 outpatients recruited August 2011 to March 2014; the example study (PMID:39621102) includes SMART2D with n=2279.

label: Women's Health Initiative
counts: postmenopausal women enrolled in the clinical trials and observational study, 1993-1998
quote: 161,808 postmenopausal women enrolled in the WHI.
note: From the WHI website timeline, under '1998: Recruitment is completed'; the same page says 'Over 68,000 women were randomized to 1, 2 , or 3 clinical trials' and 'Over 93,000women enrolled in the Observation Study (OS).' PMID:31339542 gives the components as RCT n = 68 132 and OS n = 93 676. The design paper (PMID:9492970) gives planned sizes of about 64,500 (CT) and 100,000 (OS).

label: Study of Health in Pomerania-TREND
counts: individuals examined at baseline (SHIP-TREND-0, 2008-2012)
quote: In total, 8,727 individuals underwent baseline investigations in SHIP-START (n = 4308) and SHIP-TREND (n = 4420).
note: The same paper gives SHIP-TREND's response rate as 50.1%. The example study (PMID:37731490) used a sub-sample of 976 SHIP-TREND-0 participants. The SHIP cohort profile papers were not read.

label: Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study
counts: participants enrolled across the six KoGES cohorts since 2001 (a round figure)
quote: The Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) has undergone a strategic transformation towards ageing research with its 245 000 participants, now in their sixties and seventies, providing an invaluable long-term resource for studying healthy ageing and longevity.
note: 2026 cohort profile update. The same paper says 'Since 2001, >245 000 participants have been enrolled', and gives the three population-based studies' baseline total as N = 211 562 (Ansan and Ansung 10 030, HEXA 173 195, CAVAS 28 337); the three gene-environment model studies make up the rest.

label: Netherlands Epidemiology of Obesity Study
counts: individuals aged 45-65 included 2008-2012
quote: In total, 6,673 participants have been included, of whom 5,217 with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or higher.
note: Design paper (2013); its abstract says the study 'includes 6,673 individuals aged 45-65 years'. A 2024 paper (PMC11130664) gives the sample population as 6671 participants, presumably after withdrawals.

label: Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention
counts: people enrolled since late 2001 (as of the 2017 profile)
quote: Since late 2001, Wisconsin Registry for Alzheimer's Prevention has enrolled 1561 people at a mean baseline age of 54 years.
note: Cohort profile paper (2018). Enrolment is continuing: the WRAP website (https://wrap.wisc.edu/about/) now says 'The registry includes more than 1,700 individuals', a lower bound, not an exact count.

label: Wisconsin Alzheimer's Disease Research Center
counts: Clinical Core participants, April 2009 to March 2026
quote: 1151 Clinical Core participants
note: Read from the 'Wisconsin ADRC By the Numbers' infographic image on https://adrc.wisc.edu/annual-report, which summarises the centre's activity 'since the ADRC was formally established in April 2009 through March 31, 2026'; the same graphic gives 913 with MRI, 624 with lumbar punctures and 398 with PET. The definition source (PMID:33437055) and the example study (PMID:39528826) give only analysed subsets (e.g. 532 WADRC participants with CSF metabolomics). No published cohort profile was read.

label: Food Chain Plus
counts: adults recruited at baseline, 2011-2014
quote: During the first recruitment phase referred to as baseline in the following, data were collected between 2011 and 2014 from 1811 adults (18–83 years).
note: Cohort profile (PMID:36245062). The same paper says 'After internal data pre-processing 1795 of the 1811 subjects were eligible for further data analyses (8 withdrew consent to participate, 8 were excluded for data quality reasons)' and 'The final FoCus cohort includes 1795 participants with comprehensive data'; 1795 is the figure in the COHO definition. The first follow-up (to 2020) included 820 subjects.

label: Amish Complex Disease Research Program
counts: Amish adults who have taken part in one or more of the programme's studies (a lower bound, 'over 7000')
quote: To date, over 7000 Amish adults have participated in one or more of our studies as part of the Amish Complex Disease Research Program72.
note: From the definition source, which is also the example study (PMID:35393526, 2022); the trailing '72' is a reference number. The figure is stated as 'over 7000', a lower bound. The same paper says genomic DNA was extracted from 1856 Old Order Amish individuals for HAPI chip genotyping and that 650 were used for lipidomics. The programme's own overview paper (the paper's reference 72) was not read.

label: BioVU
counts: DNA samples banked (a lower bound, 'more than 300,000'), one per patient
quote: BioVU now accrues 500-1000 samples per week, totaling more than 300,000 DNA samples as of January 2023.
note: The website counts DNA samples, not people, and gives a lower bound. PMC7807864 (2021) used 94,474 BioVU individuals genotyped on the MEGAEX array, an analysed subset. The 2008 design paper (PMID:18500243) was not searched for early counts since the website is more recent.

label: Southall and Brent Revisited
counts: people of European, South Asian and African Caribbean origin aged 40-69 at baseline (1988-91)
quote: SABRE is a population-based cohort initiated in 4,857 people of European, South Asian and African Caribbean origin aged 40 to 69 living in West London, UK9 .
note: From the example study's supplementary note (PMID:40593539); '9' is a reference number. The cohort profile (PMID:21044979, read at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3304519/) gives only a table: 'Southall and Brent Combined studies 7942 4972 (63%)', i.e. 7942 invitations delivered and 4972 agreed, including 114 of other ethnicity; it also says 'we are nearly 2 years into the follow-up study and have approached 2925 of 4127 surviving participants.' The definition source (PMC10874717) used 985 participants at visit 3 (2014-2018).

label: Gut-and-Liver Axis in Alcoholic Liver Fibrosis
counts: patients with alcohol-related liver disease (GALA-ALD) and matched healthy controls (GALA-HC); no total stated
quote: We investigated BA homeostasis in a cross-sectional ALD cohort (n = 462), alongside matched healthy controls (n = 148), and validated key findings in two independent ALD cohorts (n = 34 and n = 52).
note: Not a classic case-control study but a patient cohort with a healthy comparison group; 'cases' are the GALA-ALD patients and 'controls' the healthy participants. The same paper says 'Odense University Hospital recruited participants between 2013 and 2018'. The definition source (PMID:35654907) profiled 'liver and plasma samples from 459 patients with ALD and 137 matched healthy controls' (GALA-HP n = 137); the example study (PMID:39972214) used GALA-ALD/HP with n = 558. No source read states the total number recruited.

label: Cardiovascular Risk in Young Finns Study
counts: children and adolescents aged 3-18 at baseline, 1980
quote: The baseline study was conducted in 1980 when 3596 randomly selected children and adolescents aged 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18 years participated.
note: From the definition source (2023), a paper using the cohort; its analysed sample was 2776 participants with childhood risk-factor data and adult preclinical CVD markers.

label: Study of Colorectal Cancer in Scotland
counts: cases and controls of one genotyped SOCCS sample (analysed subset); no total stated
quote: SOCCS SOCCS study7,8 comprised 2,057 colorectal cancer cases (CRC) (61% male; mean age at diagnosis (65.8 ± 8.4) years) and 2,111 population controls (60% males; mean age 67.9±9.0 years) as ascertained in Scotland.
note: The quote is from the example study's supplementary note (PMID:40593539); the leading 'SOCCS' is its subheading and '7,8' are reference numbers. It is one genotyped SOCCS phase, and another paper calls the same set 'Scotland2 was based on an additional 2,057 cases and 2,111 controls (SOCCS Study)'. Other SOCCS samples seen: 5,675 genotyped CRC cases in the definition source (PMID:31271446); 4772 cases and 2221 SOCCS population controls in a SOCCS/Generation Scotland GWAS; 1,145 cases and 2,203 controls (Scotland3). No source read states the total number of cases and controls SOCCS has recruited since 1999; the SOCCS design papers (reference 10 of PMID:31271446) would settle it.

label: China Kadoorie Biobank
counts: adults aged 30-79 enrolled 2004-2008
quote: Briefly, 512,726 adults aged 30–79 years were enrolled during 2004–2008 from ten urban and rural areas across China.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:37601966, 2023), whose abstract gives '>512,000 adults'. Over 100,000 participants were genotyped.

label: All of Us Research Program
counts: participants consented since 2018 (a lower bound, 'over 800,000')
quote: Since its inception in 2018, the AoU program has consented to over 800,000 participants, with more than 560,000 completing the initial enrollment process, including health questionnaires and biospecimen collection.
note: From a 2026 paper that used All of Us (Cell Metab 2026), not a program source; the figure is a lower bound, and 560,000 had completed full enrolment. The design paper (PMID:31412182) says 'As of July 2019, the All of Us program had enrolled more than 175,000 core participants and more than 230,000 total participants'. The program's own pages (nih.gov/allofus, researchallofus.org data snapshots) could not be read: nih.gov returned a bot challenge and the snapshot page is rendered by script. A web search summary reported over 883,000 enrolled as of June 2026, but that was not read in a page and is not used.

label: BioMe Biobank
counts: participants enrolled (approximate, 'approximately 60,000')
quote: The Mount Sinai BioMe Biobank, founded in 2007, is an ongoing electronic health record-linked biorepository that enrols participants non-selectively from the Mount Sinai Health System, comprising approximately 60,000 participants.
note: From the definition source (Diabetologia 2023), a paper using BioMe rather than a BioMe profile; the same paper used exome data of 18,797 BioMe individuals, and the example study (PMID:35278270) applied a score to 23,241 BioMe participants. Enrolment is ongoing, so the current number is likely larger; BioMe's own pages were not read.

label: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults Study
counts: participants aged 18-30 recruited at baseline, 1985-1986
quote: The CARDIA study began in 1985 with recruitment of 5,115 participants aged 18 to 30 years at field centers located in Birmingham, AL, Chicago, IL, Minneapolis, MN, and Oakland, CA.
note: From a definition source (PMID:32692748); other versions of the same text add the reference marker '[31]'. The same paper says '3,499 participants were examined in clinic at Y25, representing 72% of the original cohort.' PMID:36853610 analysed 4808 participants. The CARDIA design paper (Friedman et al. 1988) was not read.

label: Health for Life in Singapore
counts: Asian men and women aged 30-84 recruited 2018-2022
quote: We recruited 10,004 Asian men and women aged 30 to 84 years to the HELIOS Study between 2018 and 2022 (www.healthforlife.sg).
note: From the study's own description paper (also the example study). The planned size was '~10,000 participants from the general population'.

label: Cleveland Family Study
counts: individuals from 361 families recruited
quote: Overall, a total of 2284 individuals from 361 families were recruited from the Cleveland metropolitan area.
note: From the cohort description in a CARe candidate-gene study of OSA, not the CFS design paper; the same paper says DNA was available for a subset of 1665 individuals. The example study (PMID:34446064) used 505 African-American and 485 European-American CFS participants with WGS and 225/218 with imputed chip data (analysed subsets).

label: deCODE genetics Icelandic cohort
counts: Icelanders chip-genotyped by deCODE genetics
quote: We genotyped 173,025 Icelanders using Illumina SNP chips, and their genotypes were phased using long-range phasing (90).
note: deCODE has no single enrolment count; the chip-genotyped sample is the closest to the cohort's size. The same 2023 paper says 63,460 Icelanders were whole-genome sequenced and 14,144 took part in the speech recordings of the deCODE Health Study. The 2017 example study (PMID:28596592) says 151,677 Icelanders had been chip-genotyped and 15,220 whole-genome sequenced.

label: PainOMICS Retrospective Study
counts: participants enrolled Sep 2014-Feb 2016 (the source says patients)
quote: In the period between September 2014 and February 2016, 3,400 patients were enrolled.
note: Quote from Supplementary Information (MOESM1 PDF, cohort description) of the example study PMID:40593539, whose main text says PainOmics contributed N = 1873 to the glycome GWAS. PMID:37293449 says 'The sample of 3400 participants including the residents of Italy, Belgium, England, and Croatia was composed in the years from 2014 to 2016.' The protocol paper (PMID:27798002) planned 12,000 individuals (4000 cases and 8000 controls). No source read splits the 3,400 into cases and controls; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02037789 API record gives no enrollment figure.

label: The Pomak cohort
counts: adult volunteers recruited 2010-2013
quote: We contacted the local Health Centre in Echinos and, with the cooperation of the local doctors and nurses, a total of 1702 volunteers were recruited between July 2010 and March 2013.
note: The first descriptive report of the HELIC-Pomak cohort. Later papers: 1642 Pomak samples were whole-genome sequenced (PMID:34857772); the example study (PMID:36349687) analysed 1537 Pomak participants with WGS. PMID:25373335 genotyped 2,296 samples across Pomak and MANOLIS together.

label: Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging
counts: RPGEH participants forming the GERA cohort (genotyped)
quote: The cohort included 110,266 subjects to ensure that at least 100,000 individuals were successfully genotyped by the end of the project.
note: Genotyping design paper (PMID:26092718), PDF text. Same paper: the GERA cohort of 110,266 participants was formed from RPGEH participants enrolled through February 2011; its abstract says genotyping of >100,000 subjects. The example study (PMID:35449187) analysed 63,110 non-Hispanic white GERA participants; PMID:33778338 analysed 84,996.

label: Correlated Expression and Disease Association Research
counts: healthy Europeans with blood and intestinal biopsies
quote: We collected peripheral blood as well as intestinal biopsies (ileum, transverse colon, rectum) from 323 healthy Europeans visiting the Academic Hospital of the University of Liège as part of a national screening campaign for colon cancer.
note: CEDAR design paper (Methods). Its introduction speaks of '350 healthy individuals'. The example study (PMID:40593539) used CEDAR N = 170 for the plasma glycome, and N = 187 for prediction testing.

label: Generation Scotland: Scottish Family Health Study
counts: adult participants recruited 2006-2011
quote: A total of 24 084 adult participants, including 5501 families, were recruited between 2006 and 2011.
note: 2024 cohort profile (BMJ Open), abstract. Same paper: the cohort contained 1361 singletons and 5501 families. PMID:29040551 describes the STRADL follow-up subset (7158 individuals in 2460 families plus 2460 unrelated individuals).

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Arteriopathy
counts: no overall total stated; per-site Phase I counts only
quote: These include non-Hispanic White Americans from Rochester, MN (n =1583 at the 1st exam) and African Americans from Jackson, MS (N=1854 at the 1st exam).
note: No source read states a whole-GENOA total. The dbGaP study description gives per-site Phase I counts (Rochester non-Hispanic whites n=1583; Jackson African Americans N=1854; Phase II 1,241 and 1,482) and says the Starr County Hispanic cohort was ascertained through diabetic sibships (N=1812). PMID:15121494 counts only hypertensive sibs enrolled 1997-1999 (1329 non-Hispanic blacks, 1133 non-Hispanic whites, 752 Hispanic whites). A design paper or dbGaP page giving one total would settle it; per-site numbers were not summed.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohorts
counts: 2 member birth cohorts (NFBC1966, NFBC1986); no pooled total stated
quote: We used data from two general population birth cohort studies, Northern Finland Birth Cohorts 1966 and 1986 (NFBC1966 and NFBC1986).
note: Cohort aggregation of 2 member cohorts. The definition source PMID:39820013 gives member sizes only: NFBC1966 'consisting of 12,055 mothers and 12,058 live born offsprings'; NFBC1986 'This corresponded to 9362 mothers and 9432 live births.' The University of Oulu page states no number. These were not summed. The example study (PMID:34847907) used NFBC1966 (1838 participants) with Health 2000.

label: Taiwan Biobank
counts: volunteers who had joined the biobank
quote: As of August 2021, a total of 151,406 volunteers have joined the biobank, among which 37,508 have completed the first round of follow-up.
note: 2023 resource paper (Cell Genomics). Its abstract says >150,000 individuals; enrolment was to continue to a target of 200,000 volunteers. The release analysed had 108,955 individuals with genome-wide genotypes.

label: GeneRISK study
counts: individuals collected into the prospective cohort
quote: We collected a prospective cohort of 7342 individuals (64% women, mean age 56 years) and estimated their 10-year risk for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease both by a traditional risk score and a composite score combining the effect of a polygenic risk score and clinical risk factors.
note: From the abstract of the GeneRISK study's own risk-communication paper (only the abstract was read; its full text is not on disk). The example study (PMID:37907536, PMC10618167) says 'The cohort includes 7292 participants (4642 women, 2624 men), who were recruited from Southern Finland during 2015–2017 at age of 45–66 years.', ran lipidomics on 7302 and analysed 7174. The two cohort totals differ (7342 vs 7292).

label: Healthy Aging in Neighborhoods of Diversity across the Life Span
counts: participants accrued at baseline 2004-2009
quote: We accrued 3,722 participants (Table 1): 2,200 African Americans (59%) and 1,522 whites (41%), 1,536 (41%) with household incomes below 125% of the poverty level and 2,186 (59%) above the poverty level.
note: HANDLS design paper (PMID:20828101); the abstract says 'We recruited 3722 participants from Baltimore'. The HANDLS website design page says 'a fixed cohort of 3,720 community-dwelling African American and white adults aged 30-64.' Medical examination accrual was N = 2802.

label: Mount Sinai Crohn's and Colitis Registry
counts: approximately 1500 IBD patients and controls recruited Dec 2013-Sep 2016
quote: The Mount Sinai Crohn’s and Colitis registry (MSCCR is a prospective cross-sectional cohort consisting of ~1500 IBD patients and controls recruited during their endoscopy visit from December 2013–September 2016.
note: An approximate figure from a paper that used MSCCR, not a design paper; the quote keeps the source's missing parenthesis. PMC10014487 calls MSCCR 'a discovery cohort with ~ 1200 IBD patients and controls'. The example study (PMID:34780722) recruited 484 UC, 464 CD and 365 controls for serum metabolomics; PMC8263768 immunophenotyped 728 CD, 464 UC and 334 controls. Those are analysed subsets and were not summed. PMID:32980345 and PMID:35190725, which describe the cohort, were not read.

label: Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety
counts: participants recruited: 2329 with depressive/anxiety disorder, 367 siblings, 652 healthy controls
quote: The NESDA sample recruited initially 2329 persons with a remitted or current DSM-IV based depressive (major depressive disorder, dysthymia) and/or anxiety disorder (panic disorder, social phobia, agoraphobia, generalized anxiety disorder), 367 of their siblings and 652 healthy controls, yielding a total of 3348 participants.
note: 2021 cohort profile (abstract). The 367 siblings are neither cases nor controls. The 2008 design paper (PMID:18763692) describes the baseline cohort of 2981 participants (1701 current diagnosis, 907 lifetime/at risk, 373 healthy controls, a different split); the NESDA website says 'Current NESDA cohort: 3348 subjects (2981 + 367 sibs, 67% female, 33% male).'

label: Health, Aging and Body Composition Study
counts: men and women aged 70-79 at baseline
quote: The study cohort included 3,075 men and women, aged 70-79 at baseline; 45 percent of the women and 33 percent of the men are African American.
note: Study website. PMID:32396194 agrees: the study enrolled 3075 well-functioning community-dwelling older adults aged 70 to 79 years between March 1997 and July 1998.

label: Michigan Genomics Initiative
counts: Michigan Medicine patients consented to MGI
quote: As of April 30, 2022, 91,695 patients receiving care at the Michigan Medicine health system have consented to participate in the MGI.
note: MGI resource paper (Cell Genomics 2023). Its abstract says >91,000 participants; the Freeze 3 genotyped cohort described there is ~57,000 samples, GWAS in ~51,000 European-inferred samples.

label: Immune and Metabolic Markers during Pregnancy and Child Development Study
counts: children (with their mothers) in the case-control sample: ASD 311, DD 1291, general-population controls 967
quote: Table 1Characteristics of the IMPaCT Case-Control Study Sample, Kaiser Permanente Northern CaliforniaCharacteristicAll, N = 2569ASD, n = 311DD, n = 1291GP, n = 967
note: The total comes from the caption and header row of Table 1 of the definition source (PMC10689278). Its abstract gives the groups separately: 'risk of ASD (n = 311) and DDs (n = 1291) compared with children from the general population (n = 967)'. Cases come in two groups (ASD 311, DD 1291), so no single case count is stated. The example study (PMID:42378311, PMC13340790) says 'The IMPaCT cohort included 2436 mothers across three child outcome groups (ASD N = 339, DD N = 1193, GP N = 904)'.

label: Cohorts for Heart and Aging Research in Genomic Epidemiology Consortium
counts: individuals with genome-wide data across the 5 founding cohorts (approximate)
quote: With genome-wide data on a total of about 38 000 individuals, these cohort studies have a large number of health-related phenotypes measured in similar ways.
note: Cohort aggregation: the CHARGE design paper (abstract) gives an approximate pooled count for its 5 founding cohorts (AGES-Reykjavik, ARIC, CHS, FHS, Rotterdam). CHARGE has since grown well beyond these, and later meta-analyses have their own sample sizes. The number is recorded as stated ('about 38 000').

label: Helsinki Birth Cohort Study
counts: singletons born in two Helsinki maternity hospitals 1934-1944
quote: Our study sample is a part of the Helsinki Birth Cohort Study (HBCS), comprising all 13345 individuals (52.3% male) born singleton in one of the two maternity hospitals in Helsinki, Finland, between 1934 and 1944.
note: From a definition source that used the HBCS, not a cohort profile. PMID:27699078 says 'The original Helsinki Birth Cohort Study includes 8760 women and men born between 1934 and 1944 at the Helsinki University Hospital', a different framing (one hospital); it studied 1082 subjects. PMC6416302 analysed 1872 participants.

label: Generation R Study
counts: mothers enrolled (delivery dates Apr 2002-Jan 2006)
quote: In total, 9778 mothers with a delivery date from April 2002 until January 2006 were enrolled in the study.
note: 2016 cohort design update (Eur J Epidemiol). Same paper: 'The 9778 mothers enrolled in the study gave birth to 9749 live born children.'; 91% (n = 8879) enrolled during pregnancy. The number counts mothers; the children are a second count.

label: 500 Functional Genomics
counts: healthy volunteers in the cohort
quote: The 500FG cohort consists of 534 healthy individuals of Caucasian origin and is part of the Human Functional Genomics Project (HFGP).
note: The project website (https://humanfunctionalgenomics.org/projects/500fg/) also says "The cohort consists of 534 healthy individuals", recruited 08/2013 to 12/2014. The profile paper says 45 were excluded from its analysis, leaving 489.

label: MyCode Community Health Initiative
counts: patients enrolled by end of September 2015 (stated as more than 90,000; lower bound)
quote: By the end of September, 2015 more than 90,000 Geisinger patients had enrolled, including more than 3,600 pediatric patients enrolled through parental or guardian consent.
note: Profile paper (Carey et al. 2016); enrolment was ongoing at ~4,000 per month, with a stated goal of more than 500,000, so the current size is much larger. The example study (PMID:36192519) analysed 27,529 European-ancestry MyCode participants recruited 2007-2019. The Geisinger MyCode web page (https://www.geisinger.org/mycode) was behind a bot wall; a recent MyCode/DiscovEHR paper or that page would give the current enrolment.

label: 23andMe research cohort
counts: research-consented genotyped 23andMe participants screened in a 2024 carrier study
quote: Results Demographics Out of 7,194,265 consented participants, 116,517 (1.6%) were heterozygous for pathogenic variants in genes associated with ACOG-AJ conditions (commonly referred to as “carriers” in the context of reproductive risk) ( Table 1 ).
note: 23andMe has no design paper; this 2024 23andMe carrier-screening study (PMC11613755, abstract: "Out of 7.2 million research participants") gives the research-consented pool it drew on; the data freeze date is not stated. A 2021 23andMe Parkinson's MR study (PMC8609708) used "over 2.4 million participants". The definition source and example study (PMID:34728798) analysed 132,113 European-ancestry participants (27,805 cases, 104,308 controls of problematic opioid use), a subset. The 23andMe research web pages give no count.

label: LIFE-Adult-Study
counts: randomly selected adults examined at baseline, 2011-2014
quote: The LIFE-Adult-Study is a population-based cohort study, which has recently completed the baseline examination of 10,000 randomly selected participants from Leipzig, a major city with 550,000 inhabitants in the east of Germany.
note: Design paper (Loeffler et al. 2015); baseline ran August 2011 to November 2014 and 10,000 was also the planned target; the paper gives the round figure only. It mentions a first SNP genotyping wave of 4500 participants and an additional subset of 400 participants aged 18-39. The example study (PMID:34822396) analysed LIFE-Adult subsets.

label: Red Blood Cell-Omics Study
counts: blood donors enrolled December 2013 to October 2015
quote: A total of 13,403 racially/ethnically diverse (12% African American, 12% Asian, 8% Hispanic, 64% white, and 5% multiracial/other) donors of both sexes were enrolled and ranged from 18 to 90 years of age; 15% were high-intensity donors (nine or more donations in the prior 24 mo without low hemoglobin deferral).
note: Design paper (Kanias et al. 2019). By centre: 3355 BCW, 3292 ARC, 3192 ITxM, 3564 BCP; 664 donors were recruited into the recall study; GWAS array data for 13,125 donors.

label: Corogene Study
counts: consecutive Finnish patients undergoing coronary angiography, June 2006 to March 2008
quote: For the COROGENE cohort, initially, all consecutive Finnish patients undergoing coronary angiogram between June, 2006, and March, 2008 (n=5330), in the Helsinki University Central Hospital were included and a questionnaire, information about previous medical conditions and cardiovascular risk factors, hospital records for patients' history, laboratory measurements, electrocardiogram, echocardiogram, and medication were obtained.
note: From a multi-cohort genetic risk score paper (Ripatti et al. 2010), not a dedicated Corogene profile. The same paper says 2101 cases and 3914 controls (1453 unique, the rest from FINRISK) formed the genotyped COROGENE case-control sample (Table 1: n=6015). PMID:27125947 used a nested case-control set of 80+80; the example study (PMID:27005778) analysed 828 COROGENE individuals.

label: Health 2000 GenMets Study
counts: Health 2000 participants collected as metabolic syndrome cases and matched controls
quote: The Genmets sample is subset of 2,212 individuals of the Health2000 study ( http://www.terveys2000.fi/doc/methodologyrep.pdf ) collected as metabolic syndrome cases and their matched controls.
note: From an early GenMets user paper (Perttila et al. 2009, PMC2707950), not a dedicated profile; the same paper analysed N = 2,138. Other counts: 2,173 individuals genotyped on the Illumina 610K (PMID:24969107, a definition source); a 2010 paper (PMID:20532202) describes a case/control study of about 2,000 and analysed 919 with metabolic syndrome and 932 without; PMID:24969107 table lists 979 cases and 1,031 controls; the example study (PMID:27005778) analysed 572. No source split the full 2,212 into cases and controls.

label: Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes
counts: participants with and without type 2 diabetes enrolled February-June 2012
quote: This study was embedded in the Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes (QMDiab), a cross-sectional case–control study with 374 participants [13, 20].
note: The example study's supplement (PMID:40593539) says the same: "The Qatar Metabolomics Study on Diabetes (QMDiab) is a cross-sectional case–control study with 374 participants." PMID:26049400 analysed 369 of them (Table 1: type 2 diabetes n = 188, controls n = 181); no source split all 374 into cases and controls. The example study used 325.

label: Genetic Study of Atherosclerosis Risk
counts: family members in the GeneSTAR aspirin trial, 2003-2006
quote: Of the 3003 participants in the aspirin trial, 1786 were selected for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in the Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Program based on 1) complete platelet function phenotyping and 2) largest family size.
note: From a platelet-reactivity WGS paper (PMC8206369), not a GeneSTAR profile; the same paper says participants came from 891 European- and African-American families. This counts the aspirin-trial phase only; the whole study since 1983 may be larger. PMID:24178997 (PMC3931379) says 1,478 participants were enrolled in 1993-2005 under age 60 without CAD. The definition source and example study (PMID:35312098) analysed 806 EAs in 196 families and 661 AAs in 190 families from TOPMed Freeze 6. A GeneSTAR design paper or its dbGaP record would settle the whole cohort's size.

label: Nurses' Health Study
counts: married female registered nurses enrolled in 1976
quote: We have summarized the evolution of the Nurses' Health Study (NHS), a prospective cohort study of 121 700 married registered nurses launched in 1976; NHS II, which began in 1989 and enrolled 116 430 nurses; and NHS3, which began in 2010 and has ongoing enrollment.
note: From the NHS history paper (Bao et al. 2016, abstract). PMC10173489 (a definition source) agrees: "The NHS I began in 1976 when 121,700 female registered nurses, aged 30–55 years, were enrolled by completing a baseline questionnaire". NHS II (116,430) and NHS3 are separate cohorts and not counted here.

label: Penn Medicine BioBank
counts: participants enrolled as of September 2022 (stated as over 174,000; lower bound)
quote: As of September 2022, the PMBB had enrolled over 174,000 participants, obtained biospecimens on >70,000 participants, and generated genomic data on ~44,000 of its participants.
note: PMBB profile paper (Verma et al. 2022). It also says 13,366 patients were enrolled in the initial 2008-2013 phase. The example study (PMID:37255673, 2023) says the PMBB "has so far recruited more than 175,000 patients with electronic consent".

label: Epidemiological Investigation of Rheumatoid Arthritis
counts: incident RA cases and population controls recruited 1995-2016; no total stated
quote: This case–control study involved 3515 incident RA cases and 5429 controls recruited to the EIRA study between 1995 and 2016, within 1 year since RA symptom onset.
note: From an EIRA allergy analysis (PMC8852704, 2022), not a profile; it may be the questionnaire-responding set rather than every enrolled person. The example study (PMID:37326842, 2023) says "EIRA, a case–control study established in 1996, currently contains >5000 incident RA cases" (no control count). A 2025 HLA paper (PMC11694251) studied 4,392 incident EIRA patients; the first phase (PMID:12922955) had 679 cases and 847 controls included May 1996-June 2000. No source gives a whole-study total.

label: Ludwigshafen Risk and Cardiovascular Health Study
counts: patients enrolled July 1997 to March 2002 (whole cohort)
quote: Zwischen Juli 1997 und März 2002 wurden 3.808 Personen aus dem Großraum Ludwigshafen · Mannheim · Heidelberg eingeschlossen.
note: Study website (German: "Between July 1997 and March 2002, 3,808 persons from the Ludwigshafen, Mannheim, Heidelberg area were enrolled"). The site's table gives the whole cohort as 3,808 (2,660 men, 1,148 women) and a subcohort of 3,316 recruited 07.1997-01.2000. The LURIC design paper (Winkelmann et al. 2001) describes the 3,316 recruited to January 2000, as does PMID:39003598 ("A total of 3316 patients ... were recruited between July 1997 and January 2000"); most analyses use the 3,316.

label: Diabetes Heart Study
counts: European American and African American participants from 564 families
quote: The Diabetes Heart Study (DHS) is a genetic and epidemiological study of 1443 European American and African American participants from 564 families with multiple cases of type 2 diabetes.
note: DHS review (Bowden et al. 2010, abstract); the body says "235 of the original 1442 participants are now deceased" (a one-person discrepancy), and PMID:23230101 says "Among 1,443 participants in the DHS cohort". The separate African American-DHS (AA-DHS) is not counted; PMID:29221444 analysed 691 AA-DHS individuals.

label: Genetics of Personality Consortium
counts: participants from 29 cohorts in the 2015 neuroticism GWAS meta-analysis
quote: Here we report results of the largest GWA study for neuroticism so far, conducted in 63,661 participants from 29 cohorts.
note: Cohort aggregation: the pooled count for its flagship analysis (de Moor et al. 2015, JAMA Psychiatry). The paper also refers to 30 cohorts when a further cohort is added, and to a previous meta-analysis of 17,375 subjects. The example study (PMID:27089181) reuses the GPC neuroticism results (n = 63,661).

label: Genetic Risk Assessment for Chinese Eaglet-T1D
counts: type 1 diabetes cases and controls from paediatric centres used for PRS validation
quote: Specifically, in the multi-ancestry All of Us Biobank (AoU, N=89,699; Ncases=1084; Ncontrols=88,635), in a case–control multi-ancestry cohort from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, Center for Applied Genomics (CHOP-CAG, N=6498; Ncases=1094; Ncontrols=5404), in the UK Biobank (UKB, N=427,847; Ncases=778; Ncontrols=427,069) and in a Chinese case–control cohort across multiple paediatric centres named Genetic Risk Assessment for Chinese Eaglet-T1D (GRACE, N=597; Ncases=294; Ncontrols=303).
note: The only source found is the PRS validation paper that is both the definition source and the example study (PMC13109230); its supplement also gives GRACE, N = 597. GRACE has no design paper found, so this may be the analysed subset rather than the whole collection.

label: Academic Medical Center Amsterdam Premature Atherosclerosis Study
counts: AMC-PAS patients genotyped on one or more platforms (analysed subset)
quote: We included a total of 979 unique patients from the previously described prospective cohort AMC-PAS[6], with symptomatic Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) before the age of 51 years, defined as Myocardial Infarction (MI), coronary revascularization, or evidence of at least 70% stenosis in a major epicardial artery.
note: The definition source and example study (van Iperen et al. 2017) counts only the genotyped patients (706 MetaboChip, 757 CVD BeadChip, 955 HumanExome; 397 on all three). It cites Trip et al. 2002 (PMID:12176944, Circulation) as the cohort description; that abstract reports a case-control study of 441 patients under 50 with definite CAD and 1057 population controls but does not name AMC-PAS, and the full text could not be read (ahajournals returned a bot page). A statin-response paper (PMC5558527) used 184 AMC-PAS patients. The whole cohort's enrolment is not stated in anything read.

label: Bogalusa Heart Study
counts: different children recruited in 9 childhood surveys, 1973-2016 (3780 re-examined as adults)
quote: The total number of different individuals recruited in these surveys was 8385 children and 3780 adults.
note: From a Bogalusa life-course lipid paper (PMC9535509, 2022), which says 9 surveys of children aged 4-19 and 12 of adults aged 20-58 "who were previously examined as children" were run between 1973 and 2016, and that "These adults participated at least once in the children surveys", so the 3780 adults are within the 8385; survey sizes ranged 1084-4222 (children) and 238-1930 (adults). The definition source (PMID:11876192) abstract gives no count, and its full text was not available (publisher redirect); the example study (PMID:34187551) does not name the cohort in its text. The Tulane study pages fetched gave no count.

label: Cleveland Family Speech and Reading Study
counts: families enrolled, each with a proband with SSD; no individual total stated
quote: Families (N = 296) with a child with an SSD were enrolled in the study.
note: The 2025 CFSRS review (PMC12614917) states enrolment in families only. Its Table 1 lists 296 families, 296 probands and 543 siblings (194 with SSD, 335 without, 14 unknown), but no total of individuals, so participants is left null rather than summed. Families (N = 272) provided DNA; GWAS used 435 individuals from 148 families (also the example study, PMID:34315907) and WGS 101.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Consortium
counts: no pooled GENOA total; European-ancestry samples given separately by opioid addiction definition
quote: Among the 10 independent EA cohorts contributing to GENOA, OA was defined by Diagnostic and Statistical Manual criteria for opioid abuse or dependence (DSM-based; N = 17,061) or by frequency of use (FOU) of illicit opioids (e.g., injecting heroin 10 or more times in the past 30 days; FOU-based; N = 11,976; Supplementary Table 1).
note: Cohort aggregation. The flagship paper (Gaddis et al. 2022, PMC9546890) gives GENOA's European-ancestry data only as two phenotype-specific sample sizes (DSM-based 17,061; FOU-based 11,976), which are not summed here; no African-ancestry total was found in the text. Its main gSEM GWAS used "a total sample size of 403,915 (23,367 cases and 384,619 controls; effective sample size of 88,114)", but that pools GENOA with published MVP, PGC-SUD and Partners Health summary statistics, so it is not GENOA's own count. The supplement (MOESM1) lists per-cohort meta-analysis sizes, e.g. Yale-Penn-CIDR 1,014, Yale-Penn-GO 895, VIDUS 2,175, UHS1 9,245, deCODE 275,468, COGA 7,631.

label: Genetics of Opioid Addiction Study
counts: participants recruited in the main GENOA phase (2013-2016)
quote: Briefly, participants (nGENOA = 1536, nPOST = 3319) were recruited from 76 CATC sites across Ontario, Canada (GENOA, 2013–2016, POST, 2018–present).
note: From the example study (PMID:38102185), not a profile paper. The count covers the 2013-2016 main phase only; the pilot paper (PMID:25187714) reports 'Our sample included 252 subjects (150 men and 102 women)' for the 2011-2012 pilot at four clinics. PMID:37494403 gives genotyped counts only (nGENOA PILOT = 182, nGENOA = 1314). No source read states a combined pilot-plus-main total. The pilot paper's planned size (3,465 over three years; 2,000 minimum) was not reached.

label: deCODE Health Study
counts: analysed subset: participants with speech samples
quote: Speech samples were obtained from 14,144 Icelandic participants as a part of the deCODE Health Study in Iceland, which involves comprehensive phenotyping of a general population sample.
note: No source read states the total enrolment of the deCODE Health Study; every number is a phenotyped subset. Others seen: audiometry for 11,484 Icelanders (4140 cases, 7344 controls; PMID:34108613); 3098 SARS-CoV-2-positive adults invited to a modified deCODE Health Study (PMID:37414856). Web figures of 160,000-200,000 participants refer to deCODE's research programme as a whole, not this study. A deCODE description of the Health Study's recruitment total would settle it.

label: Qatar Biobank
counts: participants enrolled by the 2019 design paper
quote: Currently, QBB has reached 28% (n = 17,065) of the targeted enrollee population and more than 2 million biological samples.
note: Quote from the abstract of the QBB design-and-first-results paper (Am J Epidemiol 2019), read via Europe PMC; the full text is not open and was not read. The target is 60,000 participants. The background-and-methods paper (PMID:26635005) reports 1209 pilot participants recruited December 2012 to February 2014; the example study (PMID:33430342) analysed 3000 whole-genome-sequenced participants. The QBB website returned no text. Enrolment has continued since 2019, so a more recent QBB figure would supersede this.

label: Reykjavik Study
counts: participants examined at entry (1967-1991)
quote: At the start of the study, there were 18 903 participants, of whom 68 (0.36%) were lost to follow-up for cause specific mortality and 110 (0.58%) had missing data on blood pressure, cholesterol concentration, or body mass index (BMI) and were omitted.
note: From a migraine-mortality analysis of the Reykjavik Study (PMID:20736269), which analysed 18 725 of these participants (9044 men, 9681 women). The AGES-Reykjavik design paper (PMID:17351290) says the Reykjavik Study 'originally was comprised of a random sample of 30,795 men and women born in 1907–1935 and living in Reykjavik in 1967', which is the sample invited, not those examined. The example study (PMID:19438929) used a nested case-control set of 5906 subjects. No Reykjavik Study profile paper was read.

label: Human Functional Genomics Project
counts: aggregation; only member-cohort counts reported
quote: 500FG The cohort consists of 534 healthy individuals, of whom 44% are male and 56% are female, all of Western-European genetic background.
note: The HFGP projects page reports sizes only for its member cohorts, not a pooled total: 500FG 534, 200FG 197, 2000HIV 1895, BCG-PRIME 6112, 300BCG 325, INFLUENZA-SHINGRIX 147, 300OB 302, 300DM 243 (the page lists these eight projects). The quote is the flagship 500FG cohort's size. No source read states the number of participants or member studies of the programme as a whole.

label: Recipient Epidemiology and Donor Evaluation Study-III
counts: aggregation; more than 25 focused research protocols, no pooled participant count
quote: Secondly, there are more than 25 focused research protocols involving transfusion recipients, blood donors, or both that are either in progress or scheduled to begin within the next 3 years.
note: REDS-III is a research programme of linked donor-recipient databases and focused protocols; its design paper (PMID:24188564) gives no participant total, only the number of protocols (a lower bound, so not a count of member studies). The example study (PMID:36602125) reports one member study: 'Of the 2,793 SCD individuals enrolled in the REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort, 1,460 were excluded, with a final set of 1,333 individuals'.

label: Research Program on Genes, Environment and Health
counts: participants with broad consent and a saliva or blood sample (approximate)
quote: The RPGEH cohort includes about 400,000 survey participants of whom about 200,000 have provided broad consent and a sample of saliva or blood for use in studies of genetic and environmental factors in health and disease.
note: From the dbGaP description of GERA (phs000674.v3.p3), a substudy of the RPGEH. The same sentence gives about 400,000 survey participants, the wider group surveyed; 200,000 is chosen because the RPGEH resource is built from consenting members who gave biospecimens. The page also says that in late 2009 the RPGEH 'had established a cohort of about 140,000 individuals who had answered a detailed survey, provided saliva samples'. GERA itself has 110,266 participants (PMID:26092718). No RPGEH profile paper was read; a current Kaiser Permanente Research Bank figure may differ.

label: Africa America Diabetes Mellitus Study
counts: T2D cases and controls studied (analysed set of participants enrolled 2000-2016)
quote: We studied 5993 individuals ( Table 1 ) including 2784 T2D cases (39% men) who had a mean age of 56 (SD 11) years and median known duration of T2D of 5 (IQR 2–10) years.
note: From an AADM analysis of T2D complications (PMID:31832618), which says 'The AADM study, which enrolled participants between 2000 and 2016'; controls from the next sentence: 'Study participants also included 3209 controls (40% men)'. It is the set analysed there, not stated to be the whole enrolment. The first-phase design paper (PMID:11164120) reports 162 individuals from 78 families enrolled by then, with a goal of 400 sib-pairs and 200 controls; the example study (PMID:34620218) used 4432 continental Africans with cytokine measures; a PRS study used 2,148 cases and 2,161 controls. No profile paper giving the total enrolment was read.

label: Danish Blood Donor Study
counts: participants included by February 2022
quote: As of February 2022, DBDS includes 138491 participants (51% women, age span at inclusion 18–70 years) who have completed a total of 371589 questionnaires and with 1091499 person-years of follow-up.
note: From the DBDS cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2023, PMID:36194120); the Europe PMC XML of the same paper prints the numbers with thin spaces ('138 491'). The example study (PMID:38228779) analysed 33,882 donors and says genotype data are available for around 114,000 participants of the DBDS Genomic Cohort. The cohort is ongoing, so later counts will be higher.

label: Howard University Family Study
counts: analysed subset: genotyped participants (pedigree members and unrelated)
quote: Methods We analyzed 1,976 African Americans from Washington, D.C, including 1,322 individuals from 328 pedigrees and 654 unrelated individuals, enrolled in the Howard University Family Study.
note: No source read states HUFS's total enrolment. The largest HUFS sample read is this uric acid GWAS (PMID:26686224); the example study (PMID:34620218) used HUFS n = 1958, and the 2009 hypertension GWAS (PMID:19609347) 1017 unrelated individuals. A 2011 paper (PMC3045279) gives the aim of enrolling 'a randomly ascertained sample of 350 African American families'. A HUFS design paper or dbGaP entry with the enrolment total would settle it.

label: Stabilization of Atherosclerotic Plaque by Initiation of Darapladib Therapy Trial
counts: patients randomised
quote: Darapladib is a selective oral inhibitor of lipoprotein-associated phospholipase A2.MethodsIn a double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 15,828 patients with stable coronary heart disease to receive either once-daily darapladib (at a dose of 160 mg) or placebo.
note: From the abstract of the main trial report (N Engl J Med 2014), read via Europe PMC; the abstract text runs the heading 'Methods' into the sentence, so the quote carries it; the clean span begins 'In a double-blind trial'. The biomarker paper (PMID:33439866) used a case-cohort subset of 605 CV-death cases and 2,788 non-cases.

label: Swedish BioFINDER Study
counts: participants enrolled 2009-2014 (stated as 'more than 1600', a lower bound)
quote: More than 1600 patients with mild cognitive symptoms, dementia and parkinsonian symptoms as well as cognitively healthy elderly was enrolled in the study with longitudnal follow-up up to 10 years.
note: From the BioFINDER-1 page of the study website, whose summary also gives 'Number of participants: >1600'; no BioFINDER-1 profile paper was read. The example/definition paper (PMID:36504281) analysed 1,591 participants with CSF proteomics and genotypes. BioFINDER-2 (NCT03174938), a separate study, lists 2960 participants on its page.

label: CROATIA-Vis Study
counts: adults recruited 2003-2004
quote: The CROATIA-Vis study includes 1,008 Croatians, aged 18–93 years, who were recruited from the villages of Vis and Komiza on the Dalmatian island of Vis during spring of 2003 and 2004.
note: From the cohort description in a proteome-by-phenome MR paper (PMID:32628676) that used CROATIA-Vis as its discovery cohort; the example study (PMID:37563310) gives no count for CROATIA-Vis. No original CROATIA-Vis design paper was read, but the number matches the definition.

label: National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center
counts: participants with data at NACC (stated as '56,000+', a lower bound)
quote: 56,000+ Participants with Data at NACC (20,000+ active participants)
note: Pooled participant count for the aggregation, from the NACC home page's data summary (same page: 37 active ADRCs across 25 states; 217,000 clinical assessments). This covers the Uniform Data Set era; NACC's 2025 history paper (PMID:41122833) says the earlier Minimum Data Set 'included ≈ 77,000 (cumulative) participants', a different, older data set, not added here.

label: Singapore Prospective Study Program
counts: participants who completed the questionnaire (2004-2007); 5157 also examined
quote: A total of 10 633 individuals were invited; 7742 subjects (response rate 74.1%) completed the health questionnaire, of which 5157 (66.6% of those who completed the questionnaire or 49.4% of all eligible subjects) also attended the health examination.
note: From an SP2 analysis of HbA1c by ethnicity (PMID:22283416); a 2020 SP2 paper (PMC7534670) agrees: 'There were 7742 participants who completed the questionnaire, of whom 5157 subsequently participated in the health examination.' If only examined participants count, the figure is 5157. A gene-diet paper (PMID:29477148) gives 'N = 11,053' for the four earlier source surveys combined, not SP2 participants. The original SP2 design paper was not read; the example study's supplementary file (PMC8562625) was not on disk.

label: Colorado Center for Personalized Medicine Biobank
counts: participants enrolled by March 2022
quote: As of March 2022, 200,673 participants have enrolled in the CCPM Biobank and 103,600 have provided a blood (n = 100,542) or saliva (n = 3,058) sample (Figure 1).
note: From the CCPM Biobank description paper (Am J Hum Genet 2024, PMID:38181729). The same paper gives 33,674 genotyped participants after QC and a demographics table of n = 196,559 (participants as of February 24, 2022). Recruitment is ongoing, so later counts will be higher.

label: Adult Changes in Thought Study
counts: cumulative enrolment to November 2022
quote: As of the most recent data freeze (25 November 2022), total cumulative enrollment in the ACT study was 5763 people with 49,422 person-years of follow-up (mean 8.6, SD = 6.1 years per person).
note: From ACT's medical-record abstraction paper (PMID:39595838). The same paper gives the waves: 2581 members enrolled 1994-1996, an expansion cohort of 811 in 2002-2003, then continuous enrolment from 2004; the active cohort was 1664 people at the freeze. Enrolment continues (goal of an active cohort of 3000 by April 2026).

label: Hypertension Genetic Epidemiology Network
counts: hypertensive siblings examined 1995-2000 (sibship component only; offspring and random samples not included)
quote: The projected sample size of 2244 hypertensive participants was surpassed, as 2407 hypertensive individuals (1262 African-Americans and 1145 whites) from 917 sibships were examined.
note: From the abstract of the HyperGEN methodology and recruitment paper (Ann Epidemiol 2000), read via Europe PMC (the full text is closed and was not read). HyperGEN also recruited untreated adult offspring and random population samples, so the whole cohort is larger, but no source read states its total. Other counts seen: 2010 African Americans and 1888 whites with metabolic-syndrome data (PMC1201342); 1,896 AA with whole-genome sequencing and 1,270 EA with GWAS (PMC13399276). The full design paper or the dbGaP entry (phs001293) would settle the total.

label: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial
counts: participants enrolled (as stated in a secondary analysis)
quote: Initially, 154,887 participants enrolled.
note: From a 2025 dietary analysis of PLCO (a definition source), which also says 'From 154,887 adults aged 55–74 years at 10 US screening centers, we formed the study group' and 'Approximately 150,000 men and women, aged 55–74 years, were recruited from ten screening centers nationwide.' The design paper (PMID:11189684; abstract only, full text closed) planned '37,000 females and 37,000 males in each of the two arms'. No trial results paper stating the randomised total was read; the main PLCO reports would give the randomised number, which may differ slightly from this enrolled figure.

label: Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank
counts: participants recruited at baseline 2004-2013
quote: The cohort includes data from 156,701 participants (94,840 men and 61,861 women) recruited from 18 health promotion centers throughout Korea (Supplementary Material 1).
note: From the KCPS-II biobank cohort profile update (Epidemiol Health 2025, PMID:40744823). The same paper reports an ongoing expansion since 2022: 'As of January 31, 2025, a total of 7,579 new participants have been enrolled', not added here; genotype data exist for 152,071 individuals.

label: Leipzig Research Center for Civilization Diseases-Heart Study
counts: patients recruited 2006-2014
quote: A total of 6,994 patients were recruited with suspected or confirmed stable coronary artery disease (CAD) or myocardial infarction.
note: From the cohort description of a 2025 GWAS/TWAS paper (PMID:41252360), which says initial data collection was 2006-2014. The design paper (PMID:22216169) gave preliminary results for a 4-year analysis of a total of 3,165 subjects (cohort 1: 1,457 men and 817 women; cohorts 2 and 3: 590 and 301). The same 2025 paper and the example study (PMID:34822396) say 5,700 samples were genotyped.

label: Bandim Health Project
counts: inhabitants covered by the urban HDSS in Bissau (rural HDSS not included)
quote: Bandim Health Project (BHP; www.bandim.org) maintains a Health and Demographic Surveillance System (HDSS) covering approximately 100 000 inhabitants in Bissau, the capital of Guinea-Bissau.
note: A surveillance platform with two parts and no stated total. Urban HDSS: approximately 100 000 inhabitants (PMID:38500576, a 2024 trial paper; PMID:35747181 says six districts with 100,000 inhabitants). Rural HDSS profile (PMID:31189684): 'Today, more than 25 000 women and 23 000 children below the age of 5 years are under surveillance.' The definition sources PMID:32114478, PMID:29579158 and PMID:25210141 give analysed subsets only (for example 39 421 children in PMID:32114478). No source gives one number for the whole platform; an urban HDSS profile would settle the urban count.

label: Center for Applied Genomics Biobank
counts: juvenile subjects (under 18) in the CAG cohort
quote: The cohort from the Center for Applied Genomics is composed of approximately 85,000 juvenile subjects below 18 years of age and of a diverse set of ancestries.
note: From the cohort description in the example study (PMID:40164604, 2025), not a biobank profile paper. PMID:35690720 extracted 51,293 genotyped subjects with phenotype data from 2006 to 2019 (16,902 controls and 10,368 psychiatric cases after its algorithm), an analysed subset. A CAG biobank profile or website stating total enrolment would settle the whole number.

label: Danish Twin Registry
counts: individuals in the register (twins, triplets, quadruplets born 1870-2009)
quote: By May 2019, the population in the DTR comprised of 175,518 individuals: 86,402 pairs of twins born from 1870 to 2009, and 874 sets of triplets and 23 sets of quadruplets born from 1931 to 2009.
note: Registry update paper (PMID:31544734). The 2013 update (PMID:23084092) said by January 1, 2012 the DTR comprised 86,398 twin pairs born 1870-2009, with a total of 105,000 twin individuals alive; its biobank held more than 51,000 specimens from approximately 20,000 twins.

label: Electronic Medical Records and Genomics Network
counts: participants in the pooled network-wide HRC-imputed GWAS dataset (phase III)
quote: The array data were imputed and merged at each phase, and the latest effort utilized the Michigan Imputation Server and HRC version 1.1, thus allowing the aggregation of data from 105,108 eMERGE participants for ∼40 million variants, both common and rare.
note: Consortium; the number is its flagship pooled genomic dataset (PMID:35047833), from 83 genotype array batches at 12 contributing sites. The same paper: the network enrolled and sequenced 24,998 participants (eMERGEseq N = 24,956); PGRNseq N = 9,010. The 2013 overview (PMID:23743551) said genome-wide data on a total of 56,955 samples are or will be available from dbGaP.

label: Sorbs Study
counts: Sorbian individuals enrolled (approximate)
quote: At present, about 1000 Sorbian individuals are enrolled in the study.
note: From the 2009 height GWAS (PMID:19729412), which analysed 929 subjects (544 females and 385 males). The example study (PMID:41520650) says participants were recruited and phenotyped between 2005 and 2007 and its final sample was 967 participants with complete data. No dedicated cohort profile read.

label: Dose-Responses to Exercise Training
counts: individuals randomised to the six study groups
quote: After these exclusions, 1410 individuals aged 57–78 y at baseline in 2005–2006 were randomly assigned to the resistance exercise, aerobic exercise, diet, combined resistance exercise and diet, combined aerobic exercise and diet, or control group.
note: Trial, so the randomised number is given. Same paper (PMID:33742194, also the example study): 3000 men and women were invited and 1479 attended baseline measurements in 2005-2006; 1401 individuals were in its cognition analyses.

label: Genetics of Lipid-Lowering Drugs and Diet Network
counts: Caucasian individuals in 184 pedigrees
quote: The GOLDN sample consisted of 1048 Caucasian individuals belonging to 184 pedigrees (average family size 6.2).
note: From the cohort description of the example study (PMID:34836252), not the GOLDN design paper; its lipidomics analysis used 668 GOLDN participants. The original GOLDN design paper was not read.

label: Study of Women's Health Across the Nation
counts: women enrolled at baseline 1996-1997
quote: Of these, a total of 3302 women, comprising 1550 Caucasian, 935 African American, 286 Hispanic, 250 Chinese and 281 Japanese, were deemed eligible and subsequently enrolled into the SWAN cohort for the longitudinal survey, completing the baseline study from January 1996 to December 1997.
note: From a 2025 SWAN analysis (PMID:40988242), not the design paper; the same number is stated in PMID:41389332 and PMID:39070021 and in the definition source (PMID:42076794, 'Among the 3302 women in the sample'). The original SWAN design chapter (Sowers et al. 2000) was not read.

label: Finnish Diabetic Nephropathy Study
counts: participants with type 1 diabetes (approximate, 'nearly 9000')
quote: Starting as a small‐scale pilot project with the goal of recruiting a few hundred individuals, the FinnDiane Study has evolved over the years into one of the largest well‐characterized cohorts of individuals with type 1 diabetes, now encompassing nearly 9000 participants from across the country.
note: From the 2024 FinnDiane review (PMID:39235140). The study website (https://research.folkhalsan.fi/genetics/finndiane-study) is inconsistent: 'nearly 10,000 well characterized participants with type 1 diabetes recruited from 93 centers' and 'over 10,000 participants'. The example study (PMID:39746953) says FinnDiane 'currently comprises of over 5000 adults' and uses 'the whole FinnDiane cohort (n = 6,019)' as an LD reference; its analysis had 3244 FinnDiane participants.

label: IMAGEN study
counts: adolescents recruited in schools around age 14
quote: Neuroimaging and clinical data were obtained from an existing large European multi-site longitudinal study of adolescent development ( https://imagen-project.org ) across eight European sites in France, United Kingdom, Ireland, and Germany, which includes 2,223 adolescents recruited in schools around age 14 (standard deviation = 0.41; age range: 12.9–15.7).
note: From a 2024 IMAGEN analysis (PMID:37819410), not a profile paper. The design paper (PMID:21102431) planned 2000 14-year-old adolescents; the 2020 decade review (PMID:32601453) says 'The IMAGEN cohort with 2000 young adolescents' and 'The initial IMAGEN sample size (>2000)', each of 8 centres recruiting at least 250. PMID:39811626 says 2,087 participants were genotyped at baseline; PMID:36603003 had 2315 participants with any data at age 14.

label: Munich Antidepressant Response Signature
counts: participants recruited by 2008
quote: Of the 842 participants recruited by 2008, 339 were included in a previously reported genome-wide pharmacogenetic study, and additional samples from this cohort have been genotyped since then, resulting in 604 (72%) samples from patients with unipolar depression available for the present meta-analysis.
note: From the example study (PMID:23377640, GENDEP/MARS/STAR*D meta-analysis); MARS recruitment continued after 2008, so the whole cohort is likely larger. The design paper (PMID:18586274, J Psychiatr Res 2009) is closed and was not read; PMID:30678080 analysed 297 patients (173 responders, 124 non-responders).

label: Minority Aging Research Study
counts: persons enrolled by the time of the 2012 design paper
quote: After discussing the study in detail with each potential participant, 223 were found to be inelligible because they were either too young, had a prior dementia diagnosis, or were taking AD medications, 112 refused, 71 were reluctant, and 366 persons enrolled in the study.
note: Design paper (PMID:22471868); enrolment is ongoing, so the current cohort is larger. A 2026 harmonisation paper (PMID:41692372) included MARS = 825 dementia-free participants with baseline activity data (an analysed subset, a lower bound on current size). The example study (PMID:37984853) gives 'The current number of enrolled participants is now at 4960' for ROS/MAP, not MARS. A current MARS enrolment count from the Rush ADRC would settle it.

label: Older Australian Twins Study
counts: twins and their siblings aged 65+ recruited
quote: OATS recruited 623 twins and their siblings, aged 65 years and older and residing in New South Wales, Victoria or Queensland from the Australian Twin Registry.
note: From a 2023 OATS analysis (PMID:36732682), not the design paper. The design paper (PMID:19943720) abstract gives a target sample size of 1000, with at least 400 pairs of twins aged 65-90; its full text (Twin Res Hum Genet) was not readable from the cache. PMID:27030319 genotyped 548 OATS samples.

label: LymeProspect
counts: adult patients with confirmed Lyme borreliosis included April 2015-October 2018
quote: The LymeProspect cohort consisted of 1138 patients with a new physician-confirmed LB (either EM or disseminated manifestation) who were included at the initiation of antibiotic therapy and followed for one year, between April 2015 and October 2018
note: From the example study (PMID:38714679), which measured cytokine responses and genomes in 1,060 participants. The protocol (PMID:30987580) gives power calculations for cohorts of 1500 or 1000 patients and a recruitment completion date for adults of 01-10-2018. The cohort's main outcome paper was not read and might give a slightly different included number.

label: 300-Tanzania-FG
counts: healthy adults aged 18-65 in the Tanzanian cohort
quote: The Tanzanian cohort comprised 323 healthy individuals (159 males, 164 females) aged 18–65 years, residing in the Kilimanjaro region of Northern Tanzania.
note: From PMID:41858114 (2026). The same paper says 317 and 324 individuals had genotype and cytokine data respectively, which does not match 323 exactly. PMID:37555575 says the cohort was enrolled between March and December 2017 and analysed 318 Tanzanians. The cohort's original description (Temba et al. 2021, cited as ref 19 in PMID:35167808) was not read and would settle the enrolled number.

label: UCLA ATLAS Community Health Initiative
counts: UCLA Health patients who consented to ATLAS (enrolled group), as of December 2024
quote: From these, 104,516 individuals consented to participate in the ATLAS Initiative and comprised the enrolled group, with the remainder of the individuals labeled as unenrolled.
note: From PMID:41812654 (2026); the preceding sentence gives the date: 'As of December 2024, the UCLA Health System EHR contained records for 1,568,927 individuals receiving care during the recruitment period and meeting our inclusion criteria for analyses.' Genotyped numbers are smaller: N=36,736 after QC (36,779 genotyped) in the 2022 flagship paper (PMID:36085083), which says the initiative aims to collect genomic data from over 150,000 individuals; a snapshot of samples up to 15 February 2024 totalled n = 53,829 (PMID:40251273).

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Family Study
counts: no whole-study total found; separate Hispanic and African American counts only
note: No readable source states the total. Per-arm counts: 'Hispanic Americans included in this report (n = 1417 individuals, 90 pedigrees) were recruited from clinical centers in San Antonio, TX and San Luis Valley, CO.' (PMC4658008, PMID:26599207); 'Members of large families of self-reported African Americans ( n  = 581 individuals in 42 pedigrees from Los Angeles, California) were recruited.' (PMC3251563, PMID:22238593).
