The design paper (PMID:12684185, Ann Epidemiol 2003, closed) abstract only gives preliminary heritability 'in the first 93 families (approximately 1000 individuals)'; its full text would settle the total. Families were recruited 2000-2002 (PMID:21816973).

label: WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network
counts: WHI hormone-trial women genotyped in the GARNET nested case-control sample
quote: Of the approximately 27,000 women who participated in the HT trial, 4,894 were genotyped on the Illumina Omni-Quad as part of WHI GARNET, a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify genetic components involved in differential responses from the HT trial.
note: dbGaP study page phs000315 (also 'Total number of consented subjects: 4894'). The same page breaks it down: 'Therefore, 4,894 subjects are available for analysis. These include 2,344 controls, 497 CHD cases, 1,043 incident diabetes cases, 342 stroke cases, 304 VTE cases, 167 cases of more than one type, and 197 QC samples (SHARe participants previously genotyped on Affy6.0).' No total case count is stated, so cases is left null. 4949 unique subjects were submitted for genotyping. The definition sources (PMC5714283 and the PMID:40537477 supplement) give no GARNET count.

label: ALS Utrecht
counts: subjects (ALS patients and healthy controls) contributed to the ENIGMA Plasticity GWAS
quote: ALS Utrecht	Case-control (ALS, healthy control)	158	101/57	European	27
note: Table row, not a sentence: Supplementary Table 1 (Cohort characteristics) of PMID:35383335, columns Cohort, Study design, # subjects, # male / female, ancestry, # healthy**; the quote is those six cells joined by tabs. The '# healthy' column (27) is taken as the healthy controls; no ALS case count is stated, so cases is left null. The number is this sample as contributed to the ENIGMA meta-analysis (the term is defined as that sample); the wider ALS Utrecht MRI or genetics cohorts at UMC Utrecht are larger, but no source read here states their size.

label: Brain Imaging Genetics study
counts: healthy volunteers in the BIG subject pool with anatomical MRI
quote: At the time of this study the BIG subject-pool consisted of 2337 self-reported healthy individuals (1248 females) who had undergone anatomical (T1-weighted) MRI scans, usually as part of their involvement in diverse smaller-scale studies at the DCCN, and who had given their consent to participate in BIG.
note: BIG is an open, growing subject pool; this is its size at the time of the 2014 handedness study (PMC3975119). The FOXP2 study (PMID:25013396) says 1301 subjects had genome-wide genotyping. The example study (PMID:35383335) gives no whole-pool size. A later count would supersede this.

label: BrainSCALE study
counts: families at baseline (not individuals)
quote: The participants were recruited from The Netherlands Twin Register (NTR) and at baseline consisted of 112 families, with 9-year-old twins and an older sibling.
note: The design paper (PMID:22856378, doi 10.1017/thg.2012.4) counts families: 112 at baseline, 89 returned at the three-year follow-up; it gives siblings N = 105 at baseline and N = 82 at follow-up but never states the total number of individuals (twins plus siblings, and parents). The example study (PMID:35383335) gives no Brainscale sample size in text. A sentence stating the number of children enrolled would settle it.

label: Norwegian Cognitive NeuroGenetics sample
counts: participants genome-wide genotyped (GWA sample)
quote: The sample on which the GWA study was successfully performed consists of 670 persons recruited through newspaper advertisements in the Oslo and Bergen urban areas.
note: The NCNG profile paper (PMID:22856377, doi 10.1017/thg.2012.8) also says the project expanded 'from ~300 to ~700' participants and that 'We genotyped over 700 NCNG participants' for candidate SNPs; 670 is the stated size of the genome-wide genotyped sample, the only exact whole-sample count given. The example study (PMID:35383335) gives no NCNG size in text.

label: NeuroIMAGE study
counts: children assessed (848 parents assessed in addition)
quote: Combined with newly recruited participants the NeuroIMAGE study comprehends an assessment of 1,069 children (751 from ADHD families; 318 from CON families) and 848 parents (582 from ADHD families; 266 from CON families).
note: The design paper (PMID:25012461) states 1,069 children and 848 parents but no combined total, so participants gives the children only; the parents are additional. It also reports the intermediate follow-up (2008-2009) of 415 ADHD families (1,001 children and 727 parents) and 141 control families (119 children and 253 parents), and the original Dutch IMAGE sample of 365 ADHD and 148 control families.

label: Inter99 Study
counts: participants examined at baseline (intervention groups)
quote: The Inter99 cohort is a randomized, non-pharmacological intervention study for the prevention of ischaemic heart disease, conducted on 6,784 randomly ascertained participants aged 30 to 60 years at the Research Centre for Prevention and Health in Glostrup, Denmark [45] (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT00289237).
note: The trial paper PMID:25886540 says an age- and sex-stratified random sample of 13,016 persons was randomised a priori into group A (n = 11,708) and group B (n = 1,308) before invitation, that 'A total of 6,906 (53.4%) turned up for the investigation at the centre', and that 3,324 of a 5,264-person questionnaire control group (group C) responded. The baseline paper PMID:14663300 (abstract only on disk) gives a participation rate of 52.5% but no count. 6,784 is the baseline participant count as the example study states it; 6,906 is the attendance figure in the 2015 trial paper.

label: iPSYCH case-cohort study
counts: samples in iPSYCH2015 (cases plus population-based cohort)
quote: The newly updated cohort, named iPSYCH2015, expands the study base with 56,233 samples, to a combined total of 141,265 samples.
note: Cases and controls from the same preprint abstract: 'In total, the expanded iPSYCH2015 sample consists of 93,608 unique individuals in the case groups and 50,615 population controls.' Cases and controls overlap (random cohort members can also be cases), so they do not add up to the total. The first wave (PMID:28924187) states 'Within the sample of 86 189 individuals, a total of 57 377 individuals had at least one major mental disorder', with a random population cohort of 30 000.

label: Long Life Family Study
counts: individuals enrolled at Visit 1 from 539 families
quote: LLFS successfully enrolled and extensively phenotyped 4,953 individuals from 539 two-generational families that demonstrated clustering for exception longevity in the upper generation (ie, with a sibship FLoSS > 7) from 3 US field sites (Boston University, Boston, MA; Columbia University, New York, NY; and University of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA) and one field site in Denmark (University of Southern Denmark, Odense, Denmark; Table 1).
note: The abstract of the same profile paper says 'The Visit 1 in-person evaluation (2006-2009) recruited 4 953 individuals from 539 two-generation families'. Table 1 splits Visit 1 into 1,727 probands and 3,226 offspring.

label: Genetic Epidemiology of COPD
counts: current and former smokers enrolled in Phase 1
quote: COPDGene enrolled 10,198 former and current smokers aged 45–80 years with a history of ≥10 pack-year smoking with and without COPD from initiation in P1 from 21 clinical centers across the United States (Figure 1) [4].
note: The design paper (PMID:20214461) gives the planned size: 'COPDGene will enroll 10,000 smokers with and without COPD across the GOLD stages.' PMID:37241208 gives the achieved Phase 1 enrolment (2008-2011) of 10,198. The example study (PMID:39057616) was not needed.

label: Genetic and phenotypic determinants of blood pressure and other cardiovascular risk factors
counts: healthy adults enrolled at baseline
quote: Briefly, the cohort is composed of a representative population of 2170 healthy adults aged 25–41 with residence in the Principality of Liechtenstein.
note: The design paper (PMID:23299990, abstract) reports enrolment in progress: 'Since June 2010, 1,333 participants have been enrolled.' PMC6085127 (PMID:29570511) says patients were enrolled from 2010 to 2013; PMC10530210 ('Of the 2170 participants enrolled at baseline') and PMC13456266 ('A total of 2170 individuals were recruited for the GAPP study.') agree. The example study (PMID:36267918) analysed 1,897 GAPP participants.

label: Women's Genome Health Study
counts: genotyped women of European ancestry (analysed GWAS sample)
quote: Analysis was performed in the Women's Genome Health Study (WGHS), including 23,294 women of European ancestry who were cancer-free at baseline and followed for 20 years for incident cancer.
note: The design paper (PMID:18070814, abstract) gives only the planned size, 'at least 25 000 initially healthy American women' (title: 'more than 25,000'). Many WGHS papers (e.g. PMID:24688000, PMID:25642633, PMID:20937264) give the same 23,294 genotyped women of European ancestry, which is the analysed genetic sample after ancestry and QC filtering rather than every WHS woman who gave blood. The example study (PMID:38052102) used 361 mothers of DZ twins and 20,183 controls from the WGHS. A statement of the number of women genotyped before QC would settle the whole-cohort count.

label: Cameron County Hispanic Cohort
counts: participants recruited 2004-2007
quote: From 2004 through 2007, we recruited 2,000 participants to the CCHC who are residents of Brownsville, Texas, which has 8 international crossing points to Matamoros, Mexico.
note: The 2010 paper (PMID:20394692, PMC2879985) also says the cohort was 'now numbering 2,000' and that its first analysis documented 810 randomly selected people aged 35-64. The CCHC kept recruiting after 2007 (a 2025 paper, PMC12495492, describes recruitment from 2014 to 2023, and PMC12443252 uses 3,063 unrelated genotyped CCHC participants), so 2,000 is an early count, not the current size; no source read gives a current total. The example study (PMID:39885687) gives no whole-cohort size. A recent cohort profile would settle it.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Genetics Consortium
counts: individuals (stated as 'over 56,000') in the 2025 ADGC multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis
quote: To identify novel loci and explore differences in genetic association across these groups, the Alzheimer’s Disease Genetics Consortium (ADGC) initiated the first large-scale multi-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis with direct genotyping and either clinical evaluation of or pathological confirmation of AD status on over 56,000 individuals across four genetic similarity groups (GSGs) with diverse ancestral genetic backgrounds, including 6728 AFA, 8899 HIS, 3232 EAS, and 37,382 NHW participants.
note: Cohort aggregation; 56000 is the stated lower bound ('over 56,000'). Cases and controls come from the same paper (PMC12273372): 'The ADGC assembled the largest multi-GSG collection of AD samples to date, containing 24,388 participants with AD and 31,853 cognitively unimpaired individuals passing quality control (QC) from 41 NHW, 12 AFA, eight HIS, and five EAS datasets (within-GSG characteristics shown in Table 1; dataset-level characteristics shown in Table S1).' Table 1 of that paper gives a total of 56,241 with a slightly different split (24,495 cases, 31,746 controls). Other ADGC analyses read: the 2025 smoking-interaction GWAS (PMID:41268768) used 34 ADGC GWAS datasets, n = 25,158; the X-chromosome study (PMID:39250132) pooled ADGC with other resources (1,152,284 individuals in total), so it does not count ADGC alone.

label: Consortium for the Analysis of the Diversity and Evolution of Latin America
counts: volunteers sampled in five Latin American countries
quote: We estimated individual ancestry proportions in a sample of 7,342 subjects ascertained in five countries (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, México and Perú).
note: The CANDELA description paper (PMID:25254375) is titled '... Based on 7,342 Individuals'. Genotyped and analysed subsets in later papers: 5,958 individuals in the 2016 facial GWAS (PMID:27193062, from photographs of 6,275), and 6,486 individuals examined with up to 5,988 analysed in the example study (PMID:37156940).

label: Mexico City Prospective Study
counts: adults recruited 1998-2004
quote: Of the 159,755 participants recruited, 22,364 (14%) were excluded.
note: From an MCPS analysis paper (PMID:41231729, 'Polygenic prediction of coronary heart disease among 130 000 Mexican adults'); a second MCPS paper (PMC12254126, PMID:40650370) states 'Of 159 755 participants recruited, 25 845 (16%) were excluded from all analyses.' The definition sources say 'more than 150,000 adults' (PMID:39948438) and 'a large prospective cohort of 150,000 individuals' (PMID:37308787). The example study (PMID:39948438) analysed 136,401 participants with exome data. The MCPS cohort profile was not read.

label: Airwave Health Monitoring Study
counts: police officers and staff enrolled 2004-2015
quote: Briefly, the study enrolled 53,245 participants between 2004 and 2015, and collected information on socio‐demographic, health, occupational and lifestyle factors via surveys and/or health screenings.
note: From a 2026 Airwave analysis paper (PMID:41251127), not a design paper. The cohort profile (PMID:25194498, abstract) gives the interim count: 'By the end of 2012, the study had recruited 42,112 participants, of whom 35,199 (83.6%) had attended the health screening.' A 2018 abstract (PMID:30014898) mentions radio-usage estimates for ~50,000 participants. The example study (PMID:33230300) gives no Airwave size in text.

label: Cohorte Lausannoise
counts: Caucasian adults aged 35-75 examined at baseline
quote: Single-center, cross-sectional study including a random sample of 6,188 extensively phenotyped Caucasian subjects (3,251 women and 2,937 men) aged 35 to 75 years living in Lausanne, and genotyped using the 500 K Affymetrix chip technology.
note: Quote from the profile paper's abstract (Methods section). The full text of the same paper (PMC2311269) says 8,121 volunteered, 'the first 6,738 were invited to attend the clinic and completed the examination', and '6,189 participants met the inclusion criteria (including ethnicity) and were included in the CoLaus study' (one more than the abstract). A 2024 follow-up paper (PMID:38388190) starts from 'the initial 6733 participants', which appears to include the non-Caucasian participants excluded in the 2008 count.

label: Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study
counts: adults recruited at baseline 1990-1994
quote: We used data from the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study (MCCS), a prospective study that recruited 41,513 middle-aged and older Australians (99 % aged between 40 and 69 years, 59 % females) of white European origin between 1990 and 1994 (baseline) (Milne et al., 2017).
note: From the definition source, an MCCS analysis paper citing the 2017 cohort profile (Milne et al.), which was not read. The example study (PMID:34996992) was not needed.

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey
counts: children in the population cohort at wave 1 (clinical cohort of 543 in addition)
quote: TRAILS consists of a population cohort (N=2230) and a clinical cohort (N=543), both of which were followed from about age 11 years onwards.
note: The cohort profile update (PMID:25431468, PMC4339762) states the two cohorts separately and never a combined total, so participants gives the population cohort only; the clinical cohort's 543 children, included from 2004, are additional. Retention of the population cohort at wave 5 was 1,778. The year is the population cohort's first wave as usually reported (not stated in the quote); the example study (PMID:42036355) was not needed.

label: ADDITION-PRO Study
counts: participants attending the 2009-2011 health assessment
quote: All individuals with impaired glucose regulation at screening, those who developed diabetes following screening, and a random sub-sample of those at lower levels of diabetes risk were invited to attend a follow-up health assessment in 2009–2011 (n = 4,188), of whom 2,082 (50%) attended.
note: Design paper (PMID:23241242, PMC3583712). The 16,136 high-risk individuals from the 2001-2006 screening are the sampling frame, not participants; 4,188 were invited. The full text also says 'In total, 2,082/4,188 (50%) people agreed to participate and attended the ADDITION-PRO health assessment (Figure 2).'

label: Finnish Cardiovascular Study
counts: patients recruited for exercise testing, October 2001 - December 2008
quote: A study population of 4178 patients (2537 men and 1641 women) was recruited.
note: From a 2019 FINCAVAS analysis paper (PMID:30354741), whose preceding sentence says all consecutive patients referred for an exercise test at Tampere University Hospital 'were enrolled between October 2001 and December 2008'. The design paper (PMID:16515696) reports 2,212 patients recruited by the end of 2004 and a goal of 'roughly 5,000 patients'. Other FINCAVAS papers give analysed subsets: 3,862 patients (PMC4794714), 3,609 (PMID:25366884), 3,456 (PMID:31638839). The example study (PMID:36050321) does not name FINCAVAS in its text, and its supplementary files (a definition source) were not downloaded.

label: Health Professionals Follow-up Study
counts: male health professionals enrolled in 1986
quote: The HPFS began in 1986 and enrolled 51,529 male health professionals, aged 40 to 75 years [18].
note: PMID:33185675 agrees: "Of 51 529 men enrolled in 1986, 5510 died prior to 1998".

label: ARGO study
counts: severe-OA patients undergoing joint replacement, Athens and Larissa (stated as more than 1,500; controls not included)
quote: More than 1,500 patients with severe OA, undergoing hip and/or knee total joint replacement were recruited from the cities of Athens and Larissa.
note: A lower bound for the patients only, from the cohort description in the 2021 osteoarthritis GWAS meta-analysis (Athens recruitment Feb 2015 - Mar 2017); no number for the healthy controls or the whole collection was found. PMID:30470734 used 712 ARGO samples (OA cases and controls from Larissa) as controls, a subset. The EGA study EGAS00001000917 page gives no count. A dedicated ARGO design paper would settle the total.

label: Ansan and Ansung Study
counts: baseline participants recruited 2001-2002
quote: Out of the 10 030 baseline participants, 633 cumulative deaths were recorded between baseline and the 5th follow-up (2001 to 2012), and the 6th follow-up was conducted in 5906 participants (out of 9397 survivor; Figure 1, and Supplementary Figure 1, available as Supplementary data at IJE online).
note: KoGES cohort profile (2017). PMID:36573383 agrees: "Baseline participants were 10,030 subjects aged 40 to 69 years who were from Ansan or Anseong in Gyeonggi-do, South Korea." The 6th follow-up examined 5906 participants.

label: Nagahama Prospective Cohort for Comprehensive Human Bioscience
counts: residents aged 30-74 who participated at baseline (2008-2010)
quote: A total of 9,809 residents voluntarily participated in the study.
note: Baseline recruitment described in PMID:26444713, which adds that "data from 9,804 individuals were finally included into the baseline dataset". The first follow-up (2013-2016) "included 9850 individuals" (PMID:40877534), which may include new entrants; the baseline enrolment is given here.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease Genetics Consortium
counts: individuals in 121 GWAS of the 2019 trans-ancestry eGFR discovery meta-analysis
quote: We performed 121 GWAS encompassing 765,348 individuals of European (n = 567,460), East Asian (n = 165,726), African-American (n = 13,842), South Asian (n = 13,359) and Hispanic (n = 4,961) ancestry (median age, 54 years; 50% female; Supplementary Table 1).
note: CKDGen's 2019 flagship eGFR meta-analysis (the paper cited by the CKDGen website's PMID:31980069 is not on disk). Replication in the Million Veteran Program (n = 280,722) gave 1,046,070 combined, and the BUN meta-analysis 416,178. The example study PMID:34272381 combined CKDGen with UK Biobank (n = 1,201,909), which is not a CKDGen-only count.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project
counts: individuals who participated in the TMM cohort studies (stated as more than 157 000)
quote: More than 157 000 individuals voluntarily participated in the TMM study by March 2016, and approximately 33 000 individuals received detailed physiological examinations, including ophthalmic examination.
note: An aggregation of two cohorts; the same paper gives the member counts: "the community-based cohort (CommCohort) study, which recruited 84 073 participants,32 and the birth and three-generation cohort (BirThree Cohort) study, which recruited 73 529 participants." The 2016 design paper (PMID:27374138) gives targets of 80 000 (CommCohort) and 70 000 (BirThree). The 'by March 2016' date is as stated, although BirThree recruitment ran into 2017.

label: Fred Hutchinson Prostate Cancer Study
counts: interviewed cases and controls of Study I (1993-1996) and Study II (2002-2005); no stated total
quote: Overall, 2,244 eligible prostate cancer patients were identified, 1,754 (78.2%) were interviewed, and blood samples yielding sufficient DNA for genotyping were drawn from 1,457 (83.1%) cases who completed a study interview.
note: PMID:19366831, describing both King County case-control studies. Controls from the same paragraph: "A total of 2,448 men were identified who met the eligibility criteria, 1,645 (67.2%) were interviewed and of these men blood samples were drawn and DNA prepared from 1,352 (82.2%) using standard protocols." No combined total is stated, so participants is left null. The example study PMID:37555839 used a subset (402 cases with radical prostatectomy, 1,133 controls); PMID:17700570 screened 290 cases aged under 55.

label: Whole Genome Association Analysis of Hematopoietic Cell Transplant (HCT) Outcomes
counts: consented subjects in dbGaP phs001918.v1 (transplant recipients and their donors)
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 9088
note: The same dbGaP page: "The study population represents a large cohort from the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center and consists of 4,471 recipients and 4,628 donors containing 4,258 recipient-donor pairs." This version (v1) is superseded by v2, not read. The definition source PMID:34996099 describes "4270 recipients of European ancestry" (1990-2011), the European-ancestry subset.

label: Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium
counts: individuals without diabetes in the 2021 trans-ancestry glycaemic-trait GWAS meta-analysis (up to)
quote: Here we aggregated genome-wide association studies comprising up to 281,416 individuals without diabetes (30% non-European ancestry) for whom fasting glucose, 2-h glucose after an oral glucose challenge, glycated hemoglobin and fasting insulin data were available.
note: MAGIC's 2021 flagship trans-ancestry meta-analysis (Nat Genet); 'up to' because trait sample sizes differ. The MAGIC website gives no count. The definition source / example study PMID:39280063 (exome-array meta-analysis) reports up to 144,060 participants (HbA1c) from up to 64 cohorts.

label: Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Childhood Study
counts: platinum-treated children of the MAGIC cisplatin cohort in the GWAS (a subset of the whole study)
quote: Therefore, a genome-wide association study was performed in the Genetics of Childhood Cancer Treatment (GO-CAT) cohort (n = 261) and the United Kingdom Molecular Genetics of Adverse Drug Reactions in Children Study (United Kingdom MAGIC) cohort (n = 248).
note: Only the cisplatin ototoxicity cohort (recruited Jan 2012 - Mar 2018 at eight UK sites) has a stated size, and only as analysed in the GWAS. The earlier definition source PMID:28445188 states: "We recruited 149 children from seven UK centres using a retrospective cohort study design." No number for the whole MAGIC study (all its adverse-drug-reaction cohorts) was found in either paper or a Europe PMC search; a study overview or website would settle it.

label: Raine Study
counts: pregnant women enrolled 1989-1991 (Generation 1); their 2868 live-born offspring are the index participants
quote: A total of 2900 women (‘Generation 1’) were enrolled into the study.
note: Raine Study cohort profile (2017). The same paper: "There were 2868 live births–the index participants of ‘Generation 2’–including 60 sets of twins (n = 120) and two sets of triplets (n = 6), from 2826 mothers (see Figure 1)." No combined total is stated. PMC12873190 agrees on 2900 mothers and 2868 offspring.

label: Prospective Study of Pravastatin in the Elderly at Risk
counts: men and women aged 70-82 randomised to pravastatin or placebo
quote: We did a randomised controlled trial in which we assigned 5804 men (n=2804) and women (n=3000) aged 70-82 years with a history of, or risk factors for, vascular disease to pravastatin (40 mg per day; n=2891) or placebo (n=2913).
note: Main trial report (Lancet 2002). The baseline paper PMID:12097148 agrees: "23,770 individuals were screened, and 5,804 subjects (2,804 men and 3,000 women), aged 70 to 82 years (average 75 years) and with baseline cholesterol 4.0-9.0 mmol/l, were randomised."

label: Genetic Epidemiology Network of Salt Sensitivity
counts: participants from 658 families recruited (2003-2005)
quote: Overall, 3,153 study participants from 658 families were enrolled in the study (Table 3).
note: GenSalt design paper. The same paper: "A total of 1,906 study participants (676 probands, 956 siblings, 69 spouses, and 205 offspring) took part in the dietary intervention." Later papers (PMID:28993450, PMC4873465) analyse the 1,906 intervention participants.

label: Kaiser Permanente Research Bank
counts: KP members consented to join (approximately 396,000)
quote: Approximately 396,000 KP members have consented to join the KPRB as of July 2021, and biospecimens have been collected on approximately 371,000 adults (94% of those consented).
note: KPRB cancer cohort profile (2022). Its abstract says the KPRB is collecting from "approximately 400,000 adult KP members" (the target); biospecimens on approximately 371,000; the cancer cohort N = 65,225; the general cohort over 330,000 adults without cancer. The example study PMID:34169730 was not needed.

label: Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research
counts: no pooled participant count stated; member studies: five established twin cohorts and one adoption cohort
quote: As a result of this early work, the MCTFR now includes five established twin cohorts and one adoption cohort.
note: The 2019 MCTFR overview gives member counts only, e.g. "The Minnesota Twin Registry (MTR) includes monozygotic (MZ) and same-sex dizygotic (DZ) twins born between 1904 and 1934 (1802 twins), 1936 and 1955 (8614 twins), and 1961 and 1964 (782 twins) who have completed assessments in middle and older adulthood."; the other cohort sizes are in its Table 1, which was not legible in the cached text. The 2006 overview (PMID:17254440) is on disk only as a publisher landing page; its full text would give the combined sample.

label: Relationship between Insulin Sensitivity and Cardiovascular disease
counts: men and women who participated at baseline (2002-2005)
quote: A total of 1,538 men and women participated in the RISC cohort.
note: PMID:19366964. PMC3636608 (PMID:23160532) agrees: "Baseline examinations began in June 2002 and were completed in July 2005 and included 1,538 subjects receiving an OGTT." The design paper PMID:14968294 planned 1500 subjects; PMID:19455304 analysed 1,276 genotyped participants from 19 centres.

label: Rotterdam Study I
counts: inhabitants of Ommoord aged 55 and over included at the start in 1990
quote: The first cohort (RS-I) started in 1990 and included 7,983 inhabitants, aged ≥55 years from Ommoord, a suburb of Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
note: From the definition source; the Rotterdam Study as a whole (RS-I to RS-III) reached 14,926 participants, which is not this term's count.

label: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
counts: children aged 9-10 enrolled at baseline (2016-2018)
quote: Out of the 11,878 participants in the study 127 (1.1%) withdrew.
note: PMID:35152002, an ABCD retention paper. PMC8579129 (PMID:34742018) gives "baseline (N = 11,878)" for Data Release 3.0 but also calls it a study "of 11,880 youth". The design paper PMID:29703560 gives the target: "The final cohort will include 9780 single births and 1720 twins" (11,500 planned). The MCTFR overview (PMID:31796137) says "over 11,875 children".

label: Study to Understand the Genetics of the Acute Response to Metformin and Glipizide in Humans
counts: individuals naive to diabetes medication who received the glipizide and metformin challenges
quote: SUGAR-MGH is a pharmacogenetic study in which 1000 individuals who were naive to type 2 diabetes medications received a single-dose glipizide challenge and a short course of metformin.
note: PMID:37233759 (2023 GWAS), which also says "We recruited 1000 individuals at risk of developing type 2 diabetes."; 890 had complete GWAS data. The 2015 design paper (PMC4374872) reported 668 enrolled of a planned 1,000 as of March 2013.

label: Colon Cancer Family Registry
counts: participants (cases, relatives and controls) from 15,049 families recruited 1998-2012
quote: The 42 489 study participants from 15 049 families were recruited between 1998 and 2012 in the USA, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
note: Cohort Profile: The Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort (PMID:29490034, 2018), key-features box. The same paper's follow-up section refers to "37 436 participants who completed baseline" follow-up eligibility, and its Table 1 gives 32,782 population-based individuals. The definition source PMC3616155 analysed 1,923 cases and 3,115 sibling controls, a subset.

label: DIAbetes COhoRtE
counts: adult type 2 diabetes outpatients recruited at baseline (2010-2014)
quote: We thus established the DIAbetes COhoRtE study (DIACORE) [21], a cohort study of 3000 patients with DM2.
note: PMID:30897159 (2019) reports baseline recruitment 2/2010-8/2014: 4226 patients contacted DIACORE, 1226 ineligible, and describes 'all 3000 DIACORE participants'; 2892 had complete data for analysis. The 2013 design paper (PMID:23409726) planned 6000 patients.

label: Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study
counts: men aged 65 or older enrolled at baseline (2000-2002)
quote: 5995 men enrolled with a mean (+/-SD) age of 73.7 (+/-5.9) years, 11% of which were minorities.
note: From the abstract of the MrOS design and baseline paper (Contemp Clin Trials 2005), read via Europe PMC. The definition sources give only analysed subsets (MrOS Sleep 3,135 men per definition; 2,175 European-ancestry men in the melatonin GWAS PMC13269534). The year of baseline is not stated in the sentence read.

label: Prevention of Renal and Vascular End-stage Disease study
counts: participants enrolled at baseline (1997-1998)
quote: PREVEND is a population-based cohort with 8592 participants enrolled between 1997 and 1998.
note: PMID:23316297 (PMC3541606) also states 'Of the baseline sample of 8592 participants, 451 had a history of CVD' and that 40 856 individuals (47.8%) returned the screening questionnaire and morning urine sample from which the cohort was drawn.

label: European Alzheimer & Dementia Biobank
counts: cases, proxy cases and controls in the 2022 EADB stage I GWAS meta-analysis
quote: Colocalization between the EGFR eQTL signal (MayoRNAseq TCX, n = 259 individuals) and the EADB GWAS stage I (n = 487,511) signal (eQTL coloc PP4 = 98.3%)
note: PMID:35379992 (Bellenguez 2022). Stage I is stated as 'based on 39,106 clinically diagnosed AD cases, 46,828 proxy-ADD cases (as defined in the Supplementary Note), 401,577 controls'; cases and controls left null because the cases come as two separately stated groups. The newly collated EADB dataset itself: 'A new dataset of 20,464 clinically diagnosed AD cases and 22,244 controls has been collated from 15 European countries.' The two-stage study totals 111,326 cases and 677,663 controls including follow-up consortia (ADGC, FinnGen, CHARGE).

label: INTERSTROKE Study
counts: first acute stroke cases and matched controls recruited 2007-2015
quote: With the sample size to 26,950 participants from 32 countries, we reported the association of stroke subtypes with active and environmental tobacco smoking in men and women, young and old, with regions of world and by level of income in countries.
note: Cases and controls from the same source: 'The INTERSTROKE study is a case–control study of acute first stroke and was undertaken with 13,462 stroke cases and 13,488 controls recruited between January 11, 2007 and August 8, 2015 in 32 countries worldwide.' PMC9841450 analysed 96% of them (12,909 cases, 12,934 controls). The genotyped subset used in genetic studies is smaller and was not sought.

label: Shanghai Women's Health Study
counts: women aged 40-70 recruited 1996-2000
quote: From 1996 to 2000, the Shanghai Women's Health Study recruited 74,942 adult Chinese women from selected urban communities, with a 92% response rate.
note: Abstract of the cohort profile paper (Am J Epidemiol 2005). PMID:22073174 gives the same 74,942 and analysed 74,857 women after exclusions.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase2
counts: MHI Biobank participants genotyped on the Illumina MEGA array (phase 2 data set)
quote: We generated the MHI Biobank phase 2 data set by genotyping 3397 participants on the Illumina MEGA array.
note: Cases and controls from the same paper: 'we also measured CEC and other lipid phenotypes in an additional 863 CAD‐free participants and 2534 patients with CAD (MHI Biobank phase 2 in Table S1)'. PMC6587223 (2019) calculated polygenic scores in 'phase 2, n=3309' (analysed subset).

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank phase1
counts: French Canadians of the MHI Biobank whose whole genomes were sequenced at low depth (phase 1 data set)
quote: Specifically, we sequenced at ~5.6× coverage the whole genome of 1970 French Canadians recruited by the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank and identified 29 million bi-allelic variants (31 % novel), including 19 million variants with a minor allele frequency (MAF) <0.5 %.
note: Abstract of the phase 1 WGS paper (Hum Genet 2016), read via Europe PMC; it does not split cases and controls. Definition sources give analysed subsets: PMC6201388 'performed low‐pass whole‐genome DNA sequencing on 1896 participants' (Table 1: 943 controls and 954 CAD cases) and CEC in '996 CAD‐free participants and 1000 patients with myocardial infarction'; PMC6587223 'phase 1, n=1964'.

label: Darmkrebs: Chancen der Verhütung durch Screening
counts: colorectal cancer patients and frequency-matched controls interviewed, recruited 2003-2020
quote: Smoking history and other known or suspected CRC risk factors were ascertained in detail in personal interviews among 6264 CRC patients and 6866 controls (frequency matched for age, sex, and county of residence) who were recruited in 2003-2020 in the DACHS study (Darmkrebs: Chancen der Verhütung durch Screening [German]; Colorectal Cancer: Chances for Prevention Through Screening [English]), a population-based case-control study from Germany.
note: PMID:36759940 (2023) is the most recent statement read; it gives cases and controls but no stated total, so participants is left null. Earlier counts: definition source PMC5946295 '3146 patients recruited between 2003 and 2010'; abstracts give 4410 cases and 3441 controls (PMID:34836419), 5104 cases and 4131 controls (PMID:35747198), 2,363 cases and 2,198 controls (PMID:29403313). The example study analysed 549 + 437 DACHS patients. The number is interviewed cases and controls; the case-only survival follow-up may count differently.

label: British Genetics of Hypertension study
counts: severely hypertensive families and affected sibling pairs (no participant total stated)
quote: Thirty-four additional microsatellites were genotyped in our severely hypertensive affected sibling pair resource (now 1635 families with 2142 affected sibling pairs), leading to a substantial increase in information content in the regions of interest.
note: No source read states a number of participants for BRIGHT as a whole; it counts families and affected sibling pairs. PMID:12826435 (2003): 'We phenotyped 2010 affected sibling pairs drawn from 1599 severely hypertensive families'; PMID:16754790 adds '712 distinct parent-offspring trios'. The definition's figure of about 2,000 normotensive controls was not found stated in the sources read (PMC2685752, the Nat Commun 2022 supplement, the example paper PMC10484788). A BRIGHT design paper giving the total of individuals (cases, relatives, controls) would settle it.

label: Genetic Investigation of ANthropometric Traits consortium
counts: individuals in the 2022 GIANT height GWAS meta-analysis (281 studies, GIANT and 23andMe)
quote: We performed genetic analysis of up to 5,380,080 individuals from 281 studies from the GIANT consortium and 23andMe.
note: Yengo et al. 2022 (PMID:36224396), listed on the GIANT website as a recent publication; the abstract rounds to 5.4 million. The trans-ancestry meta-analysis has n = 5,314,291. Counts include 23andMe participants. Other GIANT analyses: body fat distribution in 694,649 individuals (2019), height and BMI in ~700000 (2018). The example study used GIANT data with N = 210,323.

label: Hong Kong Degenerative Disc Disease Population Cohort
counts: volunteers of Southern Chinese origin aged 15-55 with lumbar MRI
quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted consisting of 2,943 volunteers of Southern Chinese origin (mean age: 41.1 years; range: 15-55 years; 59.6% women).
note: Abstract of Li et al. 2016 (Spine J), which the example paper (PMC8459317) cites as the cohort's reference; the full text is not open (doi 10.1016/j.spinee.2016.04.020 returned nothing). This may be the analysed sample rather than all recruited; the example paper gives no cohort total.

label: International Lung Cancer Consortium
counts: European-descent subjects genotyped in the ILCCO OncoArray project
quote: In this study, we analyzed OncoArray genotypic data of 36,000 subjects of European descent in ILCCO; among them, 17,037 provided individual epidemiological data and were of European descent.
note: Round figure as stated. The OncoArray GWAS paper (PMID:28604730, TRICL-ILCCO with the Lung Cancer Cohort Consortium) states '14,803 cases and 12,262 controls of European descent were genotyped on the OncoArray and combined with existing data for an aggregated genome-wide association study (GWAS) analysis of lung cancer in 29,266 cases and 56,450 controls'; no total is stated there and it includes non-ILCCO data. Earlier pooled analysis (PMC3002160): seven case-control studies, 799 BAC cases and 15,859 controls. ILCCO membership counts were not found.

label: Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project
counts: unique subjects with whole genomes in ADSP release 5 (58,507 genomes, 57 cohorts)
quote: Population breakdown for 57,302 unique subjects: 6,875 African Ancestry, 5,523 Asian, 15,390 Hispanic/Latino, 29,107 Non-Hispanic White, and 307 Other/Unknown.
note: Same page: 'Release 5 WGS: 58,507 genomes from 57 cohorts' and 'R5 WGS 58,507 samples (including R4) Released November 2024'. Release 4 (PMID:40407102): 36,361 WGS samples, '35,014 genetically unique participants'. Discovery phase (DSS page) had WES of 5,096 AD cases and 4,965 controls. Cases and controls for R5 not stated there.

label: Cebu Longitudinal Health and Nutrition Survey
counts: index children: singletons born 1983-1984 (mothers counted separately)
quote: Singletons born in a one-year (1983−84) period (n = 3080) form the cohort of index children followed to age 35 years, with surveys every 2 months for the first 2 years, and follow-up surveys in 1991, 1994, 1998, 2002, 2005, 2009 and 2018.
note: Same source (PMID:33865193): 'The CLHNS is a community-based study that recruited 3327 women from 33 randomly selected barangays (administrative units) from the 252 barangays that comprised Metro Cebu in 1982.' Which figure counts the cohort depends on whether mothers are counted; the index-child cohort is recorded. The 2011 cohort profile (PMID:20507864) was not read.

label: HerediGene Population Study
counts: participants enrolled as of 20 March 2023 (enrolment ongoing, target up to 500,000)
quote: As of March 20, 2023, 174,595 participants have enrolled in the study (from all 50 US states) and 165,119 samples have been shipped to deCODE or to IPG for analysis.
note: PMID:38222332. Recruitment was ongoing, so this is an interim count. PMC9693138 (2022): partnership 'to enroll up to 500,000 patients' and whole genome sequencing 'performed on 26,302 patients enrolled in the HerediGene Program' (sequenced subset). The example paper (PMC12807872) gives no cohort total.

label: Heart and Vascular Health Study
note: No source read states the size of the HVH study as a whole; it has several case groups (MI, stroke, VTE, AF) and a shared control group. Subsets seen: PMC11617231 (2024) '1430 participants with a first VTE from the HVH study'; Nature Genetics 2018 stroke GWAS supplement table lists HVH1 (681 cases, 1,331 controls) and HVH2 (124 cases, 570 controls) for stroke only; the example paper (PMC8769168) gives no HVH count. The NIHMS1835943 supplement was empty on disk. An HVH design paper (e.g. Psaty et al. on MI/stroke case-control methods) giving total cases per group and controls would settle it.

label: Intermountain Heart Collaborative Study
counts: unique subjects enrolled in the registry 1994-2012 (catheterisation patients)
quote: The INSPIRE biobank registry began in 1993 (19) and had a total of 19,000 unique subjects enrolled from 1994 to 2012.
note: Round figure as stated; covers the catheterisation-laboratory registry to 2012 only, before the renamed INSPIRE registry widened to any condition; no later total was found. Subsets: example paper PMC4302371 evaluated 5,294 ACS patients (2004-2009); PMID:29803983 studied 2996 angiography patients.

label: Johnston County Osteoarthritis Project
counts: original cohort enrolled 1991-1998 only; the 2003-2004 enrichment cohort (n = 1015) is additional
quote: Civilian, non-institutionalized residents aged 45+ years from six townships in Johnston County were enrolled between 1991 and 1998 (n = 3187, Original Cohort), and additional residents were enrolled from 2003 to 2004 (n = 1015, Enrichment Cohort).
note: No source read states the combined total of both enrolment waves, so only the original cohort is recorded; the enrichment cohort of 1015 is in the same quote (PMC8854450 agrees: n = 3187 and n = 1015). The Nature 2025 supplement (41586_2025_8771_MOESM1) gives 3187 at baseline 1991-1997 and 'An additional 1019 Johnston County residents' in 2003-2004, a discrepancy with 1015.

label: London Life Sciences Prospective Population Study
counts: Indian Asian and European men and women recruited 2003-2008 (approximate)
quote: The London Life Sciences Prospective Population Study (LOLIPOP) is a prospective cohort study of ~ 28000 Indian Asian and European men and women, recruited from the lists of 58 General Practitioners in West London, UK, between 2003 and 2008.
note: Approximate figure as stated (PMID:33413638, 2021). The 2016 source (PMID:27195708, PMC4873263) gives a more exact but split count with no stated total: 'an ongoing population-based cohort of 17,606 South Asian and 7,766 Northern European men and women, aged 35–75 years'. The example paper (PMC7610439) had no matching mention. A LOLIPOP profile paper stating the exact total would settle it.

label: Asian Skin Traits and Genetics Research
counts: women from Korea, Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia
quote: In this study, we established the ASTAGR (Asian Skin Traits and Genetics Research) cohort, comprising 2762 female participants from 4 Asian countries (Korea, Vietnam, Thailand, and Indonesia).
note: From the abstract of the cohort's establishing paper (Europe PMC); full text not cached, but the abstract states the cohort size directly.

label: Diet, Activity and Lifestyle Study
counts: colon cancer cases and controls who took part (1991-1994 colon study)
quote: Of the cases who were asked to participate in the study, 76% (n = 1,993) cooperated, of whom 83% (n = 1,676) provided a blood sample for DNA extraction. Controls in DALS were frequency matched to cases by 5-year age groups and sex. Controls from KPMCP were randomly selected from membership lists. In Utah, controls who were under 65 years of age were randomly selected from lists generated using random-digit dialing and driver license lists, and those 65 years of age and older were randomly selected from Health Care Financing Administration lists. In Minnesota, control participants were identified from drivers license or state identification lists. Of the controls asked to participate, 64% (n = 2,410) cooperated, of whom 85% (n = 2,004) provided a blood sample for DNA extraction.
note: No source read states a combined total, so participants is left null; cases and controls are for the original colon cancer study only (the 1997-2001 rectal cancer extension is not counted here). Analysed subsets seen: 1,461 white cases and 1,813 controls (PMC3017062, PMC3005543); non-Hispanic white colon 1470/1837 and rectal 583/775 (PMC3913564). The original DALS design paper (Slattery et al. 1997, cited as ref 34) would give the full colon and rectal numbers.

label: Invecchiare in Chianti
counts: participants recruited at baseline, aged 20-102
quote: In brief, a total of 1453 participants spanning various age groups were recruited at baseline in 1998–2000 via two-stage sampling methods and then followed longitudinally.
note: The design paper (PMID:11129752) abstract gives the same number: 1,453 persons aged 20-102, 91.6% of the eligible. Later analyses use subsets of this baseline.

label: Japan Multi-Institutional Collaborative Cohort Study
counts: adults aged 35-69 in the baseline survey
quote: After excluding 8,294 respondents under 35 or over 70 years of age and 578 who withdrew consent or became ineligible, the remaining 92,610 participants (40,880 men and 51,730 women with an average age of 55.2 [standard deviation, 9.4] years) in the baseline survey were included in the present analysis (the dataset was fixed on February 2, 2020).
note: From the cohort profile (Takeuchi et al., J Epidemiol, PMC8593573). The abstract says 'The baseline survey included 92,610 adults'. The count excludes the Kanagawa region, whose baseline survey of 5,000 participants was still ongoing; 90,319 consented to biospecimen use.

label: Nijmegen Bladder Cancer Study
counts: analysed subset: Caucasian bladder cancer patients and Nijmegen Biomedical Study controls
quote: This study included 1809 UBC patients (81% male) and 4370 controls (45% male).
note: No source read gives the whole study's enrolment or a combined total, so participants is null; cases and controls are the analysed subset (self-reported Caucasian, controls who completed questionnaires 1-3). Other NBCS subsets seen: 1,385 cases and 4,754 controls (hair dye study, PMC3369132); 1,602 patients with clinical data (PMC3934869); 1,859 patients (PMC5865728). The controls come from the Nijmegen Biomedical Study, whose 2002 survey had 9,350 participants. The design paper (Kiemeney et al. 2008) or the NBCS website would settle the full number.

label: Norwegian Breast Cancer Study
note: No sentence read states the size of the Norwegian Breast Cancer Study. Read: PMC5065698 (116 normal breast samples and 241 tumours from NBCS used for expression analysis only), the example paper PMC9006574 (NBCS only as investigators), and the supplement of PMC4754625 (BCAC study description; its Supplementary Table 2 has table cells for NBCS such as 1,712 / 1,898 / 3,610, apparently cases / controls / total genotyped by TNBCC, but no sentence states them and the column headers are not unambiguous). A BCAC study-description table with explicit headers, or a Norwegian design paper (Ullevål / Radium Hospital / Haukeland case series), would settle it.

label: QSkin Sun and Health Study
counts: men and women aged 40-69 sampled in 2011
quote: The QSkin Sun and Health Study comprises a cohort of 43 794 men and women aged 40-69 years randomly sampled from the population of Queensland, Australia in 2011.
note: From the cohort profile abstract (Olsen et al. 2012, Int J Epidemiol); full text not cached but the abstract states the number directly.

label: RIKEN Study
counts: knee osteoarthritis cases and controls genotyped in the GWAS
quote: We examined 906 individuals with knee OA and 3,396 control individuals (Table 1) using Illumina HumanHap550v3 Genotyping BeadChip.
note: No source states a combined total, so participants is null. The 2025 GO consortium supplement (41586_2025_8771_MOESM1_ESM.pdf) gives rounded figures: 'The Japanese cohort of knee osteoarthritis GWAS (disease cohort) consists of 900 cases and 3,400 controls.' The 2010 paper's Table 1 lists 899 RIKEN cases after QC (seven excluded for call rate); a separate replication set of 167 cases and 347 controls is not counted here.

label: RIKEN cohort
counts: sunitinib-treated metastatic renal cell carcinoma patients recruited
quote: For the RIKEN cohort, a total of 219 mRCC patients treated with sunitinib were recruited from 15 Japanese medical institutes.
note: The earlier pharmacogenetic paper (PMID:26914831) agrees: 'A total of 219 RCC patients were recruited to this pharmacogenetic study.'; 216 of them received sunitinib in its toxicity analysis.

label: Swedish Mammography Cohort
counts: women who took part at the 1987-1990 baseline
quote: Ultimately, 66,651 women participated in SMC in 1987–1990 (74% response rate).
note: The definition source (PMID:42319504) says 90,303 women were invited in 1987-1990 (74% response rate) and 39,227 completed the 1997 FFQ, without stating the number who took part. PMC11663681 (PMID:39717036) gives 66,651 participants; PMC4365521 instead calls 66,651 the eligible women of whom 74% responded, so sources disagree on whether 66,651 is participants or eligible. The SMC design paper or the SMC website would settle it.

label: Shanghai Men's Health Study
counts: men aged 40-74 enrolled 2002-2006
quote: By June 2006, 83033 potential eligible men had been approached for the study; 61480 were enrolled, an overall response rate of 74.0%.
note: From the cohort profile (PMID:25733578); the abstract gives the same number: 'a population-based cohort study of 61,480 men aged 40-74 years, launched in 2002'.

label: VITamins And Lifestyle Study
counts: baseline questionnaires passing quality control, 2000-2002
quote: Of these, 77 719 questionnaires passed quality control checks in the VITAL study.
note: Same paper: 364,418 questionnaires mailed, 79,300 (21.8%) responded; 77,719 passed quality control, which is the usual VITAL cohort size. This paper analysed 66,806 participants. The design paper (White et al. 2004) would confirm the enrolled number.

label: Western Australian Sleep Health Study
counts: prospective sleep clinic cohort patients with questionnaire, PSG and blood (lower bound only)
quote: To date, data has been collected on over 4,000 OSA patients with questionnaire, PSG, and blood samples with data checking and cleaning proceeding with further uploading of clinical data into the database on schedule to be completed by mid-2011.
note: The cohort paper (PMID:21318257) gives only lower bounds, so participants is null: 'over 4,000 OSA patients' (quoted), 'over 3,000 individuals' towards a target of 4,000 in the abstract, and 'over 3,500 subjects with diagnosed OSA' with clean data on the first 2,637 European-Australian subjects. The separate WASHS sleep study database covers about 20,000 individuals (over 30,000 PSG studies since 1988). The genetic papers analysed 1,647 WASHS European-Australians (PMC6467367 Table 2, replication). A later WASHS profile would give the achieved size.

label: European Medical Information Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Multimodal Biomarker Discovery study
counts: people with normal cognition, MCI or AD-type dementia pooled from 11 cohorts
quote: In total, 1221 subjects were included in the study, with a mean age of 67.9 (SD 8.3) years.
note: From the design paper (Bos et al. 2018, PMC6035398): 492 with normal cognition, 527 MCI and 202 AD-type dementia, drawn from 11 European cohorts; plasma for 1189, DNA for 929, MRI for 862 and CSF for 767.

label: NHLBI Family Heart Study
counts: family members examined at baseline
quote: In short, a total of 5710 subjects participated in baseline clinical examinations from 1993 to 1995.
note: The design paper (PMID:8651220) abstract gives families rather than people: 657 high-risk and 588 randomly sampled families had clinic examinations. The Family Heart SCAN follow-up re-examined a subset and added HyperGEN African Americans; not counted here. Analysed subsets seen: 2,396 and 2,421 Caucasian participants (PMC2409301), 1,991 (PMC8224703).

label: Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome Study
counts: pregnant women who completed the 75 g OGTT, 2000-2006
quote: Of the eligible women across 15 centers in nine countries, 28,562 agreed to participate, 25,505 of whom completed the OGTT, leaving 23,316 available for analysis following further filtering [ 19 ].
note: 25,505 is the number usually given as HAPO's size: PMC10302619 says HAPO 'recruited 25,505 participants' and PMC12281978 that 'a total of 25,505 pregnant individuals underwent a 75-g OGTT'. 28,562 agreed to participate and 23,316 were in the main analysis. The definition sources (PMID:39849370) say only 'HAPO enrolled > 25,000 pregnant individuals'. The main HAPO paper (NEJM 2008, PMID:18463375) was not read.

label: Catheterization Genetics
counts: patients in the CATHGEN biorepository
quote: The Institutional Review Board for an academic medical center in the southeastern U.S. approved the primary CATHGEN cohort biorepository (N = 9334) [19], the GWAS substudy of the first 2203 participants >18 years of age enrolled in CATHGEN [20], [21], and the present sex-stratified GWAS screen (N = 684).
note: Subsets seen: GWAS substudy of the first 2,203 participants; metabolite GWAS of 1,490 plus 2,022 (3,512) in the example paper (PMC4634848). The biorepository description (Kraus et al. 2015, ref 19) would give the recruitment period.

label: Colorectal Cancer Genetics & Genomics
counts: CRCGEN cases and controls with genetic data (both component case-control studies)
quote: This study population consisted of 3619 participants from 2 observational studies for whom genetic data were available: Colorectal Cancer Genetics & Genomics (CRCGEN; n = 1801) and Colorectal Cancer Screening (COLSCREEN; n = 1818).
note: Same paper, per component study: Bellvitge 1996-1998 'recruited incident pathology-confirmed CRC cases (n = 304) and age and sex frequency-matched hospital controls (n = 293)'; Bellvitge and León 2007-2015 'recruited a total of 633 incident CRC cases (313 Bellvitge and 320 León) and 571 population controls'. Combined cases (937 from CRCGEN) are stated in a later sentence; combined controls are not stated, so cases and controls are left null. The 1,801 counts those with genetic data.

label: Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Carlantino
counts: people from Carlantino (approximate)
quote: INGI-CAR consisted of about 1000 subjects who were drawn from Carlantino, an isolated village of southern Italy.
note: Quote is from 41467_2022_32821_MOESM1_ESM.pdf (Supplementary Information of PMC9436946) inside the Europe PMC supplementary archive; the source gives an approximate number. Genotyped subsets seen: 370 (PMC4997959), 373 (PMC10178705), 124 whole genomes.

label: EPIC-InterAct Study
counts: case-cohort: verified incident type 2 diabetes cases and a random subcohort
quote: A total of 12,403 verified incident cases of type 2 diabetes occurred during 3.99 million person-years of follow-up of 340,234 EPIC participants eligible for InterAct. We defined a centre-stratified subcohort of 16,154 individuals for comparative analyses.
note: Case-cohort design: 12,403 cases and a subcohort of 16,154 (not controls: 778 subcohort members became cases and count in both), drawn from 340,234 eligible EPIC participants. No source read states the combined number of distinct participants, so participants is null. The design paper also says 2,577 verified Danish cases were excluded for logistical reasons. A later analysis (PMID:32641421) used 9,754 cases and a subcohort of 13,662.

label: Leipzig Adults
counts: Metabochip-genotyped adults passing QC in a height GWAS supplement (analysed subset)
quote: Leipzig Adults Leipzig adults Population- based 1005 ≥95% 1) ethnic outliers 2) gender discordance 1,005 measured
note: A study-description table row (Nature Genetics ng.3097 supplement): 1,005 samples genotyped on Metabochip, 1,005 after QC with measured height. The same supplement's trait table has 399-400 men and 591-592 women with age and BMI. No design or profile paper of the Leipzig Adults sample was found; the definition sources' supplementary tables (PMC7610958 supplementary xlsx, figshare 12933737, ng 2017 MOESM3 xlsx) were not downloaded. Whole-sample number unknown; the definition's 'about 900' is ExomeChip-analysis-sized.

label: Swiss Study on Air Pollution and Lung Diseases in Adults
counts: adults examined at baseline in 1991 (SAPALDIA 1)
quote: The pattern of participation and the 9651 participants of the study, representing 59.3% of the sample, are described.
note: Methods-and-participation paper of the baseline survey. The SAPALDIA 2 follow-up paper (PMID:16167509): of 9651 participants examined in 1991, 8715 traced, 283 died, 8047 gave basic health information, 6528 agreed to the health examination and 5973 completed the entire protocol.

label: Bunkyo Health Study
counts: older adults enrolled in the registry (2015-2018)
quote: The Bunkyo Health Study registry initially enrolled 1629 individuals.
note: Stated by a Bunkyo Health Study paper. The example study (PMID:38769351) analysed 1607 samples after QC (678 men, 929 women).

label: Shimane CoHRE Study
note: An ongoing programme of annual community health examinations; no source read states how many people it has enrolled overall. Papers report only analysed subsets: the example GWAS (PMID:38769351) used 1007 samples from the 1st cohort and 838 from the 2nd cohort after QC; PMID:35010674 used data from 738 participants in 2018. A Europe PMC search found no cohort profile or design paper; a CoHRE website or profile stating total participants would settle it.

label: Fangchenggang Area Male Health and Examination Survey
counts: men surveyed at routine physical examination, Sept-Dec 2009
quote: A comprehensive demographic and health survey was conducted among a consecutive series of 4303 men participating in the routine physical examination at the Medical Centre in Fangchenggang First People’s Hospital from September 2009 to December 2009.
note: The example study (PMID:35501403) repeats 'FAMHES included 4303 Chinese males aged 17–88 years old at baseline' and analysed 1800 of them in its GWAS.

label: Italian Network of Genetic Isolates - Friuli Venezia Giulia
counts: subjects from the Genetic Park of Friuli Venezia Giulia project (approximate)
quote: The INGI-FVG cohort consisted of about 1700 subjects drawn from the project “Genetic Park of Friuli Venezia Giulia”.
note: Cohort description in the supplement of the ECG-traits GWAS (Nat Commun 2022, PMC9436946), an 'about' figure. Analysed subsets elsewhere: 1073 individuals in a sweet-liking replication (PMC10178705), 378 whole genomes (PMC7080768), 339 in the example study (PMID:35580588). No FVG design paper was read.

label: Osteoarthritis Initiative
counts: men and women aged 45-79 recruited 2004-2006
quote: The OAI cohort of 4,796 participants is 58% female and ranged in age from 45-79 at time of recruitment.
note: The OAI's own NIAMS page; the definition source PMID:23372535 (PMC3295933) says the same: 'The OAI cohort of 4,796 subjects is 58% female and ranged in age from 45 to 79 at the time of their recruitment.'

label: SWOG Cancer Research Network
note: A trials network rather than a pooled study; no source read gives a total of participants or a flagship pooled analysis. PMC7064039 counts 23 328 enrollments onto 63 SWOG therapeutic trials for selected cancers in 2004-2013 (a subset, and enrollments not people). The SWOG website (swog.org/about/history-impact) gives only its community of more than 20,000 people at over 1,300 hospitals, clinics and cancer centres (investigators and sites, not participants). Member trials such as SELECT and PCPT have their own sizes.

label: Leeds Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls in the UK-CCSG dataset, recruitment 1997-2013
quote: Overall, the UK-CCSG dataset consisted of 1910 cases and 1275 controls and the NIH-CCFR dataset consisted of 1415 cases and 986 controls.
note: From a definition source (PLoS One 2018, PMID:29425227) by the study's own group; the paper included only self-reported non-Hispanic white individuals, so the figures may be slightly below the full enrolment. No sentence states a total. The original report (PMID:12584178) described the first phase as 'A study of 500 incident colorectal cancer cases and population controls'.

label: North Carolina Colon Cancer Study
counts: interviewed cases and controls, reported per phase only
note: No source read states a total over both phases, so none is recorded. PMID:19336553 (PMC2709952): 'A total of 1691 individuals (643 cases, 1048 controls) completed interviews for the NCCCS I' and 'For the NCCCS II, 2061 interviews were completed (1045 cases and 1016 controls).' PMID:19842051 (PMC2809818) gives the same NCCCS II figures: 'A total of 2061 people completed interviews (1045 cases and 1016 controls)'. Tumour-based analyses use subsets (503 colon cancer cases in PMC4067325; 485 in PMC6013500).

label: Alpha-Tocopherol, Beta-Carotene Cancer Prevention Study
counts: male smokers aged 50-69 randomised 1985-1988
quote: Male Finnish smokers (N = 29,133) ages 50–69 years were assigned to receive either alpha-tocopherol (dl-α-tocopheryl-acetate, 50 mg/day), beta-carotene (20 mg/day), both vitamins, or placebo for 5–8 years (a median of 6.1 years).
note: PMC12329778 agrees: '29,133 male Finnish smokers, aged 50–69 years at recruitment between 1985 and 1988'. The original trial reports were not read.

label: Growth and Obesity Chilean Cohort Study
counts: children recruited in 2006 at about 3.5 years
quote: This is a longitudinal follow-up of 1195 individuals recruited in 2006 (aged 3.5 years old) at different childcare centers from the South East Area of Santiago, Chile.
note: The definition source and example study; no separate cohort profile was read.

label: Health Examinees Study
counts: participants at baseline, 2004-2013
quote: KoGES_HEXA (n¼173357)
note: From a table heading in the KoGES cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2017, PMID:27085081); '¼' is the PDF text layer's rendering of '='. The profile's Table 1 lists the same n (59,294 men, 114,063 women). The example study (PMID:38060535) says 'Among the 173,208 people who were included in the HEXA-based survey', of whom 58,700 with genetic data were used.

label: Newfoundland Colorectal Cancer Registry
counts: consenting colorectal cancer cases diagnosed under 75 in a 5-year period (1999-2003)
quote: In a 5-year period we examined every case of CRC diagnosed under the age of 75 years and obtained consent from 730 cases.
note: Registry design paper. Later papers differ: PMC4393623 (2015) says 'between 1999–2003, a total of 750 participants were recruited to NFCCR'. The population-based case-control study (PMID:21033532): 'A total of 702 cases and 717 controls consented to participate in the study and completed a set of self-administered questionnaires.' The genetic survival studies analysed about 500 patients.

label: Toshiba cohort
counts: employees who had provided genetic samples to the company (by 2024)
quote: We recruited study participants from 11 605 employees who had already provided genetic samples to the company.
note: From a sodium-reduction trial run at the company in 2024 (JAMA Netw Open, PMC12531883); the cohort has no profile paper. The example study (PMID:40222985) genotyped 2,751 participants, 2,554 passing QC, for its booster side-effect GWAS.

label: Women's Health Initiative Memory Study
counts: genotyped subjects released in dbGaP phs000675 (WHIMS+ GWAS)
quote: "cnt_subjects":{"loaded":5740
note: A field of the dbGaP study summary (consent groups HMB-IRB 5167 and HMB-IRB-NPU 573 subjects), not a sentence; the dbGaP page is script-rendered. Analysed subsets: 5,637 WHIMS participants in a VTE GWAS (Nat Genet 2019 supplement, 41588_2019_519_MOESM1) and 5,202 white WHIMS women after QC (Transl Psychiatry 2025 supplement, 41398_2025_3418_MOESM1). The parent WHI Memory Study trial enrolled 7,479 women (the definition), not read here.

label: WHI SNP Health Association Resource
counts: randomly selected African American and Hispanic WHI women
quote: The genome wide association study (GWAS) non-overlapping samples are composed of a case- control study (WHI Genomics and Randomized Trials Network – GARNET, which included all coronary heart disease, stroke, venous thromboembolic events and selected diabetes cases that happened during the active intervention phase in the WHI HT clinical trials and aged matched controls), women selected to be "representative" of the HT trial (mostly younger white HT subjects that were also enrolled in the WHI memory study - WHIMS) and the WHI SNP Health Association Resource (WHI SHARe), a randomly selected sample of 8,515 African American and 3,642 Hispanic women from WHI.
note: The source gives 8,515 African American and 3,642 Hispanic women but no total, so participants is left null. The dbGaP summary of phs000386 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gap/sstr/api/v1/study/phs000386/summary) lists "cnt_subjects":{"loaded":12010, which includes 3 non-participant genotype-control subjects (consent group NRUP). After QC the same supplement analysed 7,919 African American and 3,377 Hispanic SHARe women.

label: Isle of Wight Whole Population Birth Cohort
counts: children enrolled with parental consent for the longitudinal study (born 1989-1990)
quote: Parental consent was obtained from 1456 of the 1536 children for inclusion into a longitudinal study of asthma and allergic disease (Figure 1).
note: Cohort profile. The 1509 mothers gave birth to 1536 children on the island during recruitment, and parents of all 1536 gave basic birth information; 1456 were enrolled for follow-up. PMID:31831580 also gives n=1456.

label: Starr County Health Studies
counts: individuals aged 20+ screened in the 2002-2006 household survey (one component of the programme)
quote: Household screening of 5230 individuals aged 20 years and above followed by direct physical assessment of 1610 identified 23.7 % of men and 26.7 % of women with type 2 diabetes, 46.2 and 49.5 % of men and women, respectively with obesity and 32.1 and 32.4 % with hypertension.
note: The programme has several collections and no source gives a total over them. The same paper enumerated 8729 individuals in 2507 households in 2002-2004 and examined 1251 (1610 physically assessed per its abstract). The 1983 survey (PMID:6637993) sampled 14% of the county but its abstract gives no count. The diabetes case collections: PMID:21647700 selected 990 cases and 990 controls for genotyping (1345 oral glucose tolerance tests in the survey).

label: International Multicentre ADHD Genetics project
counts: probands with combined-type ADHD (IMAGE I), besides siblings and parents
quote: Behavioural data were collected from 1068 probands with the combined type of attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD-CT) and 1446 'unselected' siblings.
note: No total of all family members is stated; 1446 unselected siblings were also assessed and parents gave DNA. The same paper speaks of 'behavioural data from 1400 European sibling pairs'. An earlier report used a stage I sample of 680 families (PMC1559631); the first GWAS used 909 trios. IMAGE II and the ADHD meta-analysis (PMID:20732625: 2,064 trios, 896 cases and 2,455 controls) pool other samples.

label: Family Blood Pressure Program
counts: participants in the FBPP pooled database (version 3) from the 4 networks
quote: The FBPP pooled database (version 3) of 13,592 participants from 4 different networks represents one of the largest compilations of ethnically diverse data.
note: The 2002 programme description (PMID:11799070) says the pooled data set holds phenotype and genotype information from ">11 000 individuals"; the 2005 example study (PMID:16076393) gives the later, achieved size of the pooled database. Aggregation of GenNet, GENOA, HyperGEN and SAPPHIRe.

label: Women's Health Study
counts: women randomised in the aspirin and vitamin E trial
quote: The Women’s Health Study (WHS) was a randomized, double-blind, clinical trial of low-dose aspirin and vitamin E in the primary prevention of CVD and cancer among 39,876 apparently healthy women age ≥45 years.
note: The same paper says blood samples were collected from 28,263 randomized women (71.1% of participants). The trial's main reports (Ridker et al. 2005, PMID:15753114; Lee et al. 2005, PMID:15998891) were not read.

label: Genetics and Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Consortium
counts: participants with individual-level data managed by the coordinating center, from 70 studies (stated as over 130,000)
quote: The GECCO coordinating center manages individual level genetic and epidemiological data of over 130,000 participants from 70 studies from North America, Australia, Asia, and Europe.
note: A lower bound from the consortium's website, not a pooled count for a named flagship analysis. The example study (PMID:38408508) analysed the pooled GECCO dataset of 3135 early-onset cases and 29 495 controls, a subset; a larger meta-analysis it cites (100,204 cases and 154,587 controls) combines GECCO with other consortia and was not read.

label: Prostate Cancer Association Group to Investigate Cancer-Associated Alterations in the Genome
counts: prostate cancer cases and controls of European ancestry in the 2018 OncoArray GWAS meta-analysis
quote: We performed a fixed-effects meta-analysis combining the summary statistics from our OncoArray analysis and seven previous PrCa GWAS or high-density SNP panels of European ancestry imputed to the 1KGP The final meta-analysis included 79,194 PrCa cases and 61,112 controls without a known diagnosis of PrCa (Fig. 1).
note: PMID:29892016 (Schumacher et al. 2018), the consortium's main European-ancestry meta-analysis; no sentence states the total, so participants is left null. Other PRACTICAL analyses read: 13 groups in 2008 (PMID:18708398); 20,848 cases and 20,214 controls from 22 studies in the 2015 Mendelian randomisation study (PMC4596899; table title n = 41,062); 10 404 participants from 14 study groups in the 2021 ATM sequencing study (PMC8381233). The example study (PMID:37340002) only used PRACTICAL summary statistics.

label: Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort
counts: participants enrolled 2004-2010
quote: Results Among 14530 participants enrolled in the MEC study, 11101 individuals completed survey questionnaires and attended the health examination.
note: From the example study (PMID:31110091), whose abstract also gives n=14 530 recruited 2004-2010; it analysed 10215 of them. The COHO definition gives 14,465, presumably from the cohort profile (PMID:29452397, IJE 2018), whose text could not be read (only the title is cached; the OUP PDF returned 403). The profile would settle which figure is the cohort's own.

label: ADDITION-Denmark
counts: people with screen-detected type 2 diabetes in the trial, 2001-2006
quote: Between 2001 and 2006, 1615 individuals were found with screen-detected diabetes in ADDITION-Denmark practices.
note: The trial population (routine care 669, intensive treatment 524, intensive treatment plus motivational interviewing 422, per Table 1). The same paper also followed 2655 individuals with non-diabetic hyperglycaemia found by screening. No sentence read gives the number screened. The ADDITION-Europe 5-year report (PMID:21705063, PMC3136726) counts Denmark as n=1533 of the 3057 patients who agreed to take part in the European trial.

label: Anglo-Danish-Dutch Study of Intensive Treatment in People with Screen Detected Diabetes in Primary Care
counts: screen-detected patients with type 2 diabetes who agreed to take part
quote: Screening identified 3233 patients with type 2 diabetes, of whom 3057 agreed to take part (Denmark, n=1533; Cambridge, UK, n=867; Netherlands, n=498; and Leicester, UK, n=159).
note: The trial report (PMID:21705063): 343 general practices were randomised; primary endpoint data were available for 3055 of the 3057 participants.

label: Montreal Heart Institute Biobank
counts: participants recruited by February 2015 (the 20,000th participant milestone; recruitment ongoing, target 30,000)
quote: a 26-year-old patient, has become the 20,000th participant in the Montreal Heart Institute Biobank.
note: A February 2015 press release (the sentence opens with the patient's name, left out of the quote); the next sentence says the Biobank aims to recruit 30,000 volunteer patients, and a September 2015 release (newswire.ca) speaks of long-term follow-up for some 30,000 patients, a target. No design paper with an achieved size was found; the definition sources describe the MHI Hospital Cohort without a total. The example study (PMID:41022758) used 15,177 unrelated genotyped individuals from the biobank, an analysed subset. A current figure from the MHI biobank website (its pages redirected to the home page) or a cohort profile would settle it.

label: Exeter Family Study of Childhood Health
counts: families recruited (1017), not individual participants
quote: We recruited 1017 families from a postcode-defined area in central Exeter.
note: Only the abstract of the protocol paper (Paediatr Perinat Epidemiol 2006, closed) could be read; it counts families (both parents and child), not people, so participants is left null. The example study (PMID:42225636) names EFSOCH among its cohorts without a count. The protocol paper's full text, or a later EFSOCH paper giving numbers of mothers, fathers and offspring, would settle it.

label: Global Lipids Genetics Consortium
counts: individuals from 201 primary studies in the 2021 multi-ancestry lipid GWAS meta-analysis
quote: The Global Lipids Genetics Consortium aggregated GWAS results from 1,654,960 individuals from 201 primary studies representing five genetic ancestry groups: Admixed African or African (AdmAFR, N=99.4k, 6.0% of sample), East Asian (EAS, N=146.5k, 8.9%), European (EUR, N=1.32m, 79.8%), Hispanic (HIS, N=48.1k, 2.9%), and South Asian (SAS, N=41.0k, 2.5%) (Table 1, Supplementary Table 1, Supplementary Figure 1).
note: PMID:34887591 (Graham et al. 2021); the abstract rounds it to approximately 1.65 million individuals, including 350,000 of non-European ancestries. Earlier GLGC rounds were smaller and were not read.

label: Molecular Epidemiology of Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: participants genotyped (colorectal cancer cases and controls); a subset of all enrolled
quote: DNA samples from 10,364 MECC participants (5,581 CRC cases and 4,783 controls) were genotyped using four platforms.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:38664626), which describes MECC as recruited in northern Israel 1998-2017 but gives no enrolment total; the genotyped set is the largest count it states. Its T cell analysis used 2,876 tumours. The study's design reference (ref. 45 of that paper) was not read and would give the full enrolment.

label: Nurses' Health Study II
counts: female registered nurses aged 25-42 recruited in 1989
quote: Started in 1989, NHSII recruited 116,429 female registered nurses ages 25–42 from 14 states with large numbers of registered nurses.
note: From the definition source PMID:38677085 (aircraft noise and obesity in NHS and NHSII), which cites the cohort descriptions (Bao et al. 2016); those were not read. The other definition source (PMID:34450027) describes NHS II without a count.

label: National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism cohort
counts: healthy controls: 119 European American and 82 African American (no total stated)
quote: The sample consisted of 119 European American (EA) and 82 African American (AA) healthy controls that were recruited at the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), USA.
note: From the supplementary cohort descriptions of the definition source (PMID:34187551, Additional file 1). The sentence gives the two ancestry groups separately and no total, so participants is left null. After QC the GWAS analysed 103 EA and 75 AA individuals. The cohort's earlier publication (ref. 82 of that supplement) was not read and might state a total.

label: Southern Community Cohort Study
counts: adults aged 40-79 enrolled March 2002 to September 2009
quote: From March 25, 2002, to September 24, 2009, 84,735 adults aged 40–79 y were enrolled from 12 southeastern states.
note: From a 2015 PLOS Medicine SCCS analysis (healthy eating and mortality), not the cohort's own design paper (PMID:16080667, not read). The definition sources give approximations: ~85,000 enrolled (PMC12973162, PMID:41609390) and approximately 86,000 adults recruited (PMC12940208, PMID:41909911).

label: Taiwan Precision Medicine Initiative
counts: participants recruited who consented to DNA genotyping and EMR access
quote: Here we present the Taiwan Precision Medicine Initiative (TPMI), established by Academia Sinica in collaboration with 16 major medical centres around Taiwan, which has recruited 565,390 participants who consent to provide DNA samples for genetic profiling and grant access to their electronic medical records (EMRs) for research.
note: The cohort's own description paper (PMC12675286). The example study (PMID:41810385) drew 4381 Parkinson's disease cases and 43,810 controls from 463,447 TPMI participants, an earlier or analysed subset.

label: Baependi Heart Study
counts: participants with cross-sectional data (1691 at 2005 baseline plus 548 added in 2010)
quote: Cross-sectional data have been collected for 2239 participants.
note: Cohort profile (BMJ Open 2016, PMC5093390): 'At baseline, the study evaluated 1691 individuals across 95 families.' and 'In the 2010 follow-up, 548 individuals were added'; the full text also says 'Taken together, baseline measurements represent 2239 individuals.' The example study (PMID:36267918) gives no Baependi total in the text read.

label: Born in Guangzhou Cohort Study
counts: pregnant women consenting (17,214 pregnancies) by April 2016; recruitment ongoing
quote: By April 2016, we had approached 22,569 eligible pregnancies, of which 17,214 (from 17,050 women) provided consent (participation rate 76.3%).
note: Cohort profile (PMID:28321694, Eur J Epidemiol 2017), an interim count: recruitment was to continue until December 2018 towards a target of 30,000 mother-child pairs; 14,696 live births by 30 April 2016; 4080 partners participated. The example study (PMID:38297123) sequenced 4,053 BIGCS individuals, an analysed subset. A later BIGCS profile update would give the achieved size.
