label: Genetics, Osteoarthritis and Progression Study
counts: patients in 192 Caucasian sibling pairs included at baseline
quote: In this cohort, 192 Caucasian sib-pairs (384 patients), aged 40 to 70 years were included.
note: From the definition source (PLoS One 2011, GARP progression study); 117 patients completed its 2007-2008 follow-up. The original GARP description (Riyazi et al. 2005, ref. 12) was not read. The example study (PMID:34450027) names GARP without a count.

label: Physicians' Health Study
counts: US male physicians randomised in PHS I (1982) only; no combined PHS I and II total stated
quote: PHS I was initiated in 1982 and was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 22,071 US male physicians aged 40–84 years aimed at evaluating the impact of aspirin and beta-carotene on cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cancer outcomes, respectively [22].
note: From the definition source (PMID:38893188). The same paper says PHS II (1996) 'included 7641 PHS I participants plus an additional 7000 US male physicians aged ≥50 years' and counts 14,641 PHS II participants; no sentence gives the total of distinct physicians across both trials, so the PHS I figure is given. The example study (PMID:37555839) was not needed for the count.

label: Trinity Student Study
counts: eligible young adults who consented and completed the questionnaire, 2003-2004
quote: Briefly, 2508 individuals were eligible to participate, gave written informed consent, and completed a questionnaire including parameters of age, sex, height, weight, dietary habits (meat eating, vegetarian, or vegan), micronutrient intake from supplements and fortified foods, usual alcohol intake, smoking status, and contraceptive use among female participants.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:36774100); plasma inositol was measured in 2064 individuals (the abstract's '>2000'). The earlier TSS descriptions it cites (refs 36-38) were not read.

label: Yale-Penn study
counts: participants recruited (5758 African American, 5681 European American)
quote: The discovery sample was derived from the Yale-Penn sample, a cohort of 11,439 participants (5758 AAs and 5681 EAs) recruited through treatment centers and advertisements for genetic studies of cocaine, opioid or alcohol dependence11.
note: From the 2021 stimulant-dependence GWAS (PMID:34226506), which describes the whole Yale-Penn sample (Yale-Penn 1-3). PMID:30655502 (2019) reports 8318 subjects with genotype and phenotype data in Yale-Penn 1-2 only. No dedicated design paper read.

label: Cardiovascular Disease Association Study
counts: participants enrolled at baseline, 2005-2011
quote: KoGES_CAVAS (n = 28338)
note: From a table header in the KoGES cohort profile (PMID:27085081), whose Table 1 also gives n 28338 for KoGES_CAVAS; the profile says follow-up was run in 6 of 11 counties (baseline number from those six = 21 715). Two 2025-2026 papers state one fewer: 'CAVAS (2005–2012) enrolled 28,337 individuals aged ≥ 40 years from rural areas' (PMID:40405233) and 'The CAVAS cohort included 28,337 participants aged 40–69 years' (PMID:42158258).

label: China Health and Nutrition Survey
counts: individuals in the 2011 survey wave (5,884 households, 288 communities)
quote: By the last survey in 2011 the CHNS included at the primary sampling unit (province/autonomous city) 12 sample units and at the secondary sampling unit (community) 288 communities with 27,447 individuals from 5,884 households, including 60 urban neighborhoods, 60 suburban neighborhoods, 42 towns, and 126 villages.
note: From the CHNS 1989-2011 profile (PMID:24341753). This is the sample of one wave, not the cumulative number ever surveyed; the same paper's table gives 3,926 households / 14,799 individuals in 1991. No cumulative count read; a later CHNS profile or the CHNS website would give it.

label: 300-Obese
counts: overweight or obese adults enrolled (BMI 27 or more)
quote: A total of 302 individuals with a body mass index greater than or equal to 27 kg/m2 participated.
note: From the 300-OB aldosterone paper (PMC7320834, a definition source). Agrees with PMC9753387: '300OB is an obese cohort of 302 individuals aged 54–81 years old'; that paper analysed 294 of them.

label: Anti-Amyloid Treatment in Asymptomatic Alzheimer's Disease Study
counts: participants randomised (578 solanezumab, 591 placebo)
quote: A total of 1169 persons underwent randomization: 578 were assigned to the solanezumab group and 591 to the placebo group.
note: From the abstract of the A4 primary-results paper (NEJM 2023), read via Europe PMC. The definition source PMID:41569280 reports 'There were 4486 pre-randomization participants who were screened for the A4 study and underwent amyloid PET scanning.'

label: Child and Adolescent Twin Study in Sweden
counts: twins whose parents completed the age 9/12 interview
quote: By May 2019, 16,476 parental interviews concerning 32,952 twins had been completed, with an overall response rate of 69%.
note: From the 2019 Swedish Twin Registry update (PMID:31747977), the most recent count read. The 2011 CATSS profile (PMID:22506305) reported 'By January 2010, 8,610 parental interviews concerning 17,220 twins had been completed, with an overall response rate of 80%.' Recruitment is ongoing.

label: CLUE II
counts: participants at the 1989 baseline
quote: At the baseline visit (1989 for CLUE II), brief medical histories, blood pressure readings, and blood samples were collected on 32,894 participants (25,076 of which were residents of Washington County).
note: Agrees with PMC3241297: 'A total of 32,894 individuals, nearly one-third of the adult population of Washington County at that time, took part in this study.' 25,076 lived in Washington County at baseline.

label: Genetic Regulation of Arterial Pressure in Humans in the Community Study
counts: adults recruited from 520 nuclear families
quote: Of the 2024 individuals from 520 nuclear families recruited in GRAPHIC, individuals who were receiving anti-hypertensive medications (n=135) were excluded from the current analysis to avoid any confounding caused by modulation of diurnal variation in BP by drugs.
note: PMID:24391740 also gives 2024 individuals from 520 families in its abstract, but its methods say the GRAPHIC Study 'consists of 2037 subjects from 520 white British pedigrees'. The original GRAPHIC design papers (cited as refs 9-10 in PMC5144126) were not read and would settle 2024 vs 2037.

label: Monongahela-Youghiogheny Healthy Aging Team
counts: adults aged 65 and over recruited
quote: MYHAT is an ongoing population‐based study that recruited 1982 individuals aged ≥ 65 from southwestern Pennsylvania by age‐stratified random sampling from electoral rolls.
note: From PMID:40042063 (the definition source and example study), which analysed 745 MYHAT participants. The MYHAT design paper was not read.

label: Utah residents (CEPH) with Northern and Western European ancestry
counts: individuals in 30 parent-offspring trios (HapMap Phase I)
quote: The specific samples examined are: (1) 90 individuals (30 parent–offspring trios) from the Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria (abbreviation YRI); (2) 90 individuals (30 trios) in Utah, USA, from the Centre d’Etude du Polymorphisme Humain collection (abbreviation CEU); (3) 45 Han Chinese in Beijing, China (abbreviation CHB); (4) 44 Japanese in Tokyo, Japan (abbreviation JPT).
note: CEU sample as typed in HapMap Phase I (PMID:16255080, read on the PMC page). HapMap 3 (PMID:20811451) added further samples 'from the same four populations', but its per-population counts are in a table/supplement not in the text read. The example study (PMID:33575800) tested lymphoblastoid lines from up to 168 CEU individuals, which suggests the expanded HapMap 3 CEU sample; the total CEU count after HapMap 3 would need HapMap 3 Table 1 or Coriell's catalogue.

label: Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria
counts: individuals in 30 parent-offspring trios (HapMap Phase I)
quote: The specific samples examined are: (1) 90 individuals (30 parent–offspring trios) from the Yoruba in Ibadan, Nigeria (abbreviation YRI); (2) 90 individuals (30 trios) in Utah, USA, from the Centre d’Etude du Polymorphisme Humain collection (abbreviation CEU); (3) 45 Han Chinese in Beijing, China (abbreviation CHB); (4) 44 Japanese in Tokyo, Japan (abbreviation JPT).
note: YRI sample as typed in HapMap Phase I (PMID:16255080, read on the PMC page). HapMap 3 (PMID:20811451) added further samples 'from the same four populations', but its per-population counts are in a table/supplement not in the text read. The example study (PMID:33575800) tested lymphoblastoid lines from up to 177 YRI individuals; the total YRI count after HapMap 3 would need HapMap 3 Table 1 or Coriell's catalogue.

label: Copenhagen Prospective Study on Asthma in Childhood
counts: children enrolled in the COPSAC2000 birth cohort
quote: The COPSAC2000 is a single-centre clinical, prospective, mother–child cohort study of 411 individuals born to mothers with asthma who were recruited during pregnancy from the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC).
note: From the 18-year follow-up design paper (PMID:39214547); 370 (90%) of the 411 completed the 18-year visit. The 2004 design paper (PMID:15521375) is closed and its cached copy is empty, but 411 is stated consistently.

label: DemGene network
counts: cases (AD dementia and MCI) and healthy controls genotyped in the network's 2019 GWAS
quote: We collected genotype data from the Norwegian DemGene network consisting of 2,893 cases and 1,660 healthy controls. A total of 4,553 Caucasian (1000 Genome population code: CEU) individuals were recruited and successfully genotyped.
note: From the DemGene flagship GWAS (PMID:30591712). The cases are 2,135 AD dementia and 758 MCI from 7 studies. That analysis added 4,475 Norwegian blood-donor and 723 TOP controls, giving 2,893 cases and 6,858 controls analysed; those extra controls are not DemGene recruits, so the 4,553 genotyped DemGene individuals are recorded here.

label: Diabetes Genetics Replication and Meta-analysis Consortium
counts: T2D cases and controls in the DIAGRAMv3 (Stage 1) GWAS meta-analysis, 12 GWAS
quote: This genome-wide meta-analysis (“DIAGRAMv3”) includes data from 12,171 cases and 56,862 controls of European descent imputed up to 2.5 million autosomal SNPs, and augments the previously published “DIAGRAMv2” meta-analysis4 with four additional GWAS (Supplementary Table 1).
note: The source states cases and controls but no total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The same paper's Stage 2 Metabochip meta-analysis had 22,669 cases and 58,119 controls, and it says 'We have expanded T2D association analysis to almost 150,000 individuals' (approximate, so not recorded). The example study (PMID:34604815) used later DIAGRAM stage 1 summary statistics (18 studies) whose size it does not state in the text read. A later DIAGRAM paper stating a total would give a number.

label: Determining the Influence of Susceptibility COnveying Variants Related to one-Year mortality after BMT
counts: BMT recipients in the two cohorts after QC (their unrelated donors not counted)
quote: Replication and validation of these SNP associations were performed using DISCOVeRY-BMT (Determining the Influence of Susceptibility COnveying Variants Related to one-Year mortality after BMT), a well-powered genome-wide association study consisting of 2 cohorts, totaling 2888 BMT recipients with acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, or myelodysplastic syndrome, and their HLA-matched unrelated donors, reported to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research.
note: Abstract of PMID:28811306 read via Europe PMC. No source read states a single total of recipients plus donors. PMID:34746714 gives after QC 2111 and 779 patients and 2219 and 808 donors in Cohorts 1 and 2 (2053 and 763 complete pairs); PMID:34220922 used 1,769 AML and 540 MDS patients as cases and 2,814 donors as controls; PMID:36477467 refers to 'the DISCOVeRY-BMT data set of 3231 alloHCT DRPs'; PMID:26028504 describes 3532 acute leukaemia or MDS URD-HCT patients from 151 US centres (2000-2011) without naming the study in its abstract.

label: European Alzheimer's Disease Initiative
counts: AD cases and controls from France in the 2009 EADI GWAS (stage 1)
quote: To identify other risk loci, we conducted a large genome-wide association study of 2,032 individuals from France with Alzheimer's disease (cases) and 5,328 controls.
note: From the EADI GWAS (PMID:19734903). The source gives cases and controls but no total, so participants is left null rather than summed. Its supplement says 'Genomic DNA samples from 2,344 AD cases were available for analysis prior to genotype quality control steps.' Replication collections (Belgium, Finland, Italy, Spain: 3,978 cases, 3,297 controls) are not EADI's own. EADI's later count within IGAP was not read.

label: EPICURE Consortium
counts: GGE patients and controls in the consortium's two-stage 2012 GWAS
quote: To identify susceptibility variants shared across common GGE syndromes, we carried out a two-stage genome-wide association study (GWAS) including 3020 patients with GGEs and 3954 controls of European ancestry.
note: Abstract of the EPICURE Consortium / EMINet Consortium GGE GWAS (Hum Mol Genet 2012), read via Europe PMC; it states cases and controls but no total, so participants is left null. The paper is joint with EMINet, so not every sample is necessarily EPICURE's own. The definition sources (CORDIS fact sheet, PMID:34002374) give no participant count for the consortium.

label: GenEpA Consortium
note: No source read states the size of the GenEpA collection as a whole. Only per-country figures appear: PMID:20522523 (2010 partial-epilepsy GWAS) Table 2 lists patients from Finland 410, Norway 201 and Switzerland 231 among its analysed subjects, and says it used '288 controls from Finland and 285 controls from Switzerland without neurological conditions, recruited and genotyped for this study'; the supplement of PMID:30531953 lists 'GenEpa Finnish Case 422' and 'Control 293'. PMID:37653029 names Austrian, Swiss and Norwegian GenEpa cohorts without counts in the text read. A GenEpA description giving total cases and controls across the four countries would settle it.

label: Genetic and Environmental Risk in Alzheimer's Disease Consortium
counts: AD cases and controls in the GERAD1 stage 1 GWAS dataset
quote: Thus, in Stage 1, we tested 529,205 autosomal SNPs for association in up to 11,789 subjects (3,941 AD cases, 7,848 controls of which 2,078 were elderly screened controls, see Supplementary Table 1).
note: From the GERAD GWAS (PMID:19734902); 2,078 of the controls were elderly screened controls, the rest population controls. Its stage 2 replication (2,023 cases, 2,340 controls) was separate; the abstract says the study involved 'over 16,000 individuals'. PMID:29532500 used GERAD data of '3,332 cases, 9,832 controls' after its own processing.

label: Genes for Good
counts: participants who signed the electronic consent form
quote: As of March 2019, 117,652 participants had tried the app, with 81,110 signing the electronic consent form.
note: From the Genes for Good design paper (PMID:31204010). The same paper: 'Genes for Good has mailed 33,427 spit kits to eligible participants, of which 27,470 have been returned (as of March 2019)', and its genotype data freeze held 20,232 individuals. Recruitment was ongoing; no later count read.

label: Imperial-Liverpool-Melbourne Collaboration
counts: epilepsy cases from the collaboration after QC, as analysed in the 2014 ILAE meta-analysis
quote: ILM Collaboration European descent 1703 212 1263 2699
note: Table 1 row of the 2014 ILAE meta-analysis (PMID:25087078): 1703 all-epilepsy cases (212 genetic generalised, 1263 focal) and 2699 population controls, after QC; the controls are population controls paired with the collection for analysis, not people it recruited. The 2023 ILAE meta-analysis supplement (PMID:37653029, Supplementary Information) lists 'Imperial-Liverpool- Melbourne British Case 1294'. No design paper of the collaboration itself was found; the collaboration's UK heritability paper (PMID:25063994) describes 1258 UK cases after QC (1298 before exclusions of unknown status, 1485 raw) but does not name the collaboration. A figure for the whole collection would need the collaboration's own description.

label: San Antonio Family Study
counts: individuals in 42 extended families at baseline
quote: The SAFS began in 1991, and included 1,431 individuals in 42 extended families at baseline.
note: From the cohort description in the Supplementary Information of the example study (PMID:36220816), which describes the family heart component's baseline; the later diabetes/gallbladder component and new recruits are not counted in it. The 1996 family heart study paper abstract (PMID:8901667) says 'Members of 42 extended families were studied, including 1236 first-, second-, and third-degree relatives of randomly ascertained probands and their spouses.' The GAW18 data paper (PMID:25519314) describes 20 pedigrees of 1043 individuals selected for T2D-GENES; the example study analysed 619 sequenced SAFS participants. A total across both component studies would need a combined SAFS profile.

label: Swedish Adoption/Twin Study of Aging
counts: twins who responded to the first (1984) questionnaire
quote: Out of these 2018 responded (71%).
note: Swedish National Data Service catalogue entry: the preceding sentence reads 'SATSA started with a survey in 1984 where a questionnaire was sent to all surviving individuals (n=2845).' Other figures seen: a 2023 frailty paper (PMC10265292) says 'The present study includes data from 1430 participants who participated in both Qs and IPTs, if eligible.'; a 2025 epigenetic paper (PMC11881402) describes 859 twins; the definition source (PMID:40188287) analysed 535 twins with IGF-I. The baseline questionnaire respondents are taken as the cohort's enrolled number; whether later waves added twins was not checked.

label: Stroke Genetics Network
counts: ischaemic stroke cases in stage 1 of the 2016 SiGN GWAS (controls largely from public studies)
quote: The first stage consisted of 16,851 cases with state-of-the-art phenotyping and 32,473 stroke-free controls.
note: Flagship analysis of the network (Lancet Neurol 2016). The total of cases and controls is not stated as one number, so participants gives the cases the network assembled. The 2013 design paper (PMID:24021684) planned 'a total of 14,549 cases' from 24 genetic research centres, with controls mostly from public studies. Stage 2 looked up 20,941 cases and 364,736 controls in 18 independent studies, which are not SiGN members.

label: SubPopulations and InteRmediate Outcome Measures in COPD Study
counts: participants originally enrolled (SPIROMICS I)
quote: SPIROMICS originally enrolled 2,982 participants, for a three-year study of current and former smokers and individuals who had never smoked.
note: The study's own website. The design paper (PMID:24029743) planned 3,200 participants in four strata. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01969344 gives an actual enrollment of 2981 (a registry field, not a sentence). The SPIROMICS AIR design paper (PMC5595208) says 'SPIROMICS enrolled 1836 current and former smokers with COPD (strata III and IV), 944 smokers without airflow obstruction (stratum II), and 202 non-smoking controls (stratum I) across cities in the USA.'

label: Veterans Health Service Medical Center cohort
counts: eligible VHSMC subjects with microarray data in the sarcopenia GWAS
quote: Data were obtained from two cohorts: the VHSMC (n = 2518) and KARE (Ansan/Ansung study: from Korean Genome and Epidemiology Cohort, n = 5235) cohorts.
note: The only source read describes the cohort only as the samples used in this GWAS: 'A total of 7753 eligible subjects were included in this study (2518 subjects from the VHSMC cohort and 5235 from the KARE cohorts).', of which 1781 VHSMC subjects remained after exclusions. This is the genotyped subset, not necessarily all people in the Veterans Medical Research Institute Biobank; a description of the biobank or cohort itself would settle the whole number.

label: Cervical Artery Dissection and Ischemic Stroke Patients
counts: consecutive cervical artery dissection patients (plus 658 non-CeAD ischaemic stroke control patients)
quote: This case-control study is based on the CADISP (Cervical Artery Dissection and Ischemic Stroke Patients) population comprising 983 consecutive CeAD patients (mean age: 44.1 ± 9.9 years) and 658 control patients with a non-CeAD ischemic stroke (IS) (44.5 ± 10.5 years).
note: Europe PMC abstract of a 2012 CADISP analysis; a 2017 CADISP paper (PMC5345335) agrees: 'A total of 983 patients with a diagnosis of CeAD based upon predefined criteria were included in the CADISP (Cervical Artery Dissection and Ischemic Stroke Patients) study between 2004 and 2009', with 658 non-CeAD IS patients and 269 Finnish healthy subjects as controls. The total of cases and controls is not stated as one number, so participants gives the CeAD patients. The 2009 design paper (PMID:19659826) planned 'approximately 1100 patients with CAD, and 2000 healthy controls'. A 2011 paper (PMID:21444882) used 1170 referents; a 2012 migraine paper (PMID:22491867) says 968 CeAD and 653 non-CeAD IS patients were recruited. The example study supplement (PMID:36240095) says 942 CeAD patients were in CADISP-1 (2004-2009) and 451 more were recruited in 2008-2010 for CADISP2.

label: Genetics of Glucose regulation in Gestation and Growth
counts: pregnant women recruited in the first trimester, 2010-2013
quote: Gen3G is a prospective pregnancy and birth cohort that recruited 1024 pregnant women in the first trimester of pregnancy in Sherbrooke, Canada, between January 2010 and June 2013.
note: From the 2025 cohort profile of the childhood follow-up (PMID:40122564). The 2016 cohort profile (PMID:26842272) says 'We recruited a total of 1034 pregnant women between January 2010 and June 2013', noting that multiple pregnancies (n=10) were excluded from its analyses and that 31 women contributed 2 pregnancies. Follow-up: 448 and 521 mother-child dyads at the 3- and 5-year visits.

label: Manchester Asthma and Allergy Study
counts: children born into the birth cohort, February 1996-April 1998
quote: It included 1184 children born between February 1996 and April 1998.
note: From the cohort description in a 2019 paper using MAAS and ALSPAC (PMID:31441980), not a MAAS profile paper; the preceding sentence reads 'Manchester Asthma and Allergy Study is an unselected birth cohort established in 1995 in Manchester.' The 2003 definition source (PMID:12688622) abstract says '995 children at age 3 years' were recruited in utero; the example study (PMID:35931775) says 921 children were followed up at age 11 and analysed 307. A MAAS cohort profile was not read.

label: Population Assessment for Tomorrow's Health Study
counts: registry participants genotyped (via 23andMe)
quote: Two thousand and ninety‐eight participants were genotyped on Illumina Infinium® Global Screening Array as a membership service from 23andMe Inc; imputation was performed using the Michigan Imputation Server.
note: From the example study (PMID:37060189), which says its participants were from an existing research registry at St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton; 1534 unrelated European samples were analysed. The number is stated in words. A 2022 paper on the same registry (PMID:35080193) says 'The sample consisted of a cohort of community adults (n = 1388) who completed a one-time in-person assessment as part of enrollment in a health research registry at St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton.' The registry's web page (definition source) says registration is closed but gives no count. The genotyped number is a subset of all registrants; the registry's total enrolment is not stated in anything read.

label: Peking University-University of Michigan Study of Atherosclerosis
counts: participants aged 40 or over enrolled December 2011-April 2012
quote: The PUUMA study is a prospective observational cohort study of 9,540 participants age ≥40 years at enrollment between December 2011 and April 2012.
note: From a definition source (PMID:34488438). Analysed subsets elsewhere: 5,959 participants qualified for genotyping (same paper); 5,954 with blood pressure measurements (PMID:39250516); 5257 with haematological traits (example study PMID:33693786).

label: Singapore Chinese Health Study
counts: Chinese adults aged 45-74 recruited 1993-1998
quote: In brief, 63,257 subjects aged between 45 and 74 years were recruited from April 1993 to December 1998.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:35927272), which also says 'A total of 28,439 participants donated blood specimens.' The cohort's own design paper was not read.

label: Sister Study
counts: women who completed baseline activities and were enrolled, 2003-2009
quote: Of the women who signed up, 81.0% (n=50,884) completed required baseline activities and were enrolled; an additional 3,066 who completed some, but not all, of the required baseline activities before the enrollment end date.
note: The cohort's own design paper (PMID:29373861), which also says 'The Sister Study, a prospective study of 50,884 U.S. women who have had at least one sister diagnosed with breast cancer but had no personal history of breast cancer at enrollment, was designed to fill this gap.' 62,813 women gave verbal consent to join; 3,066 more completed only part of the baseline and are not counted.

label: UroLife study
counts: invited eligible patients who agreed to participate, 2014-2021
quote: Of the 3181 invited patients, 2929 met the eligibility criteria, and 1512 (52%) agreed to participate (Figure 1 ).
note: From a 2025 UroLife analysis of smoking (PMID:39499231, fetched from Europe PMC), which covers both recruitment phases (May 2014-May 2017 Ta/T1/CIS; May 2017-April 2021 T1 only); The 2019 protocol (PMID:31619424) planned 'more than 1100 newly diagnosed patients'. A 2023 paper on the first phase (PMC10652337) says 'Of the 2133 invited patients, 2025 patients were eligible and 1076 (53%) agreed to participate'.

label: Chinese Antipsychotics Pharmacogenomics Consortium
counts: acute-phase schizophrenia patients from the CAPOC trial in a 2025 GWAS discovery cohort
quote: The discovery cohort consisted of 3067 patients (2016 participants were reserved after quality control) with schizophrenia in the acute phase and was derived from the Chinese Antipsychotics Pharmacogenomics Consortium (CAPOC) [14].
note: From a definition source (PMID:40826483), the largest count seen; no design paper stating the number randomised was read. Other counts of the same trial: the 2018 Lancet Psychiatry GWAS abstract (PMID:29503163) says 'The discovery cohort contained 2413 patients and the validation cohort 1379 patients' (patients from 32 psychiatric hospitals); PMID:37269009 says 'The discovery cohort was recruited from the CAPOC trial (n = 2307)'; PMID:34093281 used 1,868 patients; the example study (PMID:38336841) a discovery cohort of 1936. The trial registration (ChiCTR-RNC-09000521) or a design paper would settle the number randomised.

label: CROATIA-Split Study
counts: Split sub-cohort participants of the 10,001 Dalmatians biobank
quote: Here, we used the data from three sub-cohorts for which we had bacterial and viral infections disease data—Korčula (N = 2833), Vis (N = 1039) and Split (N = 1012).
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:37108169), where it is the sub-cohort's size as used for infection data; 966 Split participants were in the genome-wide meta-analysis (Table 1). No Split-specific design paper was read.

label: Epidemiological study on the Genetics and Environment of Asthma
counts: total participants in the EGEA bioresource (all surveys)
quote: Total number participants: 2,121
note: From the cohort's own bioresource paper (Open J Bioresour 2017, doi:10.5334/ojb.24, not one of the term's cited sources), under 'Size of the bioresource'. Cases and controls are from the same paper's EGEA1 statement: 'EGEA1 included 388 cases with asthma, their first-degree relatives (n = 1244) and 415 population-based controls.' The same paper gives 1601 subjects with complete examination at EGEA2 (1570 adults) and 1558 EGEA3 questionnaire respondents; genome-wide data for 1,904 participants. The definition source PMID:35624665 says EGEA2 included 1602 participants with complete examination.

label: Epidemiologische Studie zu Chancen der Verhütung, Früherkennung und optimierten Therapie chronischer Erkrankungen in der älteren Bevölkerung
counts: adults aged 50-75 recruited by GPs, July 2000-December 2002
quote: Briefly, 9,940 individuals aged 50–75 years were recruited by their general practitioners (GPs) during routine health screenings between July 2000 and December 2002, and were followed up every two to three years thereafter.
note: From the definition source (a 2026 ESTHER paper, PMID:41803162), which analysed a random sample of 1930 participants with DNA methylation. No ESTHER design paper was read.

label: Gothenburg H70 Birth Cohort Studies and Clinical AD Sweden
counts: AD cases and controls in the genotyped Gothenburg dataset (2021 GWAS); no combined total stated
quote: The Gothenburg H70 Birth Cohort Studies and Clinical AD from Sweden (Gothenburg) dataset (712 cases, 2523 controls) was used as the independent test set because it was the dataset with the largest number of cases of the available genotype-level data.
note: From the Supplementary Information of the 2021 Alzheimer's disease GWAS (Nat Genet, doi:10.1038/s41588-021-00921-z), which uses the same description of the collection as the definition sources. Cases and controls both come from the collection (controls from the Gothenburg Birth Cohort Studies and PPSW), but no source states their total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The definition sources (PMID:36066633, PMID:42237039 and its supplement) describe the collection without counts; the CSF GWAS table of PMID:36066633 gives the 'Birth cohort & Clin. AD' row without a readable sample size.

label: Northern California Breast Cancer Family Registry
counts: women with incident breast cancer (and family members) enrolled from 1995, stated as approximate
quote: The Northern California Breast Cancer Family Registry (NC-BCFR) was initiated in 1995 and enrolled ~4000 women with incident breast cancer and family members (John et al., 2019).
note: From Additional file 1 (13058_2022_1524_MOESM1_ESM.docx) of the example study (PMID:35414113); the number is given as '~4000' and it is unclear whether it counts the women with breast cancer only or also their family members. The 2004 BCFR paper (PMID:15217505) gives registry-wide numbers (11,950 families as of September 2003) and San Francisco numbers only as table cells by proband type. The 2014 GWAS (PMID:25327703) pooled NC-BCFR with SFBCS and GALA1 Latinas (977 cases, 722 controls). The 2019 BCFR update cited in the supplement (John et al., 2019) was not read and would settle the site's enrolment.

label: Breast Cancer Family Registry
counts: probands and relatives enrolled 1996-2003
quote: All probands and relativesa 9116 30,086 2834 8264 50,300
note: The number is the Total column of the 'All probands and relatives' row of Table 4 of the 2004 design paper (PMID:15217505; population-based probands 9116 and relatives 30,086, clinic-based probands 2834 and relatives 8264), as of September 2003; footnote a: probands with completed family history questionnaire, relatives with epidemiology data, blood or mouthwash sample, or tumor block. The text itself counts families: 'As of September 2003, the six sites had enrolled a total of 11,950 families in the Breast Cancer Family Registry (Table 3).' Recruitment continued after 2003; no later whole-registry profile paper with a participant count was found in Europe PMC.

label: National Institute on Aging Late Onset Alzheimer's Disease Family Study
counts: family members with data, from 1756 families
quote: We recruited 1756 families and acquired data from 9682 family members.
note: From the 2022 resource paper of the NIA-LOAD Family Based Study (PMID:34978149). The same paper: 'we collected DNA from 7925 participants' and GWAS data for 7012 family members in 1340 families. Earlier: PMID:19001172 (2008) 'We investigated 1902 individuals from 328 families with LOAD and 236 unrelated control subjects'; the definition source PMID:21379329 (2011 GWAS) '3,839 affected and unaffected individuals from 992 families' and 'The final genotyped NIA-LOAD/NCRAD cohort consisted of 5,220 subjects' (with NCRAD). The definition's 992 families is the 2011 GWAS subset.

label: Northern Manhattan Study
counts: stroke-free adults enrolled 1993-2001
quote: NOMAS is a community‐based longitudinal cohort study of 3298 urban‐dwelling adults 40 years of age or older with a household telephone at the baseline visit.
note: From the definition source (a NOMAS analysis paper describing the cohort); the next sentence gives recruitment 1993-2001 by random digit dialing. The example GWAS (PMID:36658081) analysed a subset, N = 1077. The original NOMAS design papers were not read.

label: Pittsburgh Orofacial Cleft Study
counts: participants in families (approximate)
quote: The Pitt-OFC resource is a rich collection of nsOFC families across multiple racial/ethnic groups, including simplex, multiplex, and extended pedigrees (~12,000 participants) with precise and detailed information on the types of nsOFC observed within multiple generations of the relatives of the probands.
note: Approximate figure from the 2022 multiethnic GWAS of the Pitt-OFC study (PMID:35191549), which analysed 2,218 CL/CLP cases, 4,537 unaffected relatives and 2,673 pure controls. The definition/example paper (PMID:35172313) analysed only the unaffected subset: 'The first cohort for this study (n = 3,579) comes from the POFC.' No design paper with an exact whole-study count was found.

label: Australian Genetics of Depression Study
counts: participants who returned the questionnaire
quote: As of 3 September 2018, questionnaire responses had been received from 20 689 participants, 75% of whom were female.
note: From the AGDS cohort description paper (PMID:32461290). All participants had been diagnosed with depression; QSkin population controls genotyped on the same chip are a separate study and not counted.

label: Accessible Resource for Integrated Epigenomic Studies
counts: mother-offspring pairs (pairs, not individuals)
quote: A total of 1018 mother-child pairs have been profiled (v.1 data release 2014) at each of the five time points indicated, using the Illumina Infinium HumanMethylation450K BeadChip array.
note: The ARIES design paper (PMID:25991711) counts pairs, not people: also 'A sub-set of 1018 mother-offspring pairs were included in ARIES' and, rounded, 'ARIES includes 1,000 mother-child pairs'. No source states the number of individuals, so participants holds the number of pairs; the count of individuals is not stated and was not computed.

label: Bellygenes initiative
counts: IBS cases and controls in the 2021 GWAS meta-analysis (no total stated)
quote: This resulted from pooling IBS cases across all case definitions to maximize power, in a meta-analysis of data from UKB (40,548 cases and 293,220 controls; Supplementary Tables 1 and 2) and the international collaborative Bellygenes initiative (12,852 cases and 139,981 controls; Methods and Supplementary Table 9).
note: Cohort aggregation; the flagship analysis is the 2021 IBS GWAS (PMID:34741163), which gives Bellygenes cases and controls separately but never a combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The member cohorts are listed in Supplementary Table 9, which was not read.

label: CERA cohort
counts: analysed subset: AMD+ and AMD- participants after QC in the 2025 RPD GWAS
note: Row of the supplementary cohort table of PMID:41361163 (columns: age, male N, AMD+/RPD+ N, AMD+/RPD- N, AMD+ N, AMD- N, Total N; footnote: 'Total numbers are after phenotyping and genotyping quality control steps'). This is the analysed subset, not the size of the whole CERA collection, for which no design paper or website count was found. Separately, 44 AMD+/RPD++ CERA cases were whole-genome sequenced.

label: Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research - National Marrow Donor Program Research Sample Repository
counts: no single total of people stated; inventory given by category
quote: CIBMTR Biorepository as of November 2025 Number of unrelated Donor/Recipient pairs 52,147 Number of unrelated Cord blood/Recipient pairs* 6,535 Number of unique unrelated Donor ID 95,017 Number of unique unrelated Recipient ID 96,132 Number of unique Cord ID 14,582 Number of unique related Donor ID 16,770 Number of unique related Recipient ID 17,503 Number of related Donor/Recipient Pairs 14,529
note: The biorepository inventory page (fetched 2025-09-25, figures as of November 2025) gives counts by category (unique unrelated recipients 96,132, unique related recipients 17,503, unique unrelated donors 95,017, unique related donors 16,770, unique cords 14,582, and pair counts) but no overall number of individuals, so participants is left null rather than summed. The page did not state the 'more than 60,000' in the definition. The example paper (PMID:41748071) used only a subset as controls: '1054 adults from the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR)/National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) Research Sample Repository and Duke GKD study controls'.

label: Drug Interaction With Genes in Parkinson's Disease
counts: patients with PD recruited May 2009 - July 2013
quote: Of 426 patients, we excluded 11 who developed atypical parkinsonism (4 had ICDs) and 4 with missing covariates and retained 411 for the analyses (40.6% women; mean age 62.3 years, SD 9.8 years): 63.8% of the patients attended ≥4 assessments, 28.7% attended 2 or 3 assessments, and 7.5% attended the baseline assessment only.
note: From the DIGPD cohort paper (PMID:29925549), whose Methods say the study recruited patients consecutively 'from May 2009 to July 2013 in 4 French university hospitals and 4 general hospitals'; 426 is read as the recruited cohort, 411 analysed. Other counts: the definition source PMID:35813487 'Out of the 415 PD subjects in DIGPD, we excluded 27 for having only a baseline visit'; the example PMID:36348503 analysed 370 DIGPD participants.

label: Duke Genetics of Kidney Disease
counts: patients and family members enrolled (stated as 'over 2100', a lower bound)
quote: Since opening recruitment, we have enrolled over 2100 patients and family members into this study from around the world!
note: From the Fall 2017 'Genetics of Kidney Disease Research Update' participant newsletter of the Duke Molecular Physiology Institute (archived copy; the live URL now redirects to the DMPI home page). The newsletter gives IRB Protocol 00014951, the protocol the example paper gives for Duke GKD (Pro00014951), and adds 'we hope to eventually enroll 3000 people into our study'. The definition source (PMID:26413278, a case report) gives no cohort size; the example paper (PMID:41748071) used a subset ('994 multi-ancestry NS cases enrolled in the Duke Genetics of Kidney Disease (Duke GKD; Pro00014951) and Genomics of Nephrotic Syndrome studies'). The DMPI familial FSGS page says 'we have identified over 150 families from all over the world with two or more family members with FSGS.' No more recent count found.

label: European Genetic Database
counts: individuals available in EUGENDA for a 2021 imaging analysis (possibly a subset)
quote: Out of 2,783 individuals available in the EUGENDA cohort at the time of analysis for this study, 64 cases were excluded because of insufficient image quality and confounding macular or retinal diseases.
note: From the definition source (PMID:35136347), a case-control analysis; 2,783 may be only the participants with the imaging needed for that study. Other EUGENDA papers give larger analysed sets, e.g. the abstract of PMID:26441265 (2016): 'Of 3,701 individuals from the EUGENDA database, 752 (20.3%) showed early AMD, 1,179 (31.9%) late AMD, and 1,770 (47.8%) were controls.' In the example (PMID:41361163) EUGENDA contributed 3361 after QC (1735 AMD+, 1626 AMD-). No design paper or website stating the whole database size was found (eugenda.org returned no content); a EUGENDA cohort description would settle it.

label: Family Atherosclerosis Monitoring In earLY life Study
counts: newborns (index children) enrolled 2002-2009; mothers and fathers counted separately
quote: The study population included 901 babies, 857 mothers and 530 fathers.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:27453525 (2016, FAMILY study allergy analysis). The definition source PMID:37908396 agrees: 'The Family Atherosclerosis Monitoring in Early Life (FAMILY) study is a longitudinal birth cohort study with 857 families (901 newborns) enrolled from 2002 and 2009 from three hospitals in Ontario, Canada.' The 2009 design paper (PMID:19781411) gives the planned size: 'A cohort of 850 children and their families (mother, father, eldest sibling) are being recruited during pregnancy'. No source states the total number of individuals (babies, mothers, fathers and siblings), so participants holds the number of newborns rather than a sum.

label: Finland-United States Investigation of NIDDM Genetics
counts: no total of individuals stated; GWAS stage 1 case-control sample given as cases and controls
quote: FUSION—The FUSION stage 1 sample consists of 1,161 Finnish T2D cases and 1,174 Finnish normal glucose tolerant controls2.

label: Ginkgo Evaluation of Memory Study
counts: randomised participants aged 75 and over
quote: Briefly, GEM was a randomized, placebo‐controlled trial that was conducted from 2000 to 2008 across five different academic centers in the United States to assess the effectiveness of Ginkgo biloba on incident dementia in 3069 participants aged ≥ 75, including 2587 cognitively normal individuals and 482 individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
note: From the definition/example paper (PMID:40042063), describing the trial; the trial's own primary report (JAMA 2008) was not read but this figure is the well-established randomised total.

label: Genito-Urinary BioBank
counts: participants consented since 2008 (stated as 'over 16,000', a lower bound)
quote: Since its inception, over 16,000 participants have been consented to the program.
note: From the McCain GU BioBank (Princess Margaret Cancer Centre) e-poster at ISBER 2020; the poster also says the biobank has expanded to other oncology sites (gynecology-oncology, thoracic), so the count may include non-genito-urinary patients. The current McCain GU BioBank 'About us' page gives no participant count. The example GWAS (PMID:42320430) used only NMIBC subsets; its supplement: 'For the current study, information on 393 and 401 patients with NMIBC collected in two different batches (GUB-1 and GUB-2, respectively) was available.' The definition source PMID:25987846 gives no size.

label: Hisayama-FSR study
counts: ischaemic stroke cases and stroke-free controls in the GWAS (no total stated)
quote: In the genome-wide association study, 1113 cases with ischemic stroke (370 large artery stroke, 137 cardioembolic stroke, 483 small vessel occlusion, 123 undetermined subtype) were included.
note: Both numbers from the Hisayama-FSR study description in the supplementary note of PMID:29531354 (MEGASTROKE); the controls come from the sentence 'After excluding subjects with a history of stroke or coronary heart disease, 901 control subjects were included in the genome-wide association study.' The supplementary sample table row agrees: 'HISAYAMA 1,113 1,113 370 137 483 901 EAS'. No total is stated, so participants is left null rather than summed. The note cites an earlier detailed description (its ref. 75), which was not read.

label: International Genomics of Alzheimer's Project
counts: individuals across all stages of the 2019 IGAP meta-analysis
quote: To identify LOAD risk loci, we performed a large genome-wide association meta-analysis of clinically diagnosed LOAD (94,437 individuals).
note: Cohort aggregation; the number is from the 2019 IGAP meta-analysis (PMID:30820047), whose stage 1 was 'n = 21,982 cases, 41,944 cognitively normal controls' (46 datasets); overall case and control totals are not stated in the text read, so cases and controls are null. The 2013 IGAP meta-analysis (PMID:24162737, title 'Meta-analysis of 74,046 individuals identifies 11 new susceptibility loci for Alzheimer's disease') had stage 1 of '17,008 Alzheimer's disease cases and 37,154 controls' and stage 2 of '8,572 Alzheimer's disease cases and 11,312 controls'; the definition uses the 2013 stage 1 figures.

label: Mexican-American Coronary Artery Disease Study
counts: analysed subset: MACAD individuals (208 families) included in GUARDIAN
quote: GUARDIAN includes 772 of these individuals from 208 families.
note: From the MACAD paragraph of the GUARDIAN description (PMID:24124113), which follows 'Family members of probands with documented coronary artery disease were recruited from the Los Angeles area.'; it counts only MACAD members with the GUARDIAN traits measured. Other MACAD subsets in Europe PMC abstracts: PMID:29575061 (2018) 'we examined 787 subjects from the Mexican-American Coronary Artery Disease (MACAD) cohort who had undergone euglycaemic-hyperinsulinaemic clamps'; PMID:16899800 (2006) '478 subjects from 105 Mexican-American nuclear families'. No source read states the size of the whole MACAD cohort.

label: Genetics UndeRlying DIAbetes in HispaNics
counts: Mexican-American individuals in 1,346 pedigrees across seven member cohorts
quote: GUARDIAN is comprised of seven cohorts, consisting of 4,336 Mexican-American individuals in 1,346 pedigrees.
note: Cohort aggregation; quote from the Europe PMC abstract of the GUARDIAN consortium description (PMID:24124113). The full text adds 'five family-based studies (IRAS Family, BetaGene, MACAD, HTN-IR, NIDDM-Athero; total 3925 individuals) and two non-family based studies (IRAS, TRIPOD; total 411 individuals)'.

label: METASTROKE collaboration
counts: ischaemic stroke cases and controls in the 2012 discovery meta-analysis (15 cohorts)
quote: We meta-analysed data from 15 ischaemic stroke cohorts with a total of 12 389 individuals with ischaemic stroke and 62 004 controls, all of European ancestry.
note: From the METASTROKE flagship paper (PMID:23041239); no sentence states the case-plus-control total, so participants is null. The same paper replicated novel signals 'in 13 347 cases and 29 083 controls'. Member studies: 15 discovery cohorts.

label: Monongahela Valley Independent Elders Survey
counts: adults aged 65+ recruited 1987-1989
quote: MoVIES was a prospective study that recruited 1681 individuals aged ≥ 65 residing within the Monongahela Valley, Pennsylvania during 1987 through 1989 using a voter's registration list.
note: From the example study (PMID:40042063), not a MoVIES design paper. The same paper says 887 dementia-free non-Hispanic whites were APOE-genotyped, 379 genome-wide genotyped, and 378 analysed. The original MoVIES design paper (not read) would confirm the enrolment.

label: Prediction and Prevention of Preeclampsia and Intrauterine Growth Restriction Study
counts: pregnant women recruited 2005-2010
quote: Of the 4785 recruited mothers, we had data on birth outcomes from the birth register and the two-week interval self-report of positive affect, depressive symptoms, and state anxiety during pregnancy for 3376 mothers (70.6% of those recruited).
note: From definition source PMID:26919119, which also describes the subsamples: 973 high-risk women with risk factors, 110 without, and 3702 in the community-based subsample, recruited September 2005 to February 2010. The cohort profile (PMID:27639277, doi:10.1093/ije/dyw154) is closed (publisher 403) and was not read.

label: Risk Assessment of Cerebrovascular Events Study
note: The only whole-study statement read is a lower bound, not a number: the dbGaP page (phs000456.v1.p1, definition source) says 'Risk Assessment of Cerebrovascular Events (RACE) is an on-going existing case-control study of stroke now involving over 5000 imaging confirmed cases of stroke and 5000 controls, recruited from seven centers in Pakistan.' The same page says 'This study includes 1,220 cases with young onset stroke (stroke before age 60 years) who are participants of the larger RACE study.' (the dbGaP subset, with PROMIS controls). PMC4117446 Table 2 lists RACE in a replication with 1,390 ischaemic stroke cases and 5,308 controls (analysed subset). The example study PMID:36240095 gives no RACE count in its main text. No RACE design paper was found in Europe PMC; one stating final enrolment would settle it.

label: Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
counts: participants recruited 2003-2007
quote: From January 2003 to October 2007, 30,239 participants (42% AA, 55% women) were recruited from the 48 contiguous U.S. states and the District of Columbia.
note: From the definition source (a REGARDS paper, PMC9554233), not the original design paper; the figure matches the definition.

label: Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial
counts: eligible men enrolled (randomised) over a 3-year accrual period
quote: A total of 35,533 eligible men from the US, Canada, and Puerto Rico were enrolled in a 3-year period, exceeding the goals for both number of participants and for length of the accrual period.
note: From the definition source PMID:23552052, a SELECT review. The primary SELECT results papers were not read; they would confirm the randomised count.

label: Stroke in Young Fabry Patients
counts: patients aged 18-55 with acute stroke or TIA enrolled April 2007 to January 2010
quote: A total of 5023 patients with stroke (aged 18–55 years) were enrolled in the sifap1 study, 271 patients with primary haemorrhages and 217 patients without classification of the CVE were excluded.
note: From definition source PMID:25380809 (a sifap1 secondary analysis); its abstract gives the enrolment period April 2007 to January 2010 at 47 centres in 15 countries. That paper analysed 4535 patients. The sifap1 main results paper was not read.

label: SpiroMeta Consortium
counts: European-ancestry individuals in the 2010 stage-1 GWAS meta-analysis (14 studies)
quote: Here we report a meta-analysis of GWAS in the SpiroMeta consortium, comprising 20,288 individuals of European ancestry, that tested association between cross-sectional lung function measures and ~2.5 million genotyped or imputed SNPs (stage 1).
note: Founding SpiroMeta meta-analysis (PMID:20010834): 14 member studies, 'We included 14 studies of individuals of European ancestry, with sample sizes totaling 20,288'; follow-up in up to 32,184 genotyped and 22,092 in silico individuals. The definition says SpiroMeta later expanded to about 79,000; no source read in this session states that later figure. The example study (PMID:38102678) analysed 400,102 Europeans from UK Biobank and SpiroMeta together.

label: Wisconsin Longitudinal Study
counts: 1957 Wisconsin high school graduates in the original sample (siblings not included)
quote: WLS is based on a 1/3 random sample of all Wisconsin high school graduates in 1957 (n = 10 317) born between 1938 and 1940.
note: From the WLS cohort profile (PMID:24585852). The same paper gives the sibling sample separately: 'The sample also includes a randomly selected sibling of these graduates, the majority of whom were born between 1930 and 1948 (n = 7928).' No sentence states a graduates-plus-siblings total, so the number recorded is the graduate sample only; spouses were also interviewed in 2004.

label: Grady Trauma Project
counts: participants given initial interviews 2005-2008
quote: Initial interviews were performed with 1600 participants approached while in the waiting rooms of primary care or obstetrical-gynecological clinics of Grady Memorial Hospital in Atlanta, Georgia from 2005 to 2008.
note: From the definition source PMID:19892208 (2009), which describes the study to 2008; 318 of them completed the secondary phase with structured clinical interviews. Recruitment continued after 2008, so the current total is likely larger, but no source read in this session states it; a recent GTP overview giving total enrolment would settle it. The example study PMID:34187551 does not name Grady in its text.

label: 10,001 Dalmatians
counts: no achieved total found; 3 member cohorts (Vis, Korčula, Split)
quote: This study was performed on samples from three Croatian populations: from the Dalmatian islands of Korcula and Vis and the mainland city of Split, within the large-scale project of “10,001 Dalmatians” (Rudan et al., 2009).
note: No source read states how many people the biobank actually recruited. The launch paper (PMID:19260138, PMC2657560) gives only the target: 'This effort, aiming to recruit 10 001 examinees, has developed during the recent years, in collaboration mainly with the scientists from Scotland, but also from Sweden, The Netherlands, Italy, and Germany.' Analysed subsets: PMC10138356 had 'a final sample size of 960 in Vis, 2700 in Korčula and 966 in Split, contributing to the total sample size of 4624 participants in this study'; PMC6016867 analysed 2596. A recent biobank overview stating achieved recruitment per cohort would settle it.

label: Lothian Birth Cohort 1936
counts: SMS1947 members recruited to Wave 1, 2004-2007
quote: Between 2004 and 2007, 1091 members of SMS1947 were recruited to Wave 1 of the LBC1936 study, at a mean age of 70 years.
note: From the 2018 LBC cohort profile update (PMID:29546429). Of the original 1091, 550 'completers' took part in all waves to Wave 4 (2014-2017).

label: Lothian Birth Cohort 1921
counts: SMS1932 members recruited to Wave 1, 1999-2001
quote: Between 1999 and 2001, 550 of the SMS1932 were recruited to Wave 1 of the LBC1921 study, at a mean age of 79 years.
note: From the 2018 LBC cohort profile update (PMID:29546429). Of the original 550, 59 'completers' took part in all five waves, to Wave 5 in 2013.

label: National Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health
counts: adolescents in grades 7-12 interviewed in-home at Wave I (core plus special samples)
quote: The core sample plus the special samples yield a total of 20 745 adolescents.
note: From the Add Health cohort profile (PMID:31257425), fetched from PMC. It also says 'An in-school questionnaire was administered to more than 90 000 students in grades 7–12' (the school sampling frame), and gives later in-home waves: Wave II n = 14 738, Wave III n = 15 197, Wave IV 15 701; 10 974 Wave IV respondents were genome-wide genotyped. The definition source PMID:42084756 also gives 'Wave 1 (W1; aged 12–21; N = 20,745)'.

label: Basque Center on Cognition, Brain and Language cohort
counts: schoolchildren who gave saliva samples
quote: A total of 4678 saliva samples were collected from children at schools all over Spain.
note: From definition source PMID:30379906 (Results section); the number counts saliva samples collected from children, one per child as described. The example study PMID:35998220 (GenLang) names the BCBL cohort only in its funding statement in the main text; its per-cohort analysed N, likely in its supplement, was not checked.

label: Botnia Study
note: No source read states the total number of Botnia Study participants. The definition source PMID:8866565 (abstract) gives only relatives and spouses: 'To address this question, we studied 2,152 first-degree relatives of patients with NIDDM (FH+) and 528 age- and weight-matched spouses without a family history of NIDDM (FH-) in Western Finland (the Botnia study).' PMID:19017778 analysed 2,442 subjects free of diabetes at baseline with 7-8 years of follow-up. Europe PMC abstracts give other subsets: 'Families from the Botnia study (n = 4,211, 1,083 families)' (PMID:27155871); '4,432 individuals from the Botnia type 2 diabetes (T2D) study' (PMID:17183695); 'A total of 1294 type 2 diabetic patients with a median age of 69.1 years participated in the Botnia Study from 1990 to 1997' (PMID:16380522). The separate population-based PPP-Botnia study (random sample of 5,208) is a different study. A Botnia design paper (e.g. Groop et al. 1996 Diabetes, full text) giving total enrolment of patients, relatives and spouses would settle it.

label: Colorado Learning Disabilities Research Center cohort
counts: genotyped family members analysed for polygenic scores (analysed subset; 336 families)
quote: The other two were family-based samples selected for dyslexia: one from the United Kingdom (UKdys), n = 930 (595 families); the other from the United States (Colorado Learning Disabilities Research Center, CLDRC), n = 717 (336 families)92.
note: Analysed subset from the definition source PMID:36266505; the trailing '92' is a reference number. No source read states the size of the CLDRC genetic sample as a whole; the wider CLDRC twin study is larger (Europe PMC abstracts describe e.g. '457 twin pairs from the Colorado Learning Disabilities Research Center (CLDRC) twin study' (PMID:20828676) and 513 reading-disabled plus 302 control twin pairs (PMID:7755515)), and none of these gives a total. A CLDRC design or genetic-sample description would settle it.

label: DIAGEN Study
note: No source read states the size of the DIAGEN study. The definition sources' abstracts (only abstracts are on disk) do not name DIAGEN: PMID:16801592 says 'A total of 550 subjects with increased risk of type 2 diabetes were investigated; they underwent a 75-g oral glucose tolerance test, repeated after 3 years.' and PMID:21646370 says 'Six hundred eighty-seven subjects who were free of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) participated in the study.' Whether either is the whole DIAGEN cohort cannot be told without their full texts. PMC2798726 (SHBG, Table 1) lists a DIAGEN row of 255 type 2 diabetes patients and 267 controls (analysed subset, one sex stratum). Consortium papers (PMC3433394, PMC5595282, PMC3838666) mention DIAGEN only in author and acknowledgement lists; the example study PMID:34059833 does not name it in the text on disk.

label: Evaluation of COPD Longitudinally to Identify Predictive Surrogate End-points
counts: COPD patients studied at baseline; smoking and non-smoking controls given separately in the note
quote: Based upon these calculations, we studied 2164 patients with COPD (GOLD stage 2-4), 337 smoking controls and 245 non-smoking controls (Figure 1 ).
note: From the ECLIPSE baseline characterisation paper (PMID:20831787, Respir Res 2010, fetched from PMC). No sentence states the overall total, and the two control groups (337 smokers, 245 never-smokers) are given only separately, so participants and controls are left null. The design paper and definition source PMID:18216052 gives the planned sizes: 'ECLIPSE plans to recruit 2,180 COPD subjects in Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease categories II-IV and 343 smoking and 223 nonsmoking control subjects.' The example study PMID:35953715 used 2,159 genotyped ECLIPSE participants (analysed subset).

label: Early Language in Victoria Study
counts: 8-month-old infants recruited 2003-2004
quote: The Early Language in Victoria Study (ELVS) recruited 1910 8-month-olds in Melbourne in 2003-2004.
note: From the abstract of the definition source PMID:41237490 (full text closed; only the abstract is on disk). Language outcome at 11 years was available for 839 ELVS participants in that analysis. The ELVS design paper was not read.

label: German Infant Study on the Influence of Nutrition Intervention plus Air pollution and Genetics on Allergy Development
counts: healthy term newborns recruited (interventional and non-interventional arms)
quote: Of the 5,991 newborns recruited, 3,317 (55.4%) could be followed until the age of 10 years.
note: Cohort profile of GINIplus and LISAplus (PMID:30402607, PMC6040001). Recruitment 1995-1998 in Munich and Wesel; 3,317 (55.4%) followed to age 10. The separate LISAplus cohort recruited 3,097 newborns and is not counted here.

label: Gothenburg Osteoporosis and Obesity Determinants study
counts: young men who agreed to participate at baseline
quote: There were no other exclusion criteria, and 49% of the study candidates agreed to participate (n = 1068).
note: From the GOOD cohort description in a GWAS of cortical bone thickness (PMID:22792071), which is both the definition source and the example study. GOOD's original design paper was not read. The paper's statement '1,068 cases and 1,218 age-matched controls' refers to a different fracture cohort, not GOOD.

label: Genetics of Overweight Young Adults
counts: genotyped individuals passing QC (extremely overweight cases and random population controls)
quote: After data cleaning, 5,373 individuals (2,633 extremely overweight and 2,740 random controls) and 545,349 SNPs remained.
note: GOYA design and GWAS paper (PMID:21935397). Per sex, 1,960 overweight and 1,948 control women (Danish National Birth Cohort) and 673 overweight and 792 control men (draft-board cohort) were genotyped and passed QC; 102 women and 61 men failed QC. The abstract gives the same case (2,633) and control (2,740) numbers.

label: International Consortium for Blood Pressure Genome-Wide Association Studies
counts: individuals of European descent in the 2011 multi-stage GWAS meta-analysis (discovery plus follow-up)
quote: This genome-wide association study of SBP and DBP, which used a multi-stage design in 200,000 individuals of European descent, identified 16 novel loci: six of these loci contain genes previously known or suspected to regulate BP (GUCY1A3-GUCY1B3; NPR3-C5orf23; ADM; FURIN-FES; GOSR2; GNAS-EDN3); the other 10 provide new clues to BP physiology.
note: Flagship 2011 ICBP meta-analysis (PMID:21909115); the 200,000 is a rounded figure as the paper states it. The discovery stage was 69,395 individuals of European ancestry from 29 studies, with follow-up in up to 133,661 additional individuals; non-European look-ups used 29,719 East Asian, 23,977 South Asian and 19,775 African ancestry individuals.

label: Iowa LI cohort
counts: language-impairment cases and matched unrelated controls
quote: Replication cohorts Iowa LI Colorado RD Italy RD Cohort-type Case–control Family-based Family-based Number of subjects 428 1,188 878
note: The total 428 is from Table 1 of PMID:24509779 (the Iowa LI column). Cases and controls come from the text of the same paper (PMC4053598 fullTextXML): 'The Iowa LI cohort is composed of 219 LI cases and 209 sex- and age-matched, unrelated controls collected at the University of Iowa.' PMID:23691092 gives the same 219 and 209. The example study PMID:35998220 does not mention the cohort in the cached text.

label: Korea-Registries to Overcome Dementia and Accelerate Dementia Research
counts: participants registered across the three member cohorts who underwent amyloid PET
quote: As of December 2023, the K-ROAD cohort registered a total of 5,856 participants who underwent amyloid PET.
note: K-ROAD cohort profile (PMID:39512701). The abstract says 'over 5,800 participants'. By diagnosis: 5,121 Alzheimer's clinical syndrome (1,249 CU, 2,595 MCI, 1,277 DAT), 583 SVCI and 152 FTD participants. Pooled across the PREMIER consortium, LLOD cohort and SMC amyloid PET registry.

label: Mayo Genome Consortia
counts: unique genotyped participants in phase 1 (three contributing studies)
quote: Phase 1, which has been completed, includes participants from 3 studies funded by the National Institutes of Health, which sought to identify genetic determinants of peripheral arterial disease (PAD), venous thromboembolism, and pan- creatic cancer, respectively, with a combined total sample size of 6307 unique participants (Table 1).
note: MayoGC design paper (PMID:21646302). Phase 1 pooled eMERGE PAD (3197), GENEVA VTE (2497) and pancreatic cancer SPORE controls (613). The paper says phase 2 'will include more than 10,000 participants', a target, not an achieved size; a 2012 paper (PMID:23244446, PMC3554594) still analysed 'the entire MayoGC cohort of 6,307 subjects'. No later source with the achieved phase 2 size was found; the example study (PMID:38637617) names MayoGC without a count.

label: Impact of Migration and Ethnicity on Diabetes in Malmö
counts: Iraqi- and Swedish-born residents who took part in the 2010-2012 baseline
quote: Variable Country of birth Entire cohort p-value Iraq (1398) Sweden (757) 2155
note: The total is the 'Entire cohort' header of Table 1 in the MEDIM mortality follow-up paper (PMID:37061557), whose abstract says: 'A total of 1398 Iraqi- and 757 Swedish-born residents participated in the study.' Baseline was 2010-2012. The example GWAS (PMID:35227251) analysed 1201 Iraqi-born participants with complete GWAS data, a subset. Other papers give smaller analysed subsets (1881; 2081). The main MEDIM baseline paper (PMID:24842242) is closed and was not read.

label: Material and Information Resources for Inflammatory and Digestive Diseases Biobank
counts: individuals (CD, UC and non-IBD) in the MIRIAD serology dataset analysed; an analysed subset
quote: The cohorts include IBD cohorts from the Cedars-Sinai IBD Biobank (MIRIAD, size = 9231), the Risk Stratification and Identification of Immunogenetic and Microbial Markers of Rapid Disease Progression in Children with Crohn’s Disease (RISK, size = 431), and the Predictors of Response to Standardized Pediatric Colitis Therapy (PROTECT, size = 1102).
note: No source read states the size of the whole MIRIAD biobank. This number is the MIRIAD dataset used in a 2026 serology imputation study (PMID:41748696). The example study (PMID:38490347) used '1348 IBD cases with any EIM, 5303 IBD cases with no EIM' of European ancestry from MIRIAD. A 2025 ethics paper (PMC11831713) says the biobank 'holds over 20,000 samples', which counts samples, not people. A MIRIAD description paper or the Cedars-Sinai biobank page would settle it.

label: Lung Cancer and Smoking Phenotypes in African American Cases and Controls
counts: African American lung cancer cases and controls from eight studies in the stage 1 GWAS
quote: The stage 1 analysis included 1737 cases and 3602 controls among African Americans drawn from eight studies of lung cancer (Supplementary Table 2a).
note: Stage 1 of the GWAS (PMID:27393504) is the collection the term describes (eight studies). No sentence states the total, so participants is left null. The replication stage used an independent 866 cases and 796 controls from 7 studies, including 355 controls from a renal cancer GWAS; those are not part of the eight-study collection.

label: NIDDK IBD Genetics Consortium
counts: participants in the NIDDK Central Repository IBDGC collection (cases, controls and family members)
quote: 11,265 Participants
note: The NIDDK Central Repository study page gives the population as '11,265 Participants' (also 'Study Population Size' 11265 and a phenotype dataset of 11265 records); the page says the consortium 'prospectively recruits a combination of cases, controls, and trios', so this counts more than IBD patients, while the COHO term describes the patients. The definition source (PMID:36686985) analysed 3695 white non-Hispanic adults, '2744 affected by IBD and 951 controls recruited by the IBDGC GRCs between 2003 and 2012'. The example study (PMID:38490347) used 580 IBD cases with any EIM and 2059 with none.

label: Oregon Health and Science University study
counts: Caucasian AD cases and controls in the 2011 ADGC meta-analysis (analysed set)
note: Row of Table 1 ('Sample Description') of PMID:20697030; columns are cases, case autopsies, mean onset age, controls, control autopsies, mean age at last exam, total, percent. The autopsy counts (215, 461) exceed the case and control counts, so the row may hold an error in the published table. The text says OHSU subjects 'were recruited from aging research cohorts at 10 NIA-funded ADCs and do not overlap with other ADGC samples'. No OHSU-specific design paper was read; the example study (PMID:39633006) does not name OHSU in the cached text.

counts: approximate components only: healthy controls, schizophrenia patients, other diagnoses
quote: DNA samples from 1,775 unrelated healthy subjects of European ancestry were taken from the Phenomics and Genomics Sample (PAGES), which is comprised of ~3,000 controls, 1,000 schizophrenia patients and 300 individuals with other diagnoses.
note: No source read states a total for PAGES; the sources give only approximate components (~3,000 healthy controls, ~1,000 schizophrenia patients, ~300 other diagnoses), so participants is left null and only the approximate control count is recorded. PMID:32157568 (PMC7198638) says 'PAGES consists of approximately 3000 healthy individuals'. PMID:35379992 and the example study PMID:36066633 do not name PAGES in the cached text. A PAGES description paper stating the total would settle it.

counts: children with DNA or questionnaire data at the 2010 interim report (recruitment ongoing)
quote: To date 1045 children have been invited to participate and data collected in 501 (48%).
note: Interim count from the PAGES methodology paper (PMID:21134251), written while recruitment (2008-2011) was still under way; the final enrolment was not found in any open source. The definition source (PMID:25616159) had data for '391 children and adolescents of PAGES' (steroid-treated, an analysed subset); a montelukast study (PMC8457475) analysed PAGES n = 356 non-montelukast users. Later PAGES papers in PMC (PMC4931969, PMC6021964) could not be fetched as full text.

counts: patients under 18 with suspected IBD enrolled at diagnosis, 2008-2012 (all diagnoses and non-inflamed controls)
quote: 1813 patients were enrolled in our study (table 1).

quote: Over time, the TARCC sites enrolled a cohort of more than 3,600 study participants representing over 14,500 visits (an average of four annual visits for each subject).
note: The consortium's own study page; the figure is a lower bound ('more than 3,600'). The page also says about 35% of participants are of Hispanic ethnicity. The other definition source (PMID:36872777) states no cohort size in the cached text.

counts: children recruited in 2007-2009 (family risk, language concerns and typically developing)
quote: Of the 260 children recruited, none met exclusionary criteria at t1 (MZ twinning, chronic illness, deafness, English as a second language, care provision by local authority, and known neurological disorders such as cerebral palsy, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder).
note: Wellcome Language and Reading Project outcome paper (PMID:30676649). The planned size was 250; 234 children remained in the sample and were analysed (abstract: 'comparing them with controls (N = 234)'). The example study (PMID:35998220) does not give a separate count in the cached text.

counts: patients with IBD in the SHARE cohort data, 2012-2018
quote: Among 5,906 total patients with IBD, 468 (7.9%) reported a history of a colectomy with an IPAA as a treatment for UC.
note: From a SHARE pouch-disorders analysis (PMID:32744536) using data collected January 2012 to October 2018 at the 7 centres; the paper presents this as the total SHARE IBD population it drew on, not as a formal enrolment figure. label: Shanghai Changfeng Study
counts: community residents aged 45 or over enrolled at baseline, June 2009 to December 2012
quote: From June 2009 to December 2012, 6595 residents were enrolled.
note: From the 5.4-year mortality follow-up paper (PMID:31372866); 6591 were analysed after 4 lacked vital status.
