The example hip-shape GWAS (PMID:39574169) combined UK Biobank and Shanghai Changfeng (ntotal = 43 485) without a separate count in the matched text.

label: Collaborative Genetic Study of Nicotine Dependence
counts: array-genotyped COGEND participants (European and African American); an analysed/genotyped subset
quote: COGEND COPDGene ECLIPSE Array type Illumina HumanOmni2.5 Illumina HumanOmni1-Quad_v1-0_B Illumina HumanHap550v3.0 Array-genotyped data N, SNPs 2,443,179 1,051,295 561,466 Participants, total N 2,673 9,962 2,159
note: Table 1 of the example study (PMID:35953715): COGEND array data, 1,961 European and 712 African American participants. No source read states COGEND's total enrolment. The definition source (PMID:21968928) used '2666 COGEND subjects', including 612 alcohol-dependent cases and 2054 controls; a 2015 nicotine dependence meta-analysis (PMC4930126) kept 1935 participants after QC. A COGEND design description with its recruitment total would settle it.

label: EPIDG cohort
counts: pregnant women included January 2019 to February 2022
quote: Two-hundred women were included from January 2019 to February 2022 as follows: Control group -CG-, Lifestyle group -LG- (GDM not requiring insulin), and Insulin group -IG- (GDM requiring insulin).
note: The same paper gives the groups: "In the three groups, 134 women were included in the CG, 43 in the LG, and 23 in the IG.". Later EPIDG papers analyse subsets (PMID:39806399: 30 children; PMID:39408904: 32 women at baseline). Recruitment may have continued after February 2022; no later whole-cohort count was found.

label: Family Investigation of Nephropathy and Diabetes
note: No source read states how many people FIND enrolled in all. The design paper (PMID:15642484, J Diabetes Complications 2003) is closed and its abstract gives no numbers. Subsets read: the eGFR linkage paper (PMC3866106) says "A total of 3,960 FIND participants were genotyped for 6,000 single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) using the Illumina Linkage IVb panel."; the GWAS (PMID:26305897, PMC4549309) contrasted "6,197 unrelated individuals with advanced DKD with healthy and diabetic individuals lacking nephropathy", partly out-of-study samples; PMC4855449 mentions "the 869 American Indians who were recruited for the FIND"; dbGaP phs000333.v1.p1 lists 2622 consented subjects (GWAS release only). A FIND profile or the design paper's results would settle it.

label: Genetics Of Mortality In Critical Care
counts: GenOMICC critical COVID-19 cases analysed in the 2023 GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: Here we analyse 24,202 cases of COVID-19 with critical illness comprising a combination of microarray genotype and whole-genome sequencing data from cases of critical illness in the international GenOMICC (11,440 cases) study, combined with other studies recruiting hospitalized patients with a strong focus on severe and critical disease: ISARIC4C (676 cases) and the SCOURGE consortium (5,934 cases).
note: An analysed subset only, of COVID-19 cases; GenOMICC also recruits other critical illnesses. The 2022 WGS paper (PMID:35255492) analysed "7,491 critically ill individuals compared with 48,400 controls". The genomicc.org home page shows the whole-study count only through a script ("... participants have now been recruited to GenOMICC worldwide."); the script reads a UK tracker (https://genomicc.roslin.ed.ac.uk/GCC/json-summary returned {"total":37723} on 2026-09-25) and adds non-UK critical recruitment from a CSV, so no stated whole-study number was read. A GenOMICC profile paper would settle it.

label: Collaborative Oncological Gene-environment Study
counts: individuals (samples) genotyped in COGS across the four consortia, 167 research groups
quote: In all, we included 239,832 individuals from 167 research groups in COGS.
note: From the COGS final report summary on CORDIS, which also says "The total number of samples genotyped was 239,832." and "Genotyping started in September 2010 and ended in April 2011." Its table gives breast cancer cases and controls 116,065 (52 groups), prostate 51,576 (43), ovarian 47,916 (27), BRCA1/2 carriers 24,275 (45). The BCAC paper (PMID:23535729) says the arrays genotyped 114,255 DNA samples from 52 BCAC studies and analysed 45,290 cases and 41,880 controls of European ancestry.

label: Kentucky Case-Control Study
counts: incident colon cancer cases and population controls analysed (analysed subset)
quote: We analyzed data for 1,093 incident cases and 1,589 controls in a population-based case-control study of colon cancer to further clarify the GL-colon cancer relationship.
note: PMID:24611536 (recruitment April 2003 to December 2010). No sentence states a total, so participants is left null. These are the analysed participants: "We included 1,589 controls and 1,093 cases in our analyses, excluding 35 individuals with missing values for GL, and 3 individuals with missing data for family history." The example study (PMID:38749303) names Kentucky only in funding and acknowledgements.

label: Los Angeles Latino Eye Study
counts: eligible Latinos aged 40+ who had a baseline clinical examination
quote: Of the 7789 individuals eligible for LALES, 6357 (82%) had a clinical examination; an additional 524 completed only an in-home interview.
note: From the LALES design and baseline paper (abstract; full text closed). 7789 were eligible; 524 more completed only the in-home interview and are not counted here. Baseline examinations began in 2000.

label: Mexican Hypertriglyceride Study
counts: Mexican hypertriglyceridaemic cases and normotriglyceridaemic controls in GWAS stages 1 and 2
quote: A total of 4,400 Mexican hypertriglyceridemic cases and normotriglyceridemic controls were included in stage 1 and 2 (see Supplementary Table 1 for clinical characteristics).
note: PMID:23505323. The same paper says "A total of 6,073 participants were included in the study.", which also counts the follow-up sample ("1,712 additional Mexican subjects (1,056 hypertriglyceridemia cases and controls and 656 family members from 77 Mexican dyslipidemic families)"); the case-control collection itself is the 4,400. After QC 2,240 individuals were analysed in stage 1, and the joint stage 1 and 2 analysis had n=4,361. The case/control split is only in Supplementary Table 1, not read.

label: San Francisco Bay Area Breast Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls who completed the in-person interview
quote: Of those selected, 2258 (88%) completed an in‐person interview, including 1119 (89%) Hispanic, 543 (87%) African American, and 596 (86%) NHW cases.
note: PMID:29573201, describing the SFBCS (conducted 1995 to 2004). The controls come from the same paragraph: "Of these, 2706 (85%) completed the in‐person interview, including 1462 (88%) Hispanics, 598 (82%) African Americans, and 646 (83%) NHWs." No sentence states the combined total, so participants is left null. That paper analysed 2135 cases and 2571 controls with dietary data. The GWAS paper (PMID:25327703) used 351 Latina cases and 579 Latina controls. The original SFBCS design papers (John et al., cited as refs 24 and 25) were not read.

label: SIGMA Type 2 Diabetes Consortium
counts: Mexicans and other Latin Americans in the 2014 SIGMA type 2 diabetes GWAS (cases and controls)
quote: Here we analysed 9.2 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in each of 8,214 Mexicans and other Latin Americans: 3,848 with type 2 diabetes and 4,366 non-diabetic controls.
note: The consortium's flagship GWAS (Nature 2014), pooled from its member studies; the full text adds that these were unrelated samples genotyped on the Illumina OMNI 2.5 array.

label: Mexico City sample 2
counts: individuals in the sample (type 2 diabetes cases and controls), lipid GWAS Table 1
quote: Mexico City 1*Mexico City 2*Starr CountyN (F, M)1310 (833,477)1787 (895,892)1286 (858,428)
note: PMID:26780889. The total is from Table 1 (N 1787 for Mexico City 2, 895 women and 892 men); the prose says "Mexico City-sample 2: This sample comprises 898 individuals with type 2 diabetes and 889 controls." Recruitment years are not given.

label: Mexico City sample 1
counts: individuals who took part (type 2 diabetes cases and normoglycaemic controls)
quote: A total of 1,334 individuals participated in this study, 989 cases and 345 normoglycaemic controls.
note: PMID:21573907, the sample's GWAS paper. After quality control 24 were removed, and "the final sample used in the statistical analysis comprised 967 cases (664 women, 303 men) and 343 controls (169 women, 174 men)"; the 2016 lipid paper (PMID:26780889) Table 1 gives N 1310 for Mexico City 1.

label: 1982 Pelotas (Brazil) Birth Cohort Study
counts: live births enrolled in 1982
quote: In 1982, 5914 live births whose families lived in the urban are of Pelotas were enrolled in the cohort.
note: From the 2015 cohort profile update (the quote keeps the paper's typo "urban are"). At the 30-year follow-up: "In 2012-13, we tried to locate the whole original cohort; 3701 participants were interviewed who, added to the 325 known deaths, represented a follow-up rate of 68.1%."

label: Agricultural Health Study
counts: licensed pesticide applicators enrolled 1993-1997 (enrolled spouses not included)
quote: The AHS is a prospective cohort that includes 57,310 licensed pesticide applicators enrolled in Iowa or North Carolina between 1993 and 1997.
note: Applicators only. The AHS website (https://aghealth.nih.gov/about/) says "Between 1993 and 1997, 52,394 licensed private pesticide applicators (mostly farmers) from Iowa and North Carolina enrolled, as did 32,345 of their spouses.", "The study also included 4,916 commercial pesticide applicators in Iowa in its first two phases." and "More than 89,000 farmers and their spouses in Iowa and North Carolina have participated in the study." No source read states an exact total of applicators and spouses together. PMID:38381478 analysed 53,562 applicators.

label: Agricultural Lung Health Study
counts: farmers and spouses enrolled 2009-2013
quote: The ALHS enroled 3301 participants in the period 2009–2013.
note: From PMC7469973 (PMID:32381493). The same paragraph gives the asthma case definitions (876 with self-reported current diagnosed asthma without COPD, 309 with potential undiagnosed asthma, and a third group) and says "Controls (n=2078) were randomly selected from the AHS participants without the above criteria."; no sentence read gives the total number of cases.

label: AncestryDNA Human Diversity Project
counts: consenting AncestryDNA research participants who answered the 2020 COVID-19 survey (a subset of the Human Diversity Project)
quote: In less than 4 months during an early phase of the pandemic, we collected survey data from 736,723 AncestryDNA research participants who consented to research.
note: Only the COVID-19 survey respondents as of 3 August 2020; the number of customers consented to the Human Diversity Project as a whole was not stated in any source read. The 2024 influenza paper (PMID:39103650), after five surveys up to February 2021, says "About 900,000 customers completed at least one survey (66.4% female, median age 57)."; it analysed 18,448 influenza cases and 277,865 controls. A statement from AncestryDNA of the Human Diversity Project's size would settle it.

label: All New Diabetics In Scania
counts: newly diagnosed patients in the 2018 cluster analysis (analysed subset)
quote: We did data-driven cluster analysis (k-means and hierarchical clustering) in patients with newly diagnosed diabetes (n=8980) from the Swedish All New Diabetics in Scania cohort.
note: An analysed subset of an ongoing registry. No exact whole-cohort count was found. The Swedish National Data Service entry (https://snd.gu.se/en/catalogue/study/EXT0057) says "Ongoing study, currently> 11,000 patients (January 2015).", a lower bound; the Lund University infrastructure page says ANDIS started in 2008 and registers about 1500-2000 new participants a year. PMC10156700 says people were recruited from January 2008 until November 2016 (the first phase). The Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol paper (PMID:29503172) was read as its abstract only. A current count from ANDIS would settle it.

label: Brisbane Longitudinal Twin Study
counts: adolescent and young adult twins in the sample in 2013 (their 1,572 non-twin siblings not included)
quote: Currently the BLTS sample comprises both adolescent and young adult twins (3,408 individuals) and their non-twin siblings (1,572), constituting 1,703 families.
note: PMID:23187020 (Twin Res Hum Genet 2013). Twins only; the same sentence gives 1,572 non-twin siblings, and no sentence states the combined total. The paper adds "The BLTS recruits approximately 100 new twins per year". Later waves: 19Up (PMID:29550775) collected data 2009-2016 on 2773 participants (of 4156 invited); 25Up (PMID:31198126) 2540 twins and siblings in 2016-2018; a 2020 thyroid paper assessed 3415 participants at ages 12, 14 and 16. A current BLTS profile would give an up-to-date total.

label: Coronary ARtery DIsease Genome wide Replication and Meta-analysis
counts: CAD cases and controls of European descent in the 2011 discovery meta-analysis of 14 GWAS
quote: We performed a meta-analysis of 14 genome-wide association studies of coronary artery disease (CAD) comprising 22,233 individuals with CAD (cases) and 64,762 controls of European descent followed by genotyping of top association signals in 56,682 additional individuals.
note: The consortium's flagship analysis (Nat Genet 2011). No sentence states the discovery total, so participants is left null; the paper describes the whole effort as "The present genomic analysis of more than 135,000 individuals", a lower bound. The replication stage is given as 56,682 additional individuals in the abstract and "up to 60,738 additional subjects" in the text. Member studies: 14 GWAS.

label: Centers for AIDS Research Network of Integrated Clinical Systems
counts: people with HIV in the cohort, cumulative, as of early 2026
quote: As of early of 2026, CNICS contained 51,692 patients.
note: The CNICS home page (https://sites.uab.edu/cnics/) says the same: "The cohort included 51,692 participants , as of early 2026." The example study (PMID:37796845) analysed up to 7,542 PWH, with genetic data on 10,049 after QC. The 2008 cohort profile (PMID:18263650) was not read.

label: Diabetes Control and Complications Trial/Epidemiology of Diabetes Interventions and Complications Study
counts: people with type 1 diabetes randomised in the DCCT (the cohort followed in EDIC)
quote: The DCCT (1982-1993) was a controlled clinical trial in 1,441 subjects with T1DM comparing intensive therapy (INT), aimed at achieving levels of glycemia as close to the nondiabetic range as safely possible, with conventional therapy (CON), which aimed to maintain safe asymptomatic glucose control.
note: From the DCCT/EDIC 30-year overview (Diabetes Care 2014). The same paper says "At the end of DCCT, after an average of 6.5 years (range 3–9), more than 99% (1,422 of 1,441) completed the study." and "EDIC (1994-present) is an observational study of the DCCT cohort." PMC9727532 also gives 1441 volunteers from 29 centres, 1983 to 1993. The number who joined EDIC in 1994 was not stated in the text read.

label: Danish National Birth Cohort
counts: pregnant women recruited 1996-2002
quote: The DNBC is a collection of data on 92,274 pregnant women recruited between 1996 and 2002, from their first antenatal visit to their general practitioner.
note: Cohort description in the supplementary note of the example study (PMID:37012456). The DNBC website (https://www.dnbc.dk/about-the-dnbc) says the aim was to recruit 100,000 women and 'In October 2002, we reached the goal of 100.000 recruitments.' (recruitments, i.e. pregnancies, not women); it also gives 60,000 women by August 2000. The cohort profile paper was not read.

label: Environment And Genetics in Lung cancer Etiology study
counts: incident lung cancer cases and population controls enrolled 2002-2005
quote: Between 2002 and 2005, we enrolled 2101 incident primary lung cancer cases and 2120 population controls, with 86.6% and 72.4% participation rate, respectively, from a catchment area including 216 municipalities in the Lombardy region of Italy.
note: Design paper states cases and controls separately but no total, so participants is left null (not summed). It also says 2343 cases were enrolled before diagnosis review excluded 179 without lung cancer and 63 uncertain/ineligible.

label: EArly Genetics and Lifecourse Epidemiology consortium
counts: discovery cases and controls in the 2015 EAGLE atopic dermatitis meta-analysis
quote: we performed a meta-analysis of >15 million genetic variants in 21,399 cases and 95,464 controls from populations of European, African, Japanese and Latino ancestry, followed by replication in 32,059 cases and 228,628 controls from 18 studies.
note: The EGG/EAGLE consortium design paper (PMID:30887376) lists member cohorts in Table 1 but states no pooled participant count or number of member cohorts in a sentence. The example study (PMID:40164604) describes the EAGLE atopic dermatitis meta-analysis (PMID:26482879) as '~21,000 cases and 95,000 controls'; its abstract gives 21,399 cases and 95,464 controls in discovery. EAGLE runs many trait meta-analyses (asthma, ADHD, cognition...), so this is one analysis, not a consortium-wide total; no total is stated, so participants is null.

label: EAGLE BioVU
counts: non-European-American BioVU subjects genotyped on Metabochip by EAGLE
quote: The study population consists of 15,863 mostly non-European American subjects from BioVU, the Vanderbilt University Medical Center (VUMC) biorepository linked to de-identified EHRs.
note: PMID:28815105 (EAGLE study paper). The same paper says 'EAGLE genotyped 11,519 African Americans, 1,702 Hispanics, and 1,118 Asians among other mostly non-European samples'; PMID:26566401 Table 1 gives EAGLE BioVU n = 15,863. The example study (PMID:30044860) analysed only 656 EAGLE BioVU women for age at menarche (table value).

label: Elucidating Loci Involved in Prostate Cancer Susceptibility
counts: prostate cancer cases and controls in the ELLIPSE dbGaP genotype dataset (phs001120) as analysed by the example study
quote: The Elucidating Loci Involved in Prostate Cancer Susceptibility (ELLIPSE) consortium prostate cancer meta-analysis and genotypes (dbGaP Study Accession: phs001120.v1.p1) was accessed to analyze Affymetrix genotype calls for 91,644 male PrCa case/controls.
note: Example study PMID:36494783; the number is the case/control total in the dbGaP release it accessed, not a consortium-reported pooled count, and cases and controls are not separated. The dbGaP pages cited by the definition (phs001120.v1.p1, phs001391.v1.p1) give per-study counts only (e.g. UK GWAS stage 1 1854 cases/1894 controls, PEGASUS 4600/2941, iCOGS 10366 subjects) and no pooled total. The consortium's own flagship meta-analysis paper (OncoArray/ELLIPSE, PRACTICAL-linked) was not read and would settle the pooled number.

label: Helsinki 2000 Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study
note: The MEGASTROKE supplementary note (https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-018-0058-3/MediaObjects/41588_2018_58_MOESM1_ESM.pdf) describes the study but gives only its target: 'The study aims at recruiting 2000 eligible patients and the study is still recruiting patients.' (a plan, not an achieved size); the main paper (PMID:29531354) gives no sentence with its numbers. Europe PMC finds two other papers naming it: PMC8305811 lists 164 tPA-treated HELSINKI2000 patients in a table (a subset, not in a sentence); PMC6745730 had no count. MEGASTROKE's supplementary tables of per-study cases and controls, or a design paper for the study, would settle it.

label: GEN-COVID Multicenter Study
counts: SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals with samples and data collected by 16 July 2020
quote: As of July 16, 2020, we have collected samples and data from 1033 individuals (1021 without family ties and 12 with family relations).
note: Early count from the design paper, while recruitment was ongoing ('Recruitment remains ongoing with the goal of including samples and data from 2000 individuals by the end of September 2020.'). The later example study (PMID:36143338) used an exome dataset that 'comprised of the data from 2960 COVID-19 patients' (2692 of European ancestry); a more recent GEN-COVID cohort description would give the achieved size.

label: Hawaii Colorectal Cancer Studies 2 and 3
counts: interviewed colorectal cancer cases and matched controls in a Hawaii population-based case-control study (probably this one)
quote: We interviewed 727 Japanese, Caucasian or Native Hawaiian cases and 727 controls matched on sex, age, and ethnicity.
note: Abstract of PMID:12351160 (2002, 'Well-done red meat, metabolic phenotypes and colorectal cancer in Hawaii'), a population-based case-control study of Japanese, Caucasian and Native Hawaiian residents matching the definition; its abstract does not give the 1994-1998 enrolment dates, so its identity with Colo2&3 is not confirmed (the full text, not openly available, would settle it). PMID:12020105 gives the same 727/727. No total stated. The GECCO supplement (ng.2505 MOESM12) describes Colo2&3 as enrolling 'in the Oahu area between 1994 and 1998' without numbers; the definition sources (PMID:38561434, PMID:31875139) give only the genotyped GECCO subset (87 cases, 122 controls in a table of PMID:31875139).

label: Heinz Nixdorf Recall Study
counts: participants aged 45-75 at the baseline examination 2000-2003
quote: N=4814 participants aged 45–75 years were included in the baseline examination (T0) between 2000 and 2003 (recruitment rate: 55.8%).
note: Same paper: first follow-up T1 n=4157 (2005-2008), second T2 n=3087 (2010-2015). The original design paper was not read, but 4814 is the standard baseline figure repeated throughout this source.

label: INflammation, Health, Ancestry and Lung Epidemiology study
counts: genotyped lung cancer cases and controls (analysed subset, NHW and AA)
quote: These P/LP variants were genotyped in a sample of 3,040 lung cancer cases and controls from the INHALE study (non-Hispanic White: n=1,915; African American: n=1,125) and were tested for their association with lung cancer using multivariate logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, pack-years, and race.
note: PMID:39854657 (a definition source); same paper: 'Of the 3,040 participants, 1,662 (54.7%) were lung cancer cases.' Controls appear only in its table (1,378), so controls is left null. This is the genotyped subset; no source read states the whole enrolment 2012-2018. PMID:35024781 gives 912 cases and 1457 controls (ever-smokers only); the example study PMID:40341939 used 294 cases and 518 controls (African American GWAS subset); PMC9307937 used 728 cases with PFTs. The INHALE design description (cited as Schwartz et al., ref 17 of PMID:39854657) was not read.

label: Malmö Diet and Cancer Study–Cardiovascular Cohort
counts: randomly selected MDC participants enrolled into the cardiovascular sub-study 1991-1994
quote: Between October 1991 and February 1994 a randomly selected subgroup of 6103 MDC participants was included into a study focusing on carotid artery disease epidemiology (MDC-CV)12.
note: Also 'every other MDCS participant was invited to join a sub-study on cardiovascular disease risk (MDCS-CC; N = 6103)' in PMC8660752. Analysed subsets: 4338 (sRAGE GWAS, PMC11109115), 4022 (galectin-1, PMC8660752). The parent MDC cohort had 30,448 subjects.

label: MiaLAtinX Consortium
counts: post-QC IBD cases and site-ascertained non-IBD controls
quote: Post-QC, 1660 cases (939 CD, 684 UC, 37 IBDU) and 5614 controls (954 ascertained at recruiting sites and 4660 from SOL) were available for downstream analyses.
note: PMID:41661118. The analysis's 5614 controls include 4660 external HCHS/SOL population controls that are not MiaLAtinX recruits, so controls is the 954 ascertained at the recruiting sites; no total of cases plus site controls is stated, so participants is null. The abstract's '~7.3K Hispanic participants (1660 IBD cases; 5614 controls)' counts the SOL controls. Numbers are post-QC; the pre-QC recruitment count is not given.

label: Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1986
counts: live-born children with expected birth July 1985-June 1986
quote: The study was based on the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1986 (NFBC1986) [20], which is an unselected, general population sample based on 9432 live-born children with an expected date of birth between July 1 st, 1985 – June 30th, 1986, in the provinces of Oulu and Lapland [21].
note: PMID:40858910 (definition source). The cohort's mothers and total births (including stillbirths) are not counted here; the example study (PMID:42036355) was not needed. Analysed subsets in this paper are much smaller (e.g. 2334 male and 2550 female controls).

label: Ragama Health Study
counts: recruited adults with complete baseline data followed as the RHS cohort
quote: At the baseline assessment 2985 of the recruited participants had complete data and were followed-up as the Ragama Health Study (RHS) cohort.
note: Same paper: 3012 adults aged 35-64 were recruited July 2007-March 2008 ('At the commencement of the study in 2007, 3012 adults between 35 and 64 years of age living in the Ragama MOH area were recruited using age stratified random sampling...'); 2985 form the followed cohort.

label: Singapore Chinese Eye Study
counts: Chinese adults examined at baseline SCES-1 (2009-2011)
quote: We herein report the key findings from the baseline Singapore Chinese Eye Study (SCES-1), and describe the rationale and methodology of the 6-year follow-up study (SCES-2).Methods3353 Chinese adults who participated in the baseline SCES-1 (2009-2011) were invited for the 6-year follow-up SCES-2 (2015-2017).
note: Profile paper abstract. Same paper: 'Of the 3033 eligible individuals from SCES-1, 2661 participated in SCES-2 (response rate=87.7%).'

label: Singapore Epidemiology of Eye Diseases Study
counts: Malay, Indian and Chinese adults aged 40-80 who took part at baseline (2004-2011)
quote: All subjects provided written informed consent.In brief, an age-stratified random sampling method was used to select 13 271 subjects (4168 Malays, 4497 Indians, and 4606 Chinese) aged 40–80 years, from which a total of 10 033 subjects (3280 Malays, 3400 Indians, and 3353 Chinese) participated in the study, thereby achieving a response rate of 75.6%.
note: PMID:38025163. Same paper: 6762 subjects attended the SEED-2 follow-up; the abstract's 5551 is the analysed subset for incident visual impairment.

label: Singapore Indian Eye Study
counts: Indian adults who took part at baseline SINDI (2007-2009)
quote: All subjects provided written informed consent.In brief, an age-stratified random sampling method was used to select 13 271 subjects (4168 Malays, 4497 Indians, and 4606 Chinese) aged 40–80 years, from which a total of 10 033 subjects (3280 Malays, 3400 Indians, and 3353 Chinese) participated in the study, thereby achieving a response rate of 75.6%.
note: Baseline Indian count from the SEED paper (PMID:38025163); 4497 Indians were selected. The SINDI-2 methodology paper (PMID:28472538, definition source) gives the follow-up: 'Of the 2914 eligible SINDI participants invited to participate, 2200 participated in SINDI-2 (response rate of 75.2%).' The original SINDI baseline methods paper was not read.

label: TAICHI Consortium
counts: subjects genotyped with the CardioMetaboChip for the TAICHI CAD analysis (CAD cases and controls)
quote: As part of the TAICHI Consortium, we have collected and genotyped 8556 subjects from Taiwan, comprising 5423 controls and 3133 cases with coronary artery disease, for 9087 CAD SNPs using the CardioMetaboChip.
note: Pooled number for the consortium's coronary artery disease analysis (PMID:26982883); TAICHI has run other trait analyses whose sample sizes may differ. No count of member studies is stated in a sentence.

label: University of Southern California Hormone Replacement Therapy Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: women with newly diagnosed colon cancer and population control women
quote: To further investigate the relationship between menopausal hormones and risk of colon cancer, we conducted a population-based case-control study in Los Angeles County involving 831 women with newly diagnosed colon cancer and 755 population-based control women.
note: Abstract of the study's own results paper (PMID:20064828, 2010). No total is stated, so participants is null. The genotyped subset in GECCO (PMID:35512400) is 296 cases and 400 controls (table only).

label: UK Dyslexia Cohort
counts: 689 siblings from 409 families plus 676 singletons (no total stated)
quote: The family cohort was recruited by research clinics in Oxford and Reading and included 689 siblings from 409 families. The singleton cohort was recruited in clinics in Oxford, Reading and Aston, and included 676 children.
note: PMID:36780127 (definition source) states the two components separately but no total, so participants is null (not summed). Its Table 1 gives '~1300' probands for the UK Dyslexia Cohort (a table value, not a sentence). 302 children met its reading-impairment criteria. The cohort's design description (Scerri et al. 2017, cited there) was not read.

label: African Ancestry Prostate Cancer Consortium
counts: prostate cancer cases and controls of African ancestry in the AAPC GWAS (as pooled in the 2017 meta-analysis)
quote: To search for additional PCa risk variants in men of African ancestry that may contribute to their greater disease incidence, we combined genetic association results from the African Ancestry Prostate Cancer GWAS Consortium (AAPC; 4853 case subjects and 4678 control subjects) (9), the Ghana Prostate Study (474 case subjects and 458 control subjects) (10), the Kaiser/ProHealth Prostate Cancer Study (601 case subjects and 1650 control subjects) (11), and the ELLIPSE/PRACTICAL OncoArray Consortium (4274 case subjects and 4024 control subjects) (Supplementary Table 1, available online).
note: No source read states a total, so participants is null. The founding GWAS (PMID:21602798) reported stage 1 as '3,425 African-Americans with prostate cancer (cases) and 3,290 African-American male controls', with 1,844 cases and 3,269 controls in follow-up; its supplement lists the member studies (MEC, SCCS, PLCO, CPS-II, MDA, IPCG, LAAPC, CaP Genes, DCPC, KCPCS, GECAP). The 2021 multiancestry paper (PMID:33398198) gives 10,368 cases and 10,986 controls of African ancestry across several consortia, not AAPC alone.

label: Prevalence, Prediction and Prevention of Diabetes-Botnia Study
counts: individuals who participated (random population sample aged 18-75), 2004-2008
quote: Altogether 5,208 individuals (Electronic supplementary material [ESM] Table 1) participated in the study (54.7% of those invited).
note: From the definition source PMID:20454776, whose abstract says the study 'includes a random sample of 5,208 individuals aged 18 to 75 years identified through the national Finnish Population Registry' and whose methods say it was carried out from 2004 to 2008. label: The Cleft Collective

label: Children's Oncology Group
counts: no total stated; about 9,500 participants registered on COG studies each year

A COG statement of cumulative enrolment (e.g. Project:EveryChild patients enrolled) would settle it.

label: Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism
counts: individuals in 2246 families assessed in one or more waves over 30+ years

counts: cancer cases and controls in the GAME-ON GWAS data used for the 2016 height Mendelian randomization analysis

counts: HNSCC patients pooled from DAHANCA 10, DAHANCA 19 and the DAHANCA prospective biobank protocol (2000-2011)

The example study (PMID:36191651, Radiother Oncol) is not open access and its cached copy is empty, so it was not read; it is not needed for the count.

No source read states a current total.

The definition source (PMID:36629499) pools EIMS with GEMS (6635 cases, 8880 controls) without an EIMS-only count; other papers use subsets (907 cases and 907 controls, PMID:41411973).

counts: MS patients with data in the registry (of an estimated 17,500 prevalent in Sweden)

The registry keeps growing, so the current number is larger; the neuroreg.se pages fetched gave no patient count. A current registry annual report would settle it.

counts: AD cases from 9 Canadian memory clinics and cognitively normal controls in the discovery GWAS

note: From the structured abstract of the design paper (Li et al. 2008, Arch Neurol), after its 'Participants' heading; only the abstract is cached. No total is stated, so participants is null. label: Hospital-based Epidemiologic Research Program at Aichi Cancer Center

Other numbers seen: 15,655 HERPACC subjects genotyped on the Asian Screening Array (PMC12775586); HERPACC n = 4958 in the example GWAS (PMID:38277453), with an oesophageal cancer case-control set of 692 cases and 995 controls; HERPACC 1,502 men and 1,540 women in J-CGE (PMID:34897183); 55904 non-cancer controls who first visited 1988-1997 (PMID:11676850 abstract). quote: A total of 419 individuals from 176 families were included in the study.
note: PMID:35951362 (definition source). PMID:34923481 agrees: 'For the ASPS-Fam a total of 419 individuals were included.' Analysed subsets: 130 (R2* iron), 327 (sNfL), 302 (telorism GWAS).

label: B-Vitamins for the PRevention Of Osteoporotic Fractures
counts: subjects aged 65+ with elevated homocysteine in the trial
quote: The intervention comprises a period of two years, and includes 2919 subjects, aged 65 years and older, independently living or institutionalized, with an elevated homocysteine concentration (≥ 12 μmol/L).
note: PMID:22136481, the B-PROOF design paper. Planned size was 1500 per arm.

label: Canadian Partnership for Tomorrow's Health
counts: participants aged 30-74 recruited across 5 regional cohorts (2018 profile)
quote: All participant data across the 5 regional cohorts were harmonized.ResultsA total of 307 017 participants aged 30-74 from 8 provinces were recruited.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of the 2018 CPTP cohort profile (heading run-in 'harmonized.Results' as in the fetched text). The CanPath website (https://canpath.ca/about/) now says 'CanPath has collected data from approximately 330,000 volunteer Canadians', a later approximate figure after further cohorts (e.g. Manitoba, Saskatchewan) joined; the profile's exact count is used as the preferred profile source.

label: DeCOI cohort
counts: SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals with WGS after quality control
quote: These analyses comprehensively characterize the joint contribution of variants of the entire allelic spectrum to severe COVID-19.ResultsThe DeCOI cohortFollowing quality control (see Methods), the DeCOI cohort comprised 1,220 individuals from across the entire phenotypic spectrum of SARS-CoV-2 infections (Figs 1A–1C and S1).
note: PMID:39715278. 1,275 samples with phenotype data were sequenced before QC ('Of the 1,275 samples, 35 had an average coverage of <20x and/or a call rate of <90%'); 827 of the 1,220 were hospitalized COVID-19 cases; 1,017 unrelated European-ancestry individuals formed DeCOI-EUR. 1,220 is the cohort as the paper defines it; case/control splits vary by severity definition, so they are not recorded.

label: EU-RLS-GENE consortium
counts: cases and controls in the EU-RLS-GENE GWAS of the 2024 meta-analysis (no total stated)
quote: International EU-RLS-GENE consortium (7,248 cases (2,479 males and 4,769 females) and 19,802 controls (10,422 males and 9,380 females))
note: PMID:38839884; the quote is the Methods subsection heading for the consortium's discovery dataset. The paper's overall meta-analysis (116,647 cases and 1,546,466 controls) also includes 23andMe and INTERVAL, so it is not the consortium's own count. No combined total is stated, so participants is left null.

label: Familial Influences on Literacy Abilities
counts: 483 children from 307 nuclear families and 505 adults (no total stated)
quote: This dataset comprised 483 children from 307 nuclear families and 505 adults (including parents of participating children), and provided adequate statistical power to detect the effects that were previously reported.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:27198479 (only the abstract is on disk). The source gives children and adults separately but no combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The full text or the GenLang supplement of PMID:35998220 might state the total.

label: Female Lung Cancer Consortium in Asia
counts: never-smoking female cases and controls scanned in the 2012 FLCCA GWAS (no total stated)
quote: We scanned 5,510 never-smoking female lung cancer cases and 4,544 controls drawn from 14 studies from mainland China, South Korea, Japan, Singapore, Taiwan and Hong Kong.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of the consortium's flagship GWAS (Nat Genet 2012, PMID:23143601): 14 member studies; replication in 'an additional 1,099 cases and 2,913 controls'. No pooled total stated, so participants is null. The example study PMID:37236969 used FLCCA within a larger East Asian meta-analysis (11,753 cases and 30,562 controls in discovery across four studies) and refers to '4544 controls from the FLCCA study'. The definition source PMID:42152146 gives no FLCCA-specific count.

label: GlobalGout Genetics Consortium
counts: people (approx., '2.6 million') in the 2024 gout GWAS the consortium co-authored; includes 23andMe, UK Biobank and other cohorts
quote: Here, we provide insights into the molecular mechanism of the poorly understood inflammatory component of gout from a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of 2.6 million people, including 120,295 people with prevalent gout.
note: PMID:39406924 abstract (full text paywalled; only the abstract and front matter were readable). The 2.6 million is a rounded figure and covers all contributing cohorts, most of them not the consortium's own; the medRxiv preprint says '2.6 million people, including 120,282 people with gout'. The consortium's own sample appears only as a table row in the preprint supplement (media-1.xlsx): 'New Zealand/Ardea Biosciences/EuroGout' with 4713 gout cases and 2151 controls; not recorded as fields because it is a table cell rather than a sentence. A source stating the consortium's own collection size in prose would settle a narrower count.

label: Growing Up in Singapore Towards healthy Outcomes
counts: pregnant women enrolled June 2009-September 2010
quote: The study enrolled 1468 pregnant women at least 18 years of age between June 2009 and September 2010 attending their first trimester antenatal dating ultrasound scan clinic at Singapore’s two major public maternity units.
note: PMID:41829988 (definition source). The same paper later says 'Of the 1450 mothers enrolled in GUSTO, 1037 were followed until at least 7 years old.', so 1468 may include women later excluded. The cohort profile (PMID:23912809, Int J Epidemiol 2014) has no abstract in Europe PMC and was not readable; it would settle the enrolled and eligible counts.

label: Hawaii Adenoma Study
counts: analysed subset: adenoma cases and controls with DNA (no total or full enrolment stated)
quote: The present analyses were based on 914 colorectal adenoma cases and 1,188 controls with available DNA.
note: PMID:24083639 (2013, bitter-taste receptor genes); the same PLCO Hawaii / Kaiser Permanente Hawaii case-control design is described there. This is the largest subset found but is limited to participants with DNA; no source read states the full number interviewed. The definition source PMID:20501760 analysed '554 cases and 786 controls who were interviewed up to February 2007 and gave a blood sample' (participation 68% cases, 69% controls). PMID:21081473 abstract: '914 cases, 1185 controls'. A design paper giving the total interviewed would settle it.

label: Henry Ford Heart Failure Pharmacogenomic Registry
counts: heart failure patients enrolled (stated as more than 1700)
quote: The Henry Ford Heart Failure Pharmacogenomic registry has enrolled more than 1700 HF patients of any type and collected blood/plasma samples and detailed phenotypic information.
note: A lower bound ('more than 1700') from a 2017 metabolomics paper of the registry (PMID:29096792); enrolment ran October 2007 to March 2015, so this is after enrolment closed. The same paper analysed 1070 patients with EF <50%. The definition source / example study (PMID:38002962) gives only its analysed HFrEF subset (469 Black and 459 White patients); PMID:34425222 analysed 416 Black and 369 White HFrEF patients. The registry's design paper was not identified.

label: HS Program for Research and Care Excellence
counts: patients with hidradenitis suppurativa in the expanded study
quote: We expanded the HS ProCARE study to 986 patients and used METAL to conduct a GWAS meta-analysis across six studies (Table S1; see Supporting Information).
note: Most recent count. The first GWAS (PMID:37494057) says 'A total of 753 patients were recruited, with 720 included in the analysis' (August 2018 to July 2021). HS ProCARE is a patient series with no controls of its own (controls came from Add Health).

label: IARC Multicenter Case-Control Study
counts: lung cancer cases and controls in the central European GWAS (genotyped subset)
quote: To identify genetic factors that modify disease risk, we conducted a genome-wide association study by analysing 317,139 single-nucleotide polymorphisms in 1,989 lung cancer cases and 2,625 controls from six central European countries.
note: The IARC central European GWAS paper (abstract); no sentence states the total, so participants is null. These are the genome-wide genotyped subjects, not necessarily everyone recruited to the multicentre case-control study (1999-2003), whose overall recruitment was not found. The definition source (PMID:22899653) lists 'IARC GWAS Central Europe' with 1854 cases and 2453 controls in Table 1 of its 2012 meta-analysis. The example study (PMID:34815255) gives only pooled INTEGRAL-ILCCO numbers.

label: Identification and prevention of Dietary- and lifestyle-induced health EFfects In Children and infantS
counts: children aged 2-9.9 examined at baseline
quote: The baseline examination (T0) between September 2007 and June 2008 included 16 228 children aged 2 to 9.9 years from eight European countries: Belgium, Cyprus, Estonia, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Spain and Sweden.
note: Cohort profile (IJE 2017). The same paper reports 2555 children newly recruited at the first follow-up (T1) and, in the I.Family wave (T3, 2013-2014), 7105 index children and 2512 newly recruited siblings. The example study (PMID:37420130) says 16,229 children at baseline and genotyped 3099 children.

label: Insulin Resistance Atherosclerosis Study
counts: participants in the baseline examination
quote: A total of 1,625 individuals participated in the baseline IRAS examination (56% women), which occurred between October 1992 and April 1994.
note: The design paper's abstract (PMID:8680609) says 'Over 1600 men and women were recruited'; its full text (Ann Epidemiol 1995) is not open. The exact baseline count is from a 2010 IRAS paper that is also a definition source.

label: Personalized Medicine Research Project
counts: adults in the population-based biobank cohort (approximately)
quote: The Personalized Medicine Research Project is a population based cohort of approximately 20,000 individuals ages 18 and up residing within one of 19 zip codes surrounding Marshfield Wisconsin, USA, who have agreed to provide DNA, serum, and plasma samples to be linked with a dynamic medical record for research [26].
needs: McCarty CA et al. 2005, Personalized Medicine 2(1):49-79 (PMRP design and recruitment paper, doi:10.1517/17410541.2.1.49)
note: Approximate figure from the definition source; the same paper genotyped 19544 individuals who self-reported a single racial category. The 2005 design paper, which would give the exact enrolment, was not read. The example study (PMID:37196047) does not name PMRP in its cached text.

label: MD Anderson Cancer Center lung cancer study
counts: ever-smoking lung cancer cases and controls in the GWAS discovery phase (genotyped subset)
quote: In the discovery phase, we analyzed 315,450 tagging SNPs in 1,154 current and former (ever) smoking cases of European ancestry and 1,137 frequency-matched, ever-smoking controls from Houston, Texas.
note: Definition source, the MD Anderson lung cancer GWAS (2008); no sentence states a total, so participants is null. The same paper used a further Texas replication set of 711 cases and 632 controls. The 2012 TRICL meta-analysis (PMID:22899653) lists MDACC with 1150 cases and 1134 controls. The size of the whole ongoing MD Anderson case-control recruitment was not found. The example study (PMID:35138370) reports only pooled replication totals.

label: MD Anderson Cancer Center melanoma study
counts: melanoma cases and controls in the GWAS discovery cohort (genotyped, after QC)
quote: In a discovery cohort of 1804 melanoma cases and 1026 controls, we identified loci at chromosomes 15q13.1 (HERC2/OCA2 region) and 16q24.3 (MC1R) regions that reached genome-wide significance within this study and also found strong evidence for genetic effects on susceptibility to melanoma from markers on chromosome 9p21.3 in the p16/ARF region and on chromosome 1q21.3 (ARNT/LASS2/ANXA9 region).
needs: PMID:34813871 (example study, J Invest Dermatol 2022; publisher text not cached)
note: Definition source (Hum Mol Genet 2011); cases and controls recruited March 1998 to August 2008; no sentence states a total, so participants is null. These are genotyped subjects passing QC; the paper also says questionnaire data were available for 931 CM patients and 1026 controls. The full recruitment of the MD Anderson melanoma case-control study was not found.

label: National Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology Biobank
counts: hospital patients enrolled in the biobank (approximately), as of May 2025
quote: As of May 2025, the Biobank has enrolled approximately 16,000 patients from hospitals and holds around 60,000 patient-derived samples, primarily serum and plasma, along with medical information and genomic data.
note: The same page adds: 'Moreover, the Biobank has more than 27,000 research participants enrolled from other cooperative cohort studies, and their blood samples are also stored.' No combined total is stated, so the hospital-patient figure is recorded. The definition source (PMID:41951582) says only 'tens of thousands of individuals'; the example study (PMID:40045203) used 6,324 DNA samples from the biobank.

label: Nulliparous Pregnancy Outcomes Study: Monitoring Mothers-to-Be
counts: nulliparous pregnant individuals enrolled in the first trimester
quote: The study enrolled 10,038 nulliparous people from the first trimester of their pregnancy to participate in three study visits during pregnancy.
note: Definition source and example study. PMID:42557812 agrees: 'The parent study enrolled 10,038 nulliparous pregnancies from October 2010 to May 2013.' The design paper (Haas et al. 2015, AJOG) was not read.

label: Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort
counts: youths aged 8-21 who completed the clinical and neurocognitive assessments
quote: Overall, 19,161 individuals met the inclusion criteria; 9,428 (49.2%) of these completed clinical and neurocognitive assessments.
note: From the definition source, citing the cohort description (Calkins et al. 2015), which was not read. The preceding sentence says 50,293 participants were recruited by the CHOP Center for Applied Genomics between 2006 and 2012 (the genomics pool from which PNC was drawn); 8,139 were genotyped per the same paper. The example study (PMID:34563919) says the PNC has 7515 youths aged 8-22 in its analysis.

label: ProHealth Study
counts: none found for the ProHealth Study alone
note: The definition source and example study (PMID:26034056) describe ProHealth only as ascertaining KP Northern California African-American prostate cancer cases, with no count; its GWAS counts (7,783 cases, 38,595 controls) are for the combined Kaiser Permanente studies (RPGEH GERA, ProHealth, CMHS). PMID:29117387 gives 'the Kaiser/ProHealth Prostate Cancer Study (601 case subjects and 1650 control subjects)', but that is the African-ancestry Kaiser GWAS set drawn from the combined studies, not ProHealth's own enrolment. A ProHealth design description (or the dbGaP phs000674 study page) would settle it.

label: Radiogenomics Consortium
counts: radiotherapy patients in the 2023 cross-cancer GWAS meta-analysis of 19 cohorts
quote: Methods: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis was performed using 19 cohorts totaling 12042 patients.
note: Cohort aggregation; the largest pooled consortium analysis read (prostate, head and neck, breast and lung cancer patients). Other definition sources give smaller disease-specific analyses: 3871 prostate cancer patients in six cohorts (PMID:31095341) and 1780 head and neck cancer patients (PMID:35039627). The consortium's total membership across all cohorts was not found.

label: Study of Epidemiology and Risk Factors in Cancer Heredity
counts: breast cancer case families (probands) in the SEARCH breast study only
quote: Material and methods Study sample The sample included 17,425 three-generation families ascertained via population-based sampling of breast cancer probands from two studies: 2,712 families from the population-based case-control family study within the Australian Breast Cancer Family Registry (ABCFR) and 14,713 families from the prospective Studies of Epidemiology and Risk Factors in Cancer Heredity (SEARCH) study in the UK.
note: SEARCH is a series of population-based case-control studies of several cancers (breast, prostate, melanoma, endometrial and others) in East Anglia; no source read states a total across its arms or a control count, so participants is null. Cases here are the breast cancer probands (women diagnosed 1991-1996 before 55, recruited 1996-2002, plus incident cases diagnosed 1996-2011 before 70) from PMID:36206742. PMID:36539277 describes the breast study as 'containing about 12 700 breast cancer diagnosed under the age of 70 years'. The definition sources (dbGaP phs001391, PMID:25855707, PMID:20520800) give no SEARCH-specific numbers. A SEARCH study website or overview paper would settle the total.

label: SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth
counts: study participants (stated as more than 20,000) on the study website
quote: There are more than 20,000 study participants representing all different racial and ethnic backgrounds who have helped SEARCH determine the extent of diabetes in the community and its impact on different populations.
note: A lower bound from the study's website, undated (the page says SEARCH was launched in 2000 and will continue at least through 2020). The design paper (PMID:15465616, definition source; full text not open) gives only planned figures: 'An estimated 6000 prevalent and 800 incident diabetes cases per year will be identified with annual follow-up.' The 2014 overview (PMID:25414389) gives surveillance of about 5.5 million children but no participant total. The example study (PMID:34127860) does not give a SEARCH count.

label: Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register Biobank
counts: RA patients with blood samples in the biobank (stated as more than 5500)
quote: SRQb is an ongoing research project currently holding blood samples from >5500 RA patients, with either early RA or starting a bDMARD.
note: A lower bound for an ongoing collection, from the definition source and example study (Rheumatology 2023). The same paper found 7289 RA patients across EIRA and SRQb for its primary analysis and 1326 further SRQb samples added after 2017.

label: Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register
counts: patients in the register across over 100 rheumatic diagnoses
quote: Today, the registry covers over 100 rheumatic diagnoses and includes 89,000 patients.
note: From the register's own website (undated; read through WebFetch because direct requests to srq.nu returned a hosting block page). The definition source (PMID:37326842) gives no register-wide count, only that its biobank (SRQb) holds samples from >5500 RA patients. A 2014 SRQ overview (Clin Exp Rheumatol, PMID:25365105) states 'over 26,000 participants as of December 31, 2013' for ARTIS, the biologics part of the register, not for SRQ as a whole.

label: Skåne University Hospital memory clinic cohort
counts: AD patients included in the CSF-biomarker GWAS meta-analysis (analysed subset)
quote: Of the total 315 subjects included in this study, 100% of them were diagnosed as having AD.
note: Supplementary cohort description of the definition source and example study (PMID:42014397). This is the number of Skåne memory clinic patients in that analysis, not the size of the clinic's whole sample; the supplement cites an earlier description (its ref. 12) that was not identified or read.

label: Toledo Study for Healthy Aging
counts: people aged 65 and older in the final baseline sample (interviewed)
quote: Data were taken from the Toledo Study for Healthy Aging, a population-based study conducted on 2,488 individuals aged 65 years and older.
note: Definition source (J Nutr Health Aging 2011), baseline June 2006 to September 2009: 1,667 of the new cohort plus 811 of the historic cohort; the same paper says 1,972 had the physical examination and 1,752 gave a blood sample.

label: Berlin Aging Study II
counts: participants in the original baseline sample (older and younger groups)
quote: Of the original BASE-II sample consisting of 2200 participants, 1671 aged 60 years and above (=older group) were assessed medically at baseline between 2009 and 2014.
note: From the 2021 GendAge cohort profile (BMJ Open). The definition source's abstract (PMID:23505255) says baseline recruitment 'has led to the sampling of 1600 older adults (age range 60-80 years), as well as 600 younger adults (20-35 years)'. The example study (PMID:33510174) used 1,531 unrelated BASE-II participants aged 60+.

label: Rotterdam Study II
counts: participants enrolled in the second subcohort (RS-II)
quote: In 2000, the RS was extended with a second subcohort (RS-II) of 3011 participants who moved to Ommoord or turned 55 years old.
note: From the definition source, a Rotterdam Study analysis paper rather than the cohort's own design update (the 2018/2020/2024 Rotterdam Study design updates were not read); it agrees with the definition. The same paper analysed 1000 participants from the RS-II second visit.

label: MrOS Malmö
counts: men recruited and measured at Malmö, 2001-2004
quote: The participants were recruited and measured at hospitals in the three cities of Malmö (n = 1005), Gothenburg (n = 1010) and Uppsala (n = 999) between October 2001 and December 2004 with an attendance rate of 45% [16].
note: MrOS Sweden as a whole included 3014 men at baseline. The example study (PMID:33510174, supplement) gives the same site counts and says 891 unrelated participants from Malmö were included in its analysis.

label: Longitudinal Aging Study Amsterdam
counts: original cohort at the first LASA wave (wave B, 1992-1993)
quote: On average 11 months after the LSN interview (wave A), respondents were invited to participate in the first measurement wave of LASA (wave B, n = 3107).
note: Design and cohort update 2025 (definition source). No total across cohorts is stated, so the original cohort's baseline is given. The same paper: refresher cohorts of 1002 (2002-2003) and 1023 (2012-2013), a migrant cohort of 478 (2013-2014, Table 1), a fourth cohort being recruited from 2024 (no number yet); the LSN sample it was drawn from had 3805 people.

label: Finnish Gestational Diabetes Study
counts: case-control arm: pregnant women with and without GDM recruited 2009-2012
quote: The case-control cohort was recruited in 2009–12 and includes 1146 women with GDM and 1066 non-diabetic controls aged 17–48 years, their children and the children’s fathers.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:32374401). No sentence states a case-plus-control total (nor counts of the children and fathers enrolled), so participants is null. The register-based arm consists of families where a mother gave birth in 2009 ('n = 59 057 singleton pregnancies'), including 6583 women with GDM.

label: MrOS Gothenburg
counts: men recruited and measured at Gothenburg, 2001-2004
quote: The participants were recruited and measured at hospitals in the three cities of Malmö (n = 1005), Gothenburg (n = 1010) and Uppsala (n = 999) between October 2001 and December 2004 with an attendance rate of 45% [16].
note: MrOS Sweden as a whole included 3014 men at baseline. The example study (PMID:33510174, supplement) gives the same site counts and says 941 unrelated participants from Gothenburg were included in its analysis.

label: African Ancestry Anthropometry Genetics Consortium
counts: African ancestry individuals in the 2017 BMI meta-analysis (stages 1+2, sex-combined, maximum N)
quote: We performed large scale meta-analyses and replications in up to 52,895 individuals for BMI and up to 23,095 individuals for WHRadjBMI from the African Ancestry Anthropometry Genetics Consortium (AAAGC) using 1000 Genomes phase 1 imputed GWAS to improve coverage of both common and low frequency variants in the low linkage disequilibrium African ancestry genomes.
note: Consortium; pooled count for the 1000 Genomes-imputed analysis in the definition source (stage 1: 17 studies, N = 42,752 for BMI; stage 2: 10,143). The same paper says the consortium's earlier HapMap-imputed GWAS included 'up to 71,412 and 27,350 African ancestry individuals' for BMI and WHRadjBMI, a larger pooled count; either could be called the flagship analysis. Counts are 'up to' maxima per trait.

label: Accelerating Medicines Partnership Parkinson's Disease
counts: participants whose data AMP PD harmonises (Unified Cohort and Postmortem Brain Cohort), current website
quote: AMP PD generates and consolidates data from 10,908 participants from the Unified Cohort (including BioFIND, HBS, LBD, LCC, PDBP, PPMI, STEADY PD, and Sure PD) and the Postmortem Brain Cohort.
note: Aggregation of PD cohort studies; the website (fetched 2026-09-25, no date on the count) gives the current pooled number and says the joint genotyping 'totals more that 10,000 samples'. The definition source (PMID:33960523, release 1) says 'As of the time of writing, the AMP PD platform contains complete WGS data on 3941 individuals from these studies' (2005 idiopathic PD, 963 controls, 705 from genetically enriched cohorts); AMP PD news items from 2019 give 4,298 PD patients and healthy controls at the portal launch.

label: Salus in Apulia Study
counts: individuals aged 65 or older in the cohort (MICOL plus GreatAGE)
quote: The present study included individuals from the Salus in Apulia Study (MICOL Study plus GreatAGE Study), an ongoing population-based prospective cohort comprising 2192 individuals aged 65 years or older and resident in Castellana Grotte, a town located near Bari, Puglia, in the southeast of Italy.
note: From a 2021 Salus in Apulia analysis paper (PMID:34948590), not a cohort profile; none was found. The definition source (PMC9313038) gives only the sampling frame (19,675 residents, 4021 aged 65+) and an analysed subpopulation of 1657; PMC8615636 an analysed subset of 1929; the example study (PMID:35580588) included 'the Salus in Apulia study (SA; n = 1,780; formerly known as Great Age study)'. A cohort profile would settle the enrolled number.

label: Beijing Atherosclerosis Study
counts: MI cases and controls genotyped in the GWAS discovery stage
quote: BAS consisted of 509 cases of MI and 1,034 controls genotyped using the Affymetrix Human Mapping 500K Array Set including 500,568 SNPs.
note: Definition source PMID:22751097 (CAD GWAS in Han Chinese), not a BAS design paper; no sentence states a case-plus-control total of those genotyped, so participants is null. After quality control 505 cases and 1,021 controls remained ('After quality control, 1,526 samples ... remained'). A BAS design paper would settle whether more were enrolled.

label: BIObanks Netherlands Internet Collaboration
counts: individuals in the lifetime MDD GWAS mega-analysis (16 655 cases, 48 286 controls)
quote: We performed a genome-wide association mega-analysis of lifetime MDD case-control status in 64 941 individuals (16 655 cases and 48 286 controls) and evaluated the extent to which this design captured common-variant signal by estimating SNP-based heritability and genetic overlap with the latest Psychiatric Genomics Consortium major depression GWAS [10].
note: Consortium of sixteen Dutch cohorts; the pooled count is the final analysis set of its flagship MDD mega-analysis (definition source). With relaxed control screening the sample expands to N = 67 440 (16 655 cases).

label: Bone Mineral Density in Childhood Study
counts: healthy children who participated (initial cohort plus later enrolment), 5-23 years
quote: Two thousand fourteen healthy children (992 males, 22% African-Americans) aged 5-23 yr participated in the study.
note: From the abstract of the 2011 revised reference-curves paper (read via the Europe PMC REST abstract, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:21917867%20AND%20SRC:MED&format=json&resultType=core); its conclusions speak of 'a well-characterized cohort of 2012 children and adolescents'. The definition source PMID:17311856 (2007) gives the initial cohort: 'Participants included 1554 healthy children (761 male, 793 female), ages 6-16 yr, of all ethnicities.' The example study (PMID:34754074) says an ancillary study enrolled 'approximately 500 children' aged 5-18 and analysed 1047 BMDCS children.

label: Canadian Breast Cancer Study
counts: breast cancer cases and controls in the study's night shift work analysis (Vancouver and Kingston)
quote: Relationships between night shift work and breast cancer were examined among 1134 breast cancer cases and 1179 controls, frequency-matched by age in Vancouver, British Columbia, and Kingston, Ontario.
note: Read as the Europe PMC abstract (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:23817841%20AND%20SRC:MED&format=json&resultType=core); these are cases and controls examined, not an enrolment statement, and no source read states a case-plus-control total, so participants is null. Per-site recruitment from PMC9366896 (PAH paper, PMID:30541747): Vancouver 'Response rate among cases and controls were 54% ( n = 1,001) and 57% ( n = 1,014), respectively.'; Kingston 59% (n = 131) and 49% (n = 164); its analysis included 1,130 cases and 1,169 controls. The definition source PMID:30601841 analysed 920 cases and 922 controls; PMC4896919 1,037 cases and 1,050 controls after QC. A design paper giving the total enrolled would settle it.

label: NIHR Cambridge BioResource
counts: volunteers recruited by the Cambridge centre since 2005 (stated as more than 17,500)
quote: There are 13 local NIHR BioResource centres across the country, including the Cambridge centre directed by Dr Bradley on the Addenbrooke’s site, which has recruited more than 17,500 volunteers who live, work or study in the region since its inception in 2005.
note: A local news article (14 July 2019), and a lower bound ('more than'). A 2018 paper (PMC6176884, PMID:29462388) says 'The Cambridge BioResource is a panel of around 16,000 volunteers, both with and without health conditions, who have previously submitted DNA for genotyping.' Neither definition source (PMID:34581777, PMID:41194662) gives a count; the Cambridge BioResource and NIHR BioResource websites were behind a Cloudflare challenge. A current count from the BioResource would settle it.

label: Consortium of Investigators of Modifiers of BRCA1 and BRCA2
counts: European-ancestry BRCA1/2 carriers in the consortium's 2025 HGSOC GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: The genome-wide association analyses for HGSOC were based on up to 398,238 women from OCAC (N = 120,248, 30.2%), UKBB (N = 245,377, 61.6%) and CIMBA (N = 32,613, 8.2%) (Table 1, Supplementary Tables 1, 2).
note: Consortium; pooled count from its most recent flagship analysis in the example study (PMID:41266372), restricted to carriers of European ancestry ('CIMBA study participants were enrolled in 64 studies from 28 countries'; its Fig. 3 gives 28,939 unaffected and 3,674 affected carriers). The founding paper (PMID:17466083, 2007): 'CIMBA contains about 30 affiliated groups who together have collected DNA and clinical data from approximately 10,000 BRCA1 and 5,000 BRCA2 mutation carriers.' A consortium-wide count of all carriers enrolled was not found.

label: UROMOL project
counts: NMIBC patients in the 2021 multi-omics analysis (analysed subset)
quote: Here, we report an integrative multi-omics analysis of NMIBC tumors from a total of 834 patients included in the UROMOL project.
note: Definition source (PMID:33863885) analyses 862 tumours from these 834 patients; it does not state how many patients the UROMOL project enrolled in total. Earlier UROMOL transcriptomic reports analysed 460 NMIBC patients (RNA-Seq later expanded to 535). The example study (PMID:37210288) uses UROMOL only for summary-level GWAS and eQTL data without a count. A UROMOL design paper giving total enrolment would settle it.

label: Cardiometabolic Risk in Chinese Study
counts: individuals examined in the 2009 community health examination survey
quote: In the cardiometabolic risk in Chinese (CRC) study, we performed a community-based health examination survey for 6,431 individuals (18-93y) who were randomly selected from residents living in the urban area of Xuzhou, China, in 2009.
note: Both definition sources (PMID:25001365, PMID:25400699) give the same 6,431; PMID:25001365 included 2,318 subjects in its final analyses.

label: Cooperative Research Centre Cohort
counts: clozapine-treated participants recruited by the CRC and included in the 2022 GWAS
quote: Participants (N = 804) came from five independent cohorts: 470 participants were recruited by the Clozapine International (CLOZIN) [38–41] consortium in the Netherlands, Germany, Austria, and Finland; 174 participants by the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium in the Netherlands; 80 participants by the Cooperative Research Centre (CRC) in Australia; 50 participants by Hacettepe University in Turkey; and 30 participants by Mental Health Services Rivierduinen in the Netherlands.
note: The only source (definition source and example study, PMID:35393395) gives the number of CRC participants contributed to this analysis, which may be a subset of those the CRC recruited; no CRC design paper was found. A description of the CRC cohort's recruitment would settle it.

label: Consortium for Refractive Error and Myopia
counts: European and Asian ancestry individuals in the 2020 corneal curvature GWAS meta-analysis
quote: Here we present a trans-ethnic meta-analysis of corneal curvature GWAS in 44,042 individuals of Caucasian and Asian with replication in 88,218 UK Biobank data.
note: Consortium; pooled count from the definition source (corneal curvature). No single pooled CREAM count for its flagship refractive error analyses was found: the 2018 refractive error GWAS (PMC5980758, PMID:29808027) gives 'Stage 1 CREAM (CREAM-EUR, N =44,192; CREAM-ASN, N =11,935)' before adding 23andMe (160,420 in total with 23andMe); the 2013 GWAS (PMID:23396134, abstract) 'including 37,382 individuals from 27 studies of European ancestry and 8,376 from 5 Asian cohorts'. Which analysis to count as flagship is a judgement; the separate EUR and ASN figures are not summed here.

label: Doetinchem Cohort Study
counts: inhabitants examined at baseline, 1987-1991
quote: In 1987 it started with an age-sex-stratified sample (20–59 years) of the inhabitants of Doetinchem, a mid-size Dutch town, of whom 12 404 (62%) participated in the baseline examination between 1987 and 1991.
note: Cohort profile update 2018 (a definition source). The longitudinal cohort proper is the two-thirds re-invited: 'Two-thirds of those measured at baseline (n = 7768) were invited for first follow-up measurement in 1993–97'. The 2025 update (PMC13387599) repeats n = 12 404 for Wave 1 and gives 3774 participants in Wave 7 (2018-23) and a total of 7312 participants in its Table 1 (including those invited to Waves 1 and 7 only).

label: Genes-environments & Admixture in Latino Americans
counts: participants enrolled 2006-2011 (cases and controls)
quote: Results The GALA II and SAGE II studies have enrolled 4,157 and 1,281 participants, respectively, from 2006 to 2011.
note: From the 2013 GALA II/SAGE II air pollution paper (PMID:23750510), which describes both studies' recruitment; recruitment may have continued after 2011, so later papers could give a larger number. The same paper's analytic sample was 3,343 GALA II Latinos (1,688 cases, 1,655 controls); a 2014 GWAS (PMID:24406073) recruited 1893 cases and 1881 controls. The definition source (PMID:34834492) gives no GALA II total. Enrolled cases and controls are not given separately.

label: Groningen Expert Center for Kids with Obesity Drenthe study
counts: children actively participating (born April 2006 - April 2007)
quote: Of the 5326 children born between April 2006 and April 2007, 2842 started active participation in the study.
note: PMC7763711 (PMID:33167754) states the same: 'Of the 5326 newly born infants in the province, 2997 mothers consented to participate, 2842 of whom actively participated in the study.' 2997 mothers consented; the definition source (PMID:35778749) says only 'almost three thousand pregnant women'. The example study (PMID:42036355) does not name the cohort in its main text.

label: Genes and Environment in Multiple Sclerosis
counts: cases and controls with completed GEMS questionnaires, recruited 2009-2011
quote: Completed GEMS questionnaires were obtained from 6,156 cases and 5,408 controls, with a response rate of 82% for cases and 66% for controls.
note: No source read states a total, so participants is left null (cases and controls not summed). PMC12505036 says GEMS identified prevalent cases from the Swedish MS registry between November 2009 and November 2011 (n=6148). The definition source (PMID:36629499) gives only pooled EIMS/GEMS counts (6635 cases, 8880 controls); the example study (PMID:38630618) Table 1 gives an analysed GEMS subset of 8906 (4755 cases, 4151 controls). A GEMS design paper stating the total enrolled would settle it. Not to be confused with the US 'Genes and Environment in Multiple Sclerosis' at-risk cohort of first-degree relatives (PMC4962522).

label: Georgia Stress and Heart Study
counts: participants in the original cohort, rolling enrollment from 1989
quote: The original cohort consisted of 740 participants and began rolling enrollment in 1989.
note: The definition source (PMID:30234784) gives only the analysed 559 participants with pulse wave velocity; PMC5210407 an IMT substudy of 555 at visit 12; PMC12604386 470 with DNA methylation. The example study (PMID:42036355) uses the GPI cohort (835 African-American children), not clearly this cohort. A GSH design paper stating the enrolled number would confirm 740.

label: Health and Ageing in Africa: A Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH Community in South Africa
counts: consented participants aged 40+ at baseline, 2014-2015
quote: Socio-demographic data, infection history, and cognitive performance data were collected from 5059 consented participants (male (n = 2345) and female (n = 2714)) aged 40 years and older recruited from Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga (November 2014 to November 2015) and a sub-set of 2246 of these participants (male (n = 935) and female (n = 1311)) had genotype data.
note: Same paper also says HAALSI 'collected baseline cognition data for over 5000 older adults'; 2246 of them were genotyped in AWI-Gen. The HAALSI cohort profile was not read.

label: Agincourt Health and Socio-demographic Surveillance System
counts: people under surveillance (de jure population), mid-2011
quote: By mid-2011, the population under surveillance comprised 90 000 people residing in 16 000 households in 27 villages (Table 2).
note: A surveillance population, not an enrolled cohort. Same profile paper (PMID:22933647): 57 600 people at baseline in 1992; ~70 000 by 2006; Table 2 gives de jure population 90036 and de facto 66876 at 1 July 2011. Later counts from a newer profile were not read.

label: Health2006 Study
counts: persons examined 2006-2008
quote: A total of 3,471 (43.8%) persons were examined from 2006–2008.
note: The preceding sentence of the same paper says 7,931 persons aged 18-69 were invited. PMC3674994 (example study PMID:23754956) agrees: 'Health2006 is a population-based epidemiological study of general health, diabetes and cardiovascular disease of 3,471 individuals aged 18–74 years'.

label: Heidelberger Langzeitstudie zu Risikofaktoren und Diagnose chronischer Erkrankungen
counts: individuals assessed at baseline (1990s)
quote: HeiDE is a longitudinal population-based study that started in the 1990s and, at baseline, assessed an array of health-related personality questionnaires in 5133 individuals.
note: Abstract of PMID:33590662. At follow-up 3268 participants were genotyped (post-QC); PMC8503053 analysed n = 3266.

label: Heart Failure Molecular Epidemiology for Therapeutic Targets Consortium
counts: HF cases and controls of European ancestry across the 51 member cohorts (2021 design paper)
quote: In aggregate, the 51 HERMES cohorts comprise 68 157 HF cases and 949 888 controls of European ancestry with array‐based genotyping (Supporting Information, Table S1 ).
note: Cohort aggregation of 51 studies from 11 countries (PMID:34480422). No source read states a pooled total, so participants is null (cases and controls not summed). The example study (PMID:42017882) analysed 50,636 individuals with established HF from 22 HERMES cohorts.

label: International Glaucoma Genetics Consortium
counts: POAG cases and controls in the 2021 multi-ancestry meta-analysis (21 studies)
quote: We obtained 34,179 POAG cases and 349,321 controls including participants of European, Asian, and African descent from 21 independent studies across the world.
note: Cohort aggregation. Quote from the Methods of PMID:33627673. No pooled total stated, so participants is null. The example study (PMID:37386247, PMC10335935) calls this its IGGC POAG meta-analysis (ref. 6): European stage 16,677 cases and 199,580 controls, Asian 6,935/39,588, African 3,281/2,791; IGGC VCDR n = 25,180 and IOP n = 31,269. PMID:35446358 cites an IGGC CCT meta-analysis of 17 803 European and 8107 Asian participants.

label: International HIV Controllers Study
counts: HIV controllers (cases) and progressors (controls) after QC in the 2010 GWAS
quote: After quality control and imputation on the basis of HapMap Phase 3 (3), we obtained data on 1,384,048 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 974 controllers (cases) and 2648 progressors (controls) from multiple populations (table S1).
note: Analysed subset of the definition source (PMID:21051598); no total stated, so participants is null. The progressors were treatment-naive individuals enrolled in AIDS Clinical Trials Group studies rather than recruited by the consortium. The number of controllers recruited overall was not found; the consortium website (hivcontrollers.org) returned HTTP 406. The example study (PMID:37097752) uses a subset of IHCS samples without a count in the text read.

label: Immunomodulation and Multiple Sclerosis Epidemiology
counts: set of drug-specific post-marketing cohorts; no overall total found
note: IMSE is a set of drug-specific phase IV cohorts (natalizumab, fingolimod, dimethyl fumarate, teriflunomide, alemtuzumab, cladribine, ...). No source read states a total across them. Numbers seen: PMC7455371 'From the 1,714 individuals in the IMSE natalizumab cohort, we included 370 unique patients'; PMC13190381 describes IMSE as 'a cohort study including MS patients initiating different DMTs ... ( n = 1009)', an analysed questionnaire subset (68% response); PMC12996015 cites IMSE 10 (cladribine) with 194 patients. The definition source (PMID:26046553) gives no IMSE count; the example study (PMID:38630618) Table 1 gives an analysed IMSE subset of 1076 cases. A report of the total enrolled across all IMSE cohorts (e.g. from the Swedish MS registry) would settle it.

label: International Parkinson Disease Genomics Consortium
counts: PD cases and controls in the 2019 European-ancestry GWAS meta-analysis (17 datasets)
quote: Between Oct 1, 2017, and Aug 9, 2018, we analysed 7·8 million single nucleotide polymorphisms in 37 688 cases, 18 618 UK Biobank proxy-cases (ie, individuals who do not have Parkinson's disease but have a first degree relative that does), and 1·4 million controls.
note: Cohort aggregation. Flagship IPDGC meta-analysis (PMID:31701892); in addition 18 618 UK Biobank proxy-cases; controls given only as '1·4 million'. No total stated, so participants is null. The definition source (PMID:31815703, PMC7029327) describes this effort as 'more than 50,000 cases and proxy-cases, and ∼1.4 million controls' and the core IPDGC datasets as 'currently including over 20,000 cases and 20,000 controls'. The example study (PMID:35970579) meta-analysed COURAGE-PD with IPDGC data (Ntotal = 25,950).

label: Japan PGx Data Science Consortium Database
counts: healthy Japanese volunteers genotyped
quote: The database contains the genotypes of 2.5 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 5 human leukocyte antigen loci from 2994 Japanese healthy volunteers, as well as 121 kinds of clinical information, including self-reports, physiological data, hematological data and biochemical data.
note: Abstract of the database paper (PMID:25855068); the title also gives 2994.

label: Justification for the Use of Statins in Prevention: an Intervention Trial Evaluating Rosuvastatin
counts: randomised participants
quote: In brief, JUPITER was a randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial of rosuvastatin 20 mg daily versus placebo in the primary prevention of CVD in 17 802 asymptomatic men ≥50 years and women ≥60 years with low‐density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL‐C) <130 mg/dL and hsCRP (high‐sensitivity C‐reactive protein) ≥2.0 mg/L who were monitored for a median follow‐up period of 1.9 years (maximum 5 years).
note: From the definition source (PMID:32799709), a nested case-control secondary analysis of JUPITER. The primary trial report (NEJM 2008) was not read.

label: KOALA Birth Cohort Study
counts: children whose mothers were included, 2000-2002
quote: In total, mothers of 2,877 children were included in the Koala Birth Cohort Study.
note: From the definition source PMID:42116128. The design paper (PMID:16343090, abstract only on disk) gives the two recruitment groups separately: 'conventional lifestyles' (n = 2343) and 'alternative lifestyles' (n = 491) pregnant women; these were not summed. The example study (PMID:42036355) does not name KOALA in the main text read.

label: Mayo Clinic Breast Cancer Study
counts: women with breast cancer (cases) consenting to the MCBCS registry, May 2000 - May 2016; controls not included
quote: Of 7,300 women approached, 6,198 consented to the study and were asked to provide a blood sample and a baseline questionnaire on personal and family history adapted from the Breast Cancer Family Registry.
