note: PMID:32125938 describes MCBCS as 'a prospective registry offering participation to all women evaluated at Mayo Clinic Rochester for a diagnosis of first invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ between May 15, 2000, and May 31, 2016'; the count covers cases only, and no recent control count was found. The definition source (PMID:22226020, PMC3496122, 2012) gives an earlier case-control count: 'Case participation was 69% (n = 798 cases) and control participation was 71% (n = 843 controls).' The PMC9006574 supplement cited by the definition is not on disk; the example study (PMID:35418701) gives no MCBCS count in the text read.

label: Mayo Mammography Health Study
counts: women consenting at screening mammography, 2003-2006
quote: Of 38,883 eligible women, 19,924 provided written informed consented (51.2% adjusted response rate) (Figure 1).
note: Quote reproduced as printed ('informed consented'). Abstract of PMID:23152984 agrees: 'Mayo Mammography Health Study (MMHS) cohort, comprised of 19,924 women (51.2% of eligible)'. Eligible cohort in Table 1: 19,865.

label: North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium
counts: multicase RA families (initial genome screen); no count of individuals found
quote: The North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium, using well-defined clinical criteria, has collected 257 families containing 301 affected sibling pairs with RA.
note: Counts families and sib pairs, not participants, so participants is null. Later numbers seen: PMC2795874 cites 'the NARAC linkage study of RA using 642 Caucasian families' and a GAW16 NARAC GWAS set of 868 cases and 1,194 controls; the example study (PMID:20453842, PMC4243840) cites a NARAC-III/Canada GWAS of 2,418 cases and 4,504 controls. A NARAC design paper giving the total number of individuals across the family and case-control collections would settle it.

label: National Biobank of Korea
counts: biospecimens with related information secured by the Korea Biobank Project by Dec 2011 (counted as specimens, not explicitly persons)
quote: As of December 2011, a total of 525,416 biospecimens with related information have been secured: 325,952 biospecimens from the general population obtained through cohort studies and 199,464 biospecimens of patients from regional biobanks.
note: Cohort aggregation. The source counts biospecimens, though its Figure 2 is titled 'Number of participants in biobanks in Korea' and the project goal was 500,000 specimens; treat as approximate persons. PMID:24159540 (PMC3767092) states 'Specimens from 300,000 people have been collected by population-based cohorts established by the government, and the remaining specimens have been collected from 200,000 people who came to the university-affiliated hospitals', and 'biospecimens from more than 300,000 participants through various cohorts and biospecimens from more than 200,000 patients from hospitals' in the first phase. Newer totals from the National Biobank of Korea website were not read. The example study (PMID:39862296) used NBK data on 803 gastric cancer patients and KoGES controls.

label: Northern Sweden Health and Disease Study
counts: individuals enrolled, as of May 2020
quote: As of May 2020, 141 910 individuals were enrolled in the NSHDS, with a median age of 50 years and 53% women (Table 1).
note: Cohort profile (definition source). Sub-cohorts in Table 1: VIP 127 069, MONICA 12 298, MSP 28 822 (18.5% took part in more than one); >240 000 blood samples.

label: Ontario Familial Breast Cancer Registry
counts: probands (population-based case and control probands and clinic-based probands) enrolled at the Ontario site, 1996-2003; relatives not counted
note: From Table 3 of the Breast Cancer Family Registry design paper (John et al. 2004, PMID:15217505), 'Breast cancer status and sex of probands, by ascertainment source and recruitment site (1996–2003)', whose columns are San Francisco, Ontario, Melbourne and Sydney, New York, Philadelphia, Utah, Total; the Ontario column is the second. The same table gives Ontario population-based control probands (female) as 1711. The paper gives no Ontario-only count of relatives, and no sentence stating the Ontario total. BCAC genotyped subsets seen: 1175 cases and 511 controls (COGS, ng.3242 supplement) and 1407 cases and 367 controls (PMC3107570 pooled analysis). A later OFBCR profile with the whole registry's enrolment (probands plus relatives) would settle it.

label: Prolonged Anticoagulation During eighteen months vs placebo after Initial Six-month treatment for a first episode of idiopathic Pulmonary Embolism
counts: adults randomised to warfarin or placebo
quote: Randomized, double-blind trial (treatment period, 18 months; median follow-up, 24 months); 371 adult patients who had experienced a first episode of symptomatic unprovoked pulmonary embolism (ie, with no major risk factor for thrombosis) and had been treated initially for 6 uninterrupted months with a vitamin K antagonist were randomized and followed up between July 2007 and September 2014 in 14 French centers.
note: The trial's main results paper (JAMA 2015); randomised participants, as SIZE asks for a trial. Year is the end of follow-up.

label: Polish Breast Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls who agreed to the interview, 2000-2003; no total stated
quote: A total of 2386 cases (79% of eligibles) and 2502 controls (69% of eligibles) agreed to participate in a personal interview regarding known and suspected risk factors for breast cancer.
note: From the study's main description paper (Garcia-Closas et al. 2006, Br J Cancer, PMID:16755295), whose abstract also says 'a population-based case–control of 2386 breast cancers and 2502 controls in Poland'. No source read states the case-plus-control total, so participants is null. The definition sources give analysed subsets only (PBCS 1,008 tumours in PMID:20520800).

label: Predicting Risk Of Cancer At Screening
counts: women who agreed to enter PROCAS, October 2009 to June 2015
quote: A total of 57,902 women agreed to enter PROCAS.
note: Of 131,373 women invited between October 2009 and June 2015 (same paper). The BCAC supplement (PMC9006574 supplementaryFiles, a definition source) says 'Over the following 6 years 57,900 women were recruited at routine breast screening appointments in the UK NHS breast screening programme', with saliva DNA from a subset of 10,000 and OncoArray genotypes for 2,500. The main analysis of PMID:32203222 used 47,042 women.

label: Qingdao Twin Registry
counts: twin PAIRS recruited by 2005 (not individuals)
quote: By 2005, a total of 10,655 twin pairs had been recruited.
note: From the abstract of the registry's 2013 status update (Twin Res Hum Genet, PMID:23182450; full text not read). The number counts twin pairs, not people; no source read gives the number of individual twins. The 2006 registry profile (PMID:17254404, the definition source) says 'Over 11,000 pairs of twins and multiples of all ages have been recruited into the registry.' The example study PMID:35876483 gives no count for the registry.

label: Chinese National Twin Registry
counts: twin PAIRS registered from 11 provinces or cities (not individuals)
quote: The Chinese National Twin Registry (CNTR) currently includes data from 61 566 twin pair from 11 provinces or cities in China.
note: The number counts twin pairs, not people; no source read gives the number of individual twins. The same abstract: 'Of these, 31 705, 15 060 and 13 531 pairs are monozygotic, same-sex dizygotic and opposite-sex dizygotic pairs, respectively'. The 2019 Twin Res Hum Genet update (PMID:31708009, abstract) agrees: 'had recruited 61,566 twin-pairs by 2019'. The example study (PMID:36606461) used 1197 pairs.

label: Reproductive Genetics Consortium
counts: women of European descent from 57 studies in the 2014 age-at-menarche meta-analysis (stated as up to)
quote: Here, using genome-wide and custom-genotyping arrays in up to 182,416 women of European descent from 57 studies, we found robust evidence (P < 5 × 10(-8)) for 123 signals at 106 genomic loci associated with age at menarche.
note: ReproGen's website (https://www.reprogen.org/research.html, the definition source's research page) lists its publications and gives no participant count; Perry et al. 2014 (Nature) is its menarche paper, read as abstract only. ReproGen's flagship menopause paper, Day et al. 2015 (PMID:26414677, abstract), says 'We report a dual strategy in ∼70,000 women'; the example study (PMID:34050765) used ReproGen age-at-natural-menopause summary statistics with 'ReproGen; N = 69 626'. The later menarche (Day 2017) and menopause (Ruth 2021) meta-analyses were larger but not read. Which analysis counts as the flagship is a judgement.

label: Singapore and Sweden Breast Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls who participated in the parent case-control study, 1993-1995; no total stated
quote: Eighty-four percent of eligible cases ( n = 3345) and 82% of the controls ( n = 3454) ultimately participated in the parent study.
note: From the SASBAC description paper cited by the BCAC supplement (Wedren et al. 2004, Breast Cancer Res, PMID:15217512). No source read states the case-plus-control total, so participants is null. For SASBAC's genetic study, 'In total, 1801 cases and 1712 controls were selected' (same paper). Analysed subsets seen: 726 postmenopausal controls (definition source PMID:22226020); 1163 cases and 1378 controls genotyped with iCOGS and 571 cases and 742 controls with density and genotype data (BCAC supplement PMC9006574).

label: Samuel Lunenfeld Research Institute Study
counts: lung cancer cases and controls genome-wide genotyped, contributed to the 2012 TRICL meta-analysis (analysed subset); no total stated
quote: SLRIc /Toronto 331 499 Toronto, Canada Hospital-based case–control 317 K 314285
note: Only source is a row of Table 1 of the definition source (Timofeeva et al. 2012, PMID:22899653; columns Subjects (n) Cases, Controls, Location, Study design, platform, number of SNPs): the genotyped subset, not the study's enrolment. The example study (PMID:35138370) pools SLRI with seven other studies (7378 cases and 9503 controls) and gives no count for it. No design paper of the Toronto hospital-based lung cancer case-control study was found in the cache; its own description (the study's recruitment paper, or the IARC GWAS of Hung et al. 2008, which the TRICL paper cites for it) would settle the enrolled numbers.

label: Seoul National University Bundang Hospital cohort
counts: participants genotyped in the SNUBH GWAS cohort (gastric cancer patients and non-cancer controls)
quote: The Seoul National University Bundang Hospital (SNUBH) cohort comprises 1,216 participants, consisting of 610 patients with GC and 606 non-cancer controls, with ages ranging from 26 to 80 years, who were recruited from the enrolled participants who visited the Digestive Disease Center, SNUBH.
note: From the definition source and example study (PMID:39862296). The cohort was drawn from a larger pool of participants enrolled at the Digestive Disease Center, whose size the paper does not give. After QC, 968 participants (527 GC patients and 441 controls) remained; the abstract says 998 participants were analysed. The SNUBH2 validation set added 102 patients from the same pool.

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study
counts: adults who gave informed consent to join, 2013-2015 baseline
quote: All participants agreed to measure genome information and to distribute their information widely.ResultsAs a result, 87,865 gave their informed consent to join our study.
note: From the cohort profile (Hozawa et al. 2021, J Epidemiol). Its Table 4 gives 67,355 Type 1 survey and 19,846 Type 2 survey participants (fiscal 2013-2015) and a figure caption counts n = 86,913 participants; the profile's introduction says the study 'recruited more than 80,000 participants'. The quote runs across the abstract's 'Results' label as the cached text joins it; the number-bearing sentence alone is '87,865 gave their informed consent to join our study.'

label: Tohoku Medical Megabank Project Birth and Three-Generation Cohort Study
counts: persons in the 'fetus' origin cohort (pregnant women, fetuses and family members), recruited 2013-2017
quote: In the TMM BirThree Cohort Study, 74 116 persons participated as the ‘fetus’ origin cohort, and 73 529 persons participated as the ‘newborn’ origin cohort (Figure 3).
note: From the cohort profile (Kuriyama et al. 2020, Int J Epidemiol, PMID:31504573). The 'fetus' origin count is taken as the cohort's size since the study enrols fetuses as probands; the 'newborn' origin count (73,529) counts newborns instead of fetuses. The planned size was 'approximately 70 000 participants'. Table 1 gives 22,230 mothers and 8,763 fathers among the family roles; the profile also says 'The 23 143 newborns included 275 sets of twins and three sets of triplets.'

label: TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey Clinical Cohort
counts: clinic-referred children included at baseline from 2004
quote: Data collection in this cohort started a few years after the population cohort, in 2004, with the inclusion of 543 children (response rate 43%).
note: From the TRAILS cohort profile update (Oldehinkel et al. 2015, Int J Epidemiol, PMID:25431468), whose abstract also says 'a clinical cohort (N=543)'. Retention: 462, 419 and 422 at waves 2-4.

label: Taiwan-US Diabetic Retinopathy Study
counts: unrelated type 2 diabetic Taiwanese subjects in the TUDR study (1007 discovery plus 479 NPDR extension)
quote: A total of 1486 unrelated type 2 diabetic Taiwanese subjects were included in this study.
note: From the TUDR GWAS paper (Sheu et al. 2013, Hum Mol Genet, PMID:23562823), which says 'The TUDR study is a collaborative effort between Taichung Veterans General Hospital (VGH) in Taiwan and Cedars-Sinai Medical Center (CSMC) in the USA.' The GWAS discovery set was '437 cases and 570 controls for a total of 1007'; the paper's abstract total of 2071 includes 585 Hispanic GOLDR subjects. The definition source (PMC5697951) lists TUDR with 434 severe-DR cases and 549 controls (analysed subset). Cases and controls are left null because the 1486 also includes 479 NPDR subjects who are neither.

label: Breakthrough Generations Study
counts: women who returned the questionnaire and became study members, 2003-2011
quote: Of these women, 112 049 (47%) have returned the questionnaire and become study members.
note: From the study's recruitment/design paper (Swerdlow et al. 2011, Br J Cancer, PMID:21897394), whose abstract also says the method was used 'during 2003–2011 to recruit 112 049 motivated participants'. Of the 237,203 women sent the study pack; 102,778 (92%) gave a blood sample.

label: DiaGene Study
counts: patients with type 2 diabetes and diabetes-free controls included, 2006-2011; no total stated
quote: A total of 1886 patients with T2DM and 854 diabetes-free controls were included.
note: From the DiaGene design paper (van Herpt et al. 2017, BMC Endocr Disord, PMID:28649285). 'Between 2006 and 2011, physicians at all three centers included a total of 2065 patients with T2DM', of whom 1886 remained after exclusions. No source read states the patient-plus-control total, so participants is null; the study is a cohort of patients with controls at baseline, recorded as cases and controls.

label: Copenhagen Prospective Studies on Asthma in Childhood
counts: member counts only: 2 member birth cohorts (COPSAC2000, COPSAC2010)
quote: COPSAC2000 is a mother child cohort where all the mothers had a history of a doctor’s diagnosis of asthma after 7 years of age and thus this is a high risk asthma cohort comprising 411 children.
note: The definition source and example study (PMID:37402774) supplement describes the two member cohorts separately and gives no pooled number; the next sentence reads 'COPSAC2010 is a mother child cohort comprising 700 children born to unselected mothers from Denmark as described previously in detail9,10 .' Other COPSAC cohorts (e.g. COPSAC2019) exist but are not in this term's definition and were not read. A COPSAC source stating the pooled number of children would settle it.

label: ProHealth Kaiser GWAS
counts: prostate cancer cases (RPGEH, ProHealth, CMHS) and GERA controls in the 2015 GWAS, after exclusions; no total stated
quote: Our analyses included 7,783 cases and 38,595 controls after exclusions described here.
note: From the GWAS paper that defines this sample (Hoffmann et al. 2015, Cancer Discov, PMID:26034056); the abstract says '(7,783 cases, 38,595 controls; 80.3% non-Hispanic white, 4.9% African-American, 7.0% East Asian, and 7.8% Latino)'. No source read states the case-plus-control total, so participants is null. The example study (PMID:36872133) used only the African-ancestry subset of the Kaiser sample within a 19,378-case, 61,620-control meta-analysis.

label: Genetics of Pancreatic Beta-cell Failure in Mexican-Americans
counts: individuals analysed cross-sectionally (stated as up to; analysed subset)
quote: We tested rs10830963 for association with cross-sectional diabetes-related traits in up to 1,383 individuals or with rate of change in the same phenotypes over a 3-5 year follow-up in up to 374 individuals from the family-based BetaGene study of Mexican Americans.
note: No source read states BetaGene's total enrolment; all give analysed subsets. This is the largest: the abstract of a 2014 BetaGene paper (Diabetologia, PMC4117246; full text not retrievable from Europe PMC). Others: the definition source (GUARDIAN, PMID:24124113) says 'GUARDIAN includes 1217 of these individuals in 390 pedigrees, 238 families of probands with previous GDM and 152 families of probands with normal pregnancies'; a 2015 air-pollution paper used 'Mexican American adults (n = 1,175 ...)' from BetaGene (PMID:25677718, abstract); earlier papers genotyped 473 individuals in 89 families (2008) and 717 individuals from 146 families (2009); the BetaGene II follow-up recalled 390 participants. A BetaGene design paper giving the number enrolled would settle it.

label: Gene-Lifestyle Interactions in Dental Endpoints
counts: participants from nine GLIDE studies in the 2019 dental caries (DMFS) meta-analysis
quote: There were two principal analyses; one combining DMFS (n = 26,792 from nine studies) and dentures (ncases = 77,714, ncontrols = 383,317); the other combining periodontitis (ncases = 17,353, ncontrols = 28,210 from seven studies) and loose teeth (ncases = 18,979, ncontrols = 442,052).
note: From the consortium's flagship GWAS (Shungin et al. 2019, Nat Commun, PMID:31235808, the definition source). The GLIDE parts are the DMFS (n = 26,792, nine studies) and periodontitis (17,353 cases and 28,210 controls, seven studies) meta-analyses; the dentures and loose-teeth counts are UK Biobank, not GLIDE. No sentence gives GLIDE's total number of distinct participants across all its studies. The example study (PMID:39192244) repeats: 'Dental caries in GLIDE were evaluated using the DMFS index, resulting in continuous data with a sample size of 26,792.' and 'For periodontal disease in GLIDE, there were 17,353 cases and 28,210 controls.'

label: Harvard Aging Brain Study
counts: cognitively normal older adults in the longitudinal cohort (baseline)
quote: The longitudinal dataset consists of a 284-subject cohort with the following modalities acquired: demographics, clinical assessment, comprehensive neuropsychological testing, clinical biomarkers, and neuroimaging.
note: Dataset paper Table 1 gives n 284 (167 F, 117 M). The example study (PMID:37101235) used HABS = 258 with raw phenotypic amyloid data, an analysed subset.

label: Hong Kong Osteoporosis Study
counts: Southern Chinese women and men recruited 1995-2010
quote: Between 1995 and 2010, a total of 9449 southern Chinese women and men were recruited from the community.
note: From the definition source (PMID:39458530), which analysed 7420 of them. The cohort profile paper it cites as [28] was not read; the example study (PMID:39046104) is a CHARGE meta-analysis whose HKOS row was not examined.

label: Study of Asthma Phenotypes and Pharmacogenomic Interactions by Race-Ethnicity
counts: analysed subset: SAPPHIRE participants in the 2022 food allergy analysis
quote: Of the 7,627 SAPPHIRE participants included in this analysis, 6,253 (82%) had a prior diagnosis of asthma, and 1,374 (18%) had no earlier history of asthma at the time of enrollment.
note: No source read states the whole cohort's enrolment. The definition source and example (PMID:37794016, supplement) describe SAPPHIRE without a count; CAAPA (PMC6382865) used 566 non-asthmatics and 1325 asthmatics (1891); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01142947 (SAPPHIRE) gives actual enrollment 362, apparently the registered treatment sub-study, not the cohort. The 7,627 is the largest count seen, an analysed subset (PMID:36403896). A SAPPHIRE design paper (refs 15-17 of PMID:36403896) giving total enrolment would settle it.

label: South Asian Birth Cohort
counts: mothers and children (families) in the Maelstrom catalogue entry
quote: Number of Participants 3,024
note: The Maelstrom entry gives 3,024 participants, with 'Mothers (3 sub-groups): 1512 participants Children (3 sub-groups): 1512 participants' and sub-populations of 1,012 mothers in Canada and 250 each in urban and rural India. The design paper (PMID:23356884) planned 'a minimum of 750 mother-infant pairs'. PMID:29400265 reports 'Pregnant women (n 843)' at the two Indian sites, more than Maelstrom's 250+250, so the Indian sub-group sizes there look like targets; a START paper stating total enrolment would settle it. The example study (PMID:42225636) gives no START count in the text read.

label: TRanslational Initiative on Unique and novel strategies for Management of Patients with Heart failure
counts: acute heart failure patients enrolled in the clinical cohort
quote: A total of 496 patients were enrolled in the TRIUMPH clinical cohort.
note: Definition source PMID:29187387; abstract also says 496 enrolled in 14 Dutch hospitals 2009-2014. Planned sample size was 490 (earlier estimate 780); 475 formed the galectin-3 analysis set.

label: Australian Stroke Genetics Collaborative
counts: ischaemic stroke cases and Hunter Community Study controls genotyped for the discovery GWAS
quote: We conducted a GWAS of ischemic stroke in an Australian sample of European ancestry involving 1,230 cases and 1,280 population controls.
note: From the definition source PMID:22941190 (Methods: 'a total of 1,230 ischemic stroke cases were included'; 'A total of 1,280 HCS participants were genotyped'). No source read states the total, so participants is null. After QC 1,162 cases (421 LAA) and 1,244 controls were analysed.

label: Early Growth Genetics Consortium
counts: individuals with own birth weight in the 2019 EGG fetal birth weight GWAS meta-analysis
quote: In expanded genome-wide association analyses of own birth weight (n = 321,223) and offspring birth weight (n = 230,069 mothers), we identified 190 independent association signals (129 of which are novel).
note: The consortium website (definition source) lists GWAS summary data by trait but gives no participant or member-study count. The 2019 birth weight GWAS (abstract, Europe PMC) was taken as the flagship analysis; its maternal analysis had 230,069 mothers, and it includes UK Biobank as well as EGG cohorts. Other EGG analyses are smaller: the 2020 childhood BMI GWAS (Vogelezang et al.) had discovery maximum N = 39,620 from 41 studies, as reported in the example study PMID:39885687, whose own meta-analysis with EGG and MoBa totalled 84,804 individuals.

label: Oxford Vascular Study
counts: analysed subset: patients with TIA or stroke recruited 2002-2012
quote: Among 2305 patients (mean age 74·4 years [SD 13·0]), 688 (30%) had transient ischaemic attacks and 1617 (70%) had strokes.
note: OxVasc is an incidence study of all acute vascular events in a defined population; its enrolled patients grow over time and no source read gives a total across all event types. The definition source (PMID:30784556) gives the underlying population ('a defined population of 92 728'); a Neurology 2022 supplement gives 'all 91,105 individuals' registered with 101 GPs. These are the population at risk, not participants. The 2305 is the TIA/stroke cohort 2002-2012 analysed for dementia. The example study (PMID:39286457) gives no OxVasc count in the text read. An OxVasc cohort-profile or website figure for all recruited patients would settle it.

label: Prospective Epidemiological Risk Factor Study
counts: postmenopausal Danish women enrolled at baseline (PERF I) 1999-2001
quote: PERF is comprised of 5855 post-menopausal Danish women, enrolled at baseline (PERF I) between 1999 and 2001.
note: Definition and example source PMID:38155185; its analysis used 4369 of them (5516 genotyped). The original PERF design paper (ref 13) was not read.

label: Multiethnic Genome-wide Scan of Prostate Cancer
counts: consented subjects (cases and controls) in the dbGaP study
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 9457
note: From the dbGaP study page (definition source), phs000306.v4.p1; it gives no separate case and control counts. The parent Multiethnic Cohort had 'more than 215,000 men and women' at entry in 1993-1996. The example study (PMID:32986714) gives no count for this dataset in the text read. The GENEVA prostate cancer GWAS paper would give cases and controls.

label: Army Study to Assess Risk and Resilience in Servicemembers
counts: soldiers surveyed across Army STARRS components (lower bound only)
quote: In total, Army STARRS surveyed more than 100,000 soldiers.
note: The review (definition source PMID:30104726) states the total only as 'more than 100,000 soldiers', a lower bound, so participants is left null. Its Table 1 gives component sizes: HADS administrative records for '> 1.6 million' soldiers; NSS new-soldier survey 55,814 (34,986 gave blood); the Consolidated AAS N = 29,982; GWAS of NSS and PPDS used 608 cases and 16,657 controls. An exact total of survey respondents from an Army STARRS design paper would settle it.

label: Barbados Asthma Genetics Study
counts: consented subjects in the TOPMed BAGS dbGaP study
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 1527
note: The same dbGaP page and the example study's supplement (PMID:38714703) say 'the current sample of >1300 participants continues to grow', a lower bound; 1100 individuals from 190 families were whole-genome sequenced. The 1527 is the consented subjects in the TOPMed release, taken as the best stated count of BAGS participants. The definition source PMID:15940135 (abstract only; full text at Elsevier not read) gives no count.

label: CECILE Breast Cancer Study
counts: breast cancer cases and population controls interviewed, 2005-2007
quote: Among the 1556 eligible cases identified, 163 refused to participate, 151 could not be contacted and 7 died before the interview, leaving 1235 cases included in the study.
note: Controls from the same page (definition source PMID:30669331): 'Among the 1731 eligible controls identified by phone, 1317 (76%) accepted to participate to an in-person interview, and 1055 (80%) accepted to have a blood draw and were included in the present study.' No source read states the total, so participants is null. The OC analysis used 695 cases and 1055 controls; the example study (PMID:35418701) used 519 postmenopausal cases and 604 controls.

label: Cardiovascular Health Improvement Project
note: No source read states how many participants CHIP has enrolled. The definition source (PMID:33648514) says recruitment is ongoing and gives only subsets: 240 thoracic aortic dissection cases and 258 controls exome sequenced, and 'After opt-in became available in 2016, 94% of participants (3423/3627) requested to have clinically-actionable variants related to cardiovascular disease returned' (a subset consented after 2016). The example study's supplement (PMID:37845353) gives 534 CHIP AAA cases, analysed jointly with MGI. The CHIP design reference ([15] of PMID:33648514) or a Frankel Cardiovascular Center page with the biobank's enrolment would settle it; the Michigan Medicine page fetched returned no content.

label: GENetic and clinical Predictors Of treatment response in Depression
counts: participants randomised to citalopram or reboxetine
quote: The final number randomised to the trial was 601.
note: From the trial protocol paper (definition source, Europe PMC abstract and full text PMC2426669). The original target sample size was 887, later revised to 676 and then a final analysis target of 570.

label: Tyypin 1 Diabetekseen Sairastuneita Perheenjäsenineen
counts: analysed subset: independent type 1 diabetes cases genotyped on ImmunoChip
quote: IDDMGEN Finland Independent 1111 1073 9 (5, 12) 156,343
note: A row of Table 1 of the definition source PMID:28983737 (columns Cohort, Country, Type, Genotyped, Included, AAD median (IQR), SNPs after QC): 1111 IDDMGEN cases genotyped, 1073 included. This counts only independent cases in one analysis, not the family members the collection also holds. The example study (PMID:34127860) lists IDDMGEN among contributing studies without a count. A description of the IDDMGEN collection with its total cases and relatives would settle it.

label: Indianapolis-Ibadan Dementia Project
counts: enrolment given per site and wave only (1992 and 2001)
quote: In 1992, 2,212 African Americans were enrolled while 249 (9.6%) refused, and 121 (4.7%) were too sick to participate.
note: No source read states a total across sites and waves, so participants is null. From the same paper (definition source PMID:26218444): 'In 1992, 2,486 Yoruba individuals were enrolled while 41 (1.6%) individuals were too sick or refused.' and, for African Americans in 2001, 'Of those eligible, 866 were already enrolled in the 1992 cohort, and 1,939 were enrolled in the 2001 cohort.' The 2001 Yoruba enrolment is given only for those aged 70 or older (1895). The other definition source PMID:11176911 (abstract) gives 2459 Yoruba and 2147 African Americans without dementia at risk in the 1992 cohort. A source stating total IIDP enrolment would settle it.

label: European Study into Digestive Illnesses and Genetics
counts: pancreatic cancer cases and controls recruited (2020 smoking analysis)
quote: Tobacco smoking habits and other relevant information were obtained from 2,009 cases and 1,532 controls recruited in the PanGenEU study using standardized tools.
note: Largest recruitment count seen, from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:32051190; no source read states a total, so participants is null. Other PanGenEU abstracts give smaller sets: 1705 cases and 1084 controls (PMID:30229903), 1297 cases and 1024 controls (PMID:26628509), 688 cases and 558 controls with IgE (PMID:40098454). The definition and example source PMID:33517887 genotyped 1317 cases and 700 controls after QC (plus 916 SBC/EPICURO controls). Neither definition source gives total recruitment across 2009-2014 and 2016-2018.

label: Seoul Breast Cancer Study
counts: breast cancer cases (2001-2007) and cancer-free controls
quote: Details of the study have been previously published.12 The cases (N = 4601) consisted of women diagnosed with breast cancer admitted to 3 university hospitals in Seoul from 2001 to 2007, which accounts for about 15% to 18% of the total treated breast cancer patients in Korea.
note: Controls from the same page (definition source PMID:27057831): 'The controls (N = 4647) were recruited from health examinees without cancers in the same hospitals as the cases or in community health screening programs in urban areas.' No source read states a total, so participants is null. Other definition sources give subsets: PMID:24349656, 3242 cases and 1818 hospital controls (2001-2007) after exclusions; PMID:22452962, SeBCS stage I GWAS of 2,385 cases (controls from KoGES). The study began in 1995, so counts from 2001-2007 may not cover all enrolment.

label: Molecular Epidemiology of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
counts: incident NHL cases diagnosed 2001-2006 and population controls
quote: A population-based case-control study of NHL (2,055 cases, 2,081 controls) that included incident cases diagnosed from 2001 through 2006 was conducted in the San Francisco Bay Area.
note: From the definition source PMID:25133503; no source read states the total, so participants is null. Subsets analysed: 681 cases and 749 controls (CNV analysis, PMID:25133503); 1,292 cases and 1,375 controls genotyped for candidate genes (PMID:18636124). The example study (PMID:36273105) was not needed.

label: Janssen lifetime suicide attempt cohort
counts: suicide-attempt cases and controls in the ISGC GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: Janssen (EUR) 255 1684
note: From Table 1 of the ISGC GWAS (PMID:34861974), which lists SA cases and controls per cohort; no total for the Janssen cohort is stated and none is computed here. The per-cohort description is in Supplement 1 of that paper, which could not be downloaded (PMC returned a challenge page); it would give the whole sample's size.

label: Enhancing NeuroImaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis Consortium
counts: people with imaging and genetic data in ENIGMA's genetic studies ("more than 50,000")
quote: In addition, ENIGMA’s genetic studies are now analyzing imaging and genetics data from more than 50,000 people to uncover genetic markers that most robustly associated with brain structure and function, or imaging derived neurobiological traits related to various disease conditions13–16.
note: A lower bound from ENIGMA's 2020 decade review; the same paper says brain scans in the consortium grew "beyond 50,000 MRI scans" and reports a hippocampal-volume GWAS of 33,536 individuals. The 2014 review (PMID:24399358) says the first project analysed neuroimaging data "from over 12,826 subjects", with 12,171 CHARGE individuals for replication, "in a total of 24,997 subjects". Working groups report their own samples (e.g. 4474 schizophrenia cases and 5098 controls). No single pooled total for the whole consortium is stated.

label: Tirschenreuth Study
counts: individuals aged 14+ enrolled at baseline
quote: Of 4203 individuals aged 14 years or older enrolled at baseline (BL, June 2020), 3546 participated at FU1 (November 2020) and 3391 at FU2 (April 2021).
note: The baseline paper (PMID:34200766) agrees: 6608 randomly selected residents invited, 6540 contactable, and "Of the contactable individuals, 4203 individuals participated". 3546 took part at the November 2020 follow-up, 3391 at April 2021, and 3196 in all three.

label: Amsterdam Cohort Studies on HIV infection and AIDS
counts: two cohorts reported separately: MSM ever included (2915) and people who use drugs (1661)
quote: Of the 2915 MSM who were ever included in the ACS, 926 were HIV-negative and had at least one ACS study visit between 1 January 2012 and 31 December 2021 (Fig. 1 ).
note: No combined total is stated and none is computed. MSM cohort: 2915 ever included (2025 HCV paper, quoted). Drug-user cohort, from the definition source PMID:33407562: "Up until the last year, a total of 1,661 PWUD had been included in the ACS of whom 1,303 had at least two cohort visits." (data collection ended 2016). An older re3data description says "about 2100 homosexual men and 1630 (injecting) drug users have been included". The 1998 overview (PMID:9586643) is closed (Ovid abstract only) and the ACS website is offline.

label: Broad Cardiovascular Disease Initiative Study
counts: participants contributed to the collection ("over 35,000")
quote: Over 35,000 participants were contributed to this collection with an average case control mix of 2:1.
note: Supplementary note of the AF meta-analysis (PMID:40050429); a lower bound, with 91% of participants of European ancestry. The main text uses the TOPMed-imputed European-ancestry participants as an LD reference (n = 32,715), a subset. Case and control numbers for the whole collection are not stated.

label: Canadian Multicentre Osteoporosis Study
counts: men and women aged 25+ recruited 1995-1997 (main cohort)
quote: Study Population Our study population, recruited between 1995 and 1997, includes 9 423 men and women age 25 and older among which 6539 are women and 2884 are men.
note: The website adds: "A youth cohort composed of 474 young men and 527 young women aged 16-24 were recruited between 2004 and 2006." (no combined total stated). The example study (PMID:22792071) also gives 9,423. An early prevalence paper (PMID:11199195) describes "a random sample of 10,061 women and men aged > or = 25 years"; the website's achieved baseline is preferred.

label: Cardiovascular and Metabolic Disease Etiology Research Center-High Risk
counts: individuals in the cohort
quote: Among 3470 individuals in the CMERC-HI cohort, 1569 males underwent coronary calcium scoring; 65 individuals with a study-feasible Framingham score but showing a score of 0 for coronary calcium were enrolled as supernormal.
note: From the example study, not a design paper, and no date for the count is given. The definition source (PMID:28740058) reports an earlier enrolment: "A total of 1,958 participants were enrolled from November 2013 to May 2016 at the Severance Hospital in Seoul, Republic of Korea." A CMERC-HI cohort profile paper would settle the final enrolment.

label: French CF Modifier Gene Study
counts: patients with CF included by 1 January 2017
quote: As of January 1, 2017, 4,798 patients with CF had been included (corresponding to ~80% of all French patients with CF9).
note: The same paper analysed 3,328 pancreatic-insufficient patients born after 1985 (a subset). The example study (PMID:36921087) used 1,207 FrGMS patients with pancreatic insufficiency and lung function measures (an analysed subset). Enrolment may have continued after 2017.

label: German Dupuytren Study
counts: cases from the German Dupuytren Study and PopGen/KORA controls in the 2017 GWAS replication
quote: The German cohort consisted of 768 case subjects from the German Dupuytren Study and 1,353 control subjects from the PopGen and KORA studies.
note: No total is stated and none is computed. These may be the numbers selected for the replication rather than all cases the study group collected; the example meta-GWAS (PMID:38172110) gives no German-specific numbers in its text (per-cohort counts are presumably in its tables or supplement).

label: German Study on the Genetics of Addiction
counts: male alcohol-dependent patients and population controls in the target sample
quote: The target sample comprised 1333 male patients with German ancestry having severe AD requiring hospitalization and 1307 population-based controls, previously described in Treutlein et al.
note: After QC and removal of overlapping samples the final sample was 1330 cases and 1051 controls. No total is stated and none is computed. The original description (Treutlein et al., cited by the paper) was not read; the example study (PMID:35331647, a pancreatitis paper) is not open in the cache.

label: Korean Psychiatric GWAS Project
counts: bipolar disorder patients and shared healthy controls (schizophrenia patients counted separately)
quote: A cohort of 1538 individuals diagnosed with bipolar I or II disorder (DSM-IV) and 2271 healthy controls were recruited from seven academic institutions and their affiliated hospitals in South Korea through the Korean Psychiatric Genome-Wide Association Study (GWAS) Project.
note: The project has two patient groups sharing one control group. Bipolar: 1538 patients (quote above). Schizophrenia, from the abstract of PMID:39293130: "In the Korean psychiatric GWAS project (KPGP), seven academic institutes and their affiliated hospitals across South Korea recruited a cohort of 1670 patients with DSM-IV-defined schizophrenia and 2271 healthy controls." No overall total is stated and none is computed; cases is left null because the two case groups are reported separately.

label: Quebec Founder Population cohort
counts: QFP samples in the Pfizer AD GWAS replication set
quote: 1502 samples from the Quebec Founder Population (QFP) were included in the study as a replication set (case/control ratio = 1).
note: Cases and controls from the same paper: "We further tested our top markers in 751 independent cases and 751 matched controls." This is the set used in that study, which may be a subset of Genizon's QFP collection. The example study (PMID:31349112, Neurobiol Aging 2019) is not open in the cache and its abstract gives no numbers; its full text would give the QFP GWAS sample size.

label: German Sepsis Competence Network
counts: SepNet patients (VISEP/MAXSEP, genetic consent) in the ARDS GWAS; ARDS cases and at-risk sepsis controls
quote: We included a total of 805 patients from the GEN-SEP cohort (304 ARDS cases and 501 at-risk controls), 740 patients from SepNet (91 ARDS cases and 649 at-risk controls), and 3570 patients from UKBB (321 ARDS cases and 3249 at-risk controls).
note: The same paper says "All individuals from the GEN-SEP and SepNet cohorts were considered in the analyses" and that all 740 SepNet patients were also in the earlier ARDS GWAS. This counts the network's genetic sample, not all patients randomised in VISEP and MAXSEP (the trial reports were not read). The second definition source (PMID:18320153, a German guidelines review) gives no numbers.

label: Study of ALS Reversals 2: Genetic Analyses
counts: participants with documented ALS Reversal consented and enrolled
quote: A total of 23 participants with previously documented ALS Reversal were successfully consented and enrolled.
note: Whole-genome sequencing was analysed for 22 of them ("WGS from 22 participants with documented ALS Reversals"). The comparison groups (103 PGB ALS patients, 140 Target ALS patients) are other cohorts, not part of this one.

label: Steno 2007
counts: individuals with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes in the sub-cohort
quote: The first sub-cohort, Steno 2007, consisted of 500 individuals with T1D, of which 77 were excluded due to insufficient material.
note: From the only paper describing it (a DanDiabKids sub-cohort); 423 of the 500 had enough material for that study. The sub-cohort's original description is in references the paper cites (not read).

label: Studies of a Targeted Risk Reduction Intervention through Defined Exercise
counts: adults randomised across STRRIDE I, STRRIDE AT/RT and STRRIDE-PD
quote: A total of 947 adults with dyslipidemia (STRRIDE I, STRRIDE AT/RT) or prediabetes (STRRIDE-PD) were randomized to either inactive control or to 1 of 10 exercise interventions, ranging from doses of 8–23 kcal/kg/week, intensities of 50%–75% V˙O2 peak, and durations of 6–8 months.
note: The same paper: "Of the 947 participants enrolled 295 (31%) dropped out of the STRRIDE trials." Per-trial numbers were not read here.

label: Rare Variants for Hypertension in Taiwan Chinese
counts: THRV subjects selected for TOPMed whole-genome sequencing (all three cohorts)
quote: All 2,353 THRV subjects were selected for whole genome sequencing through the NHLBI TOPMed WGS program.
note: The dbGaP description gives the member cohorts: "The SAPPHIRe Family cohort (N=1,271), TSGH (Tri-Service General Hospital, a hospital-based cohort, N=160), and TCVGH (Taichung Veterans General Hospital, another hospital-based cohort, N=922), all based in Taiwan." It also says "WGS sequencing is performed on all 2,353 samples".

label: Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Program
counts: participants whose genomes were sequenced in the flagship freeze 5 analysis
quote: Among all variant alleles, 46.0% were singletons, observed once across all 53,831 participants.
note: The programme's flagship paper (Taliun et al. 2021, TOPMed freeze 5) from 33 NHLBI-funded research projects. The same paper says "altogether more than 130,000 TOPMed samples are now available in dbGaP" and that its imputation reference panel "now includes 97,256 individuals". The programme has grown since; a current TOPMed total from its website would update this.

label: Umeå Fracture and Osteoporosis Study
counts: fracture cases and controls in the UFO-hip and UFO-forearm GWAS subcohorts (approximate)
quote: The UFO-hip and UFO-forearm GWAS fracture cohorts (recruited in 2008) are subcohorts of the UFO cohort, currently including approximately 5000 fracture cases and approximately 5000 controls (30).
note: Both numbers are stated as approximate, and they count the GWAS subcohorts, not the whole UFO cohort; no total is stated. The same paper describes the forearm study as "comprising a total of 2172 subjects" (1086 forearm and 1086 hip fracture cases identified 1993-2008). The example study (PMID:22792071) says "In total, 1,068 cases and 1,218 age-matched controls were included from this cohort." (an analysed set). UFO's design reference (ref. 30 of PMID:32067027) was not read.

label: Multicenter Study of Hydroxyurea in Sickle Cell Anemia
counts: patients randomised in the trial (1992-1995)
quote: Seventy-five of the original 299 patients died, 28% from pulmonary disease.
note: The same abstract gives the arms: "In the MSH, patients were randomly assigned to receive hydroxyurea (n = 152) or placebo (n = 147)." Follow-up data through May 2001 were complete for 233 patients.

label: PanCareLIFE Work Package 4b
counts: cisplatin-treated patients without cranial radiotherapy enrolled in WP4b
quote: Compared to WP5, WP4b investigated a more restricted study population of 598 patients.
note: Protocol paper; the wider WP5 genetics study enrolled 1124 patients. The example GWAS (PMID:34262104) analysed a discovery cohort of 390 cisplatin-treated, non-cranial-irradiated children (168 with hearing loss), a genotyped subset.

label: African American Breast Cancer Consortium
counts: cases and controls sampled from the nine member studies for the GWAS
quote: Of the 5,984 samples from these studies (3,153 cases and 2,831 controls), we attempted genotyping of 5,932, removing samples (n = 52) with DNA concentrations < 20 ng/ul.
note: Consortium of 9 studies; the flagship GWAS (PMID:22923054) analysed 3,016 cases and 2,745 controls after QC, and replicated in 3,607 cases and 11,330 controls from 9 further studies outside the consortium. PMID:21852243 gives the same 3153 cases and 2831 controls.

label: African American-Diabetes Heart Study
counts: participants analysed with CT calcified plaque measures (analysed subset)
quote: To determine this, 717 African American-Diabetes Heart Study participants underwent computed tomography to determine coronary artery-, carotid artery-, and aorta-calcified atherosclerotic plaque mass scores in addition to the urine albumin:creatinine ratio (UACR), eGFR, and C-reactive protein (CRP).
note: No source read states the total enrolled. The largest count seen is this analysis (abstract read via Europe PMC). Others: the 2011 DHS review (PMID:21409311) says 'an additional 566 unrelated African Americans with T2D have been recruited' (recruitment then ongoing, excluding DHS African Americans); PMID:19825824 says 213 unrelated AA-DHS subjects were recruited by then; GWAS on up to 697 (PMID:34014961) and 691 (PMID:29221444); 675 in PMID:29855664. A cohort profile or dbGaP record would settle it.

label: Anti-Aging Study Cohort
counts: community residents who attended the Anti-aging Center health check-up, Feb 2006 to Mar 2023
quote: Of the 2244 community residents who participated in the health check-up program between February 2006 and March 2023, mid-thigh computed tomography images and postural instability measurements were obtained for 1983.
note: From PMID:38280978, the most recent definition source. Earlier: 'From a total of 2034 individuals who participated from February 2006 to December 2016' (PMID:29491417); 1518 subjects (PMID:28371474) and 838 (PMID:28406166) are analysed subsets. Not a formal cohort profile; the count is of check-up attendees, not all necessarily consenting to J-SHIPP follow-up.

label: Department of Defense Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative
counts: non-demented veterans with baseline neuropsychological testing
quote: Briefly, participant flow proceeded from the full non-demented DoD-ADNI cohort with baseline neuropsychological testing (n = 289) to the analytic WMH sample (n = 228) and the FreeSurfer subset (n = 183), with participants excluded for incomplete neuropsychological data (n = 5), incomplete/inconclusive TBI/PTSD screening data (n = 17), missing WMH data (n = 39), missing T1 data (n = 11), and FreeSurfer QC failures (n = 34).
note: From PMID:42316769 (2026). The 2017 design/interim paper (PMID:28758146) says DOD ADNI aims 'to enroll approximately 400 elderly Veterans' (planned) and reports 180 at baseline in its Table 1 groups (interim). The example study (PMID:37101235) used 169 ADNIDOD participants with amyloid PET. No source read states final total enrolment.

label: Anorexia Nervosa Genetics Initiative
counts: individuals with lifetime AN and controls with blood samples and clinical information
quote: Blood samples and clinical information were collected from 13,364 individuals with lifetime AN and from controls.
note: Design paper PMID:30287268. The PubMed/Europe PMC abstract gives 13,363 in the same sentence; the PMC full text gives 13,364. The sentence is ambiguous whether 13,364 counts cases only or cases and controls; the planned target was 13,000 individuals with AN plus matched controls. Case/control split by site is in Table 1, not read as text. Australian controls came from 17,158 QSkin participants.

label: Ashford study
counts: babies born to the 625 recruited women

note: No source read states the number of BoSCO participants. The 2022 multi-ancestry meta-analysis (PMID:36539618) gives 100,204 cases and 154,587 controls, 27% East Asian, without a separate ACCC count.

counts: no network-wide participant total stated

label: Atherosclerotic Disease, Vascular Function, and Genetic Epidemiology Study
counts: Kaiser Permanente members enrolled into three case and two control groups, 2001-2003

note: GCNKSS finds all hospitalised and autopsied strokes and TIAs 'among the 1.3 million inhabitants of a five-county region' (PMID:9472883), so the 1.3 million is the source population, not participants. I read only per-period or per-analysis counts, none for all periods: PMID:28645938, first-ever ischaemic stroke patients: 'The numbers of patients were 1458, 1455, 1403, and 1475 in 1993–1994, 1999, 2005, and 2010, respectively.' PMID:38533959: 'A total of 5592 (2010, N=2644; 2015, N=2948) physician‐adjudicated and confirmed hospitalized strokes' from 15 hospitals. PMID:38700029: 'Of 4048 patients, 853 Black and 3195 White patients were included.' The example study (PMID:39286457) does not name the study in its text.  Also, Table 1 of the SiGN design paper (PMID:24021684) lists 'GCNKSS Greater Cincinnati region, USA Population-based 1999–2006 642', meaning 642 ischaemic stroke cases contributed to SiGN (a genetic subset). A GCNKSS methods or profile paper giving the number of cases ascertained in each period would settle it.

label: Genotek COVID-19 study
counts: Genotek customers used as controls (mild to moderate COVID-19) in the severe COVID-19 GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: Genotek customer data were added to the study cohort for further analysis as controls (N = 6,400).
note: PMID:39364016. The GWAS had 7,124 individuals (6,400 controls with mild to moderate COVID-19 and 724 severe cases); the cases were hospital patients in Moscow and Ufa, not Genotek customers, so cases and controls are left null. The preceding sentence says the included individuals 'provided informed consent for their data to be used for research purposes and responded to an online questionnaire.' The Genotek long-COVID sample of PMID:40399555 is given only in its Supplementary Tables 11-12, which I did not read. No source I read gives the total number of Genotek customers in its COVID-19 research.

label: Genetics of Kidneys in Diabetes Study
counts: participants (case and control probands, singletons and trio members including parents) as of November 2005
quote: As of November 2005, GoKinD included 3075 participants who comprise 671 case singletons, 623 control singletons, 272 case trios, and 323 control trios.
note: The GoKinD design paper (PMID:16775037). The 3075 includes trio parents. Cases and controls are the proband counts from PMID:19252134: 'In total, 1,879 subjects (935 case and 944 control subjects) were recruited into GoKinD.' The two papers count at different dates and differ slightly: 671+272 case and 623+323 control units in 2005.

label: Graz Stroke Study
counts: ischaemic stroke cases recruited 1992-2011, contributed to SiGN (as of April 2013)
quote: GRAZ Graz, Austria Hospital-based 1992–2011 685 19–101 41 100 0
note: The quote is the GRAZ row of Table 1 of PMID:24021684 (SiGN), 'Cases of ischemic stroke (N = 17,298) classified using the Causative Classification of Stroke (CCS) system as of April 3, 2013'. Its columns are GRC, location, recruitment source, recruitment years, cases (n), age range, % female, % white, % black. PMID:23041239 (METASTROKE, 2012) lists Graz as a cross-sectional cohort; its table row, as extracted, reads 'Graz657116108207848', which I read as 657 cases (116 cardioembolic, 108 large-vessel, 207 small-vessel) and 848 controls. The controls are Austrian Stroke Prevention Study participants, not members of this case series, so only cases are counted here.

label: Head and Neck 5000
counts: people enrolled April 2011 - December 2014
quote: We enrolled 5511 people into the study.
note: PMID:26436654, the HN5000 recruitment paper (fetched from Europe PMC; not on disk), titled 'Recruitment, response rates and characteristics of 5511 people enrolled in a prospective clinical cohort study: head and neck 5000'. Recruitment ran from April 2011 to the end of December 2014. The paper also says 'The percentage of people enrolled in the study was 5511 from 11 158 people who were identified as potentially eligible (49%).' The 2014 protocol (PMID:25519023) based its power calculation on 4,000 participants. The example study (PMID:34642315) analysed 534 oropharyngeal and 445 oral cavity cancer cases from HN5000.

label: International Agency for Research on Cancer Central Europe Study
counts: upper aerodigestive tract cancer cases and controls
quote: A multicenter case-control study comprising 811 upper aerodigestive tract cancer cases and 1,083 controls was conducted in: Bucharest (Romania), Lodz (Poland), Moscow (Russia), Banska Bystrika (Slovakia), and Olomouc and Prague (Czech Republic).
note: The abstract of PMID:16614111 (Hashibe et al. 2006), the study's own report. No total is stated, so participants is null. PMID:21437268 (INHANCE GWAS) says the study was conducted from 2000 to 2002 in 6 centres from 5 countries. Its Table 4 row for 'Central Europe' reads, as extracted, '8082,5877232,200', which I read as 808 cases and 2,587 controls before QC and 723 and 2,200 after GWAS QC; that control count includes controls shared with the lung and kidney cancer arms. PMID:22655231 likewise pooled all Central Europe lung and kidney controls with the head and neck controls.

label: Institute for Behavioral Genetics
note: No readable source states the pooled number of genotyped IBG participants. The example study (PMID:35378236, PMC10859168) gives only the 22-cohort total (64,641 individuals); IBG's own sample size is in its Tables S1-S6/Supplement 1, which PMC serves only behind a download challenge and Europe PMC does not hold. Component numbers read: the Colorado Adoption Project 'was capped at 245 adopting families' (PMID:23158098); the Colorado Twin Registry's Longitudinal Twin Sample 'is 483' families (PMID:23092589). The supplement of PMID:35378236 would settle it.

label: International Collaboration for the Genomics of HIV
counts: HIV-1-infected participants with genotype and clinical data pooled in the ICGH viral-load analysis
quote: Although it is the largest collection of genomic data in HIV, this multiethnic sample of 9,705 people is 81.3% male.
note: Full text of PMID:37097752 also says 'we accessed genotype and clinical data from 9,705 participants from the ICGH (19)' (7,890 male; 6,315 European, 2,535 African American, 855 southern African ancestry). The earlier ICGH acquisition GWAS (PMID:23935489) started from 'a data set of 11,860 HIV-1 infected individuals' and analysed '6,334 HIV-1 infected cases and 7,247 controls' (the controls being general population samples, not ICGH participants). The 9,705 is taken as the pooled ICGH sample in its most recent analysis.

label: International Endometriosis Genetics Consortium
counts: cases and controls in the 2023 IEGC GWAS meta-analysis
quote: The two most recent GWAS analyses of endometriosis, comprising 928,413 participants (including 44,125 cases; 30% non-European ancestry)7 and 762,600 participants of European descent (including 60,674 cases)4, identified up to 45 loci.
note: Reference 4 of the example study (PMID:42056605) is the IEGC meta-analysis (PMID:36914876), whose abstract states: 'A genome-wide association study meta-analysis, including 60,674 cases and 701,926 controls of European and East Asian descent, identified 42 genome-wide significant loci comprising 49 distinct association signals.' Its methods add that the 24 datasets contribute '58,961 cases, and 700,345 controls of mainly European ancestry and one dataset from Japanese ancestry (1,713 cases: 1,581 controls)'. The IEGC 2020 review (PMID:32423502) anticipated 'analysis of 60,000 cases'. The 762,600 total is the example study's statement; the IEGC paper itself states only cases and controls separately.

label: INGI-Val Borbera
counts: adults recruited in Val Borbera
quote: As a part of a research program aimed at the identification of genes and variants associated to common disorders, we present here the analysis of a cohort of 1803 adult subjects from Val Borbera, selected based on their ancestry to represent the general population in the valley.
note: The cohort's design paper (PMID:19847309) also says the descendant population 'now includes approximately 3,000 people' (the source population, not participants). A later analysis (PMID:37174278) used 1109 VBI participants (an analysed subset). No later whole-cohort count was found in the sources read.

label: Ischemic Stroke Genetics Study
counts: ischaemic stroke patients enrolled (cases only; no enrolled-control count found)
quote: A total of 673 patients were enrolled; 50.5% reported aerobic physical activity less than once a week, 28.5% reported aerobic physical activity one to three times weekly, and 21% reported aerobic physical activity four times a week or more.
note: The ISGS protocol (PMID:12848902) planned 'a total of 900 participants, including 450 patients with ischemic stroke (cases) and 450 stroke-free volunteers (controls)'. An interim report (PMID:17845914) states 'A total of 505 patients were enrolled'. The SiGN design paper (PMID:24021684, Table 1) lists ISGS with 675 CCS-phenotyped cases recruited 2002-2008. Patient-control series from ISGS appear in PMID:24086431 (802 Caucasian and 298 African American, cases and controls together) and PMID:17534386 (484 cases and 263 controls, not stated to be ISGS alone). No source read states the total number of controls ISGS enrolled; a later ISGS summary giving cases and controls would settle the total.

label: Karolinska Mammography Project for Risk Prediction of Breast Cancer
counts: women recruited 2011-2013
quote: During the recruitment period, a total of 210 233 women were invited to participate in the KARMA study and 70 877 women (34%) joined the study (Figure 2).
note: From the cohort profile (PMID:28180256), which also says 'A total of 70 877 women (21–95 years of age) were recruited between 2011 and 2013'. Its Table 1 describes 70 773 women; about 15 000 have been genotyped.

label: Kathleen Cuningham Foundation Consortium for Research into Familial Breast Cancer
counts: people (from the first 822 families) with data held
quote: Data are available for 11,422 consented participants, including 900 carriers of pathogenic or splice site BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations, and germline DNA biospecimens for 7,389, including 773 carriers.
note: From the resource description (PMID:16507150), whose abstract also says 'Data are currently held for 11,422 people and germline DNAs for 7,389' from 'kConFab's first 822 families'; questionnaires were 'collected from 7,039 individuals, with more limited data concerning a further 4,383 deceased relatives collected by proxy'. The count is from 2006 and recruitment has continued: the kConFab website (https://www.kconfab.org/) now says 'kConFab has accumulated data on more than 1,900 multigenerational, multi-case kindreds' but gives no number of people. A current participant count from kConFab would supersede this.

label: Krakow stroke genetics study
counts: ischaemic stroke cases phenotyped for SiGN as of April 2013 (cases only)
quote: KRAKOW Krakow, Poland Hospital-based 2001–2011 1487 19–100 48 100 0

The same paper says controls 'from the KRAKOW and LEUVEN sites (n = 1,282)' were to be genotyped, a combined figure for two sites, so the Krakow control count is not stated. The MEGASTROKE supplement description gives recruitment from 2002 to 2010 but no number. A Krakow-specific study description giving cases and controls would settle the total.

note: Cases and controls are from the most recent MADCaP report found (PMID:41812093, abstract via Europe PMC); no source read states their total, so participants is left null rather than summed. Earlier counts: the network paper (PMID:30260755) piloted with 'a total of 311 patients with CaP and 218 matched controls recruited at the seven SSA centers'; PMID:34783926 says 'Between 2016 and 2020, we recruited 2,200 PCa cases and 1,985 age-matched controls'; PMID:36100952 analysed 1298 cases and 1333 controls (genotyped subset). A MADCaP source stating the total enrolled would settle participants.

label: Maywood Cohort
counts: African Americans in the hypertension family study (US arm)
quote: As part of a study of the genetics of hypertension, we examined families that included 1449 Nigerians and 1147 African Americans.
note: The abstract of PMID:10818078 (Loyola group, US blacks versus Nigerians) does not name Maywood; the US families of this hypertension genetics study are taken to be the Maywood cohort, which is why confidence is low. Other counts read: a genome scan of '618 black individuals from 202 families residing in a suburb of Chicago' (PMID:11812767); 'an independent African-American sample comprising 545 individuals in 128 families' (PMID:12716766); 809 US participants from Maywood in a 1994-1999 analytical data set (PMID:18433493); 743 genotyped African-Americans from Maywood plus a replication panel 'Maywood family, n = 756' (PMID:20400458); 'Maywood (N=743)' in the example study (PMID:21998595). A cohort description naming Maywood and its total enrolment would settle it.

label: Minnesota Breast Cancer Family Study
counts: at-risk women (relatives and marry-ins) of 426 probands, followed through 1996
quote: A total of 9073 at-risk women were studied: 56% were biological relatives of the case probands, whereas the others were related through marriage.
note: From the cohort's follow-up report (PMID:10613336, abstract), which describes 'a historical cohort study of relatives of a consecutive series of 426 breast cancer cases (probands) identified between 1944 and 1952'. The 9073 excludes the probands and any male relatives, so the whole family cohort is larger; no source read states that total. The example study (PMID:35414113) does not mention the cohort in its main text.

counts: ischaemic stroke patients enrolled in the registry 2000-2009

The SiGN design paper (PMID:24021684, Table 1) lists 'MCISS New Jersey, USA Hospital-based 1999–2009 876', the cases CCS-phenotyped for SiGN as of April 2013 (a subset). The registry enrolled cases only; SiGN used external controls.

label: HARMONISATION study
counts: memory-clinic patients recruited 2010-2020

counts: genotyped melanoma patients analysed for melanoma-specific survival
quote: First, we conducted two GWAS of MSS in the MIA cohort (5762 patients with melanoma and 800 melanoma-specific deaths) and in UKB cohort (5220 melanoma patients and 241 melanoma-specific deaths).
note: From PMID:36064556 (definition source); the abstract also gives 'MIA; 5,762 patients with' melanoma. This is the number with genotype and survival data in that analysis, which may be a subset of all genotyped MIA patients. An earlier paper (PMID:32716505) identified 1740 patients with germline DNA in the MIA Biospecimen Bank and retained 1660 unrelated MIA cases after cleaning (first genotyping phases only). The example study (PMID:34813871) abstract gives no MIA count; its full text is closed.

counts: 3C Study participants aged 75+ with an initial eye examination
quote: In 2009-2011, 1153 participants from the 3 Cities Study, aged 75 years or more, had an initial eye examination and were scheduled for eye examinations.

label: MUNICH stroke study
counts: ischaemic stroke cases collected at the Munich stroke unit (cases only)
quote: The Munich samples included 1383 ischemic stroke cases.
note: From the WTCCC2 description in the MEGASTROKE supplementary note (definition source). The collection is of cases; its controls came from the separate KORA population study. After quality control the WTCCC2 discovery set held '1,174 German' cases (PMID:22306652). The SiGN design paper (PMID:24021684, Table 1) lists 'MUNICH* Munich, Germany Hospital-based 2002–2009 524' cases still being CCS-phenotyped in 2013.

label: Norwegian, Exeter and King's College Consortium for Genetics of Neuropsychiatric Symptoms in Dementia
counts: AD cases from 11 cohort studies in the consortium's 2019 psychosis PRS analysis
quote: Schizophrenia PRS was calculated using Psychiatric Genomics Consortium data at ten GWAS p value thresholds ( P T ) in 3111 AD cases from 11 cohort studies characterized for psychosis using validated, standardized tools.
note: PMID:31641104 (Creese et al. 2019) is the paper that PMID:34112972 cites for 'Additional details for the NEXGENS cohort'; its 3111 AD cases come from AddNeuroMed, ADNI, IRCCS, HMS, REDIC, NorCog, SAM-AKS, NordNorge, PADR, DemVest, NACC and NIAGADS, which includes US sources (ADNI, NACC) that the COHO definition does not list, hence low confidence. In the psychosis GWAS meta-analysis (PMID:34112972, Table 1B) the NEXGENS summary statistics cover 652 AD without psychosis and 663 AD with psychosis; that paper states no NEXGENS total. The example study (PMID:38784964) gives only the 9988-participant total over six source programs. A NEXGENS-specific description of its pooled sample would settle it.

label: NeuroGenetics Research Consortium
counts: cases and controls analysed in the 2010 NGRC genome-wide association study
note: Supplementary Table 1 (Subjects) of PMID:20711177: columns are subjects genotyped (N), exclusions, and subjects analyzed (N); 4013 genotyped, 3986 analyzed. The abstract states the same split: 'We performed a genome-wide association study of 2,000 individuals with Parkinson's disease (cases) and 1,986 unaffected controls from the NeuroGenetics Research Consortium (NGRC).' This is the genotyped GWAS set, not necessarily everyone NGRC has enrolled; PMID:32566740 reports separate NGRC microbiome datasets (212 PD and 136 controls in 2014; 323 PD and 184 controls in 2015-2017). No source read gives a total NGRC enrolment.

label: Genetics of Hypertension in Blacks
counts: unrelated Nigerian adults in the quality-controlled genome-wide dataset
quote: The final cleaned dataset thus consisted of 1614 unrelated adult hypertensive (n = 790) and normotensive (n = 824) subjects, 940 females and 674 males with 759,215 SNPs across both the 22 autosomal and X chromosomes.
note: PMID:22615923 (2012), the most recent definition source; 790 hypertensive and 824 normotensive, so not strictly a case-control design and cases/controls left null. Earlier GWAS sample, PMID:20400458 (2010): 'The sample comprised 1098 unrelated adults with normal or elevated blood pressure and 155 unrelated participants from Ibadan with elevated blood pressure recruited as controls in the Africa-America Diabetes Mellitus (AADM) study' and 'Curated genotype data on 792 857 SNPs were available on 1188 unrelated adults (510 males).' PMID:21573225 is a Maywood (US) sample of 977 African, European and Hispanic Americans, not this Nigerian sample. No source gives the total size of the long-term hypertension study beyond the genotyped sample.

counts: NSCLC cases and controls genotyped on the Global Screening Array
quote: For the present study, we newly performed genome-wide scan for 19,546 samples (NJMU GSA project: 10,248 cases and 9,298 controls) using Illumina Global Screening Array (GSA), which included three studies (Nanjing GSA study: 4,149 cases and 3,198 controls from Nanjing and Shanghai; Beijing GSA study: 2,155 cases and 2,035 controls from Beijing and Tianjin; and Guangzhou GSA study: 3,944 cases and 4,065 controls from Guangdong).
note: PMID:31326317 (Lancet Oncol 2019), the paper that introduced the NJMU GSA project; the quote gives the three component studies' counts. The example study PMID:42152146 repeats 'the NJMU Global Screening Array project (10,248 cases and 9,298 controls)'. Counts are samples genotyped (19,546), i.e. participants.

label: Parkinson's Disease Cognitive Genetics Consortium
counts: PD patients enrolled and clinically assessed at the eight consortium sites
quote: We enrolled and clinically assessed 1,424 participants with PD in studies at eight sites which together comprise the PD Cognitive Genetics Consortium (PDCGC; Appendix e-1).
note: PMID:26296077 (2015); its final GBA dataset was 1,369 patients. dbGaP phs001664.v1.p1 (Stage I NeuroX dataset): '1,219 PD patients were genotyped' and 'Total number of consented subjects: 1219'; 1,105 after QC. PMID:27571329: 740 patients at 7 sites with longitudinal assessments. PMID:38870440 (2024): 1,057 screened at baseline at 4 Pacific Udall sites, 841 analysed. Pooled PD patients only (no controls: 'the PDCGC did not consistently recruit healthy control participants'). No source gives a later consortium-wide total.

note: Table 1 of PMID:21673961 gives, per study, invasive cases N (mean age) and controls N (mean age) among white non-Hispanic women; no source read states a total for the study, so participants is null. Other counts seen for the same study: Supplementary Table 1 of the 2009 OCAC GWAS (doi 10.1038/ng.424) 'Polish Ovarian Cancer Study (1) POL1 Poland Population based 555 (35) 517 (10)'; the 2013 OCAC GWAS supplement (doi 10.1038/ng.2564) 'POC Poland: Szczecin, Poznan, Opole, Rzeszów Case-‐control 423 417'; PMID:23513043 lists 355 cases in a survival analysis. All are analysed subsets; a design paper of the study itself would settle the full enrolment.

quote: Weighted PRS models were constructed and analyzed on 4602 individuals from the Asian Indian Diabetes Heart Study/Sikh Diabetes Study (AIDHS/SDS) as discovery/training and test/validation datasets.

counts: childhood cancer survivors enrolled (signed consent) by March 2020
