note: Cohort profile PMID:33374007 (2021). Same source: 'Of the 8192 survivors, 6560 have agreed to participate and 5223 have completed a baseline clinical assessment.' and 'As of 12 March 2020, 736 (target accrual of 1250) community controls have completed on-campus evaluations.' (controls not included in the 6005). The 2011 design paper PMID:21370418 reported 3,900 eligible survivors and 908 completed evaluations as of 1 January 2010.

label: Swedish Low-risk Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: more than 3,300 consecutive colorectal cancer cases recruited 2004-2009 (lower bound)
quote: The CRC low-risk study is a Swedish multicenter cohort study including more than 3,300 consecutive CRC cases recruited in 2004–2009 (15).
note: PMID:39665592 (2024); the number is stated as a lower bound ('more than 3,300') and counts cases only. The same paper: 'A total of 1,642 controls were recruited, 870 male patients and 772 female patients.' (controls are healthy spouses or blood donors). Earlier: PMID:20648012 (2010) '1786 consecutive CRC patients of Swedish origin recruited through the Swedish Low-Risk CRC Study Group from 14 different hospitals from central Sweden during 2004–2006' with 1749 controls (1319 blood donors, 430 spouses); example study PMID:34758156 '2663 CRC cases and 1642 controls in the discovery analysis'; PMID:39543761 2637 cases after genotyping QC. An exact total, e.g. from the study's design paper (ref 15 of PMID:39665592), would settle it.

label: Screening Markers for Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: participants with genotyping data from both recruitment phases (genotyped subset)
quote: This resulted in 1,859 study participants (340 from phase 1 and 1,519 from phase 2) with genotyping data available, comprising 489 cases with adenomas only, 401 cases with serrated polyps only, 188 cases with synchronous adenomas and serrated polyps, and 781 polyp-free controls (Table 2).
note: PMID:24875374 (2014). Cases are given only by polyp type (489 adenoma only, 401 serrated only, 188 both), so the cases field is left null rather than summed. This counts participants who gave a DNA sample and were genotyped; no source read states the number enrolled or interviewed in the two phases (1998-2003, 2004-2007). PMID:30510241 and the example study PMID:36576985 are consortium meta-analyses that do not give SMS-specific counts in the text read.

label: Siblings With Ischemic Stroke Study
counts: probands and siblings in the final genome-wide scan after QC (analysed subset)
quote: After quality control filtering, the final study population consisted of 223 probands, 248 stroke-affected siblings, and 84 stroke-unaffected siblings (total sample size, 555).
note: PMID:21940970 (2011 results paper, after the original recruitment goal was reached): 'A total of 312 affected sibling pairs (312 probands) were enrolled at 70 centers across the US and Canada.' No source states the total number of people enrolled (probands plus all siblings), so the analysed total is given. The SiGN design paper PMID:24021684 lists SWISS with 407 CCS-phenotyped ischaemic stroke cases ('SWISS Multi-center, USA Cases with affected siblings 1999–2011 407'). The 2002 protocol PMID:11882254 planned 800 subjects (300 concordant pairs and 200 discordant siblings).

label: Saguenay Youth Study
counts: 1029 adolescents and 962 parents (no combined total stated)
quote: The Saguenay Youth Study (SYS) is a two-generational study of adolescents and their parents (n = 1029 adolescents and 962 parents) aimed at investigating the aetiology, early stages and trans-generational trajectories of common cardiometabolic and brain diseases.
note: Cohort profile PMID:27018016 (abstract; the full text says 'The SYS cohort includes 1029 adolescents and their 962 parents' from 481 families; wave 2 (2012-15) fully assessed 664 parents). Participants is null only because no source states the combined number of adolescents plus parents, and it must not be summed; the two group counts are exact. The 2007 design paper PMID:17469173 reported 408 adolescents and 195 sets of parents as of October 2006.

label: ThyroidOmics Consortium
counts: euthyroid individuals (maximum N) in the 2024 reference-range thyroid function GWAS meta-analysis of 46 cohorts
quote: We conducted GWAS meta-analyses of reference range thyroid function including up to 271,040 euthyroid individuals from European ancestry across 46 predominantly population-based cohorts from the ThyroidOmics Consortium.
note: PMID:38291025 (2024), the consortium's largest meta-analysis; 'up to' means the maximum across traits. Its case-control GWAS: 'a subset of 27 and 20 studies with 6712 and 4212 cases (146,529 and 137,337 controls)' for high and low TSH. The earlier ThyroidOmics GWAS PMID:30367059 (2018) tested 'up to 72,167 individuals' from 22 discovery cohorts. The consortium website (genepi.med.uni-greifswald.de/thyroidomics/) gives no participant count. The example study PMID:41238958 (482,873 with TSH) is a meta-analysis of biobanks, not a ThyroidOmics count.

label: Treatment Options for Type 2 Diabetes in Adolescents and Youth
counts: participants randomised to a treatment group
quote: Of the 1211 children and adolescents who were screened, 927 (76.5%) entered the run-in phase and 699 (75.4%) were randomly assigned to a treatment group, for an overall enrollment rate of 57.7%.
note: Main trial report PMID:22540912 (NEJM 2012); recruitment 2004-2009. Confirmed by PMID:38815053: '699 participants, 10 to 17 years old, ... were enrolled across 15 clinical centers in the United States'. The 2007 design paper PMID:17448130 planned 800 patients. The example study PMID:34568709 mentions 'over 2000 youth with T2D from the TODAY ancillary genetics study', a separate screening-based collection not counted here.

label: Tracking Parkinson's
counts: Parkinson's disease patients recruited (recent onset and young onset); siblings not included
quote: 2247 PD cases were recruited (1987 recent onset, 260 young onset).
note: Baseline cohort paper PMID:26485428 (2015). Unaffected siblings were still being recruited: 'Recruitment of first degree relatives, to a target of 840 unaffected siblings, is underway.' No source read states the number of siblings enrolled or a later total. The example study PMID:38849413 is a 12-cohort progression meta-analysis (6766 PD patients overall); its per-cohort Table 1 was not needed here.

label: Universitatsklinikum Saarlandes case-control dataset
counts: AD cases and population-based controls in the UKS case-control dataset
quote: UKS: The UKS cohort is a thoroughly diagnosed case-control cohort from Universitatsklinikum Saarlandes, consisting of individuals clinically diagnosed with sporadic Alzheimer’s disease (N = 596; age-at-onset [mean ± SD]: 72.2 ± 6.6 years) and cognitively healthy, age-, gender-, and ethnicity-matched population-based controls (N = 170; age-at-exam: 64.1 ± 3.0 years).
note: From the Supplementary Note of the definition source and example study (PMID:42237039, EADB/ADGC consensus meta-analysis). No source read states a case-plus-control total, so participants is left null. The Supplementary Note says UKS was described in earlier ADGC/IGAP papers, which were not read.

label: Viborg Vascular
counts: men randomised to screening or no screening
quote: A cost-effectiveness evaluation was conducted alongside an RCT involving all men from a region in Denmark (50 156) who were allocated to screening (25 078) or no screening (25 078) and followed for up to 5 years.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of the VIVA cost-effectiveness paper (2018). The protocol (PMID:20507582, definition source) planned 'approximately 50,000 65-74 year-old Danish men will be randomized'. The main mortality results paper was not read. The example study (PMID:37845353) uses VIVA jointly with UKAGS in a GWAS meta-analysis without a VIVA count.

label: West Bank Cancer Registry
counts: no total of registered cases stated
note: A cancer registry that keeps accruing incident cases, so it has no fixed enrolment. The UN/WHO Health Inforum newsletter (definition source) gives only period counts for the predecessor Palestinian Cancer Registry: 'In the West Bank, about 1,481 cases of cancer were reported in the same period with an incidence rate per 100,000 population of 60.1 (61.8 in male and 58.5 in female).' (the period being 1998-1999). PMID:41969536 (definition source) is about the Gaza registry and gives no West Bank count; the example study (PMID:40887045) is a lymphoma case-control study in Israel and the West Bank whose counts (716 controls, 404 DLBCL, 171 FL, 58 MZL) are not the registry's. A recent West Bank cancer registry annual report stating cumulative registered cases would settle it.

label: Washington University St. Louis Stroke Study
counts: ischaemic stroke cases recruited 2008-2012 (cases being phenotyped for SiGN)
quote: WUSTL* St. Louis, USA Hospital-based 2008–2012 535 20–90 42 47 28
note: A row of Table 1 of the SiGN design paper (PMID:24021684, definition source): columns GRC, Location, Recruitment Source, Recruitment Years, Cases (n), Age Range, Female (%), European Descent (%), African Descent (%); the asterisk footnote reads '*Cases being phenotyped.' and the table caption counts cases 'as of April 3, 2013'. It is a case-only collection, so participants equals cases. The MEGASTROKE supplementary note (definition source) describes WUSTL without a count; the example study (PMID:39286457) does not name WUSTL in the cached text. The WUSTL count in the final SiGN GWAS (PMID:26708676) was not read.

label: Sea Islands Genetics Network – Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke
counts: SIGNET-REGARDS participants with GWAS genotyping (1,141 with and 1,243 without diabetes)
quote: GWAS genotyping was completed for 2,384 SIGNET-REGARDS participants used in this study, including 1,141 with diabetes and 1,243 without diabetes.
note: From Text S1 of the MEDIA T2D meta-analysis (PMID:25102180, definition source). The same text says 'All SIGNET samples (n= 4,298) were genotyped', which covers the whole SIGNET study (REGARDS, Project SuGAR, COBRE Oral Health, SLEIGH), not only its REGARDS part; dbGaP phs000433.v1.p1 gives 'Total number of consented subjects: 4291' for the whole SIGNET study. The 1,243 without diabetes include the Low Country participants as well as the matched controls. It is the count 'used in this study', possibly after QC.

label: Wellcome Trust Case Control Consortium 2 Parkinson's disease study
counts: PD cases and WTCCC2 population controls before exclusions
quote: Prior to any exclusion, the full data set comprised 2190 individuals with idiopathic PD, and 5667 population controls.
note: From the Europe PMC full text (PMC3005904) of the WTCCC2 PD GWAS (definition source). After sample QC: 'our final data set consisted of 1705 cases and 5175 controls.' The controls are the shared WTCCC2 controls ('2930 samples from the 1958 Birth Cohort (58C) and 2737 samples from the UK Blood Services Controls (NBS)'), not recruited for this study. No source states a case-plus-control total, so participants is null. The French replication set (1039 cases, 1984 controls) is a separate collection.

label: CALGB 80303
counts: patients enrolled and randomised 2004-2006
quote: Between June 2004 and April 2006, 602 patients were enrolled onto the study and 535 were treated.
note: The results paper (definition source) also says 602 patients were randomly assigned, 302 to gemcitabine/bevacizumab and 300 to gemcitabine/placebo; 535 received study treatment. The ClinicalTrials.gov record (definition source) was not in the cache and was not needed. The example study (PMID:34616010) analysed a genotyped subset.

label: CALGB 90401
counts: men randomly assigned
quote: In total, 1,050 patients were randomly assigned.
note: From the results paper's abstract (definition source). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00110214 (definition source, fetched) agrees: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":1050,"type":"ACTUAL"}. The example study (PMID:34616010) analysed a genotyped subset.

label: Colonomics
counts: stage II colon cancer patients (paired tumour/normal) and healthy mucosa donors
quote: Colonomics is a multi-omics dataset that includes 250 samples: 50 samples from healthy colon mucosa donors and 100 paired samples from colon cancer patients (tumor/adjacent).
note: From the abstract of the Colonomics data descriptor (definition source); the full text (https://europepmc.org/api/getPdf?pmcid=PMC9526730) says 'One hundred patients were included, with the criteria of a confirmed adenocarcinoma of the colon, diagnosed in stage II and the tumor was microsatellite stable (tested with five markers).' and 'As a control group, 50 healthy mucosa donors (M) were prospectively invited to participate in this study'. The 250 are samples (100 tumour, 100 adjacent normal, 50 donor mucosa), not people; no source states a person total, so participants is null.

label: CALGB 40503
counts: women enrolled across the letrozole phase III and tamoxifen phase II parts (registry actual enrolment)
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":394,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: The registry record (definition source, fetched) covers both endocrine partners (tamoxifen or letrozole), matching the definition's two parallel comparisons; its participant flow shows 195 and 199 started in the two arms. The phase III results paper (PMID:27138575, definition source) gives the letrozole part only: 'From May 2008 to November 2011, 350 women were recruited; 343 received treatment and were observed for efficacy and safety.' (target 352). The tamoxifen phase II results were not read.

label: 23Mofang cohort
counts: no whole-cohort count stated; only analysed subsets
note: No source read states how many 23Mofang customers are in the research cohort. Analysed subsets only: the refractive-error GWAS (PMID:42009823, definition source and example study) used 'in 47,305 self-reported people with myopia and 8,209 nonmyopic people from 23Mofang, Inc.'; the photic sneeze reflex GWAS (PMID:30899065, definition source) says 'A total of 3519 individuals (all Chinese citizens) voluntarily participated in the project studying the association between genetic variants and PSR phenotype.' and analysed 3417. A Europe PMC search for 23Mofang found a Y-chromosome study of '207,333 Han Chinese males published by 23Mofang', a count of male customers' haplogroup data rather than the research cohort. A company statement of consented research participants would settle it.

label: 3D Facial Norms cohort
counts: participants in the 3DFN database (952 males, 1502 females)

note: From the 3DFN resource paper (PMID:26492185, definition source), which also says 'The current dataset contains 2454 individuals: 952 males and 1502 females.' The sexual dimorphism paper (PMID:27110347, definition source) analysed 1555 individuals aged 3-25. The example study (PMID:39622794) pools 3DFN with other US studies (n = 4680) without a 3DFN count.

label: 4D-SZ cohort
counts: Shenzhen participants with high-depth whole-genome sequencing (as of 2021)
quote: The 4D-SZ cohort (multi-omics, with more data to come, from Shenzhen, China) at present have high-depth whole-genome sequencing data from 2984 individuals (mean depth of 33×, ranging from 15× to 78×, Supplementary Table S1 and Fig.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC full text (PMC8648780) of the oral mgGWAS paper (definition source); the sentence continues past 'Fig.' into a figure reference. It counts only the sequenced Shenzhen participants, not everyone recruited. The example study (PMID:36660475) says 'This study at present included a total of 4,478 individuals', but that total adds a replication cohort of 1,494 recruited 'in multiple cities (Wuhan, Qingdao, etc.) in China', outside the Shenzhen cohort the definition describes. Other subsets: 632 discovery and 663 replication individuals in the gut mgGWAS (PMID:33563976); 516 women in 2017 and 632 in 2018 in the vagino-cervical study (PMID:34118463). No source states the total enrolled.

label: Age-Related Eye Disease Study
counts: participants enrolled 1992-1998
quote: A total of 4757 participants were enrolled, 157 more than planned for by design.
note: From the AREDS design paper (AREDS report no. 1, PMID:10588299, definition source), which also calls AREDS 'a long-term multicenter, prospective study of 4757 persons age 55 to 80 years'. The AMD trial enrolled 3640 (AREDS report no. 8, PMID:11594942) and the cataract trial 4629 for its primary comparison. dbGaP phs000001 (definition source) was not read.

counts: participants enrolled and randomised at 82 US centres
quote: We enrolled 4203 participants at 82 clinical centers located in the United States.
note: From the Europe PMC abstract of the AREDS2 baseline paper (definition source). The main results paper (PMID:23644932, definition source) agrees: 'conducted in 2006-2012 and enrolling 4203 participants aged 50 to 85 years'.

label: African Research on Kidney Disease
counts: people who underwent measured GFR testing (Malawi 1020, South Africa 986, Uganda 1019)
quote: Of 3025 people who underwent measured GFR testing (Malawi n=1020, South Africa n=986, and Uganda n=1019), we analysed data for 2578 participants who had complete data and adequate quality measurements.
note: From the Europe PMC abstract of the ARK results paper (Lancet Glob Health 2022, definition source). The protocol (PMID:31941441, definition source) planned 'We intend to recruit 3000 participants in total.' (1000 per country). 2578 had complete data and were analysed.

label: Berkeley Aging Cohort Study
counts: no whole-cohort count stated; only analysed subsets
note: BACS is an ongoing cohort and no source read states how many people it has enrolled. Analysed subsets only: PMID:37502020 (definition source) describes 'Berkeley Aging Cohort Study (BACS), a cohort of elderly individuals who had psychometrically normal cognition at baseline, residing in the community in the San Francisco Bay area (n = 188).'; PMID:40441049 clustered 'longitudinal lifestyle testing sessions from 203 BACS participants'; PMID:38334195 used 78 older adults with tau PET. The example study (PMID:37101235) used BACS summary statistics only. A web search and an arXiv paper returned by it gave no total. A BACS cohort profile or the Jagust lab's own statement of enrolment would settle it.

label: Diabetes UK Warren 1 Repository
counts: families recruited 1989-1996 (505); no count of individuals stated
quote: Between 1989 and 1996, 505 British families with at least two siblings affected by Type 1 diabetes were recruited.
note: The quote counts families, not people, so participants is null; the same abstract mentions 1010 parents ('Type 1 diabetes was recorded in 63/1010 (6.2%) parents'), but no sentence gives the total number of individuals. Table 1 of the T1DGC HLA paper (PMID:20595243, definition source) lists 1791 'Samples received (N)' for 'BDA Warren I' (row text 'BDA Warren IcUKEUd1791'), which counts DNA samples typed, not necessarily all repository members. PMID:11507694 (definition source) used 356 Warren families in an earlier genome scan. A repository description stating the number of individuals would settle it.

label: Brain Development and Air Pollution Ultrafine Particles in School Children
counts: children whose families agreed to participate (of 5,019 invited)
quote: All school children (n = 5,019) without special needs in grades 2 through 4 (7–10 y of age) were invited to participate, and families of 2,897 (59%) children agreed.
note: From the Europe PMC full text (PMC4348510) of the BREATHE cognitive development paper (definition source); 2,715 children with complete data were analysed. The MRI paper (PMID:31539824, definition source) agrees: 'a total of 39 representative schools of the city of Barcelona and 2897 children agreed to participate in the whole survey', with 186 in the MRI subsample.

label: National Cancer Institute Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium
counts: prostate cancer cases and controls genotyped in the 2011 pooled BPC3 analysis of 39 GWAS SNPs
quote: We therefore genotyped 39 SNPs from regions identified by several prostate cancer GWAS in 10,501 prostate cancer cases and 10,831 controls from the NCI Breast and Prostate Cancer Cohort Consortium (BPC3).
note: A consortium with separate breast and prostate case-control sets and no single flagship total. The design paper (PMID:16341085, definition source) describes 'a pooled analysis of multiple large cohort studies with a total of more than 5,000 cases of breast cancer and 8,000 cases of prostate cancer' (only its abstract and references were readable). Other pooled analyses in the definition sources: breast IGF pathway, 6,912 breast cancer cases and 8,891 matched controls (PMID:18596909); ER-negative breast cancer GWAS, 1998 cases and 2305 controls (PMID:24523857); aggressive prostate cancer GWAS, 2,782 cases and 4,458 controls (PMID:23255287). The largest, the 2011 prostate analysis, is given as cases and controls; no source states a case-plus-control total, so participants is null.

label: Biomarkers and Stratification To Optimise outcomes in Psoriasis
counts: participants recruited so far (stated as over 10,000)
quote: BSTOP has so far recruited over 10,000 participants and collected more than 34,000 biological samples.
note: The study website gives a lower bound ('over 10,000'), recorded as 10000; recruitment is ongoing. PMID:41408349 analysed 4151 BSTOP participants ('a cohort of 4151 participants in the UK-based severe psoriasis registry, BSTOP'), a genotyped subset.

label: Black Women's Health Study
counts: Black women enrolled in 1995
quote: The BWHS is a “follow-up” study, following the 59,000 women who enrolled in 1995 over time.
note: The example study (PMID:40050615) gives the same figure: 'a U.S. prospective cohort study of 59,000 United States Black women who enrolled in the study in 1995'.

label: Coronary Artery Calcification in Type 1 Diabetes Study
counts: adults enrolled at baseline (652 with type 1 diabetes, 764 non-diabetic controls)
quote: The study enrolled 1416 individuals between 19 and 56 years of age, with no known history of CHD: 652 subjects with type 1 diabetes and 764 nondiabetic control subjects.
note: Source is PMID:30943964. PMID:24130360 says 1,420 were enrolled but 4 did not meet inclusion criteria, 'leaving 1,416 (652 subjects with type 1 diabetes and 764 subjects without diabetes)'. The baseline abstract PMID:14578303 reports 656 with type 1 diabetes and 764 controls examined. 'cases' here are the participants with type 1 diabetes.

counts: consented subjects in the dbGaP release (cases, controls and others)
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 2875
note: Cases and controls are from the GAIN genome-wide scan of the collection (PMID:19169254): 'we carried out a genome-wide association scan of 1,409 psoriasis cases and 1,436 controls in partnership with the Genetic Association Information Network (GAIN)'; after QC 1,359 cases and 1,400 controls were analysed. dbGaP gives consent groups 'General research use (GRU): 1677 (950 cases, 692 controls, 35 others) Autoimmune disease (AD): 1198 (449 cases, 734 controls, 15 others)', so its total includes 50 'others' beyond cases and controls.

label: California and Uganda Prostate Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls genotyped on the H3Africa array (analysed set); no total stated
quote: For men of African ancestry, GRS replication was conducted among 1,586 cases and 1,086 controls from California and Uganda (CA UG Study) genotyped with the Illumina H3 Africa array and imputed using Phase 3 of the 1000 Genomes Project15 as the reference panel and Minimac4 on the Michigan Imputation Server27 (Supplementary Table 1 and 2).
note: Source is PMID:33398198. No source read states the total, so participants is left null (cases and controls are not summed). The study has no design paper found; PMID:37945903 and PMID:36872133 only list CA UG among contributing studies. Supplementary Table 1 of PMID:33398198 or PMID:37945903 may give the per-study total, and a separate breakdown by California and Uganda sites.

label: Cryptosporidiosis and Enteropathogens in Bangladesh Birth Cohort
counts: children enrolled at birth; only per-site counts stated
quote: Following delivery, 250 infants at Mirpur and 262 at Mirzapur were enrolled.
note: The design paper PMID:29897482 gives enrolment only by site (250 Mirpur, 262 Mirzapur in the full text; its abstract says 'urban, n = 250; rural, n = 258'), never a total, so participants is left null rather than summed. It also reports 'Pregnant women in urban Mirpur (n = 407) and rural Mirzapur (n = 330)' assessed in the second trimester. PMID:35420468 says 'From the CBC, 630 infants were genotyped', which exceeds these site counts and suggests later enrolment; PMID:34181697 followed 392 Mirpur infants. A later cohort profile stating the whole cohort's size would settle it.

counts: five-year survivors diagnosed 1970-1999 (stated as 38K+; siblings not included)

note: The study website gives a rounded lower bound ('38K+'), recorded as 38000; it excludes the sibling comparison cohort. counts: patients in the core study (analysed); registry counted separately

needs: PMID:31526754 full text (Lancet Neurol, doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(19)30232-7; only the abstract is on disk)
note: The quote is the abstract of the case-mix paper, whose heading 'Findings' is run into the preceding sentence in the cached text; the number is patients analysed in the core study, which may be slightly below the number recruited. counts: no count for this study alone

counts: children enrolled at birth in 1977

quote: Briefly, VETSA includes 1608 men who were recruited from the Vietnam Era Twin Registry (VETR), a nationally representative registry, which includes male twins, who were in the military at some time during the Vietnam era (1965–1975).

The 2019 status paper (PMID:31933447) says 'It comprises a subset of over 1600 twins from the Vietnam Era Twin Registry.'; the 2013 design paper (PMID:23110957) gives wave 1 as 'A total of 1,237 twins participated (349 monozygotic pairs, 265 dizygotic pairs, and 9 unpaired).'

label: VHIR-FMT-Barcelona
counts: ischaemic stroke cases and controls genotyped for the NINDS-SIGN GWAS (analysed set)
quote: VHIR-FMT-BARCELONA Spain HumanCore ExomeChip EUR 545 320
note: A row of Table 1 of the NINDS-SIGN GWAS (PMID:26708676; columns Cohort, Location, Array, Ancestry, Cases, Controls); no sentence states a total, so participants is left null. The MEGASTROKE supplement (doi:10.1038/s41588-018-0058-3) row reads 'Barcelona 520 520 119 215 315 EUR' (520 any/ischaemic stroke cases, subtypes and apparently 315 controls, the column layout being ambiguous in the extracted text). The collection is itself a genotyped case-control set, so these are its analysed sizes rather than an enrolment count; no description of its full size was found. The example study (PMID:39537608) gives no cohort-level count.

label: Virginia Twin Study of Adolescent Behavioral Development
counts: twin children in 1412 families who took part in wave 1
quote: Of 1894 putative twin pairs, 1412 families (75%, 2775 children) participated and were included in the first wave of data collection.
note: PMID:23461817. The 1997 papers agree in pairs: PMID:9413795 'A population-based, unselected sample of 1412 Caucasian twin pairs aged 8-16 years was ascertained through Virginia schools.'; PMID:9294370 'Families of 2762 white twins aged 8 to 16 years participated.' (a slightly smaller analysed count). PMID:23461817 also reports 2,962 individuals after quality control in its genotyped multi-study sample.

label: Vanderbilt Atrial Fibrillation Registry
counts: consented subjects in the registry's TOPMed dbGaP study
quote: Total number of consented subjects: 1134
note: This is the number deposited in dbGaP for TOPMed whole-genome sequencing (a case set of probands and family members), not necessarily the whole registry's enrolment. PMID:30271950 genotyped a sample set of 759 cases and 759 controls from the registry. No source read gives the registry's total enrolment since 2001; a registry design or profile paper from Vanderbilt would settle it.

label: WeGene cohort
counts: analysed subset: participants in the myopia GWAS
quote: We enrolled 5,952 Han Chinese participants (see Supplementary Note 1 for myopia status distribution), who had given informed consent and undergone genotyping as part of the WeGene Personal Genome Services.
note: WeGene's research cohort is its consenting customer base; no source read states the size of the whole research cohort, and each study reports only the subset that answered its survey. This is the example study's subset. Other subsets: 14,675 adult participants in PMID:39359028 ('We recruited 14,675 adult participants drawn from the customer base of WeGene'), 4101 in PMID:34457340, 2139 male individuals in PMID:28442769, 2152 unrelated individuals in PMID:34995520. Kang et al., 'Direct-to-consumer genetic testing in China and its role in GWAS discovery and replication' (Quantitative Biology), not in the cache, may give the whole customer/research base.

label: Wisconsin Sleep Cohort Study
counts: people who took part in the baseline in-laboratory sleep study
quote: There were 1545 individuals (53% of those invited) who agreed to come in for a baseline sleep study (the primary reason for non-participation was the burden of being away from home overnight).
note: The cohort's rationale and design paper (PMID:19743755) gives a round figure: 'we chose a 2-stage probability sampling scheme to yield a final cohort sample (n=1500)' and its abstract reports 'data from 1500 participants'. The example study (PMID:35670608) gives the achieved baseline number used here; it also reports that 5091 of 6947 surveyed state employees returned the 1988 mailed survey and that 2884 were invited to polysomnography; 962 WSC participants were in its GWAS.

label: ZOE 2.0
counts: children aged 3-5 enrolled 2016-2019
quote: Between 2016 and 2019, the study enrolled 8059 3–5-year-old children attending public preschools in North Carolina, United States.
note: From the cohort's design paper (PMID:33139633), which also states that about 13,000 were invited and 62% (n = 8059) enrolled, that 6470 were seen for clinical assessments and 6404 gave usable ECC data. The example study (PMID:39885687) included 6,055 ZOE 2.0 participants in its BMI GWAS.

label: Protection Against Allergy: Study in Rural Environments
counts: children recruited at birth 2002-2005
quote: PASTURE recruited 1133 children in 2002-2005 from rural areas in 5 European countries: Austria, Finland, France, Germany, and Switzerland (6).
note: The same paper (PMID:33986744) refers to 'the PASTURE birth cohort (N=1133)'. PMID:36356926 compares 769 included and 364 excluded children at 10.5 years. The cohort's design paper (PMID:16512801) is only available as its abstract in the cache, which states no number.

label: Project Viva
counts: eligible pregnant women enrolled 1999-2002
quote: After recruitment we found 329 of them to be ineligible (Figure 1), leaving a total of 2341 eligible enrollees, of whom 2128 were still enrolled at the time of delivery and had live births.
note: From the cohort profile (PMID:24639442): 'We recruited 2670 women (64% of those who were approached for participation)', 329 of whom were found ineligible; 2128 live births (the child cohort); 1279 mother-child pairs at the mid-childhood visit. The number counts mothers; children are counted separately as 2128 live births.

label: GERO cohort
counts: planned enrolment only (target 300)
quote: The GERO cohort aims the recruitment of 300 elderly subjects (> 70 years) from Santiago (Chile), following them up for at least 3 years.
note: The protocol paper (PMID:33238908) gives only the target of 300 ('The final sample chosen was 300 participants') and says 'Up to date, the recruitment has not been completed.' ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04265482 also gives an estimated enrolment of 300 (last updated 2020). The example study (PMID:37985413) used only 32 AD cases and 20 controls from GERO. A GERO cohort profile (Alzheimer's & Dementia conference abstract, 'Cohort Profile: The Community-based Cohort of Functional Decline in Subjective Cognitive Complaint elderly study of the Geroscience Center for Brain Health and Metabolisms (GERO)') was found by title in a web search but not read; it would likely give the achieved number.

label: Alzheimer's Genetics in Argentina–Alzheimer Argentina consortium
counts: analysed subset: Argentinian samples in the 2023 GWAS after QC
quote: A total number of 1018 samples from Argentina and 375 samples from Chile remained after QC.
note: No source read states the consortium's total recruitment. The example study (PMID:37985413) is the most recent; its Table 1 lists the Argentina sample (N = 1018) as 416 AD cases and 602 controls (table, not a sentence, so cases/controls are left null). Earlier: PMID:30705288 '905 participants were recruited from different regions of the country' (419 AD cases and 486 controls); PMID:37333771 AGA-ALZAR (n = 962). The GAAIN partner page (https://www.gaaindata.org/getPartner?project=AGA) is a script-rendered page and returned no text.

label: STORK study
counts: healthy pregnant women included 2001-2008
quote: A total of 1031 healthy pregnant women who gave birth at Oslo University Hospital, Rikshospitalet, Norway were included in the study (Figure 1).
note: From PMID:22723995, which also says 'The cohort consisted of 1031 women and their newborns' and that data from the first 553 women had been published earlier.

label: San Antonio Longitudinal Study of Aging
counts: people who completed the 1992-1996 baseline examination
quote: Of the remaining 1,062 individuals, 749 completed the baseline examination for a response rate of 70.5%.
note: From PMID:21054295: of 1,247 eligible San Antonio Heart Study subjects, 166 died before SALSA started and 19 before completing baseline. PMID:21216857 agrees ('The SALSA baseline response rate was 70.5% (749 of 1,062 eligible candidates)'). PMID:25597562 used the 394 Mexican American baseline participants.

label: Northern Ireland GRID Collection
note: No sentence read states the collection's size. Table 1 of PMID:28983737 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5719131/) has the row 'NI NI Independent 524 509 7 (4, 10) 156,343', i.e. 524 Northern Irish GRID cases genotyped and 509 included after QC (ImmunoChip analysed subset); it is a table row, not a sentence, so it is not recorded as the number. The example study (PMID:34127860) and its supplements only name the collection. A description of the Northern Ireland type 1 diabetes collection (for example in the T1DGC ImmunoChip papers or a Queen's University Belfast resource page) would settle it.

label: Genome-wide assessment of the gene variants associated with severe COVID-19 phenotype in Iran
note: No sentence read states the study's size; the HGI papers (PMID:35922517, PMID:40399555) name it only in author and cohort lists. Their supplementary tables give counts in table cells only: the 2022 HGI table (https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41586-022-04826-7/MediaObjects/41586_2022_4826_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx) lists IranCovid with 210 cases and 183 controls (release R6), and the long COVID table (https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41588-025-02100-w/MediaObjects/41588_2025_2100_MOESM3_ESM.xlsx) lists IrCovid with 114 long COVID cases and 242 controls. A paper from the Shariati Hospital / Digestive Disease Research Institute group describing the Iranian COVID-19 GWAS would settle the total.

label: Northern Ireland Young Hearts Project
counts: adolescents surveyed at the initial 1989/1990 screening (YH1)
quote: Briefly, the initial screening (YH1), conducted in 1989/1990, surveyed 1015 adolescents (12-year old boys, n 251;12-year old girls, n 258; 15-year old boys, n 252; and 15-year old girls, n 254) randomly selected from post-primary schools.
note: This counts the longitudinal cohort (YH1), which was re-examined at YH2 (younger group, 1992/93) and YH3 (1997-1999, 48.2% response; 245 males and 231 females assessed at 15 and in young adulthood in PMID:15462676). The second school sample, Young Hearts 2000 (1999-2001), is counted separately: 'The Young Hearts Project 2000 had a total of 2,017 participants from Northern Ireland, consisting of 12- and 15-year-olds from 36 nationally representative schools; the response rate was 65.4%.' (PMID:20864003). The term covers both samples, but no source gives a single total for the project.

label: Active Life Expectancy, Ageing, and Disability Related to Obesity Study
counts: individuals in the ALEXANDROS cohorts (as stated in 2022)
quote: The cohort consists of 3086 individuals (2880 of which were randomly recruited from the registers of health centers).
note: The sentence in PMID:36013179 follows a description of the three ALEXANDROS cohorts (SABE, the 2005-2008 primary care cohort and ISAPRES), but it is not explicit whether 3086 is the whole study or only one of them. Other sources give the three cohorts separately: PMID:35887574 '1173 Subjects born before 1940' (SABE), '950 people born between 1940–1948' and '266 people of high socio-economic status'; PMID:22286726 gives SABE as 1235 people born before 1940, Alexandros 950 and ISAPRES 266. PMID:33883888 followed 2311 community-dwelling people from the Alexandros cohort; the example study (PMID:37985413) used 791 Alexandros controls. A design paper of the whole study would settle the total.

label: Genetics of Glaucoma in People of African Descent Consortium
counts: cases and controls in the consortium's 2019 two-stage GWAS (discovery and validation)
quote: A total of 26 295 individuals were included in the study.
note: From the consortium's flagship paper (PMID:31688885). Cases and controls from the same paper: 'An overall meta-analysis of rs59892895*C involving the 9257 individuals with primary open-angle glaucoma and 17 038 individuals without primary open-angle glaucoma from all cohorts'. Discovery: 2320 cases and 2121 controls; validation: 6937 affected and 14 917 unaffected individuals, including participants of existing studies. The example study (PMID:38242088) used a GGLAD dataset of n = 2,952 and a second GGLAD dataset (GGLAD-2) of n = 1,492 (also given as 1,490).

label: International Collaboration on Ovarian Neoplasms 7 trial
counts: women randomised 2006-2009
quote: Between Dec 18, 2006, and Feb 16, 2009, 1528 women were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive chemotherapy (n=764) or chemotherapy plus bevacizumab (n=764).
note: From the final overall survival report (PMID:26115797, abstract as served by Europe PMC). The quality-of-life report (PMID:23333117) agrees: 764 women randomly assigned to each group.

label: Genetics of Parkinson's in India – Young Onset Parkinson's Disease
counts: people with Parkinson's disease recruited over two years
quote: 674 subjects with PD were recruited through a network of 10 specialty movement disorder centers and/or neurology clinics located across India.
note: The 2023 medRxiv genetics preprint gives 674; the 2021 clinical study (PMID:33685545) reports 'A total of 668 subjects (M:F 455:213) were recruited with a mean age at onset of 38.7 ± 8.1 years.', and the 2022 MDS abstract analysed 609 genetic samples 'from a cohort of 668'. The preprint's 1,376 controls were drawn from GenomeAsia, not recruited by the study.

label: SweCovid study
counts: critical COVID-19 ICU patients in the PronMed cohort from which SweCovid is drawn
quote: The study includes 374 COVID-19 patients from the Pronmed cohort admitted to the ICU at Uppsala University Hospital.
note: No source read gives SweCovid's own count (the number genotyped or followed up); this is the PronMed ICU cohort it draws from, per PMID:36271419 ('The Pronmed cohort consisted of 374 patients out of which 165 had data on all of the osmolytes, 54 of these patients completed follow-up after 3–6 months'). An earlier PronMed paper (PMID:35052684) reported 229 ICU patients admitted 14 March 2020–2 March 2021. The SciLifeLab news page and the HGI papers (PMID:34597274, PMID:40399555) give no SweCovid count; the HGI supplementary study tables would give the number contributed.

label: COVID-19 Kohortenstudie am Klinikum München Rechts der Isar
note: No source read states the size of the COMRI cohort/registry. Only analysed subsets are given: PMID:35613127 'Hospitalized patients (ICU, n = 80 and non-ICU, n = 130) were prospectively included in the COVID-19 registry COMRI at the University Hospital rechts der Isar.'; PMID:35174781 sequenced samples from 108 COVID-19 and 22 post COVID-19 patients at Klinikum rechts der Isar; PMID:34235400 draws lymphoma patients from the CORKUM/COMRI registries. The HGI papers (PMID:34597274, PMID:40399555) name COMRI without a count in the text read; their supplementary study tables, or a COMRI registry description from TUM, would settle it.

label: Placental Abruption Genetic Epidemiology study
counts: analysed subset: women in the preterm-birth GWAS (PTB cases and controls)
quote: Our study included data from the PAGE study which were 2,212 women, 933 of whom were PTB cases.
note: No source read gives PAGE's total enrolment across all its case groups. The example study (PMID:39302385, published version of the preprint) states 'Mean GA was 30 ± 4 weeks in PTB cases (N = 933) and 39 ± 1 in the controls (N = 1,279).' The placental abruption GWAS (PMID:29884306) states 'Participants from PAGE study included 522 PA cases and 1147 controls.' (1,597: 507 cases and 1090 controls after QC). The two analyses overlap in controls to an unknown extent, so neither is the whole study; a PAGE design paper (the preprint's refs 42-43) would settle the total.

label: STORK Groruddalen
counts: pregnant women included 2008-2010
quote: 823 women were included, 59% of non-Western origin.
note: The same 823 (74% of eligible) is given in PMID:22108914 ("From May 6, 2008 to May 15, 2010, 823 (74% of eligible) women were included.") and PMID:34388220 (EPIPREG sub-study n = 480). Offspring not counted.

label: Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank
counts: individuals enrolled April-June 2020 (495 COVID-19 inpatients, 72 controls)
quote: In this study, 567 individuals (495 hospitalized with COVID-19 and 72 healthy and hospitalized controls) were enrolled in the Mount Sinai COVID-19 Biobank Study between April and June 2020 (Fig. 1).
note: PMID:36482101. The founding correspondence (PMID:32719485, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-020-1004-3) says only "In total, over 700 participants were accrued in 49 days", a lower bound that disagrees with 567; the 567 may be the participants retained for analysis. Of the 567, 232 later completed the post-acute sequelae checklist. The example study (PMID:40399555, Long COVID HGI GWAS) gives no Mount Sinai count in the text read.

label: Die Deutsche Diabetes Dialyse Studie
counts: patients randomised to atorvastatin or placebo
quote: The 4D Study was a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, prospective study enrolling 1255 participants with T2DM receiving maintenance HD at 178 centres who were randomly assigned to receive 20 mg of atorvastatin or matching placebo daily.
note: PMID:37779851. Same 1,255 in PMID:37806305 ("a prospective, randomized, double-blind trial enrolling 1,255 patients with type 2 diabetes on hemodialysis in 178 German dialysis centers"). The 1999 design paper (PMID:10412782) abstract read gives no achieved size.

label: African Descent and Glaucoma Evaluation Study
counts: participants of the original observational cohort (ADAGES I/II)
quote: A prospective, multicenter observational cohort study of 1221 participants of African descent and European descent with no glaucoma (normal), suspected glaucoma, and glaucoma.
note: The design paper also says "ADAGES obtained baseline clinical, visual function, and optic nerve structure data on 803 individuals of African descent and 418 individuals of European descent." The term also covers ADAGES III, a separately recruited case-control genomics sample (PMID:29361356): "The 3266 ADAGES III study participants in this report include 2146 AD POAG patients, 695 ED POAG patients, 198 AD control participants, and 227 ED control participants." The two phases' numbers are not summed. The example study (PMID:38242088) used an African-ancestry ADAGES subset of n = 1,999.

label: ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia Study
counts: African American children in the GWAS (840 B-ALL cases, 3360 controls)
quote: In this study, we show differences in the genetic architecture of childhood B-ALL risk in African ancestral populations with an analysis of 4200 African American children, including 840 B-ALL cases, as a part of the ADMIxture and Risk of Acute Leukemia (ADMIRAL) Study.
note: PMID:41125582. Controls from the abstract: "Leveraging multi-institutional datasets with 840 African American children with B-ALL and 3360 controls, nine loci achieved genome-wide significance (P -8) after meta-analysis." Discovery n = 3280 (656 cases), replication n = 920 (184 cases). This is the analysed GWAS sample; no separate profile of the whole study was found.

label: Amish Family Osteoporosis Study
counts: family members with DXA bone density in the 2006 linkage analysis
quote: BMD was measured at the spine, hip, and radius using DXA in 964 participants (mean age, 50.2 +/- 16.3 [SD] years; range, 18-99 years) from large multigenerational families.
note: This may be the analysed subset rather than all enrolled; no source read states the total enrolment. Other numbers: 424 parous women aged 40+ (PMID:15899951); 1,510 Amish adults with BMD pooled from AFOS, the Amish Family Longevity Study and PAPI (PMID:29739999), not AFOS alone. The example study (PMID:22792071) describes AFOS without a count. A cohort profile or the NIAMS grant report would settle the total.

label: Asian Genetic Epidemiology Network
counts: cases and controls in the 2020 AGEN type 2 diabetes meta-analysis (23 GWAS)
quote: Identification of type 2 diabetes loci in 433,540 East Asian individuals.
note: Cases and controls from the same abstract: "Here, to examine T2D risk in East Asian individuals, we carried out a meta-analysis of GWAS data from 77,418 individuals with T2D and 356,122 healthy control individuals." Full text: "The East Asian meta-analysis included 77,418 T2D cases and 356,122 controls from 23 GWAS, including three biobanks, CKB, KBA51,52, and BBJ2". Other AGEN analyses: kidney traits in 71,149 east Asian subjects from 11 cohorts (PMID:22797727); HbA1c in 16 cohorts of 32,602 individuals (PMID:24647736); AGEN-BP 19,608 subjects (cited in PMID:23105927); AGEN adiponectin n = 7,825 from four studies (PMID:37859345).

label: AIDS Linked to the IntraVenous Experience
counts: people who inject drugs enrolled since 1988 across all enrolment periods (stated as "over 5500", a lower bound)
quote: Since 1988, over 5500 PWID have been enrolled across several enrollment periods.
note: PMID:42461483. The source gives only a lower bound ("over 5500"). Initial enrolment: "Between 1988 and 1989, 2946 IDUs in Baltimore, MD were enrolled into a cohort study of the natural history of HIV-1 (AIDS Linked to the IntraVenous Experience [ALIVE]) study) and followed semi-annually." (PMID:20450418, PMC2874101); PMID:42461483 also says "2938 PWID were initially screened". Later subsets: 1,615 enrolled before 2015 analysed (PMC11056308); 1323 HCV-infected enrolled 2006-2019 (PMC9706936). An exact cumulative total would need a current cohort profile or the study website.

label: Australian Melanoma Family Study
counts: probands recruited 2001-2005 (629 cases, 240 population controls, 295 spouse/friend controls); relatives not counted
quote: From 2001 to 2005, the authors recruited 1,164 probands including 629 cases with histopathologically confirmed, first-primary cutaneous melanoma diagnosed before age 40 years, 240 population-based controls frequency matched for age, and 295 spouse/friend controls.
note: Controls are stated only as two groups (240 population-based and 295 spouse/friend controls), so controls is left null rather than summed. The same paper adds relatives: "Information on lifetime sun exposure, phenotype, and residence history was collected for probands and nearly 4,000 living relatives." No total including relatives is stated.

label: Anxiety NeuroGenetics STudy
counts: unrelated individuals in the 2016 anxiety-disorder GWAS meta-analysis of nine samples (stated as "over 18 000")
quote: Meta-analysis for each phenotype combined results across the nine samples for over 18 000 unrelated individuals.
note: A lower bound in the text. Table 1 of the same paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/research/bionlp/RESTful/pmcoa.cgi/BioC_xml/PMC4940340/unicode) has the row "Total 31 060 7016 14 745 18 186/17 310" under the columns N Phenotyped, N Cases (ANX=2), N Controls (ANX=0) and N Analyzed (FS/CC): 31,060 phenotyped, 7,016 cases, 14,745 supernormal controls, 18,186 analysed for factor scores and 17,310 for case-control. Seven member studies, nine samples.

label: Anglo-Australasian Osteoporosis Genetics Consortium
counts: postmenopausal women with extreme high or low hip BMD in the GWAS discovery sample
quote: In order to improve study power and to address the demographic group of highest risk from osteoporotic fracture, we have used a unique study design, studying 1,955 postmenopausal women with either extreme high or low hip bone mineral density.
note: PMID:21533022. Abstract gives the two groups: high BMD n = 1055 and low BMD n = 900; methods: "The discovery sample population included 1128 Australian, 74 New Zealand and 753 British women". An AOGC replication cohort also exists, whose size was not found in the text read. The example study (PMID:22792071) used 155 forearm fracture cases and 1,672 controls from the AOGC GWAS.

label: Anakinra for Pustular Psoriasis: Response in a Controlled Trial
counts: participants randomised October 2016 - January 2020 (31 anakinra, 33 placebo)
quote: From October 2016 to January 2020, 374 patients were screened and 64 eligible participants were enrolled; 33 were randomized to placebo and 31 to anakinra (Figure 1).
note: PMID:34411292. The protocol (PMID:30157880) planned the same size: "A total of 64 participants will be randomised to anakinra or placebo in a 1:1 ratio."

label: Assessment of Renal and Cervical Artery DysplasIA
counts: patients recruited into the registry 2009-2014 (FMD confirmed in 469)
quote: As previously reported, among the 499 patients recruited in the ARCADIA study, FMD was confirmed in 469 patients, of whom 75 (16%) were men and 415 (89%) were Caucasian (Table 1).
note: PMID:33998257. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02884141 (API fetched) gives enrollment count 499, type ACTUAL. The FMD GWAS (PMID:34654805) used 431 ARCADIA cases with 1487 controls from the Three-City Study.

label: Anglo-Scandinavian Cardiac Outcomes Trial
counts: hypertensive patients randomised in the Blood Pressure-Lowering Arm
quote: ASCOT was a prospective randomised controlled trial of two different blood pressure-lowering strategies in 19 342 hypertensive subjects with three additional risk factors for CV disease—ASCOT Blood Pressure-Lowering Arm (BPLA).
note: PMID:40139683. PMID:38291599 (PMC10984564) instead says "Nineteen thousand two hundred and fifty-seven participants were randomized to the BPLA." (19,257; the difference was not explained in the text read). Lipid-Lowering Arm: "A total of 10 305 participants were randomised to the LLA"; ASCOT Legacy Cohort: 8580 UK participants.

label: The Ashkenazi Jewish Dataset
counts: Parkinson's disease cases and controls genotyped for the AJ GWAS
quote: A total of 268 cases and 178 controls were genotyped using the Illumina Human 610-quad bead arrays (Cases n = 91 and Controls n = 96) or the Illumina Human 660-quad bead arrays (Cases n = 191 and Controls n = 84).
note: PMID:21812969. The paper states cases and controls separately but never a combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. Confirmed: "The AJ dataset had a slightly larger number of cases (n = 268) versus controls (n = 178)". The 2,050 cases and 1,836 controls are the joint analysis with the NINDS and CIDR dbGaP datasets, not this cohort.

label: Assessment, Serial Evaluation, and Subsequent Sequelae of Acute Kidney Injury Study
counts: hospitalised adults with or without AKI (matched pairs) completing the 90-day visit; children not counted
quote: The full ASSESS-AKI cohort included 1538 hospitalized adults who did or did not experience an episode of AKI and survived to complete a study visit 90 days after discharge.
note: PMID:37273234. Cases and controls from PMID:32707221 (PMC7374148): "We enrolled and individually matched 769 adults with AKI and 769 adults without AKI, with 39.8% having preexisting CKD" (a matched cohort, AKI vs non-AKI). The design paper (PMID:20799966) planned "1200 participants (1100 adults, 100 children)"; the achieved number of children was not found. The GWAS analysed 1369 participants.

label: Age-related diseases: Understanding Genetic and non-genetic influences - a study at the University of Regensburg
counts: participants of the two baseline surveys (AugUR1 2013-2015: 1133; AugUR2 2017-2019: 1316)
quote: Among the 2449 AugUR participants (AugUR1: n = 1133 and AugUR2: n = 1316; and no overlap between the 2 datasets), information on AMD stages for at least one eye, as well as genetic data were available for 2188 persons (AugUR1: n = 1010 and AugUR2: n = 1178).
note: PMID:37721739. The protocol (PMID:26489512) planned: "In the long term, we aim to recruit 3,000 persons of Caucasian ethnicity with at least 70 years of age via residents' registration offices and conduct 3-year follow-ups." The 2188 with AMD grading and genotypes are an analysed subset.

label: Bambui (Brazil) Cohort Study of Ageing
counts: residents aged 60+ enrolled at the 1997 baseline
quote: Briefly, the baseline cohort population comprised 1,606 (92.2%) of all the 1,742 residents aged 60 years or more on January 1st, 1997, who were identified by means of a complete census carried out in the city.
note: PMID:23251690. 1,742 eligible residents. The BMI admixture study (PMID:33633342) had genotype, BMI and covariate data for 1342 Bambui participants.

label: Biology, Affect, Stress, Imaging and Cognition study
counts: women enrolled September 2009 - November 2018 (6478 pregnancies)
quote: From September 2009 to November 2018, the BASIC study at Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, has enrolled 5492 women, in 6478 pregnancies, of which 46.3% first-time pregnancies and with an average age of 31.5 years.
note: Cohort profile; recruitment ended November 2018, so this is the final enrolment.

label: Baltimore Breast Cancer Study
counts: breast cancer cases and cancer-free controls analysed in the 2006 MDM2 study (possibly a subset)
quote: We used multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses to study the relationship of SNP309 status and the status of a second MDM2 SNP in exon 12 at codon 354 (SNP354) with breast cancer incidence and with disease-specific survival among 293 case patients and 317 cancer-free control subjects.
needs: PMID:16818855 full text (JNCI, not open access)
note: Abstract read from Europe PMC (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=TITLE:...&resultType=core); PMID:16818855 is the design reference (ref. 29) that PMID:22357627 cites for the Baltimore Breast Cancer Study. No total is stated, so participants is null rather than summed; these may be the analysed subset. African American subsets: "A total of 117 African Americans incident cases and 111 African Americans controls were included in this study." (PMID:22357627); "After quality control, we included 94 cases and 102 controls of African ancestry from BBCS in the ROOT consortium." (41588_2024_1736 supplement). The full text of the design paper would settle the whole enrolment.

label: Beaver Dam Eye Study
counts: persons examined at baseline (1988-1990)
quote: In brief, a private census identified 5924 persons living in the city and township of Beaver Dam, Wisconsin aged 43–86 years, of which 4926 participated in the baseline examination in 1988–1990 and in up to four follow-up examinations in 1993–1995, 1998–2000, 2003–2005 and 2008–2010.
note: The census identified 5924 eligible residents (PMID:30208419 says aged 43 to 84); 1181 persons took part in the 25-year follow-up in 2014-2016 (PMID:29242907). PMID:32200810 describes the study as 'of 5000 participants'. The example study analysed 1740 BDES individuals after QC.

label: BioImage Study: A Clinical Study of Burden of Atherosclerotic Disease in an At-Risk Population
counts: subjects who completed enrolment (all three groups)
quote: Of this population, 7687 subjects completed enrollment, of which 865 were enrolled as “survey-only” participants, 718 were enrolled in the Framingham-only group, and 6104 were enrolled in the full study group (see Fig. 1).
note: Design paper; enrolment completed June 2009. 6104 were in the full imaging group. The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT00738725 was not on disk and was not needed. The example study is a multi-cohort meta-analysis that does not give the BioImage count in the matched sentences.

label: Barbados National Cancer Study
counts: breast cancer arm: incident cases and age-matched female controls (2002-2006)
quote: The BNCS included 241 incident BC cases and 481 age-matched female controls, with mean ages of 57 and 56 years, respectively.
note: Breast cancer design paper (abstract; results repeat it with participation rates of 80% and 82%). No sentence states a total, so participants is null. The prostate arm is described in separate papers as the Prostate Cancer in a Black Population (PCBP) Study: 'a large case-control investigation including 1,007 incident PC cases and 1,005 controls' (PMID:24399209 abstract, Europe PMC); whether COHO counts it within this term is for the curator. The example study's Table 1 lists 84 BNCS cases and 217 controls (PMID:34706928); PMID:22357627 used 93 cases and 244 controls from Barbados.

label: Brigham and Women's Rheumatoid Arthritis Sequential Study
counts: patients enrolled (actual enrolment in the registry record)
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":1598,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: Structured field of the ClinicalTrials.gov record (last updated 2025-09-26, status active, not recruiting, enrolment from 2003-03). PMID:33002337 (definition source): 'All 1,443 patients enrolled in BRASS as of November 13, 2015 were included in the PC and cluster analysis.' PMID:31002669 describes BRASS as 'a single-center, prospective, observational cohort of over 1,300 RA patients'. The example study (PMID:20453842) used 483 BRASS RA cases in its GWAS.

label: British Society for Surgery of the Hand Genetics of Dupuytren's Disease study
counts: Dupuytren's disease case subjects in the 2017 GWAS
quote: The UK cohort consisted of a total of 5,408 case subjects from the BSSH-GODD Study and 9,961 population-based control subjects from the United Kingdom Household Longitudinal Study (UKHLS), which were divided into 4,891 control subjects for the discovery phase and 5,070 control subjects for the replication phase.
note: BSSH-GODD collects cases only; the controls in this GWAS come from a separate study (UKHLS), so cases/controls are left null. This is the number of BSSH-GODD cases in the analysis (discovery plus replication), not a stated total recruited. The EGA study page (EGAS00001001206) was not on disk; the example study (PMID:38172110) gives no BSSH-GODD count in its text.

label: Cambridgeshire Parkinson's Incidence from GP to Neurologist
counts: incident Parkinson's disease cases meeting diagnostic criteria, followed up
quote: Those meeting diagnostic criteria (n=142) were followed-up until 1 January 2012.
note: 10-year follow-up paper (abstract); the cohort was collected between December 2000 and 2002. The 13-year paper (PMID:31965629) excluded one of these 142 after a change of diagnosis, giving n = 141. This counts the idiopathic PD cohort only; the whole incident parkinsonism cohort identified in 2000-2002 (all causes of parkinsonism) should be stated in the 2004 baseline paper (PMID:14691062, Brain), whose full text was blocked (403) and whose abstract gives only incidence rates.

label: Canadian Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection Study
counts: SCAD patients enrolled in the first phase (Canadian SCAD Cohort Study)
quote: We prospectively enrolled 750 SCAD patients from June 2014 to June 2018.
note: Phase 1 design/outcomes paper (abstract; results: 'from 22 centres'); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02188069 also gives 750 (actual). The extension, NCT04906356, gives only a planned enrolment of 3000 (estimated, recruiting, last updated 2021-05-28); no source read states the achieved enrolment of the extended study. PMID:32887874 used 272 CanSCAD cases (enrolled 2017-2018) for GWAS discovery and 163 (2018-2019) for replication.

label: Copenhagen City Heart Study
counts: persons examined at the first examination (1976-1978)
quote: Of the original 14,223 examined at the first examination 3,092 (21.7%) have been examined in all four examinations, and of the 5,106 non-responders from the first survey in 1976–1978, 1,698 responded and were examined in one or more of the following surveys.
note: Study review (Glob Cardiol Sci Pract 2015). It also says '19,329 persons, 9,145 men and 10,184 women, were invited for the first examination' and that 'The total number of participants invited to the first four examinations was: 19,329+500+3,000+1,062 = 23,891 men and women'; the abstract calls it a study 'of 20,000 women and men'. No source read states the total number of distinct people examined across all five examinations (including 2011-2013), which a CCHS cohort profile would settle. The example study (PMID:35379992, EADB) gives no CCHS count in the matched text.

label: Chicago Cancer Prone Study
counts: participants registered since 1992
quote: Briefly, CCPS is a local registry of diverse high‐risk families at a hospital‐based preventive oncology clinic that has registered 5685 participants as of September 2024 since its establishment in 1992.
note: Most recent source (definition source, PMC12818384 full text). Its breast cancer case-control arm is described in PMID:22792352 as providing '607 case patients and 555 controls' for that analysis (an analysed subset). The example study (PMID:34706928) Table 1 lists 317 CCPS cases and 107 controls.

label: Comprehensive Sickle Cell Centers Collaborative Data Project
counts: children and adults with sickle cell disease enrolled (actual enrolment in the registry record)
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":3640,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: Structured field of the C-Data ClinicalTrials.gov record (terminated; study period March 2005 - September 2008); the genotype-phenotype repository record NCT00528203 gives the same actual count, 3640. BioLINCC says 'The available data includes 3638 participants.' PMID:20658620 (paediatric quality-of-life analysis): 'The study enrolled 1,772 subjects (53% boys) with a mean age of 9.6 years (SD 4.7).', the children only.

label: Cardiovascular Genome Center cohort
counts: individuals in the CGC cohort screened for a genetic study
quote: Among 8839 individuals in the CGC cohort, 4425 males received coronary angiography; 7 individuals showing a study-feasible Framingham score but normal coronary arteries were enrolled as supernormal.
note: From the example study (2022), which screened this cohort; it does not give the date the count refers to, and no design paper of the registry was found. Earlier papers give smaller subsets: PMID:27736948 'Between November 2000, and March 2011, 2693 study subjects were enrolled from Cardiovascular Genome Center'; PMID:35352885 screened 1300 ACEI users (2001-2007) and 1186 (2008-2018); PMID:24142632 used 498 registry subjects.

label: Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility
counts: cases and controls in the first (prostate cancer) genome-wide scan, 2007
quote: While conducting a genome-wide association study in the Cancer Genetic Markers of Susceptibility project with 550,000 SNPs in a nested case-control study (1,172 cases and 1,157 controls of European origin), we identified a new association at 8q24 with an independent effect on prostate cancer susceptibility.
note: Aggregation with two flagship GWAS; no source states a single pooled total, so participants is null. Prostate scan abstract (Europe PMC); its combined analysis with four further studies totalled '4,296 cases and 4,299 controls'. Breast scan (PMID:17529973): 'Thus, the GWAS analysis was performed on 1,145 cases and 1,142 controls.' (1,183 cases and 1,185 controls from the Nurses' Health Study were genotyped), with replication in 1,776 cases and 2,072 controls. The CGEMS portal abstract (PMC2291937) says 'The first whole genome scan includes approximately 1200 prostate cancer cases and 1200 controls.'

label: Canadian Cystic Fibrosis Gene Modifier Study
counts: patients with CF recruited 2003-2006 (parents not included)
quote: The Canadian CF Modifier Study population consists of 2,441 patients diagnosed with CF between 1951 and 2006 and 3,092 parents.
note: PMC2248329 full text: patients and family members were recruited from 37 CF clinics across Canada, 2003-2006. The same sentence gives 3,092 parents; no sentence states the combined total, so the patient count is recorded. No source read states the size after the second recruitment phase. Later consortium papers give the CGS subsets analysed: 285 in GWAS2 (PMID:26417704 Table 1) and 1,614 in the example study (PMID:36921087 Table 1).

label: Center for HIV/AIDS Vaccine Immunology
counts: HIV-1-infected individuals genotyped in the Host Genetics Core's 2009 GWAS of HIV control (Euro-CHAVI and MACS)
quote: A total of 2554 HIV-1 infected individuals of self-reported Caucasian ancestry were genotyped on Illumina whole-genome chips (Table S1).
note: Aggregation: the number is the pooled sample of its flagship host-genetics GWAS (Euro-CHAVI N = 1397, MACS N = 1157, per the next sentence). CHAVI's own clinical studies are described without a total in PMID:24910414: 'The longitudinal multicenter CHAVI studies enrolled participants that were HIV-infected [acutely- (n = 376), chronically- (n = 420), undefined (n = 184)] and uninfected [with autoimmune disease (n = 322) or without (n = 348)], on multiple visits.' Other analyses: HIV acquisition GWAS with 6,334 infected cases and 7,247 controls (PMID:23935489); Malawi GWAS of 1,532 individuals (PMID:21160409). No source gives the consortium's total enrolment or number of member cohorts beyond Euro-CHAVI's '8 European cohorts and 1 Australian cohort' (PMID:20205591).

label: Chinese Keratoconus Cohort Study
counts: keratoconus patients enrolled January 2019 to June 2023
quote: The CKC cohort is hospital-based and dynamic and was established in Zhengzhou, China; KC patients (n = 1114) from a large geographical area were enrolled from January 2019 to June 2023, with a mean age of 22.23 years (6‒57 years).
note: Cohort profile (abstract); 918 patients completed the first follow-up by June 1, 2023. The cohort is ongoing (dynamic), so later papers draw on it: 958 patients in the example study (PMID:38767907, with 7186 external controls) and PMID:39186261; 395 patients and 396 controls in PMID:40642536.

label: Chronic Kidney Disease in Children Study
counts: participants enrolled across cohorts 1-4 (only a lower bound stated)
quote: Over 1,000 participants have enrolled in CKiD, and many are continuing to be actively followed-up.
note: The study website gives only a lower bound, so participants is null. Its study-design page (https://statepi.jhsph.edu/ckid/study-design/) says Cohort 1 (2005-2009) 'enrolled approximately 600', Cohort 2 (2011-2014) 'approximately 300', Cohort 3 (2016-2020) 'roughly 200', and Cohort 4 is enrolling from 2025. The design paper (PMID:17699320) planned 540 children; PMID:37871960 says CKiD 'enrolled children aged 6 months to 16 years with eGFR 30-90 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ( n =569)'; PMID:35518833 analysed 953 US participants enrolled 2005-2019; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00327860 gives an estimated enrolment of 1300 (recruiting). A current exact enrolment figure from the coordinating centre would settle it.

label: UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics
counts: participants (healthy adults and psychiatric patients) with DNA and task data
quote: One sample (n = 1138) comprised healthy participants and some psychiatric patients (53 schizophrenia, 42 bipolar disorder, 47 ADHD); the other (n = 911) excluded for recent treatment of various psychiatric disorders but not ADHD.
note: Example study (abstract of PMC10618088); the first sample is the CNP. Its methods say 'In total, 996 healthy individuals, 53 participants with schizophrenia, 42 with bipolar disorder, and 47 with ADHD were evaluated.' The number counts those in this genetic analysis; the CNP's full screened community sample may be larger and no source read gives it. The imaging data descriptor (PMID:27922632) covers the MRI subset: 130 healthy, 50 schizophrenia, 49 bipolar disorder and 43 ADHD subjects.

label: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease in Dusty Areas
counts: participants enrolled for baseline examinations 2012-2017
quote: Overall, 504 participants (362 males and 142 females) were enrolled between 2012 and 2017 for baseline examinations.
note: PMID:41136451 (2025) agrees: 'Of a total 504 patients in the CODA cohort'. Earlier or subset counts: 400 in PMID:29117798 (recruited 2012-2014); 500 subjects (324 COPD, 176 controls) in the example study (PMID:35886039); 185 enrolled aged 50-80 in PMID:41436567. The cohort's design paper (Hong et al.) was not read.

label: Cohort in Lung Transplantation
counts: lung transplant candidates included (before transplantation), 2009-2019
quote: By February 2021, COLT had included 1874 patients and among them, 1,618 have been transplanted; of these, 1,106 (68.4%) could be followed up over 3 years, 905 (55.9%) over 5 years, and 117 (7.2%) over 10 years.
note: COLT enrolled candidates before transplantation, so the included count is given. The later genomic biobank paper (PMID:39164465, 2024) says 'COLT comprises a total of 1413 transplanted patients from whom clinical data and biological samples were collected', which disagrees with the 1,618 transplanted above; its GenCOLT subset has 392 donor-recipient pairs (n = 784 individuals). The example study (PMID:41864285) was not readable on disk (publisher page empty).

label: Cooperative Study of Sickle Cell Disease
counts: participants of all ages enrolled in Phase 1 (1978-1988)
quote: A total of 4,085 participants, ranging in age from newborns to adults, were enrolled in Phase 1 from 23 centers across the US.
note: BioLINCC study page. Later phases followed subsets: 709 infants enrolled in Phase 1 were followed in Phases 2 and 3 (450 enrolled in Phase 2 follow-up plus 17 children; 378 continued in Phase 3), and 359 adult Phase 1 participants entered Phase 2A. PMID:36138487 analysed 1904 participants meeting its inclusion criteria; the example study (PMID:40025045) used CSSCD n = 841. The 1982 design paper (PMID:7114401) had no text on disk beyond its record.

label: Dallas Heart Study
counts: DHS-1 participants with completed interviews (survey phase), 2000-2002
quote: Completed interviews were obtained for 6,101 subjects (54% black), phlebotomy visits for 3,398 (52% black), and clinic visits for 2,971 (50% black).
note: Design paper (PMID:15194016, abstract) gives 6,101 interviewed, 3,398 with phlebotomy and 2,971 with clinic visits in DHS-1. The example study (PMID:33619548) reports a probability sample 'n = 3557' collected 2000-2002 and analysed DHS-1 n = 3538, DHS-2 n = 3283; PMID:24531328 analysed 4,708 DHS-1/DHS-2 participants with clinical examination. No single source read states the combined DHS-1 plus DHS-2 enrolment.

label: Danish Testicular Cancer Late Treatment Effects Cohort
counts: testicular cancer survivors who returned the questionnaire, 2014-2016
quote: By December 31, 2016, a total of 2,572 (60%) of questionnaires distributed was filled in and returned, and this number of TCS make up the DaTeCa-LATE study population.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:29515973): 5,367 patients treated 1984-2007 in DaTeCa, 4,271 eligible survivors invited, 2,572 responders make up the cohort; 1,699 non-responders. Reference population of 162,283 from the Danish National Health Profile is not part of the cohort.

label: Drakenstein Child Health Study
counts: pregnant women enrolled who gave birth (mothers; 1143 live-born children)
quote: Over 3 years, 1137 women (median age 25.8 years; 21% HIV-infected) gave birth to 1143 live babies.
note: The protocol paper (PMID:25228292) gives the planned size: 'enrolled with 1000 mother–child pairs followed for at least 5 years' and 'The sample size of 1000 mother-infant pairs'. The achieved number is from the cohort's maternal health and birth outcomes paper (PMID:31751344, abstract via Europe PMC). The number counts mothers; the 1143 live babies are the children. Women who were not enrolled form a separate control cohort, not counted. The example study (PMID:38177345) gives no Drakenstein count in the text matched.

label: Dental Strategies Concentrating on Risk Evaluation
counts: Heart SCORE participants given dental assessments, 2007-2010
quote: Dental assessments and related data collection were carried out between 2007 and 2010 on a subgroup of 552 participants, known as the Dental Strategies Concentrating on Risk Evaluation (Dental SCORE) study.
note: PMID:41006734 gives 552 Dental SCORE participants (subgroup of the 2,000 Heart SCORE participants). The example study (PMID:35172313) analysed 'Dental SCORE, n = 548' in its enamel hypoplasia GWAS, presumably the genotyped analysed subset. No dedicated design paper found.

label: Diabetes Gene Discovery Group
counts: stage 1 GWAS cases and controls genotyped on both platforms (analysed sample)
quote: A total of 661 cases and 614 controls were successful in both Stage 1 platforms.
note: Sladek et al. 2007 supplement (PMID:17293876): stage 1 cases were recruited in Lille ('N=271') and Corbeil-Essonnes ('N=423'); its Table S1 lists 686 cases and 669 controls on Human1 and 694 cases and 654 controls on Hap300. No sentence read states a combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The example study (PMID:35551307) text cached gives no DGDG count (its supplementary cohort table was not read). The stage 2 replication sample (2,617 cases, 2,894 controls) is a separate sample.

label: Diabetes Multi-omic Investigation of Drug Response
counts: DIAMOND participants genotyped (not necessarily all enrolled)
quote: A total of 2,158 DIAMOND participants were genotyped;
note: Only source found is the definition/example paper (PMID:37639712, Wu et al. 2024 Diabetes Care): 2,158 participants genotyped, 13 failed QC; analysed sets were 447 African American and 466 European American DIAMOND participants on metformin. No design paper or website giving total enrolment was found (Europe PMC search for the cohort's full name returns only this paper).

label: Detroit Neighborhood Health Study
counts: adults recruited at baseline (wave 1)
quote: The Detroit Neighborhood Health Study (DNHS) recruited 1,547 adults aged 18 years or older at baseline from the city of Detroit.
note: Chang et al. 2012 (PMID:22745713): 1,547 adults at baseline; venipuncture specimens from a subsample of 501 in wave 1. PMID:41821625 analysed RNA from 389 wave-2 and 243 wave-4 participants. Some later DNHS papers may count additional participants recruited in later waves; none read here states a larger total.

label: Endometrial Cancer Association Consortium
counts: cases and controls in the 2018 ECAC-led endometrial cancer GWAS meta-analysis
quote: Here, we present an expanded meta-analysis of 12,906 endometrial cancer cases and 108,979 controls (including new genotype data for 5624 cases) and identify nine novel genome-wide significant loci, including a locus on 12q24.12 previously identified by meta-GWAS of endometrial and colorectal cancer.
note: Quote from O'Mara et al. 2018 (PMID:30093612, abstract). That meta-analysis also includes E2C2 cases (2695 cases, 2777 controls) and other non-ECAC GWAS. ECAC's own iCOGS stage (PMID:27135401): 4,330 cases of European ancestry 'recruited via 11 studies'; OncoArray: 4710 cases and 19,438 controls after QC. The 2016 meta-analysis had 7,737 cases and 37,144 controls; the 2025 example study (PMID:40633141) 17,278 cases and 289,180 controls, mostly biobank data. No sentence gives a combined total, so participants is null.

label: European Challenge for Healthy Aging
counts: long-lived probands (aged 90+) in the handgrip analysis; analysed subset, probands only
quote: Among 598 very old people (median age = 98 years) a clear North-South gradient was observed:
note: No source read states the total ECHA enrolment (probands plus offspring and cousins). PMID:16870633 (abstract) analysed only the long-lived probands (598). PMID:17989723 (abstract): 'A total of 234 trios composed by one centenarian, his/her child and a child of his/her concordant or discordant sib were collected.' PMID:20584770 (abstract): handgrip measured 'in 290 subjects aged 90 years and older and in one of their offspring'. The full texts of PMID:16870633 and PMID:17989723 (closed) might give the total recruited per region.

label: Pittsburgh Epidemiology of Diabetes Complications Study
counts: participants examined at the 1986-1988 baseline
quote: All participants (n = 658) were diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, or seen within 1 year of their diagnosis, at Children’s Hospital of Pittsburgh between 1950 and 1980.
note: Miller et al. 2025 (PMID:39932735). The life-expectancy paper (PMID:22851572) describes 'a prospective cohort study of 933 participants' diagnosed 1950-1980, which is the wider registry-based mortality cohort of eligible people rather than the 658 examined at baseline. PMID:37533055 analysed n = 368 with DNA and no CVD at baseline; PMID:39932735 analysed 300 women and 304 men without CVD.

label: Scottish AMD study
counts: Scottish replication cases and controls in the 2007 C3 study
quote: The common functional polymorphism rs2230199 (Arg80Gly) in the C3 gene, corresponding to the electrophoretic variants C3S (slow) and C3F (fast), was strongly associated with age-related macular degeneration in both the English group (603 cases and 350 controls, P=5.9x10(-5)) and the Scottish group (244 cases and 351 controls, P=5.0x10(-5)).
note: Yates et al. 2007 (PMID:17634448, abstract). No sentence gives a combined total, so participants is null. The International AMD Genomics Consortium paper (PMID:26691988) text read names no Scottish counts; its supplementary study table (docx, not readable from the cache) would give the numbers of Scottish cases and controls contributed to the 2016 GWAS.

label: Estudo Longitudinal de Saúde do Adulto
counts: civil servants enrolled at Visit 1 (baseline, 2008-2010)
quote: At Visit 1, we enrolled 15 105 civil servants from predefined universities or research institutes.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:24585730, abstract and full text): 16 435 expressed interest, 15 821 pre-enrolled, 'A total of 15 105 participants were enrolled, 6887 men and 8218 women'; 9916 had completed the second visit by December 2013.
