label: Epidemiology of Burkitt Lymphoma in East African Children and Minors
counts: suspected Burkitt lymphoma cases and population controls enrolled 2010-2016
quote: We therefore conducted a population-based case-control study of eBL in children aged 0-15 years old in six regions in Northern Uganda, Northern Tanzania and Western Kenya, enrolling 862 suspected cases and 2,934 population controls (response rates 98.5-100%), and processing ~40,000 vials of samples using standardized protocols.
note: Peprah et al. 2020 (PMID:31054214, abstract), the main EMBLEM case-control paper: 80.9% of the recruited cases were diagnosed as eBL. The EMBLEM website design page (https://emblem.cancer.gov/design) says 'EMBLEM accrued 800 cases and 2900 matched population controls'. The example GWAS (PMID:40646133) says 'we enrolled 575 BL cases and 3,645 BL-free community controls' from Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya. No sentence gives a combined total, so participants is null.

label: Essen-Heidelberg
counts: melanoma cases and healthy controls genotyped
quote: 1,218 melanoma cases were genotyped using 848 HumanCytoSNP-12v1-0_D arrays [Illumina] with 300,000 SNPs and 1,223 healthy controls from Germany were genotyped using HumanOmniExpress12_v1_C arrays [Illumina] with 731,000 SNPs.
note: Supplementary Note of Law et al. 2015 (PMID:26237428, the example study); its Supplementary Table 1 lists Essen-Heidelberg with 1,212 cases and 1,219 controls after QC in stage 1. No sentence gives a combined total, so participants is null. PMID:32341527 main text names the study only in the investigator list.

label: FActeurs de RIsque et de récidives de la maladie thromboembolique Veineuse
counts: adults enrolled 2003-2007: first-VTE cases and matched controls
quote: We conducted a case-control study involving 1,454 adults enrolled in 11 French centers between 2003 and 2007, comprising 727 consecutive cases with a first documented episode of VTE and 727 age- and sex-matched controls.
note: From the abstract of PMID:19967159 (Thromb Haemost 2009; full text behind a bot wall), which covers enrolment to 2007 only, while the study ran until January 2009 (PMID:36002395). Later descriptions: PMID:37399490 says FARIVE 'is a multicenter case–control study composed of 607 patients with a documented episode DVT and/or PE and 607 healthy individuals' (probably the genotyped set); the example study (PMID:37286573) used n = 1158 (582 cases, 576 controls). No source read gives the final 2003-2009 enrolment.

label: European/International Fibromuscular Dysplasia Registry and Initiative
counts: FMD patients enrolled December 2015 to 30 April 2019 (database lock)
quote: Since December 2015, the European/International Fibromuscular Dysplasia (FMD) Registry enrolled 1022 patients from 22 countries.
note: Pappaccogli et al. 2020 (PMID:32282921, abstract; full text at the orbi.uliege.be PDF: 'One thousand twenty-two patients were enrolled in 46 centres from 22 countries ... between 1 December 2015 and 30 April 2019 (database lock)'). The registry is ongoing, so later enrolment may be larger. The example GWAS (PMID:34654805) used 243 FEIRI cases with 615 controls.

label: FinDonor 10 000 study
counts: blood donors recruited May 2015 to December 2017
quote: A total of 2584 blood donors (N = 8003 samples) were recruited into the study alongside standard donation at three donation sites in the capital region of Finland between 5/2015 and 12/2017.
note: Cohort paper (PMID:31657023, abstract and full text). The '10 000' in the study name refers to a target, not the achieved size.

label: National FinHealth 2017 Study
counts: no exact participant count found; the sample drawn was 10,247 adults
quote: For the FinHealth 2017 Study, a representative sample of adults aged 18 years and above (n = 10,247) was drawn from the Population Register using one- and two-stage stratified, random sampling.
note: The quote gives the sample invited, not participants, so participants is null. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03650127 says FinHealth 2017 'involved more than 7,000 Finns from around the country' (a lower bound, not recorded). The example study (PMID:38413574) lists 'FinHealth (N = 10,049)' for its GWAS, which cannot be reconciled with the sample drawn. PMID:34784307 reports a 58% participation rate for the health examination; several papers analysed 5,587 or 5094 health-examination participants. The THL methods report (julkari.fi, blocked by a bot check) should give the numbers of questionnaire respondents and health-examination participants.

label: FinnTwin12 Cohort
counts: twins who completed the baseline survey at age 12 (parents not counted)
quote: This represents 61.3% of the individuals who completed the young adulthood survey (Mage = 22 years) and 40.2% of the individuals who completed the baseline survey at age 12 (N = 5,184).
note: Age-37 follow-up paper (PMID:39920525). The same paper says 'A total of 2,724 families (87% of those identified) returned this questionnaire' at baseline, with an intensively studied sub-sample 'targeting 1,035 families'; 2,085 individuals completed the age-37 survey. The 2019 updated review (PMID:31640839) gives no exact baseline count in the text matched. The count covers twins only; biological parents also took part.

label: Finnish Twin Study on Aging
counts: women (103 MZ and 114 DZ twin pairs) examined at baseline, 2000-2001
quote: The final sample included 114 DZ and 103 MZ twin pairs (434 individuals) aged 63–76 years.
note: PMID:36682031: an invitation was sent to 414 female twin pairs; the final sample was 434 individuals, examined 2000-2001. PMID:18350156 gives the same pairs ('total n = 434 subjects'). PMID:36682031 analysed N = 395 with DNA methylation data.

label: Follow-up of Ovarian Cancer Genetic Association and Interaction Studies
counts: cases and controls in the 2017 OCAC OncoArray analysis (FOCI-OncoArray)
quote: The analyses included 66,450 samples from seven genotyping projects: 40,941 controls, 22,406 invasive cases and 3,103 borderline cases.
note: Phelan et al. 2017 (PMID:28346442), which the example study (PMID:40973091) cites as the FOCI-OncoArray dataset and whose OncoArray genotyping was funded by the FOCI grant U19-CA148112; its abstract says 'we pooled data from multiple genome-wide genotyping projects totaling 25,509 EOC cases and 40,941 controls'. Other FOCI analyses are smaller: the 2013 GWAS meta-analysis with iCOGS follow-up (PMID:23535730, also funded under U19-CA148112) genotyped 18,174 cases and 26,134 controls; a 2013 survival analysis (PMID:23382860) used 'approximately 2,600 cases in the FOCI collaboration'. The dbGaP record (phs001133) gives no sample counts. FOCI is a programme rather than a fixed sample, so this is the pooled number of its largest susceptibility analysis.

label: Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study
counts: people deeply phenotyped at baseline (patients, at-risk and healthy controls)
quote: All human subjects (n = 2500) have been deeply phenotyped (see Table 2) and are followed up after 2 years.
note: FOR2107 consortium design paper (Kircher et al. 2019, PMID:30267149); its abstract says 'A human cohort of MP patients, healthy subjects at genetic and/or environmental risk, and control subjects (N = 2500) has been established', and it lists the round sample breakdown (700 MDD, 300 BD, 200 SZ, 100 SZA, 500 at risk, 1000 healthy), so 2500 may partly be the recruitment target. Later analysed subsets: 1683 MACS participants with structural and resting-state MRI (PMID:38036604), 1789 FOR2107 participants with genotype and resilience data in the example study (PMID:39112778), 796 in PMID:42598116. No later source read states the final achieved baseline total.

label: Genes and Blood Clotting Study
counts: healthy individuals recruited in 507 sibships
quote: A total of 1189 healthy individuals (ages 14-35) representing 507 sibships (with 2-6 siblings per family) from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, were recruited between June 26, 2006, and January 30, 2009.
note: PMID:40756183. The same 1189 in 507 sibships is given in PMID:25208887. After genotyping QC, 1152 individuals in 502 sibships remained (PMID:23267103, PMID:40756183); the dbGaP release (phs000304.v3.p1) holds 1151 individuals in 503 sibships (PMID:40071514).

label: Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium
counts: cases and controls in the GAPC Immunochip dataset of the 2012 meta-analysis
note: Supplementary Table 1 of Tsoi et al. 2012 (PMID:23143594); the main text states 'the Genetic Analysis of Psoriasis Consortium (GAPC: 2,997 cases and 9,183 controls)'. The consortium's earlier GWAS with WTCCC2 (PMID:20953190) studied '2,622 individuals with psoriasis and 5,667 controls' (2,178 cases and 5,175 controls after QC), with replication sets of 10,060 individuals pre-QC; the GAPC Immunochip samples overlapped those replication sets. Controls came partly from national control collections (e.g. 4822 WTCCC2 controls for the UK). The consortium reports no single pooled total of its own collections, so this is its Immunochip case-control dataset.

label: Ghana Breast Health Study
counts: women enrolled 2013-2015: suspected-breast-cancer cases and population controls
quote: We therefore conducted a population-based case-control study in Accra and Kumasi, Ghana, enrolling 2,202 women with lesions suspicious for breast cancer and 2,161 population controls.
note: Design paper (Brinton et al. 2017, PMID:28295287) states cases and controls separately but no combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. 'Cases' are women with lesions suspicious for breast cancer, of whom 54.5% were diagnosed with malignancies. The control-recruitment paper (PMID:30990841) says '2,106 were enrolled' as controls out of 2,528 sampled; the later analysis PMID:38082317 used 1071 invasive cases and 2096 controls.

label: GenomALC
counts: cases and drinking controls of the GenomALC case-control study (GenomALC-1)
quote: We conducted a multicenter case-control study (GenomALC) comparing 1,293 cases (with alcohol-related cirrhosis, 75.6% male) and 754 controls (with equivalent alcohol exposure but no evidence of liver disease, 73.6% male).
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:32868629 (full text not read). No combined total is stated, so participants is left null. Other numbers: the 2015 design paper (PMID:25872595) aimed at 5,000 participants and had recruited 859 by September 2014; the risk-score paper PMID:34656649 analysed 'GenomALC-1: n = 1,690, GenomALC-2: n = 3,037' (genotyped subsets); the example study (PMID:38727677) used 2432 cases and 605 controls from GenomALC-2 after removing overlaps, and 1128 cases and 999 controls in the combined GenomALC-1 plus LNG GWAS.

label: Melanoma Genetics Consortium
counts: melanoma cases and study-specific controls in the discovery phase of the 2011 GenoMEL GWAS
quote: Our discovery phase included 2,981 individuals with melanoma and 1,982 study-specific control individuals of European ancestry, as well as an additional 6,426 control subjects from French or British populations, all of whom were genotyped for 317,000 or 610,000 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs).
note: Flagship GWAS of the consortium (Barrett et al. 2011). No pooled total is stated, so participants is left null; 'controls' counts only the GenoMEL study-specific controls, with a further 6,426 French or British population controls. After QC the analysis used 2,804 cases and 1,835 GenoMEL controls plus 5,783 French and WTCCC controls; replication added 1,579 cases and 2,036 controls. A family-based GenoMEL analysis (PMID:20876876) included 815 CDKN2A mutation carriers from 186 families at 15 centres. The genomel.org pages read give no participant or family totals. The example study (PMID:34813871) had no readable text in the cache.

label: GENetics of SEPsis-induced ARDS Network
counts: sepsis patients in the 2025 ARDS GWAS (analysed subset; 304 with ARDS, 501 without)
quote: We included a total of 805 patients from the GEN-SEP cohort (304 ARDS cases and 501 at-risk controls), 740 patients from SepNet (91 ARDS cases and 649 at-risk controls), and 3570 patients from UKBB (321 ARDS cases and 3249 at-risk controls).
note: The example study (PMID:41033104) says 'All individuals from the GEN-SEP and SepNet cohorts were considered in the analyses', so 805 is the largest genotyped GEN-SEP set read, but no source states the total number of patients ever recruited. Earlier: the 2022 sepsis-survival GWAS (PMID:36335405) used 475 patients from the 1st period (2002-2015) and 212 from the 2nd period (2016-2019), 687 in all; the 2018 ARDS study (PMID:29987654) studied 429 patients with severe sepsis. Cases are sepsis patients who developed ARDS and controls are sepsis patients who did not.

label: Genetics of Early Onset Stroke Study
counts: GEOS participants: first ischaemic stroke cases and stroke-free controls
quote: Characteristics of the 1737 GEOS study participants (830 cases - 43% African-American and 907 controls - 39% African-American) are summarized in Table 1.
note: PMID:23459313 (ATP1A2 and migraine analysis of GEOS). The GEOS GWAS (PMID:22384361, Europe PMC abstract) genotyped 'a biracial population of 889 IS cases and 927 controls, ages 15-49 years'; the 2022 early-onset stroke meta-analysis supplement lists GEOS with 843 cases and 881 controls; the OC study (PMID:38094903) used a subset of 332 premenopausal women. No source read states the total number enrolled across the four recruitment periods (1992-2008), so the figure is the largest stated total of genotyped participants.

label: Genetics of Osteoarthritis Consortium
counts: individuals in the 2025 GO 2.0 GWAS meta-analysis (osteoarthritis cases and controls)
quote: Here we conducted a large-scale GWAS meta-analysis across 1,962,069 individuals, achieving a 2.64-fold increase in effective sample size compared with the next largest GWAS3.
note: Hatzikotoulas et al. 2025 (Nature), the consortium's second meta-analysis (GO 2.0, 87 datasets); same page: 'Here we perform a genome-wide association study meta-analyses across up to 489,975 cases and 1,472,094 controls'. The first GO meta-analysis (Boer et al. 2021, PMID:34450027) covered '826,690 individuals (177,517 with osteoarthritis)'. The consortium website pages read give no pooled total.

label: Genetics of Childhood Cancer Treatment
counts: subjects in the GO-CAT clinical dataset
quote: In summary, of the 971 subjects in the clinical dataset of GO-CAT, a total of 591 subjects met the clinical inclusion criteria, of whom 360 subjects had genetic material available for genotyping.
note: Hurkmans et al. 2022 (PMID:36699085), the only source. Of the 971, 591 met the ototoxicity-study criteria, 360 had DNA and 261 remained after QC for the GWAS (the abstract's 'GO-CAT cohort (n = 261)'); genotyping QC was done in a larger set of 848 paediatric oncology subjects. The 971 is the GO-CAT clinical dataset used for this platinum ototoxicity study, not necessarily every patient in the consortium's osteosarcoma and brain-tumour cohorts.

label: Genetic Origin of Dupuytren Disease and Associated Fibromatosis study
counts: Dupuytren disease case subjects from GODDAF in the 2017 GWAS
quote: The Dutch cohort consisted of 2,195 case subjects from the GODDAF Study and 1,983 control subjects from the Lifelines cohort study.
note: Ng et al. 2017 (PMID:28886342). GODDAF is a case-only collection; the 1,983 Lifelines controls are from another cohort and are not counted. Sources disagree: a 2023 study of the same Groningen collection (PMID:37257093, ethics 2007/067) says 'phenotype and genotype data of total of 1669 DD patients were collected between 2007 and 2016'; a 2019 recurrence study (PMID:30688894) analysed 1730 GODDAF individuals. The largest stated count is given; no design paper states the final number recruited.

label: Genetics of Impulsivity project
counts: young adults assessed in the laboratory battery at the two sites
quote: Participants were 1252 young adults (62% female) with low levels of addictive behavior who were assessed in individual laboratory rooms at the University of Chicago and the University of Georgia.
note: MacKillop et al. 2016 (PMID:27449350), the phenotypic paper of the full sample; 426 (34%) came from the Georgia undergraduate research pool. The genetic analyses used subsets of European ancestry: 1,000 with valid genotypes and 983 analysed (PMID:29120849); 934 Caucasian-ancestry participants in the example study (PMID:37582857).

label: Genetics of Latinos Diabetic Retinopathy
counts: Latinos with type 2 diabetes and readable retinal images (diabetic subset)
quote: We evaluated such a group in search of novel factors that might signal protection from DR, using a large cohort of Latinos with type 2 DM and readable retinal images in the GOLDR study (n=614).
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of a 2020 Endocrine Society meeting abstract (SUN-686, J Endocr Soc, PMC7208167), fetched through a Europe PMC search. The definition source PMID:25452868 says 'In total, there were 585 type 2 diabetic participants from 212 families' used in its analysis, after removing relatives found non-diabetic; PMID:22330960 recruited 473 Hispanic type 2 diabetic subjects from October 2007 to December 2010. No source read states the total enrolled, including the non-diabetic siblings and parents, so these are diabetic subsets.

label: Global Parkinson's Genetics Program
counts: PD cases and controls across nine ancestries in a 2026 GP2 analysis
quote: Using genotyping, imputed, and whole-genome sequencing data from 36,127 PD cases and 19,475 controls across nine ancestral populations from the Global Parkinson's Genetics Program, we aimed to identify novel regions of homozygosity contributing to PD heritability.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:41808632 (runs of homozygosity study, 2026). GP2 is an ongoing programme with successive data releases, and no source read states a pooled total, so participants is left null. Its launch paper (PMID:33513272) planned to 'generate dense genetic data in more than 150,000 participants' and whole-genome sequences for more than 10,000 (a target, not achieved). Other GP2 analyses: 28,710 PD cases, 9,614 other neurodegenerative cases and 15,821 controls (PMID:41988218); 33,733 cases and 18,703 controls (PMID:41331295). The example study (PMID:37633302) included 197,918 individuals (1488 cases, 196,430 controls), but most controls came from 23andMe rather than GP2. gp2.org blocked the request (Cloudflare 403); its data-release pages would give the current total.

label: Genomic Research on Asthma in the African Diaspora
counts: African American asthma cases and non-asthmatic controls in the GRAAD GWAS (after QC)
quote: We performed a genome-wide association study in 2 independent populations of African ancestry (935 African American asthmatic cases and control subjects from the Baltimore-Washington, DC, area and 929 African Caribbean asthmatic subjects and their family members from Barbados) to identify single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) associated with asthma.
note: Mathias et al. 2010 GWAS (PMID:19910028); the Barbados families are a separate population, not GRAAD. The full text gives the split: 'resulting in a total of 464 asthma cases and 471 non-asthmatic controls', from 994 GRAAD samples whose genotypes were released. The constituent studies are larger (e.g. BASS 539, REACH 387 African Americans), but no source read states a GRAAD-wide total beyond the genotyped sample. In CAAPA (PMID:30787307) the GRAAD sample appears as GRAAD(1) and GRAAD(2) rows.

label: Genomic Research in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency and Sarcoidosis Study
counts: sarcoidosis patients recruited (sarcoidosis arm only; alpha-1 arm not counted)
quote: GRADS recruited 368 patients with sarcoidosis from 9 sarcoidosis centers across the United States [27].
note: Hoth et al. 2022 (PMID:35806883). The sarcoidosis design paper (PMID:26193069) aimed to 'enroll 400 participants'. No source read states how many PiZZ/PiMZ alpha-1 participants were enrolled, so the whole-study total is unknown; the alpha-1 design paper (PMID:26153726) gives no target in the sentences read. Other GRADS subsets: 320 with chest CT radiomics (PMID:41708686), 215 with BAL RNA-seq (PMID:34083402).

label: Genomics of Resistance to Immunodeficiency Virus
counts: HIV-1-infected French individuals of European descent: long-term non-progressors and rapid progressors
quote: The GRIV cohort comprised 275 LTNP and 86 RP French HIV-1 seropositive individuals of Caucasian descent.
note: PMID:21750674 gives the two groups separately (275 long-term non-progressors, 86 rapid progressors) but no combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed; its 697 seronegative controls come from the D.E.S.I.R. programme and are not GRIV members. Other numbers: the NP group of 270 in PMID:26367535; 250 GRIV LTNPs with documented viral load, 50 of them elite controllers (PMID:38146367). Neither case nor control fields apply, since GRIV's comparison groups are both HIV-infected and its controls are external.

label: Guangzhou Twin Eye Study
counts: 1291 twin pairs enrolled 2006-2018 (stated in pairs, not individuals)
quote: At present, there are 1291 sets of twins enrolled, and 11 year’s follow-up visits were completed in 2018 (Table 1).
note: 2019 cohort update (PMID:32014069; abstract: 'approximately 1300 pairs of twins, aged 7-15 years, were enrolled at baseline'). The enrolment is stated as twin pairs, and parents and siblings were also enrolled, so no individual count is stated; participants is left null rather than doubled. Other numbers: 1,221 twin pairs participated 2006-2012 and a GWAS scan was done for 'more than 3,000 participants (including twins and their parents or siblings)' (PMID:23186635); 2259 twin children were analysed in PMID:41117591 (analysed subset); the parent Guangzhou Twin Registry lists over 9,700 twin pairs (PMID:17254403).

label: Guangzhou cohort
counts: high myopes and hyperopes of the Guangzhou (GZ) cohort in the 2023 axial-length GWAS
quote: A genome-wide association study meta-analysis was conducted in totalling 2644 Chinese individuals from 3 cohorts: the Guangzhou cohort (GZ, 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes), Wenzhou cohort (334 high myopes and 6 hyperopes) and Guangzhou Twin Eye Study (1051 participants with normally distributed AL).
needs: PMID:37524447 full text (Br J Ophthalmol, doi:10.1136/bjo-2023-323596; only the abstract and publisher landing page were readable)
note: The only source (Han et al., PMID:37524447) gives the Guangzhou cohort as 537 high myopes and 151 hyperopes, with no combined total, so participants is left null rather than summed. The extreme-phenotype groups are not a case-control split, so the case and control fields are left empty. The closed full text may state the cohort total and its recruitment.

label: Guangzhou Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls from the four Guangzhou collections contributed to the 2014 Asia CRC Consortium GWAS
quote: The four Guangzhou studies contributed a total of 3,197 cases and 3,424 controls to this project.
note: No source read states a single participant total for the study, so participants is left null; cases and controls are the numbers the four collections contributed to the 2014 GWAS (PMID:24836286 supplement), which may be a subset of everyone recruited. The same supplement gives per-collection sizes: Guangzhou-1 (n = 1,603), Guangzhou-2 (n = 809), Guangzhou-3 (n = 2,408), Guangzhou-4 (n = 1,791); the 2012 GWAS (PMID:23263487) gave Guangzhou-1 n = 1,613, Guangzhou-2 n = 2,892 and Guangzhou-3 n = 2,638. The recruitment papers cited as refs 1 and 7 of the supplement would give the full recruited numbers.

label: Hemophilia Growth and Development Study
counts: boys and young men with hemophilia enrolled (siblings not counted)
quote: A total of 333 children and adolescents were enrolled.
note: The baseline design paper (PMID:8498644) agrees: 'Sixty-nine percent (n = 333) of a population of males between the ages of 6 and 19 years with moderate to severe hemophilia participated in a comprehensive baseline examination.' The sibling comparison group is extra: PMID:11075607 reports 'HIV-positive hemophiliacs (n = 207), HIV-negative hemophiliacs (n = 126), and their siblings (n = 47)'. No source read states a total including siblings.

label: Hordaland Health Study
counts: residents who took part in HUSK1 (1992/93) and/or HUSK2 (1997/99), approximate
quote: Approximately 36,000 residents of Hordaland county participated in the studies, ca. 18,000 in 1992/93 and ca. 26,000 in 1997/99.
note: Approximate figure from the study website; the Norwegian site (http://husk.w.uib.no) gives the same waves: 'Det deltok ca. 18000 personer født 1925-52.' (HUSK1) and 'Da deltok ca. 26000 personer.' (HUSK2), with 'Omtrent 7000 av de som deltok i HUSK1 deltok også i HUSK2.' No number is given for HUSK3 (from 2018). The example study (PMID:38671141) gives no HUSK participant count.

label: Hong Kong Children Eye Study
counts: children and parents examined in 5708 complete child-parent trios (trio subset)
quote: A total of 17 124 participants from 5708 trios (2964 boys and 2754 girls) at a mean (SD) age of 7.32 (0.87) years, and 11 416 parents were examined.
note: The study is ongoing and no source read gives the whole cohort's enrolment. Counts seen: 2020 (PMID:31981300) 'A total of 4257 children aged 6-8 years, and 5880 parents were recruited in the Hong Kong Children Eye Study.'; 2021 (PMID:34226578) 'A total of 4273 children (2236 boys and 2037 girls) responded to the invitation and completed ophthalmological examinations.'; 2023 (PMID:36542383) 5708 trios, the number recorded, which counts only complete trios. A 2025 paper by the same group (PMID:40111372, abstract) reports 'The cohort consisted of 21 655 children' examined 2015-2023, but its abstract does not name the HKCES and its full text was not available to confirm it. A cohort profile or a recent paper stating total HKCES enrolment would settle it.

label: Hong Kong Diabetes Biobank
counts: people with diabetes enrolled 2014-2019 (stated as 'more than 20,000', a lower bound)
quote: Over the period from 2014 to 2019, the study consecutively enrolled more than 20,000 individuals with diabetes.
note: The number is a lower bound ('more than 20,000'), not an exact count. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05282680 (fetched, status active, not recruiting) gives an estimated enrolment of 48000 as a structured field, not a sentence, so it is not recorded. Subsets seen: PMID:32722720 'A total of 6,914 unrelated patients from HKDB were genotyped.'; PMID:37125963 used 4,055 HKDB phase 1 and 1,079 cases plus 2,474 controls from phase 2. A cohort profile stating the achieved enrolment would settle it.

label: Healthy Zhejiang One Million People Cohort
counts: participants recruited June 2021 to July 2024 (stated as 'over 100,000', a lower bound)
quote: It has recruited over 100,000 participants from June 2021 to July 2024.
note: The number is a lower bound ('over 100,000') for an ongoing cohort whose target is one million. Subsets seen: PMID:40728933 whole-genome sequenced 10,763 participants; PMID:42324270 enrolled 1493 (analysed 1401) at one project site between January 2022 and June 2023. A cohort profile would give the exact achieved enrolment.

label: Health and Prevention Enhancement
counts: health examinees with a check-up October 2003 to December 2014
quote: The H-PEACE study collected data from 91 336 Koreans aged 45.5±11.7 years (50 507 men and 40 829 women) who received a health check-up between October 2003 and December 2014 at the SNUH Gangnam Center (IRB no.
note: From the cohort profile; its abstract agrees: 'A total of 91 336 health examinees were included in the cohort'. Its GENIE subcohort has 17 455 members with blood samples, 6579 of them genotyped. The example study (PMID:38320993) genotyped 7999 H-PEACE participants.

label: Initiative on Nephropathy, of relevance to public health, which is Chronic, possibly in its Initial stages, and carries a Potential risk of major clinical End-points
counts: adults enrolled in 2006 (62% of the 6200 randomly selected)
quote: Results In the INCIPE study, 3870 (62% of the randomized sample) subjects were enrolled.
note: From the design paper (PMID:20813860): 6200 patients were randomly selected and 3870 enrolled; its analysis used 3629 with complete data. PMID:21711121 analysed 3,757 participants; PMID:36865011 genotyped 3046 (INCIPE-1 893 and INCIPE-2 2153). The example study (PMID:35331647) was not readable (no full text on disk).

label: International Stuttering Project
counts: clinically ascertained people who stutter in the collection used for the 2022 GWAS
quote: The ISP comprises 1,345 clinically ascertained developmental stuttering cases collected from the Curtin Stuttering Treatment Clinic in Perth, Australia; the SpeechMatters Clinic and the Irish Stammering Association, in Dublin, Ireland; the National Stuttering Association, USA; online recruitment on reddit.com; and Dr.
note: The collection recruits continually, so this is the size at the 2022 GWAS (PMID:35047858); the 6,759 matched controls in that study came from the Vanderbilt BioVU biobank, not from the ISP, so they are not counted. The project website states no number.

label: INTERHEART study
counts: cases of first acute myocardial infarction and controls enrolled 1999-2003
quote: 15152 cases and 14820 controls were enrolled.
note: The main INTERHEART paper's abstract gives cases and controls but no stated total, so participants is left null rather than summed. Other counts seen: the psychosocial paper (PMID:15364186) used '11119 patients with a first myocardial infarction and 13648 age-matched' controls, 24767 people; PMID:37414411 describes 'a standardized case–control study involving 11 931 cases of first acute MI and 14 260 controls'. The Lancet full text of PMID:15364185 (closed, not on disk) may state a total.

label: International Tuberculosis Host Genetics Consortium
counts: pulmonary TB cases and healthy controls in the 12 GWAS of the 2024 multi-ancestry meta-analysis
quote: The ITHGC includes 12 case–control GWAS from nine countries in Europe, Africa, and Asia (total of 14,153 pulmonary TB cases and 19,536 healthy controls).
note: Consortium; the flagship meta-analysis pooled 12 case-control GWAS. No sentence states a single total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null rather than summed.

label: Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis cohort
counts: unrelated volunteers analysed in the 2017 head-hair shape GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: US sample consists of 743 unrelated volunteers (498 females, 245 males) recruited in the USA, who were of European (98%), and non-European ancestry (2% South American/South Asian/Middle Eastern).
note: PMID:29220522 calls this the 'US study' and gives it the IUPUI ethics protocol (Indiana University protocol 1409306349) and National Institute of Justice funding, so it is this collection, but 743 is the unrelated subset analysed in 2017, not the whole collection. The facial-shape papers (PMID:33288918, PMID:33692830, PMID:39622794) pool IUPUI with 3DFN and PSU into a US dataset of 4,680 and do not give IUPUI's own number. No source read gives the whole collection's size.

label: International Warfarin Pharmacogenetics Consortium
counts: warfarin-treated patients pooled for the 2009 dosing-algorithm analysis
quote: The research groups contributed clinical and genetic data for a total of 5700 patients who were treated with warfarin.
note: Consortium; flagship analysis is the 2009 pharmacogenetic dosing algorithm (PMID:19228618), which used 4043 patients for derivation and 1009 for validation. The pooled dataset was later expanded: PMID:20203262 'The IWPC dataset was expanded to include 6256 chronic warfarin users'. The African-American GWAS (PMID:23755828) had 533 discovery and 432 replication participants.

label: Karolinska Breast Cancer Study
counts: cases and controls contributed to the BCAC COGS genotyping (table row: controls, cases, ER+, ER-)
quote: Karolinska Breast Cancer Study (KARBAC) Sweden 662 722 338 63
note: The quote is a row of Table 1 of PMID:24943594 (columns Controls, Cases, ER+, ER−), not a sentence; no source read states a total, so participants is left null. Other counts: the hospital-series design paper (PMID:15345109) says 'All incident breast cancer patients treated surgically in a 19-month period were eligible for the study and 70% (489/696) participated.'; the example study (PMID:35267517) used 'KARBAC (n = 503)' cases, 'KARBAC1 (n = 394)' consecutive cases recruited 1998-2000 and 'KARBAC2 (n = 109)' BRCA-negative familial cases recruited 2000-2012, with controls from KARMA rather than KARBAC.

label: Korea National Cancer Center gastric cancer case-control study
counts: participants (cases and controls) enrolled March 2011 to December 2014
quote: Of these initial 1,727 participants who were enrolled in this study, 56 individuals with an incomplete semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQFFQ) and 15 individuals with an implausible total energy intake (< 500 or > 4,000 kcal/day) were excluded.
note: From PMID:33634021, which does not split the 1,727 enrolled into cases and controls; after exclusions and 1:2 matching it analysed 1,245 (415 cases and 830 controls). The example GWAS (PMID:37340842): 'From NCC, 450 GC cases and 1,134 healthy controls were sequenced using an Axiom Exome 319 chip'. PMID:38810984 analysed 377 cases and 756 controls with genotype data. It is not certain that 1,727 is everyone recruited rather than those with genotype data; the recruitment description cited as 'outlined elsewhere' in PMID:38810984 would settle it.

label: Korea-NCC (National Cancer Center) Colorectal Cancer Study
counts: CRC patients who agreed to take part (Aug 2010 to Sep 2020) and health check-up controls, before exclusions
quote: Of the 1,780 patients who agreed to participate in this study, 290 participants were excluded due to incomplete data from the semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire (SQFFQ) or general questionnaire, and 13 others were excluded due to implausible energy intake (< 500 or > 4,000 kcal/day).
note: Both numbers are from PMID:38514198; the controls come from the next sentence of the same text: 'Of the 18,471 controls, 5,409 participants with incomplete SQFFQ or general questionnaire data and 196 others with implausible energy intake (< 500 or > 4,000 kcal/day) were excluded.' No total is stated, so participants is left null. That paper analysed 1,420 cases and 2,840 matched controls. The example study (PMID:35765848) used a Korea-NCC validation set of 622 cases and 832 controls; the 2014 ACCC GWAS supplement lists Korea-NCC with 1,392 cases and 1,329 controls.

label: Low Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression Study
counts: children randomised in phase 1 (2016-2017)
quote: ParticipantsA total of 438 children aged 4 to 12 years with myopia of at least -1.0 diopter (D) and astigmatism of -2.5 D or less.
note: From the abstract of the trial's design and primary-results paper (PMID:30514630); the quote carries the abstract's run-together 'Participants' heading as the text gives it. The example GWAS (PMID:40410244) used 373 LAMP children; the 3-year gamma-zone substudy (PMID:41732593) included 238 children at baseline.

label: Leipzig Childhood Obesity cohort
counts: patients in the cohort as rescreened for a genetic study (2022)
quote: As the type of mutation escapes standard genetic screening algorithms, we rescreened the Leipzig Childhood Obesity cohort of 1,745 patients and identified four additional patients with the identical mutation, ectopic ASIP expression and a similar phenotype.
note: Quote from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:36536132 (fetched in this session); it may count only patients with DNA available for screening. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04491344 (fetched) gives an estimated enrolment of 3000 as a structured field, not a sentence. The definition sources give only subsets: PMID:41168416 adulthood follow-up of N = 209; PMID:37465325 pooled it with LIFE Child. The example study (PMID:34059833) does not name the cohort in its cached text.

label: Lung Oncology Research & Discovery
counts: genotyped lung cancer surgery patients of European descent passing QC (analysed subset)
quote: After the QC filters, 4002 cases of European descent confirmed at genotyping were available for subsequent analyses.
note: Case-only cohort of patients operated on 1999-2021. No source read states the total number of patients in LORD; 4002 is the genotyped, QC-passed subset used in the PRS study (PMID:38970920), with its 20,010 controls taken from CARTaGENE, not LORD. The tumour-sequencing study (PMID:40209611) used 1,603 adenocarcinoma patients. A description of the whole LORD collection would settle it.

label: Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study
counts: men enrolled across all enrolment waves
quote: A total of 6,972 men have been enrolled.
note: From the cohort description in the supplement of the example study (PMID:37532928, 2023), which does not say the date of the count. The 1987 design paper (PMID:3300281) reports the first wave: 'Nearly 5,000 homosexual men volunteered for semiannual interview, physical examination, and laboratory testing in four metropolitan areas.' The MWCCS paper (PMID:33675224) describes enrolment waves in 1984-1985, 1987-1990, 2001-2003 and 2010-2017 but gives no MACS total; it reports 1,901 men at 2018-2019 visits. A MACS cohort profile with the cumulative enrolment would confirm it.

label: Manchester Lung Health Check
counts: attendees of the 2016 pilot Lung Health Checks
quote: Out of 2541 attendees, 56% were high-risk (n=1430/2541) and offered screening; 44% were low-risk (n=1111/2541) and not screened.
note: Number is for the 2016 pilot only (ever-smokers aged 55-74 at 14 practices); the same paper says 26% of 9926 invited ever-smokers participated, and the pilot's baseline paper (PMID:29440588, abstract) gives 'n=1893/2541' in the lowest deprivation quintile and 1384 screened. The second round (PMID:30420406) scanned 1194 of 1323 eligible. No source read gives the size of the later, expanded programmes; the example study (PMID:37154150) used 550 high-risk cancer-free participants.

label: Mayo Vascular Disease Biorepository
counts: patients consented up to December 2012
quote: Up to December 2012, 8800 patients referred for vascular ultrasound examination and non-invasive lower extremity arterial evaluation were approached, of whom 5268 consented.
note: From the biorepository's design paper; the same paper describes 'the initial 2182 patients recruited' in detail. Enrolment continued to 24 July 2020 (PMID:33287626; example study PMID:37845353 supplement), so the final size is larger, but no source read states it; a later Mayo VDB description with a total enrolment would settle it.

label: Manchester Cancer Research Centre Biobank
note: The MCRC Biobank pages (about, landing, information for patients, accessing) and the HRA research summary were read; none states the number of donors or samples. A Europe PMC search for the biobank's name found only papers using its samples, no profile paper. The example study (PMID:37154150, Genet Med) is not on disk in full text and would in any case give only its analysed lung cancer surgical patients. A biobank annual report or profile giving donor numbers would settle it.

label: MELARISK study
counts: European-ancestry melanoma cases recruited 1992-2011
quote: The MELARISK study comprised of 1,244 European-ancestry melanoma cases who were recruited through a nationwide network of French Dermatology Departments and Oncogenetic clinics between 1992 and 2011.
note: MELARISK recruited cases only; its GWAS controls came from other French population studies. PMID:25892537 says 'The discovery dataset comprised of 1,244 CM cases from the MELARISK study and 3,144 population-based controls' (3,976 subjects, 1,179 cases and 2,797 controls after QC). PMID:27347659 kept 966 cases after QC; the example study (PMID:32341527 supplement) lists 'MELARISK (535 cases)' for its GenoMEL contribution. The 1,244 counts genotyped GWAS cases; the full clinical collection may be larger, but no source read gives it.

label: Multicenter Hemophilia Cohort Studies
counts: subjects in the first study (MHCS-I) only, as of 1989
quote: We evaluated a multicenter cohort of 1219 subjects with hemophilia or related disorders prospectively, focusing on 319 subjects with documented dates of seroconversion to human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1).
note: The term covers MHCS-I and MHCS-II; this number is MHCS-I only, from its 1989 NEJM abstract (Europe PMC). A 1997 MHCS paper (PMID:9342256, abstract) studied 'a cohort of 1253 patients with hemophilia', so MHCS-I enrolment grew beyond 1219. For MHCS-II, PMID:20337924 gives only its analysed subset ('The study included 1,266 persons with hemophilia' who were HCV-viraemic and interferon-naive) and PMID:16204310 (abstract) 712 HCV-seropositive subjects in another analysis; no source read states MHCS-II's total enrolment or a combined total. The MHCS-II design papers (refs 4-5 of PMID:20337924) would settle it.

label: Myeloma XI trial
counts: newly diagnosed patients recruited across both pathways
quote: Across two pathways, for TE and TNE patients, 4420 newly diagnosed, symptomatic, patients with myeloma were recruited.
note: Quote from a Myeloma XI report (PMID:36541152, vorinostat maintenance). The definition source (PMID:30559051) gives the maintenance randomisation only: 1971 patients accrued between Jan 2011 and Aug 2017 (its abstract misprints 1917), and says 1512 patients had been accrued before the June 2013 protocol amendment.

label: MRC Myeloma IX trial
counts: patients enrolled May 2003 to November 2007
quote: 1970 patients were enrolled between May, 2003, and November, 2007, of whom 1960 were eligible for intention-to-treat analysis: 981 in the zoledronic acid group (555 on intensive chemotherapy, 426 on non-intensive chemotherapy); and 979 on clodronic acid (556 on intensive chemotherapy, 423 on non-intensive chemotherapy).
note: Main trial report; 1960 were eligible for intention-to-treat analysis. The example study (PMID:39103364) used 183 Myeloma IX patients' expression data.

label: Mexican Genomic Database for Addiction Research
counts: participants whose buccal DNA samples passed quality criteria
quote: The MxGDAR/Encodat database included 7171 of the 13,228 buccal epithelial samples collected (54.21%) that met the following quality criteria: i) 230/260 and 260/230 ratios > 1.8, ii) concentration > 50 ng/µL, and iii) no signs of DNA degradation.
note: The database holds 7171 samples, one per participant, drawn from 13,228 buccal samples collected in the second phase of Encodat 2016. The same paper genotyped a preliminary subsample of 1728 (1657 after QC). The example study (PMID:38714835) uses a MxGDAR-Encodat subsample without giving the database's size.

label: Nicotine Addiction Genetics Finland study
counts: individuals with interview, blood sample and consent
quote: Data from diagnostic interview, blood samples, and informed consent were available on 2188 individuals.
note: The sentence follows the description of NAG Finland recruitment in 2001-2005. PMID:24927283 analysed 1428 of them genetically; the GWAS in PMID:29532581 had 1715 individuals with both phenotype and genotype data from 739 families. No source read gives the number invited or recruited.

label: Netherlands Study of Cognition, Environment and Genes
counts: general-population sample (sample 1) only
quote: Sample 1 (S1, n = 837) was recruited through media advertisement or through the Science Live Program of the NEMO Science Center in Amsterdam (www.sciencelive.nl).
note: NESCOG has two samples; the same paper says 'Sample 2 (S2, n = 560; 330 females) was a general population-based family sample', and analysed 559 of sample 1. No source read states a total for the whole study, and the two are not summed here. The example study (PMID:36376304) does not name NESCOG in its cached text. A NESCOG design description (e.g. the Vinkhuyzen et al. 2010 paper cited for sample 2) might give the total.

label: UK Nephropathy Family Study and Oxford Regional Prospective Study
counts: analysed subset: ORPS and NFS participants with more than one HbA1c (84% of both cohorts)
quote: The study population consisted of 1,232 participants in the Oxford Regional Prospective Study (ORPS, n = 418) and Nephropathy Family Study (NFS, n = 814) with more than one A1C assessment, representing 84% of the whole cohorts.
note: No source read gives the combined size of the two cohorts; this is the analysed subset of the paper, which says it is 84% of them. The NFS alone recruited 1,066 young people (PMID:19918004, PMID:19171721). The example GWAS (PMID:27647854) gives only the four-study discovery total ('3135-5156 subjects with T1D, depending on phenotypic comparison'); its Table 1 and Supplemental Tables 2-3, which would give the NFS-ORPS contribution, are not in the cached text.

label: Nephropathy Family Study
counts: young people with type 1 diabetes recruited 2000-2005 (parents not counted)
quote: Between 2000 and 2005, 1,066 subjects, aged 10–16 years, who had developed type 1 diabetes before the age of 16 years, were recruited throughout four English regions (East Anglia, Birmingham, Bristol, and Oxford) for detailed phenotypic and genetic study of the early pathogenesis of microalbuminuria.
note: PMID:19171721 gives the same number ('A total of 1,066 subjects, aged 10–16 years'). Parents were also recruited, but no source read gives their number; ambulatory blood pressure was done in 509 children, 311 fathers and 444 mothers.

label: Nigerian Breast Cancer Study
counts: invasive breast cancer cases and controls recruited in Ibadan 1998-2009
quote: Between 1998 and 2009, 1,233 invasive breast cancer cases and 1,101 controls were recruited.
note: No source read states a total number of participants, so participants is left null and cases and controls are given as stated (Nigeria only, to 2009). Enrolment continued to 2018 and extended to Cameroon and Uganda (PMID:40249615), whose full text says 'There were 3054 participants in the present study with information on both genetic and nongenetic factors' and analysed 1686 (996 cases, 690 controls); PMID:30130155 says 'The study enrolled 1,136 cases and 997 controls (386 hospital based and 611 community based)' for its sequencing analysis. A recent profile giving the total enrolment to 2018 would settle it.

label: National Joint Registry
note: The registry counts procedures, not people: its About page (https://www.njrcentre.org.uk/about-the-njr/, fetched) says 'The largest national orthopaedic registry in the world – with currently over 4.6 million records' and 'Around 250k procedure records are usually submitted annually, with year-on-year growth.' No source read gives the number of patients. The example study (PMID:41912496) used a subset: 'the National Joint Registry cohort, which at the time included 5 411 adult individuals living in England who had undergone a hip replacement surgery for DDH.' The NJR annual report (reports.njrcentre.org.uk, a script-rendered site that returned no text) would give patient numbers.

label: National Psoriasis Victor Henschel BioBank
note: The NPF biobank page (cached) gives only a target: the biobank launched 'with the ambitious goal of securing 2000 samples in its first year'. PMID:26626624 says '1,526 PsA case subjects and 1,508 unaffected control subjects were recruited by four collection centers—Michigan, Toronto, Newfoundland, and the National Psoriasis Foundation', without the NPF share. PMID:32725812, PMID:23143594 (Europe PMC full text) and the example study (PMID:39885523) name the biobank without its size; the CARD14 paper PMID:22521419 was not retrievable as full text. An NPF report of total donors would settle it.

label: National Survey of Physical Traits
counts: volunteers recruited in Zhengzhou, Taizhou and Nanning
quote: Samples in the NSPT cohort included 3,557 Chinese individuals recruited as volunteers from three regional districts in China: Zhengzhou, Taizhou, and Nanning.
note: Sources disagree slightly: PMID:40118068 says 'In total, 3564 samples of Han Chinese participants were collected' (recruited 2015-2018); the most recent source (PMID:40938633, 2025) is preferred. Analysed subsets: 2,487 (PMID:37459304, ear GWAS), 2,679 (PMID:34995520, fingerprints), 3,451 (PMID:40938633, multi-omics).

label: New York Genome Center ALS Consortium
counts: donors whole-genome sequenced (4,746 passed QC)
quote: WGS was performed on 4,828 donors, with a final set of 4,746 passing quality control.
note: From the consortium's full-dataset preprint. It describes the dataset as 'WGS on 4,746 donors' (after QC), of whom 3,293 have classical ALS and 443 are non-neurological controls, and RNA-seq from 2,574 samples from 695 donors, all with matching WGS. The QC-passed 4,746 could equally be used; 4,828 counts every donor sequenced.

label: NZ AAA Genetics Study
counts: genotyped cases and controls, stated per genotyping set only
quote: All participants were genotyped in two separate case-control cohorts using the Affymetrix SNP6 (cohort 1; 608 AAA cases and 612 controls) or Illumina Omni2.5 (cohort 2; 397 cases and 384 controls) GeneChip arrays and had call rates >95% 27 (mean 99.2%).
note: From the example study's supplement (PMID:37845353). The numbers are given for the two genotyping sets separately (608 cases and 612 controls; 397 cases and 384 controls) and no total is stated, so participants, cases and controls are left null rather than summed. The definition source PMID:27899403 gives only consortium totals (Online Table I, not in the cached text, would give the New Zealand set).

label: Pancreatic Cancer Case-Control Consortium
counts: cases and controls genotyped in the PanC4 GWAS after QC (9 member studies)
quote: After quality control (Online Methods, Fig. 1, Supplementary Table 2), 7,956 individuals (4,164 cases and 3,792 controls) and 654,470 SNPs with call rates greater than 98% were analyzed.
note: Cohort aggregation; the number is the consortium's own genotyped sample (8052 genotyped from nine PanC4 studies before QC). Its largest pooled risk-factor analysis read here is the smoking analysis (PMID:22104574): '12 case-control studies ... including 6507 pancreatic cases and 12 890 controls', for which no total is stated; the early-onset analysis (PMID:26646264) pooled 8 studies with 1,954 cases and 3,278 controls.

label: UPenn Local TGCT Study
counts: TGCT cases and PennCATH male controls in the 2009 genome-wide scan
quote: We performed a genome-wide scan among 277 TGCT cases and 919 controls.
note: No source read states a total, so participants is left null. PMID:19483682 also says 'Male controls (n=932) were selected from PennCATH' (919 after QC). The TECAC meta-analysis (PMID:28604732) table lists the Penn study with 918 controls and 480 cases, but only as table cells. The dbGaP page (phs001307.v1.p1) gives only the recruitment goal: '550 TGCT cases and 1100 age, race and cell phone use matched controls'; its subject telemetry report would give the deposited numbers.

label: Phenotype, Genotype & Biomarkers in ALS and Related Disorders
counts: patients with ALS or a related disorder enrolled (primary participants)
quote: The PGB study enrolled 705 patients with ALS (n = 472), primary lateral sclerosis (n = 47), progressive muscular atrophy (n = 20), hereditary spastic paraplegia (n = 162) and other related disorders (n = 4).
note: The paper says patients were enrolled between 2014 and 2019 at 12 US centres and 1 in South Africa. The CReATe study page (https://create.rarediseasesnetwork.org/research-study/8001) planned approximately 700 patients and ~700 secondary participants (family members); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02327845 gives an actual enrollment count of 708 (structured field, not a sentence). Family members are not counted here.

label: PLATelet inhibition and patient Outcomes
counts: patients with acute coronary syndrome randomised
quote: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized trial, we compared ticagrelor (180-mg loading dose, 90 mg twice daily thereafter) and clopidogrel (300-to-600-mg loading dose, 75 mg daily thereafter) for the prevention of cardiovascular events in 18,624 patients admitted to the hospital with an acute coronary syndrome, with or without ST-segment elevation.
note: Main results paper (NEJM 2009), abstract read from Europe PMC. The design paper (PMID:19332184) planned '>18,000 patients'; the BMJ substudy (PMID:21685437) says '5216 (28%) of 18 624 patients' were planned for non-invasive management. Genetic and biomarker substudies used subsets.

label: Pustular Psoriasis, Elucidating Underlying Mechanisms
counts: patients with palmoplantar pustulosis enrolled through PLUM 2016-2020 (analysed subset only)
quote: The remaining 161 patients were enrolled between 2016 and 2020 through the sister research study Pustular Psoriasis, Elucidating Underlying Mechanisms (PLUM).
note: Only a subset: the palmoplantar pustulosis patients in this severity analysis (42 more came through APRICOT). PLUM also recruited people with other forms of pustular psoriasis, disease controls, healthy volunteers and relatives, and no source I read gives its total. The HRA research summary gives no number. PMID:30036598 reports 78 patients ascertained prospectively through APRICOT and PLUM combined. The PPP GWAS (PMID:38815935) was read only as an abstract; its full text is closed and the medRxiv version (PPR790159) had no full text in Europe PMC. A PLUM protocol or final report would settle the total.

label: Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics Study
counts: individuals of African descent recruited (cases, controls and glaucoma suspects)
quote: The Primary Open-Angle African American Glaucoma Genetics (POAAGG) study recruited 10,255 individuals of African descent from the Philadelphia area, representing the largest single-city study of POAG nationwide.
note: Most recent source (2025; recruitment July 2010 to August 2024). Earlier: the 2015 baseline paper (PMID:25576993) had 2520 recruited, of whom 2067 (807 controls, 1260 POAG cases) met all criteria; PMID:28705151 says the study exceeded its discovery-cohort target of 5500; the example GWAS (PMID:38242088) thanks coordinators for enrolling 'more than 10,200 individuals'. No source gives the current case/control split of the whole cohort.

label: Project MinE
counts: DNA profiles (whole genomes) collected by Project MinE: ALS cases and controls
quote: DNA Profiles Collected Project MinE data 11385 Cases 8,835 Controls 2,550
note: Counter on the project's home page (fetched 2026-09-25), which also lists 'Plus External data 18574 Cases 11,176 Controls 7,398'; not a prose sentence. The aggregation reports samples rather than a pooled analysis size. The design paper (PMID:29955173) targets at least 15 000 ALS patients and 7500 controls (the about page says the same) and reports a Dutch pilot of 1169 patients and 608 controls; the telomere study (PMID:36589292) had 6,580 whole genomes (6,195 after QC); the example exome study (PMID:41917433) used Project MinE discovery data of 7,614 cases and 2,605 controls and replication data of 1,510 cases and 169 controls. Groups from 16 countries take part.

label: Pulmonary Hypertension and the Hypoxic Response in Sickle Cell Disease
counts: children and adolescents with sickle cell anaemia (HbSS) recruited (HbSS subset only; controls and other genotypes excluded)
quote: A total of 381 participants were recruited from Howard University, Children’s National Medical Center, National Institutes of Health and the University of Michigan where they received care for SCD.
note: From PMID:21890147 (2012), whose analysis was restricted to HbSS patients of the PUSH cohort, so this is a subset. The design/first-results paper (PMID:19211639) says the study was 'prospectively designed to enroll 600 patients with sickle cell disease and 100 controls' and reports a mid-point analysis of 310 patients and 54 matched controls; PMID:19956689 reports 237 patients and 43 controls enrolled as of early 2008. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00495638 (NIH Clinical Center site only) gives 29 enrolled. No source read gives the final total enrolment; a final PUSH cohort description would settle it.

label: Queen Square Brain Bank for Neurological Disorders
counts: brain donors in the collection (no number read)
note: The HRA research tissue bank summary gives no number. The example study (PMID:38849413) analysed 308 pathologically confirmed PD cases from QSBB, a small subset. PMID:12784275 (cached abstract) states no collection size. The UCL QSBB pages (about page and main page) return HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch; a web-search summary claimed 2437 disease cases plus 286 controls (2723 in all), but I could not read that text, so it is not recorded. The UCL 'About Queen Square Brain Bank' page, read in a browser, would settle it.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study on Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis in Quebec
counts: first-phase (QUEBEC-CAVS-1) cases and controls passing QC; no stated total
quote: A GWAS on 1009 cases and 1017 ethnically matched controls was combined with a large-scale eQTL mapping study of human aortic valve tissues (n = 233) to identify susceptibility genes for CAVS.
note: Cases and controls of the first phase only (after QC); no source read states their total, so participants is left null. The second phase (QUEBEC-CAVS-2, controls from CARTaGENE) is in the 2024 meta-analysis (PMID:38494474), whose per-cohort counts are in its Supplementary Data 1, not read; that paper's QUEBEC-CAVS-RNA set has 500 aortic valves. PMID:31141105 repeats 1009 cases and 1017 controls. Supplementary Data 1 of PMID:38494474 would give both phases.

label: REDS-III Brazil Sickle Cell Disease Cohort
counts: people with sickle cell disease enrolled at six Brazilian sites
quote: A total of 2795 participants at six Brazilian sites were enrolled between 2013 and 2015.
note: Cohort design/baseline paper (recruitment goal 3000). The example stroke GWAS (PMID:36602125) says 2,793 individuals were enrolled in the REDS-III Brazil SCD Cohort, of whom 1,333 were analysed.

label: Raine Eye Health Study
counts: Raine Study Generation 2 participants given the eye assessment at the 20-year follow-up
quote: A total of 1344 participants (51.3% male) were assessed over a 24-month period.
note: Design paper of the Raine Eye Health Study (abstract read). The example exome-array meta-analysis (PMID:36596879) used 1,020 REHS individuals after QC.

label: Racial Variability in Genotypic Determinants of Breast Cancer Risk Study
counts: African-ancestry cases and controls included in the ROOT consortium after QC (analysed subset); no stated total
quote: After quality control, we included 143 cases and 254 controls of African ancestry from BNCS in the ROOT consortium.
note: The sentence closes the supplement's section 4.3 on RVGBC but names 'BNCS', apparently a copy error (the BNCS section above it gives 92 cases and 227 controls). These counts are the African-ancestry subset genotyped for ROOT, not the whole study, and no total is stated. The age-at-menarche paper (PMID:34706928, PMC9011920) Table 1 lists RVGDBCR with 130 cases and 242 controls (table cells, not a sentence). No design paper of the study was found; one would settle the number enrolled.

label: Genome-Wide Association Study of Adiposity in Samoans
counts: adult Samoans recruited in 2010
quote: A total of 3,504 participants were recruited into the study.
note: Design/baseline paper; 29 were later excluded, leaving 3,475 eligible participants (the abstract's n = 3,475). dbGaP phs000914 says DNA and phenotypes were collected from 3,119 adult Samoans and gives 'Total number of consented subjects: 3501'. The example TOPMed study (PMID:40216759) included 1274 Samoans.

label: Sanford Biobank
counts: European-origin patients from the Sanford Biobank and the Imagenetics program together (genotyped analysis cohort)
quote: The Sanford Health population is a cohort of 26 291 European‐origin patients from the Sanford Biobank and the Imagenetics program.
note: Counts the biobank together with the Imagenetics (Sanford Chip) program and only European-origin patients, so not the biobank's own enrolment; the same paper analysed n=25 166. PMID:33777099 says more than 11,000 patients had taken part in the Sanford Chip Program. The example study's supplement (figshare 45157534, fetched) gives only table counts for the analysed type 2 diabetes subset. No source read states the number of biobank enrollees; a Sanford Biobank description would settle it.

label: Salvador-SCAALA study
counts: children recruited in the first (2005) resurvey with questionnaires completed
quote: The total number of children recruited in the first resurvey with questionnaires completed was 1,445.
note: Design paper of SCAALA Salvador (full text read). The example H. pylori GWAS (PMID:37497783) says it included '1161 of a total of 1445 children'. The earlier sanitation-evaluation cohorts (1997, 2001, 2003) from which the children came are not counted here.

label: San Francisco City Clinic Cohort
counts: homosexual and bisexual men recruited 1978-1980
quote: PATIENTS--Cohort included 6705 homosexual and bisexual men originally recruited from 1978 to 1980 for studies of sexually transmitted hepatitis B.
note: Abstract of the 1990 BMJ natural-history paper. PMID:1546772 (mortality study) analysed data from 6704 men of the cohort. Smaller subsets were followed for HIV (489 men in the Kaplan-Meier analysis of PMID:2261554).

label: Silent Cerebral Infarct Multi-Center Clinical Trial
counts: children randomised to transfusion or observation
quote: A total of 196 children (mean age, 10 years) were randomly assigned to the observation or transfusion group and were followed for a median of 3 years.
note: Main results paper (NEJM 2014). The same paper says 'Among the 1074 children who underwent screening MRI of the brain, 20 (1.9%) had strokes and 379 (35.3%) had infarct-like lesions'; genetic studies such as the example (PMID:40025045) may draw on the larger screened group. Planned sample size was 204.

label: Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension
counts: participants recruited at baseline in Lausanne, Geneva and Bern
quote: The Swiss Kidney Project on Genes in Hypertension (SKIPOGH) is a multicenter cohort including 1128 participants recruited from the general population of Lausanne, Geneva and Bern (2009-12).
note: Most recent cohort description (2026 kidney-stone paper). The 2014 paper (PMID:24663506) analysed 652 participants with complete ambulatory blood pressure data. The example urinary zinc GWAS (PMID:41325371) used SKIPOGH within a 10,113-person meta-analysis.

label: SLOVENIA study
counts: children and young people with asthma aged 5-19 in the study, as listed in the PiCA design paper
quote: Slovenia Slovenia Asthma cohort Tertiary care 350 5–19 162 (46) 89.9 (14.85) 193 † † 86 Peripheral blood
note: A row of Table 1 of the PiCA design paper (PMID:28639505), not a prose sentence: study, country, design, setting, N = 350, age 5–19. The same paper says 400 SLOVENIA DNA samples would be genotyped ('SLOVENIA (n = 400)'), which disagrees with the table. The example GWAS (PMID:34442380) included 166 patients (94 ICS non-responders, 72 responders). The abstract of the earlier Slovenian study (PMID:22986918) gives no count; its full text is closed.

label: Santiago Longitudinal Study
counts: infants enrolled 1991-1996 in the iron-deficiency preventive trial and neurophysiology study
quote: Briefly, from 1991 to 1996, 1798 infants with no major health problems, born at term and weighing ≥ 3.0 kg, participated in a randomized trial of iron supplementation to prevent IDA, a neurophysiology study of those with IDA, and nonanemic controls.
note: From PMID:30515969 (2019 GWAS of BMI in the SLS). Sources disagree slightly: PMID:32108435 (2020) says the SLS 'initially involved 1,790 Chilean infants' and that the preventive trial randomised 1,657 non-anaemic infants; PMID:32499257 says 1657 infants completed the preventive trial and analysed 1412. Later follow-ups: 1,039 assessed at age 23 (PMID:34556688), about 1000 at 30-31 years (PMID:35501766); the example BMI GWAS (PMID:39885687) included 861 SLS participants.

label: Shanghai Women's and Men's Health Studies
counts: member counts only: 2 member cohorts (SMHS 61,491 men 2002-2006; SWHS 74,941 women 1997-2000)
quote: The SMHS and SWHS are two ongoing population-based prospective cohort studies, which were established in 2002–2006 and 1997–2000, when 61,491 men aged 40–74 years and 74,941 women aged 40–70 years completed a face-to-face baseline survey, respectively.
note: The sources give the two member cohorts' sizes, not a pooled total, so participants is left null. Other statements: the example study (PMID:35621206) says the cohorts 'recruited 75 000 women and 61 500 men'; PMID:40576378 gives 74 940 women and 61 469 men. The joint green-tea analysis (PMID:28135196) kept 115,954 participants (51,920 men and 64,034 women) after exclusions, an analysed subset.

label: Swedish National Myeloma Biobank
counts: MM patients from the biobank genotyped in the Swedish GWAS discovery set (analysed subset)
quote: For the Swedish-Norwegian discovery sample set, we obtained 1,668 and 157 samples from the Swedish National Myeloma Biobank (Skåne University Hospital, Lund, Sweden) and the Norwegian Biobank for Myeloma (Trondheim, Norway), respectively.
note: No source read states the biobank's total size. This is the analysed subset used in the 2015 GWAS; a further 223 MM cases from the biobank formed the replication series (PMID:26007630, PMID:27363682). PMID:39103364 gives the Swedish GWAS data set as 2338 cases and 11,971 controls but does not attribute them all to the biobank; PMID:31363079 used 871 patients' clinical data from the Swedish Multiple Myeloma Registry. A biobank description stating its total enrolment would settle it.

label: Seoul National University Hospital Diabetes Study
counts: T2D cases and nondiabetic controls in the AGEN-T2D stage 3 replication
quote: Seoul National University Hospital (SNUH) Study The Seoul National University Hospital (SNUH) case-control samples were consisted of 761 T2D patients of the Diabetes Clinic of SNUH and 632 nondiabetic control subjects.
note: Cases and controls from the quoted sentence; the total 1393 is stated in the same supplement's sample-size table row "SNUH SNUHDS Korean 632 761 1393 Case-control" (the table lists the two groups in the opposite order to its case/control headers; the text sentence is taken for cases and controls). These are the samples used in the AGEN meta-analysis (PMID:22158537); no separate design paper for the study was read.

label: Hispanic Community Children's Health Study/Study of Latino Youth
counts: youth aged 8-16 enrolled 2012-2014
quote: Between 2012 and 2014, SOL Youth enrolled 1466 youth aged 8 to 16 years living in the household of a parent/caregiver who were participants in HCHS/SOL.
note: The design paper (PMID:24120345), written during recruitment, states no enrolment number. The example study PMID:39885687 also says SOL Youth recruited n = 1,466 children.

label: Sao Paulo Heart Failure Cohort
note: Read the SPHFC description in the Supplementary Note of Christophersen et al. 2017 (ng.3843 MOESM307) and the study lists in the supplements of Roselli et al. 2018 (s41588-018-0133-9) and the 2024/2025 AF GWAS (PMID:40050429, s41588-024-02072-3): none states how many patients the cohort enrolled or how many were analysed; the per-study sample sizes are in supplementary spreadsheets that are not on disk. The per-study sample-size table of ng.3843 or a design paper of the São Paulo heart failure cohort would settle it.

label: Singapore Preconception Study of Long-Term Maternal and Child Outcomes
counts: unique women enrolled preconception 2015-2017
quote: Between February 2015 and October 2017, the S-PRESTO study recruited 1039 Chinese, Malay or Indian (or any combinations thereof) women aged 18-45 years and who intended to get pregnant and deliver in Singapore, resulting in 1032 unique participants and 373 children born in the cohort.
note: 1039 recruitments correspond to 1032 unique women, since nine women took part in two recruitment visits; 475 women conceived and 373 children were born in the cohort. The number counts the enrolled women, not their children.

label: Swiss Pediatric Sepsis Study
counts: children enrolled Sept 2011-Dec 2015 (1181 sepsis episodes)
quote: Between Sept 1, 2011, and Dec 31, 2015, we enrolled 1096 children to our study.
note: From the cohort's epidemiology paper, which reports 1181 episodes of blood culture-proven bacterial sepsis in these children. The 2025 GWAS example (PMID:42241732) states "During the study period, a total of 1269 blood culture-proven sepsis episodes were recorded in 1164 children." with eligibility widened to bacterial or fungal sepsis; its GWAS used 650 sepsis cases and 1395 population-based controls. The profile paper's number for the defined bacterial-sepsis cohort is given.

label: Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder
counts: outpatients aged 15+ with bipolar disorder enrolled
quote: Data were drawn from the Systematic Treatment Enhancement Program for Bipolar Disorder (STEP-BD), a naturalistic study of 4360 outpatients 15 years or older with BD.
