label: Simultaneous Study of Gemcitabine-Docetaxel Combination adjuvant treatment, as well as Extended Bisphosphonate and Surveillance-Trial
counts: patients randomised 2005-2007 from 251 centres
quote: From 2005–2007, 3754 patients from 251 study centers were randomly allocated to treatment groups (1898 FEC → Doc, 1856 FEC → Doc/Gem).
note: The trial's primary results paper. The GWAS example (PMID:35653140) also states "A total of 3754 patients were randomized between September 2005 and March 2007." and genotyped 3,322 of them; the CTC analysis (PMID:24832787) used 2026 patients.

label: Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for Renal Cell Carcinoma-Nephrectomy
counts: registered RCC patients with stored blood, included in the 2024 GWAS (analysed subset)
quote: We included the cases of 1,120 patients with RCC who were registered in the Seoul National University Prospectively Enrolled Registry for RCC-Nephrectomy (SUPER-RCC-Nx) and had their blood stored in the human biobank [21].
note: No whole-registry count for the nephrectomy sub-cohort alone was found. The SUPER-GUC profile paper (PMID:31294132) states "At the end of December, 2018, a total of 929, 796, and 1,221 patients were enrolled in SUPER-PC, SUPER-RCC, and SUPER-UC, respectively.", i.e. 796 in the whole SUPER-RCC arm (nephrectomy and metastatic sub-cohorts) by 2018. The later 1120 is the patients with stored blood included in the GWAS, a lower bound on the sub-cohort's size.

label: Triple A Barcelona Study
counts: individuals with AAA included, 2019 to March 2025
quote: Cohort DescriptionA total of 471 individuals, 454 males and 17 females (3.6%), with AAA were included.
note: From the cohort's own description paper (PMID:40649094); recruitment ran from 2019 to March 2025. Its abstract says "So far, 469 individuals with measurements of the abdominal aortic diameter, along with anthropometric, clinical information, and blood samples for most follow-up visits, have been recruited." and Table 1 describes N = 469, excluding 2 individuals with diameters >100 mm. The quote runs the section heading into the sentence as the cached text does. The GWAS example (PMID:37845353) names TABS as a discovery cohort without a count in the text read.

label: Trans-National Asthma Genetic Consortium
counts: asthma cases and controls in the 2018 multi-ancestry meta-analysis
quote: These studies included 56 studies of European-ancestry (19,954 cases, 107,715 controls), seven studies of African-ancestry (2,149 cases, 6,055 controls), two Japanese studies (1,239 cases, 3,976 controls) and one Latino study (606 cases, 792 controls), making a total of 23,948 cases and 118,538 controls.
note: The paper states cases and controls separately but no single participant total; its only total is "genome-wide data available in >142,000 individuals of diverse ancestries", a lower bound, so participants is left null rather than summed. The flagship meta-analysis pooled 66 studies (56 European-ancestry, 7 African-ancestry, 2 Japanese, 1 Latino); the childhood-onset subgroup had 8,976 cases and 18,399 controls.

label: LITMUS Metacohort
needs: PMID:33045403 (full text, Contemp Clin Trials, not open access)|PMID:36958367 (full text, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol)
note: No source read states the whole metacohort's size; the analysed subsets disagree. PMID:36958367 abstract: "Of 1430 participants with NAFLD in the LITMUS metacohort with serum samples, 966 (403 women and 563 men) were included after all exclusion criteria had been applied." PMC11771619 (PMID:39865358) evaluated "966 adult participants with biopsy‐proven MASLD from the LITMUS metacohort"; PMC12969424 (PMID:41810432) says "The LITMUS metacohort consisted of 946 individuals with biopsy-proven MASLD"; but the machine-learning paper PMID:38421999, drawing on the LITMUS Metacohort, analysed "cohort size ranging between 5385 and 6673 subjects", so the serum-sample subsets are not the whole metacohort. The GWAS example PMID:32298765 used 1,483 European NAFLD cases (abstract), not attributed to the metacohort as such. A registry or metacohort description giving the total enrolled would settle it.

label: Brain Bank for Aging Research
counts: more than 6,500 cases with brain paraffin blocks accumulated, as of 2005 (a lower bound)
quote: 現在までの蓄積は, 脳パラフィンブロック6,500例以上, 凍結脳 (部分) 1,500例以上, 凍結半脳450例以上で, 30件以上の共同研究を実行中である.
note: The Japanese abstract of the 2005 brain bank description (PMID:16248404) says the holdings so far are over 6,500 cases of brain paraffin blocks, over 1,500 partial frozen brains and over 450 frozen hemibrains; 6,500 is stated as a lower bound and is 20 years old. Later period counts: PMID:33150517 "TMGHIG performed 738 autopsies between October 2008 and June 2018 and obtained consent to register them to the BBAR"; PMID:26091809 used 286 consecutive autopsy brains from February 2008 to July 2012. A current registration total would settle it.

label: Tasmanian Ophthalmic Biobank
note: No source read states the biobank's total enrolment; only subsets. PMID:42026177: "Whole genome sequencing data from 1057 healthy participants in the Tasmanian Ophthalmic Biobank (TOB), all of white European ancestry, underwent opportunistic screening" (controls recruited January-February 2018). PMID:34013049: "A total of 243 patients receiving anti-VEGF injections were identified in the Tasmanian Ophthalmic Biobank." The example GWAS (PMID:40136285) has an Australian cohort of 551 cases and 599 controls drawn from TOB and GRFCD together. A biobank description with total cases and controls would settle it.

label: Transcriptomic Analysis of Left Ventricular Gene Expression
counts: aortic valve surgery patients enrolled (as reported in 2017)
quote: A large cohort of patients (n = 140) undergoing elective cardiac surgery for aortic valve replacement were enrolled in this study.
note: Largest achieved enrolment found. The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT00985049 (status unknown, verified 2024-08) gives only a planned size: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":350,"type":"ESTIMATED"}. PMID:27923400 used LV samples from 76 Caucasian patients undergoing aortic valve replacement. The example GWAS (PMID:41645906) gives no TRANSLATE count in the text read. The quote is from the Europe PMC abstract of PMID:28687077.

label: Trondheim Parkinson's Disease Study
counts: participants in the cohort by end of January 2020
quote: By the end of January 2020, the Trondheim PD cohort contained 1,221 participants (65% males).
note: From the cohort's own mortality paper, which describes the study population. The example GWAS of PD progression (PMID:38849413) analysed 6766 PD patients across 12 cohorts and gives no Trondheim-specific number in the text searched.

label: Taiwan Super Control Study
counts: non-diabetic participants analysed for HbA1c (analysed subset)
quote: We tested the association of the SLC2A10 polymorphism with HbA1c in the Taiwan Super Control Study (TWSC) [35]. Subjects with diabetes were excluded, as defined by physician diagnosis, medication use, or HbA1c ≥ 6.5%. A total of 920 participants were included.
note: No source read states the whole study's size; this is the non-diabetic subset analysed in PMID:32453789. The HbA1c GWAS (PMID:24647736) Table 1 lists TWSC with n 920 as well ("TWSC920PopulationChinese"). The example study PMID:34059833 and the kidney-function meta-analysis (ng.2352) mention TWSC without a count in the text read. A description of the TWSC sample (for example the per-study tables of the AGEN papers' supplements) would settle it.

label: Taizhou Longitudinal Study
counts: adults aged 20-80 recruited since 2007 (stated as over 201,000)
quote: The Taizhou Longitudinal Study (TZL) is a population-based prospective cohort initiated in 2007, recruiting over 201,000 adults aged 20-80 from urban and rural areas of Taizhou, Jiangsu Province, China.
note: From the 2026 cohort profile abstract; the number is stated as a lower bound ("over 201,000"). The same abstract says genome-wide genotyping was done for approximately 50,000 participants recruited 2009-2014. The 2009 design paper (PMID:19589173) planned "at least 100,000 adults aged 30–80 years" and reported 17,314 subjects in the pilot phase. The example study (PMID:37565938) is not open access and was not read.

label: UK Aneurysm Growth Study
counts: men with AAA included in the 2023 growth analysis (analysed subset; controls not counted)
quote: Some 3670 participants were included in the analyses, each with one or more completed questionnaire responses and two or more post-recruitment scans, with at least one scan >= 30 mm in diameter (Table 1).
note: No source read gives the cohort's total recruitment of cases and controls. PMID:38055889 (recruitment 2011-2019) reports 3670 AAA cases included and 995 AAA cases excluded, and says UKAGS also recruited non-AAA controls not counted in its table. The 2018 quality-of-life paper (PMID:29405273, recruitment September 2011 to July 2015) included "No AAA (n = 4630)" and "AAA (n = 381)" men. PMC6818029 (PMID:31595818) used 268 UKAGS patients with AAA and 162 controls. A cohort description giving total cases and controls recruited would settle it.

label: Danish T2D Case-Control Study
note: Read the DIAMANTE paper (PMID:35551307) and its Supplementary Information (s41588-022-01058-3 MOESM1), which describe the Danish T2D Case-Control Study (UCPH) by funding and ethics only, and the DIAGRAM 2018 paper (PMID:30297969): neither states the study's numbers of cases and controls in the text read. The per-study sample sizes are in the supplementary tables (spreadsheets) of these papers, which are not on disk; one of those tables would settle it.

label: CoFAR Eosinophilic Esophagitis Registry
counts: subjects enrolled May 2011 to March 2016
quote: 708 subjects were enrolled between May 2011 and March 2016, and 705 subjects were analyzed, as 3 were determined to be ineligible.
note: Registry profile paper (PMID:30075341). 705 subjects analysed after 3 ineligible. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01323803 gives actual enrollment count 709.

label: Vanderbilt Online Musicality Study
counts: participants who consented, completed at least part of the online study and passed QC
quote: In total, 3,258 participants (1,948 females, 727 males, 583 unknown) consented to the study, completed at least a portion of the online study, and passed quality control filters (see Figure 2).
note: PMID:36718543. Saliva kits sent to 2,286; 1,931 returned; 1,865 genotyped; 1,805 passed genetic QC; 1,792 unrelated adults analysed. PMID:41715922 mentions a larger phenotyped sample including non-genotyped individuals (n = 2,508) for the speech rhythm task. The count is after quality-control filters, so the number who ever enrolled may be larger.

label: Viva la Familia Study
counts: children (probands and siblings) in 319 families
quote: The Viva la Familia cohort consisted of 1030 children from 319 families selected based on an overweight proband between the ages of 4 and 19 y.
needs: PMID:16960181 full text (AJCN; only the abstract is cached)
note: Design paper abstract. Parents were also recruited but their number is not stated in the abstract read; the full text of PMID:16960181 would settle the total including parents. PMID:23251661 genotyped 815 children from 263 families.

label: Western Australian Melanoma Health Study
counts: consenting melanoma cases
quote: The final sample consisted of 1643 consenting cases out of 3420 cancer notifications (48.04%), of which 1455 cases completed one or more components of the study and 1157 completed all components.
note: Design paper abstract (PMID:21474410). A case collection only (no controls). 1455 completed at least one component, 1157 all components. PMID:26237428 is a melanoma GWAS meta-analysis that does not give a WAMHS-specific count in the text read.

label: Warfarin Anticoagulation in Patients in sub-Saharan Africa
counts: actual enrollment registered on ClinicalTrials.gov
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":681,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: No paper sentence gives the whole cohort. PMID:36210801: 'Out of 638 eligible black-African participants recruited from Uganda and South Africa between June 2018 and March 2020, 561 samples had been shipped to the University of Liverpool by the time of analysis' (548 after QC). PMID:39163621 adds War-PATH cohort 3, 133 mixed-ancestry participants from the same South African sites 2018-2020 (cohort 1 = 548 Black Africans). PMID:34889080: development cohort 364 (June 2018-July 2019) and validation cohort 270 (Aug 2019-Mar 2020). The registry record's eligibility lists only Black African ethnicity, so whether 681 includes the mixed-ancestry participants is unclear.

label: Women's Environmental Cancer and Radiation Epidemiology Study
counts: CBC cases and UBC controls who completed interview and biospecimen, WECARE I and II
quote: The population-based WECARE Study included 1521 cases with CBC and 2212 age- and year of first diagnosis-matched controls with unilateral breast cancer recruited during two phases in the USA, Canada, and Denmark.
note: PMID:27400983 (WECARE I and II combined). No source read states the combined total, so participants is left null. Same paper: 'A total of 2354 cases and 3599 controls were eligible and invited'. The WECARE I design paper (PMID:15084244) planned 700 cases and 1400 controls. The example GWAS (PMID:38263039) analysed 2829 participants (1161 cases, 1668 controls).

counts: uveal melanoma cases recruited and controls selected from the Penn Medicine Biobank
quote: We recruited 409 UM cases via the UPenn Genetic Diagnostic Laboratory from patients receiving treatment at the Wills Eye Hospital (Philadelphia, PA, USA).
note: PMID:40495383. Controls from a separate sentence of the same source: 'We also selected 937 controls originally recruited as part of the Penn Medicine Biobank.' No source states the combined total, so participants is null. After QC, 401 cases and 762 controls were analysed.

note: WOBASZ II design paper abstract. Of a drawn sample of 15,120 persons, 1557 were not eligible. A later paper (PMID:41144382) says 'the WOBASZ II study included 6163 patients (3406 women and 2757 men)', presumably after exclusions; the design paper's examined count is used.

label: Oxford Regional Prospective Study of Childhood Diabetes
counts: children recruited at diagnosis 1986-1997

label: Study of Underlying Genetic Determinants of Vitamin D and Highly Related Traits

quote: We have performed a large 25-hydroxyvitamin D meta-GWAS involving 31 studies with a total of 79,366 individuals.
note: Cohort aggregation (SUNLIGHT consortium); pooled number of its largest meta-analysis (PMID:29343764). The first SUNLIGHT GWAS (PMID:20541252) studied 33 996 individuals of European descent from 15 cohorts (16,125 discovery). Replication in 40,562 EPIC and 2195 SOCCS individuals is not included in the number.

label: International Cannabis Consortium
counts: individuals of European ancestry in the 13 discovery cohorts of the 2016 lifetime cannabis use meta-GWAS
quote: We conducted a meta-analysis of genome-wide association data of 13 cohorts (N=32 330) and four replication samples (N=5627).
note: Cohort aggregation; pooled number of its first meta-analysis (PMID:27023175), plus 5627 in four replication samples. In the 2018 GWAS (PMID:30150663) the ICC contributed 'data from 35,297 individuals of European ancestry from 16 cohorts' alongside 23andMe (22,683) and UK Biobank (126,785); that later ICC count could be preferred as the most recent.

label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia cohort 1
note: No source read states the size of the whole COHRA1 cohort. The protocol paper (PMID:18522740) gives no enrolment count. PMID:26106416 analyses two populations, 'West Virginia (WV, N = 1997) and Pennsylvania (PA, N = 1080)', but gives no combined total. Other COHRA1 analyses give subsets: 449 families with 868 adults (PMID:30993747); 1,311 adults aged 18-59 (PMID:33368457); 1,178 children aged 1-10 (PMID:34292949); a family-based sample 'N = 2,663; 740 families' (PMID:25612913, cohort not named in the abstract). dbGaP phs000095 gives 5417 consented subjects, but that pools the PITT (COHRA), DRDR and Iowa sites. A COHRA1 cohort-profile source stating the total enrolment would settle it.

label: Shikamachi health improvement practice genome cohort study
counts: residents aged 40 and over in the four model districts (questionnaire survey, 2015-2016)
quote: The study population of the Shika study consisted of 4121 individuals from 40 years of age.
note: PMID:29207502; invitation letters were sent to all residents aged 40+ of four model districts between January 2015 and January 2016. The health examination arm is smaller: 1191 participants examined March 2014 to January 2017 (PMID:34347822) and 1150 participants 2013-2017 (PMID:36599956). PMID:35633918: in two model districts, 2199 of 2314 invited adults answered the questionnaire and 972 attended the health examination. No cohort profile paper was read; the number of all participants since 2011 is not stated.

note: An ongoing recruitment; no source read states its total enrolment. PMID:35288444 studied 'participants of the University of Leicester Bicuspid aoRtic vAlVe gEnetic research-8 pedigrees with multiple affected family members and 381 sporadic patients' (a sequenced subset). PMID:32720365 is a single-family report. The example GWAS meta-analysis (PMID:41645906, 9631 cases among 65 677 participants) mentions BRAVE only in its funding statement in the text read; its supplementary cohort table might give the BRAVE contribution.

label: Defining the Basis of Fibromuscular Dysplasia
counts: subjects enrolled by July 2019 (stated as 'over 375', a lower bound; about half cases, half controls)
quote: DEFINE-FMD continues to recruit subjects and as of July 2019 over 375 subjects have been enrolled (approximately 50% cases, 50% controls).
note: PMID:31424497. The source says 'over 375', so the number is a lower bound, and recruitment is ongoing. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01967511 gives an ESTIMATED enrollment of 600 (still recruiting). The forerunner CAUSE study closed at n=34 subjects. PMID:39271816 analysed 154 subjects (83 FMD cases, 71 controls) from DEFINE-FMD and CAUSE.

label: Center for Oral Health Research in Appalachia cohort 2
counts: analysed subset: mothers enrolled Nov 2011-Feb 2017 who completed at least one postpartum visit
quote: The current study included 1,015 participants from COHRA2 continuously enrolled between November 2011 and February 2017 (followed through May 2020) and 116 participants from COHRASmile enrolled between October 2017 and March 2019 (followed through August 2021) (Fig. 1).
note: PMID:38404680; the same paper says the analysis included women 'who completed at least one postpartum visit', so this is an analysed subset and the total enrolled may be larger. The protocol paper (PMID:26089906) planned 'a total initial sample size of over 1000 mother-baby pairs' and reported that 'As of January 31, 2015, the COHRA2 study has enrolled 744 pregnant women, 368 from Pittsburgh and 376 from West Virginia' (727 independent women). No source read gives the final enrolment.

label: Genetic Analysis of Idiopathic Thrombophilia 2 Project
counts: individuals in 35 extended families
quote: This sample consisted of 935 individuals in 35 extended families selected through a proband with idiopathic thrombophilia.
note: PMID:26784699 abstract; the example study (PMID:35272364) likewise says 'The GAIT-2 project included 935 individuals from 35 extended Spanish families selected through a proband with idiopathic thrombophilia.'

label: Human Reproductive Behaviour Consortium
counts: individuals in the 2021 age-at-first-birth meta-GWAS of 36 studies
quote: For Age at First Birth (AFB), we included 542,901 individuals (n=124,088 males; n=418,758 females) from 36 studies.
note: Cohort aggregation; pooled number of its largest meta-analysis (PMID:34211149). The same paper's age-at-first-sex GWAS had N=387,338, and its Methods say 'we included 397,338 pooled individuals' from UK Biobank for AFS (the two numbers disagree within the paper). Earlier consortium GWAS: AFS n=125,667 and AFB n=343,072.

quote: The SerGenCovid-19 project successfully collected data from 7,169 participants across Italy.
note: PMID:41659846, which also calls it 'a cohort study comprising 7,169 genetically characterized individuals from the general Italian population'. The CNR press release and IRIB project page give the planned selection of 10,000 participants from about 100,000 EPICOVID-19 respondents. The GWAS analysed 1,968 unrelated vaccinated individuals.

quote: In all, 799 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned; 16 did notstarttreatment:eightwererandomlyassignedtopaclitaxel,fourto nab-paclitaxel, and four to ixabepilone (CONSORT diagram; Fig 1).
note: Primary results paper PMID:26056183 (abstract: 'In all, 799 patients were enrolled, and 783 received treatment'). Planned enrollment was 900. PMID:33981951 and ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00785291 (actual enrollment 799) agree. The quote keeps the PDF text's missing spaces as extracted.

label: Asklepios Study
counts: subjects examined at baseline (round 1, 2002-2004)
quote: The Asklepios study comprises 2524 subjects (1301 women) approximately 35 to 55 years of age at the baseline examination in 2002–2004 (round 1), with a complete re-examination of 91% of subjects after a median of 10.1 (9.8–10.8) years of follow-up (round 2: in 2011–2016).
note: PMID:31357728. The design paper (PMID:17446795) abstract also gives 2524 participants (1301 women); PMID:29695838 says 2524 volunteers were included. 2221 participants had lung function measurements in PMID:31357728 (analysed subset).

quote: The CORNET consortium extended its genome-wide association meta-analysis for morning plasma cortisol from 12,597 to 25,314 subjects and from ~2.2 M to ~7 M SNPs, in 17 population-based cohorts of European ancestries.
note: Cohort aggregation; 17 member cohorts. The first CORNET GWAMA (PMID:25010111) had 12,597 participants from 11 cohorts, replicated in 2,795 participants from three further cohorts; that paper also says collaborators with samples from more than 15,000 people were recruited.

label: Amsterdam Born Children and their Development
counts: pregnant women recruited at the first prenatal visit (of 12,393 eligible)
quote: Pregnant women living in Amsterdam between January 2003 and March 2004 were eligible to participate in the Amsterdam Born Children and their Development cohort study (n = 12,393) and were recruited at the first prenatal visit (n = 8266) [44].
note: The study website says about 8,000 children are followed from pregnancy into adulthood. Of the recruited women, 4389 consented to blood sampling (PMID:41550966). The cohort profile (PMID:20813863, Int J Epidemiol 2011) was not on disk; it would confirm the figure.

label: 100-plus Study
counts: centenarians included by September 2018 (family members and partners not counted)
quote: To date (September 2018), 332 centenarians were included in the study.
note: Ongoing study, so the count grows; the design paper gives no count of the first-degree relatives and partners enrolled since 2017. The example study (PMID:33216869) used 358 participants from the 100-plus Study cohort as cases (343 after QC) plus 86 partners of centenarians' children as controls. A more recent cohort update would give the current total.

counts: young-onset breast cancer cases enrolled 2008-2010 and their breast cancer-free control sisters from the Sister Study
quote: We conducted the Two Sister Study, a sister-matched case-control study, by enrolling 1422 women between September 2008 and December 2010, who were younger than age 50 years at diagnosis with breast cancer and were enrolled within 4 years of diagnosis, and 1669 breast cancer-free control sisters from the Sister Study.
note: No source states a single total of cases plus controls, so participants is left null. The study website says: 'Over 1,400 young-onset sisters enrolled in the study by completing questionnaires and/or providing saliva samples for DNA, along with 1,700 of their sisters in the Sister Study.' and 'Of their parents, 1,438 provided a saliva sample.'; about 1,300 cases completed all requirements and are followed prospectively.

label: Women's Health Study: From Adolescence to Adulthood

quote: The Women's Health Study: From Adolescence to Adulthood (A2A) is a longitudinal observational cohort study that enrolled 1,549 participants [n = 787 surgically confirmed women with endometriosis (cases) and n = 762 controls] from November 2012–June 2018, enrolling 85% of those who were eligible to participate in the study.
note: PMID:38495219 also says 'Of the 1549 participants enrolled in the A2A cohort' but gives n=785 with endometriosis in its methods. PMID:32833998 analysed a subset of 282 cases and 293 controls.

label: African Ancestry Breast Cancer Genetic Consortium
counts: female cases and controls of African ancestry from 26 studies in the 2024 GWAS
quote: In brief, we analyzed whole-genome sequenced and high-density genotyped data from 18,034 female cases with breast cancer and 22,104 female controls of African ancestry from 26 studies participating in the AABCG, with 85.3% of participants from the United States and 14.7% from the African continent and Barbados.
note: PMID:38741014, the consortium's flagship GWAS; no single total is stated, so participants is null. The PRS paper (PMID:41629673) used 17,391 cases and 18,800 controls of AABCG data.

label: Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium
counts: individuals in the 2011 Australian asthma GWAS (cases and controls)
quote: The Australian GWAS included data from 7,197 individuals of whom 5,523 (77%) were genotyped with Illumina 610K (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA) array 1,674 (23%) with Illumina 370K array as part of four genotyping projects that are summarised in the webappendix (pp 11): the AAGC (n=1,810), QIMR_610K (n=2,483), QIMR_370K (n=1,674) and Busselton (n=1,230) projects.
note: PMID:21907864. Cases and controls from its abstract: 'We did a genome-wide association study (GWAS) in 2669 physician-diagnosed asthmatics and 4528 controls from Australia.' PMID:24388013 repeats the 2,669 cases and 4,528 controls under the heading 'Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium (n = 2,137)' (the number in its hay-fever analysis). The 2011 paper also calls a single genotyping project 'the Australian Asthma Genetics Consortium (AAGC) cohort (n=1,810)'; the 7,197 is the consortium's pooled GWAS, matching this term's definition.

note: Only source is a row of the study table in the supplement of PMID:29892016 (Nature Genetics 2018 OncoArray paper), whose columns are No. of Cases, No. of Controls, No. of Cases in Analysis, No. of Controls in Analysis: 1140 cases and 570 controls, of which 1079 and 550 were analysed. quote: Amsterdam Breast Cancer Study (ABCS) Netherlands 1429 1325 420 153

No single total is stated, so participants is null. These are the ABCS-F samples in that 2016 HOXB13 study; no ABCS-F design paper was found.

counts: breast cancer donors in the biobank as at 15 May 2014
quote: Size of the bioresource 6,225 donors as at 15 May 2014 On-going recruitment of 500-600 new donors per annum
note: From the bioresource description table of the ABCTB's 2014 Open Journal of Bioresources paper (doi:10.5334/ojb.aa). label: Anonymous Blood Donor Cohort

quote: In a case–control study involving 8133 first-onset MI cases and 8124 controls recruited in Bangladesh, we calculated odds ratios (ORs) for MI adjusted, for age, sex, smoking status, history of diabetes, history of hypertension, family history of MI, and LDL-cholesterol.
note: From the 2024 BRAVE case-control paper (PMID:39811539), the most recent definition source; no sentence read states the total. The design paper (PMID:25930055) says 'By early 2015, the ongoing BRAVE study had recruited over 5000 confirmed first-ever MI cases, and over 5000 controls', with 3000 cases and 3000 controls genotyped. The example study (PMID:32762905) used 491 BRAVE participants.

label: Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk
counts: bladder cancer cases and population controls in the study
quote: Two-tailed p values < 0.05 were considered to reflect statistical significance.ResultsA total of 586 participants (200 cases and 386 controls) were included in the study.
note: From the example study (PMID:21203820); the quote includes the preceding sentence and the 'Results' heading because the extracted text runs them together. The earlier papers (PMID:16380991, 16504378) report 200 cases and 385 controls; dietary analyses used 198 cases and 377 controls.

label: Breast Cancer Study of the University Clinic Heidelberg
counts: cases and controls after quality control in the BCAC iCOGS genotyping (analysed subset)
quote: BSUCH Breast Cancer Study of the University Clinic Heidelberg 13 Germany All cases diagnosed with breast cancer in 2007- 2009 at the University Women`s Clinic Heidelberg. Female blood donors recruited in 2007- 2009 at the Institute of Transfusion Medicine & Immunology, Mannheim. 848 954
note: Row of the study-description table in the supplement of PMID:23535729 (header 'Sample size Post quality control Cases Controls'). The COGS non-synonymous SNP paper (PMID:24943594, Table 1) lists BSUCH with 954 controls and 852 cases. No source read states BSUCH's own recruitment total, so participants is null.

label: Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies
note: No source I could read gives the size of the Beijing Type 2 Diabetes Studies on their own. PMID:22961080 gives only the pooled stage 2 replication sample of three studies: 13,517 unrelated Chinese Hans (6,570 T2D cases and 6,947 controls) from GBTDS, BTDS and HTDS; its per-study counts are in Supplementary Table 1, which is not in PMC or the Europe PMC supplementary files and the journal supplement page returned 403. PMID:25993007 uses LHAPGC and BTDS and has a 701-person northern Chinese middle-aged panel (MI_N), but does not say that panel is BTDS. The separately named Beijing Diabetes Survey (798 cases, 659 controls in the stage 1 GWAS of PMID:22961080) is not stated to be the same study. Supplementary Table 1 of PMID:22961080 would settle it.

label: Brisbane Twin Nevus Study
counts: 12-year-old twins and nearest-age siblings examined 1992-2016
quote: Among 3957 participants (158 per year), we saw an approximate halving of naevus counts over the 25-year period, and examined multiple explanations for this trend.
note: From the abstract of PMID:40576277 (only the abstract is cached), the analysis of the whole 1992-2016 series of twins and siblings; it may exclude participants without usable naevus data, and it does not count the twins' parents, who are also in the study: PMID:24949998 used 1630 parents of twins from the study as controls ("The control sample (n = 1630) were parents of twins ascertained as part of the Brisbane Twin Naevus Study"). PMID:21655089 drew part of 2,353 melanoma GWAS controls from it. The 85,965 of PMID:41807453 is a 14-study meta-analysis.

label: Bus Santé
counts: Geneva residents examined since 1992 (a lower bound: 'more than')
quote: More than 20,000 Geneva residents have already participated in the Bus Santé study since it was launched in 1992.
note: The study website (Specchio Hub, run by the Geneva University Hospitals' population epidemiology unit) gives the cumulative total only as 'more than 20,000'; it is undated. Each year about 1000 new residents are sampled (PMID:37250185: '∼1000 men and women'; PMID:40235578). Period counts: 12′294 total sample 2008-2019 (10′739 analysed, PMID:39081844); 11,278 adults 2005-2023 (PMID:40235578); 18,515 participants 1993-2018 in a spatial analysis (preprint 10.1101/2022.01.16.22269160); 18 963 participants 1993-2014 (PMID:28298370 abstract). The example study PMID:24068962 genotyped 4670 Bus Santé participants.

label: Camargo Cohort Study
counts: all subjects enrolled at baseline 2006-2011
quote: In the present study, 2997 serum samples from all the subjects included in the Camargo Cohort have been analyzed.
note: PMID:37924421 says the 2997 samples are from all subjects of the cohort (set up February 2006 to February 2011); its Table 1 splits them into 1941 women and 1056 men. PMID:40983397 used 455 DISH cases from the cohort; PMID:35906442 refers to earlier cohort descriptions. The example study PMID:30158200 is a 25-cohort fracture GWAS meta-analysis.

label: Cantabria Osteoporosis Case-control
counts: participants with DNA and BMD and/or fracture data (GEFOS replication sample)
quote: CABRIO‐CC Cantabria Osteoporosis Case‐control Case‐control, cross‐sectional Clinic‐based plus volunteers Spain Santander Caucasian (Spanish) 2,321
note: The quote is a row of Supplementary Table 20A of the 2012 GEFOS BMD meta-analysis (Nature Genetics ng.2249), under the column 'Total sample size with DNA and BMD and/or fracture data available', so it counts the sample available for that analysis, not necessarily everyone recruited; Table 20B of the same file gives 538 men and 1,771 women with age data, and the QC table 2178 genotyped. The study's own papers report smaller subsets: PMID:17118999, 135 women with vertebral fractures and 312 controls; PMID:17218734, 572 individuals over 50 (381 postmenopausal women and 191 men). No cases/controls split of the whole study was found.

label: Coronary Artery Disease and Genomics
counts: CAD cases and population controls in the discovery GWAS
quote: A GWA study using the Genome-Wide Human SNP 6.0 Array (Affymetrix, Santa Clara, USA) was conducted to discover SNPs associated with CAD in the CADomics study (Coronary Artery Disease and Genomics), a case-control study of CAD (2,078 CAD cases and 2,953 controls).
note: Cases and controls from the quote; the total is stated in the same paper (PMID:21606135): 'In the present study, a genome-wide association case-control study in 5,031 individuals followed by two stages of replication and a final meta-analysis of 59,789 cases and controls was performed.' These are the samples passing QC in the CADomics GWAS, the study's defining analysis. The Lancet supplement (definition source) used a nested subset of CADomics (N=1,804; 1214 MI+ and 592 MI- patients with angiographic CAD).

label: Caerphilly Prospective Study
counts: men aged 45-59 recruited at baseline (phase 1, 1979-1983)
quote: The CaPS was set up to study the influence of CVD risk factors in the development of coronary heart disease (CHD) [12], and recruited an initial 2512 men, aged 45 to 59 years living in the town of Caerphilly and five adjacent villages, South Wales, UK (response rate 89%).
note: Baseline recruitment from PMID:28106791. The MORGAM cohort description (thl.fi) says a further 447 men who had moved into the area were added at the 1984-1988 re-examination, and gives MORGAM round sizes of 2398 (round 2), 2171 (round 3, 1989-93) and 1161 (round 5, 2002-04); PMID:28106791 followed 1838 men from phase 2; PMID:37844990 reports 1225 men at the 2002-2004 phase. No source states the total ever enrolled including the phase 2 additions.

label: Amagasaki Study
counts: individuals recruited at baseline, September 2002 to August 2003
quote: The Amagasaki Study (CAGE-‐Amagasaki) is an ongoing population-‐based cohort study of 5,745 individuals (3,435 males and 2,310 females), aged >18 years and recruited for a baseline examination between September 2002 to August 2003
note: PMID:23050023 agrees ('from 5745 individuals consecutively enrolled in the population-based setting, which is known as Amagasaki Study', 4990 analysed). PMID:26648100 gives the same description with the same sex split but 5,743 individuals, apparently a typo. The 2011 BP GWAS supplement used 5325 to 5,331 Amagasaki samples in stage 2; PMID:26648100 used 200 Amagasaki subjects.

label: Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study
counts: participants in the baseline survey, February 2004 to August 2007
quote: The Kyushu University Fukuoka Cohort Study is a community-based prospective epidemiologic cohort of 12,959 subjects, who participated in the baseline survey during the period from February 2004 to August 2007.
note: The same sentence with 12,959 is in the 2011 BP GWAS supplement (ng.834, CAGE-Fukuoka). PMID:21297916 (a review) says 'a total of 12,949 persons' constructed 2003 to 2009, probably a slip. Analysed subsets: 12,020 men and women aged 49-76 at baseline in the example study PMID:20205615; 4,427 postmenopausal women in PMID:34313618.

label: Hospital-based Cohort Study at the National Center for Global Health and Medicine
note: No source I read states how many people the NCGM hospital-based cohort enrolled. PMID:24647736 (example) used 323 CAGE-NCGM participants in its HbA1c GWAS (Table 1); PMID:26648100 used 200 Tokyo subjects selected from the cohort. PMID:23050023 and PMID:21971053 only thank the cohort. A cohort description from NCGM (a design paper or the CAGE Network documentation) would settle it.

label: Calcium Intake Fracture Outcome Study
counts: women randomised to calcium or placebo in 1998
quote: The participants were 1460 women aged 75.1 ± 2.7 years at baseline (1998) recruited from the general population and randomized to receive 1200 mg of calcium carbonate daily or an identical placebo.
note: The trial enrolled 1500 women (PMID:38477757: 'A total of 1500 women who were at least 70 yr old ... were recruited'; PMID:41346785: 'Of the 1500 enrolled women, 40 were excluded from this analysis due to calcium and vitamin D supplement prescription'), and PMID:41346785 says 1460 were randomised, 730 to calcium and 730 to placebo. The randomised number is recorded, as SIZE.md asks for trials. PMID:38477757 analysed 1261 women.

label: CALEX-family study
counts: family members with DNA and BMD and/or fracture data (GEFOS replication sample)
quote: Calex‐family Calex‐family study Cohort Population‐based, fami Finland Jyväskylä and its surrondings North European 647
note: The quote is the Calex-family row of Supplementary Table 20A of the 2012 GEFOS BMD meta-analysis, column 'Total sample size with DNA and BMD and/or fracture data available' (Table 20B: 190 men, 457 women), so it is the analysable sample rather than everyone measured. PMID:26439744 describes the study as 'the Calex family study (n = 282 families)'. PMID:25279460 (example) gives the 2007-8 participants by role, without a total: 235 young women, and 40 brothers, 214 mothers, 121 fathers, 120 grandmothers and 65 grandfathers invited. The underlying Calex girls' cohort had 396 girls at baseline (PMID:19171028, PMID:24358145).

label: Cancer de Mama
counts: breast cancer cases and matched population controls recruited 2004-2007
quote: In the present case-control study, we examined the association between serum concentrations of thyroid hormones and BC in 2074 Mexican women who participated in the Cáncer de Mama (CAMA) study.
note: Cases and controls from PMID:20084545 (abstract, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID%3A20084545+AND+SRC%3AMED&format=json&resultType=core): 'One thousand incident cases and 1,074 matched controls to cases by 5 years of age, site and health institution participated in the study.' PMID:25805146 agrees ('Incident BC cases (n 1000) and controls (n 1074) ... were recruited'). PMID:30092822 elsewhere says 'out of 1000 cases and 1070 controls' and measured hormones in 645 cases and 697 controls. The example study PMID:31553449 pooled CAMA with seven other studies.

label: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Cancer Hospital Study
counts: never-smoking female cases and controls in the 2012 FLCCA GWAS (analysed subset only)
quote: CAMSCH Mainland China 642 555 32 334
note: No source I read gives the size of the whole CAMS Cancer Hospital case-control study (1997-2008, men and women, smokers and never-smokers). The quote is the CAMSCH row of the supplementary table 'Demographic characteristics of cases and controls from participating study centers in a GWAS of lung cancer among never-smoking Asian females' of PMID:23143601 (columns: all cases, adenocarcinomas, squamous cell, controls), i.e. only its never-smoking women; no total is stated, so participants is left null. PMID:20700438 used 287 never-smoking female cases and 287 controls from it. Its design reference (Wu et al. 2009 Cancer Res, PMID:19491260, not open access) reports pooled Northern and Southern Chinese samples, not CAMSCH alone; the original CAMSCH description would settle the whole-study size.

label: Canadian screening study
counts: nested lung cancer cases and controls in the OncoArray lung cancer study
quote: Canada Canadian screening study UHN, BCCA Lam/Tsao/Liu Canada screening cohort 2004-2011, 2008-2013 267 463 730
note: Row of Supplementary Table 1 ('Characteristics of OncoArray Studies'; columns Case no., Control no., Total) of the 2017 OncoArray lung cancer GWAS (PMID:28604730), the aggregation's defining analysis. The same supplement gives the size of the three member screening programmes together: 'A total of 9759 individuals participated in the CT screening program in Canada from these 3 programs.' (I-ELCAP Toronto 4782 enrolled; BCCA 4274 smokers enrolled 1990-2007), and says the samples are a subset of nested case-control pairs at a 1:2 ratio.

label: Prostate Cancer Genetics Study
counts: cases and controls in the 2001-2004 Cleveland case-control study
quote: To investigate this, the authors undertook a case-control study (n = 1,012) of the association between NSAIDs and more advanced prostate cancer in Ohio men recruited between 2001 and 2004 and evaluated whether this association was modified by a functional polymorphism in the lymphotoxin alpha (LTA) gene (LTA C+80A, where the CC genotype results in higher LTA production).
note: From the abstract of the definition source PMID:16931544 (full text not read); the number may be the analysed sample. A later paper by the same group on what appears to be the same Cleveland 2001-2004 study, though it does not name it (PMID:22132129, PMC3223211), says 'A total of 501 cases were fully recruited into the study' and 'A total of 538 controls were recruited into the study.' (470 cases and 512 controls analysed). The two sources disagree, so cases and controls are left null. PMID:21637779 describes the African American part of the Prostate Cancer Genetics Study (CaP Genes) as 160 men: 75 cases and 85 controls. The example PMID:29117387 is a multi-study meta-analysis.

label: Canadian Asthma Primary Prevention Study
counts: high-risk infants identified before birth and randomised
quote: A total of 545 high-risk infants (at least 1 first-degree relative with asthma or 2 first-degree relatives with other IgE-mediated allergic diseases) identified before birth.
note: From the abstract of the trial's first report, PMID:10891016 (251 intervention and 242 control infants assessed at 12 months). PMID:15100668 also says 'We identified 545 high-risk infants'. PMID:19566956 counts families: 'In total, there were 545 families recruited into this study (549 infants, 4 sets of twins).' PMID:35686384 analysed 525 children over the 15-year follow-up.

label: Carotid Atherosclerosis Progression Study
counts: members of a primary health-care scheme who agreed to take part at baseline
quote: In the Carotid Atherosclerosis Progression Study (CAPS), members of a German primary healthcare scheme were invited of whom 6,962 participants (attendance rate 21%) agreed to take part.
note: From the pooled carotid stenosis meta-analysis PMID:20431077 describing its member studies, not a CAPS design paper. CAPS's own papers give analysed samples: n=5056 aged 19-90 with baseline IMT and follow-up (PMID:16339465), 4995 followed for 10 years (PMID:22617119), 3383 with 3-year IMT progression (PMID:15243147), and 3000 genotyped (PMID:17332447). The CAPS baseline paper would confirm the enrolment.

label: Cáncer de Pulmón en Asturias
counts: incident lung cancer cases and hospital controls recruited October 2000 to December 2010
quote: All 877 cases and 840 controls were Caucasian.
note: PMID:28819433 (2017) describes the whole CAPUA recruitment: 'Briefly, a total of 877 incident lung cancer cases aged 30-85 years were recruited and interviewed in four main hospitals of Asturias in northern Spain from October 2000 to December 2010.' and 'A total of 840 controls were selected from the same hospitals among patients with unrelated diseases.' No source states the combined total, so participants is left null. Earlier or analysed counts: 789 cases and 789 matched controls (PMID:23013535); 402 cases and 383 controls genotyped (PMID:28819433); 796 cases, 772 controls, total 1568 in the OncoArray study supplement (PMID:28604730, recruitment given there as 2002-2012).

label: Collaborative Atorvastatin Diabetes Study
counts: patients randomised to atorvastatin or placebo, 1997-2001
quote: 2838 patients aged 40-75 years in 132 centres in the UK and Ireland were randomised to placebo (n=1410) or atorvastatin 10 mg daily (n=1428).
note: From the abstract of the main trial report, PMID:15325833. PMID:25899452 agrees ('the total CARDS study population consisted of 2,838 type 2 diabetic men and women, aged 40–75 years') and analysed CRP in 2,322; the example study PMID:27174798 used the 2838 CARDS patients for external validation.

label: Cholesterol and Recurrent Events
counts: patients randomised (3583 men, 576 women)
quote: In a double-blind trial lasting five years we administered either 40 mg of pravastatin per day or placebo to 4159 patients (3583 men and 576 women) with myocardial infarction who had plasma total cholesterol levels below 240 mg per deciliter (mean, 209) and low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels of 115 to 174 mg per deciliter (mean, 139).
note: Main results paper. The 1995 baseline paper (PMID:7572695) also says 4,159 were randomly assigned; the 1991 design paper (PMID:1746424) gives the planned 4,000. The example study (PMID:25748612) says a genetic substudy included 1,999 individuals.

label: Childhood Asthma Research and Education Network
counts: member counts only: CARE Network trials (PEAK, CLIC, PACT reviewed)
quote: Therefore, PACT enrolled 285 children (ages 6–14 years) with mild-to-moderate persistent asthma based on symptoms, but who all purposefully had baseline FEV1≥80% predicted.
note: A clinical research network of trials; no source read gives a pooled number of participants across its trials. The 2006 review (PMID:17141853) describes three CARE Network trials (PEAK, CLIC, PACT) and gives the PACT enrolment (285); the PEAK design paper (PMID:15157730) abstract gives no number. The example GWAS (PMID:22792082) used 207 non-Hispanic white CARE subjects from CLIC, PACT and MARS (analysed subset). A network-level summary of all its trials would settle it.

label: Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial
counts: participants randomised (smokers, former smokers and asbestos-exposed workers)
quote: The Beta-Carotene and Retinol Efficacy Trial (CARET) tested the effect of daily beta-carotene (30 mg) and retinyl palmitate (25,000 IU) on the incidence of lung cancer, other cancers, and death in 18,314 participants who were at high risk for lung cancer because of a history of smoking or asbestos exposure.
note: The 1996 main results paper (PMID:8602180) also gives a total of 18,314. Earlier accrual reports: 8129 randomised by July 1991 of 18,000 needed (PMID:1844268); 1,845 pilot plus 13,260 efficacy participants by April 1993, and a projected 14,420 smokers and 4,010 asbestos-exposed participants (PMID:8137335).

label: Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness
counts: patients with schizophrenia randomised in phase 1
quote: A total of 1493 patients with schizophrenia were recruited at 57 U.S. sites and randomly assigned to receive olanzapine (7.5 to 30 mg per day), perphenazine (8 to 32 mg per day), quetiapine (200 to 800 mg per day), or risperidone (1.5 to 6.0 mg per day) for up to 18 months.
note: Phase 1 results paper; 1432 received at least one dose. The GWAS paper (PMID:18347602) says 1,894 subjects were evaluated and 1,460 entered CATIE, and genotyped 738 CATIE cases (analysed subset). The example study (PMID:42473435) analysed 1334 participants.

label: Comorbidity and Trauma Study
counts: heroin-dependent cases and neighbourhood controls in the candidate-gene study
quote: A total of 1459 Australian cases ascertained from opioid replacement therapy clinics, 531 neighborhood controls ascertained from economically disadvantaged areas near opioid replacement therapy clinics, and 1495 unrelated Australian Twin Registry controls not dependent on alcohol or illicit drugs selected from a twin and family sample.
note: The 1495 Australian Twin Registry controls in the quote are not CATS participants. No source read states the whole study's recruited total with a case/control split; other CATS papers give: 1513 heroin-dependent participants interviewed (PMID:20833480), 1511 opioid-dependent individuals (PMID:21134015), 1484 with interviews and blood (PMID:24690055), 1459 cases and 531 neighbourhood controls (OPRD1 study PMID:22500942), 1439 cases and 507 controls with BPD data (PMID:23245376), and 'CATS; N = 1981' as a replication sample (PMID:26688007). dbGaP phs000277 gives 6487 consented subjects, but that includes other studies' controls. The example study (PMID:30482948) uses CATS as one of 28 alcohol dependence datasets. A CATS design paper would settle the recruited total.

label: Croatian Colorectal Cancer Genetic Study
counts: colorectal cancer cases and population controls genotyped genome-wide (analysed set)
quote: Finally, a case–control CRC study from Croatia consisting of 764 cases and 460 population-based controls was also included in the analysis.
note: From the example study (vitamin D Mendelian randomisation), the most recent statement read; no total stated. The 2013 candidate-gene paper (PMID:24066093) recruited 338 cases from November 2008 to July 2009 (18 excluded) and analysed 320 cases and 594 controls from '10,001 Dalmatians'. The 2019 GWAS (PMID:31089142) gives Croatia's numbers only in Supplementary Data 2 (not read). A study profile would settle the enrolled total.

label: Cambridgeshire Case-Control Study
counts: type 2 diabetes cases and matched controls in the collection
quote: The Cambridgeshire Case-Control Population (Poulton et al. 2002; Halsall et al. 2003) consists of a collection of 517 Type 2 diabetics and 517 matched controls.
note: No source read states the total. The 2002 mtDNA paper (PMID:12045211) analysed n=932; the example study (PMID:22039354) included 506 cases and 512 controls (white Europeans with DNA and BMI, analysed subset). The same 2003 paper mentions a planned 500 cases and 500 controls in its power calculation.

label: Cleveland Clinic GeneBank Study
counts: GeneBank participants included in the example analysis
quote: The present analysis included a total of 9,880 GeneBank participants in the score derivation using the XGBoost algorithm, 8,987 of which had DASI score calculated.
note: The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT00590200 (API, read this session) gives enrollment count 9880, type ACTUAL, matching this number, and a target of 15,000 in its description; the quote is from the example study because the registry gives the number only as a data field. Other sources give analysed subsets: n=8,668 with complete clinical data (PMID:26822151), 6575 Ohio residents (PMID:27468926).

label: Cleveland Clinic FMD Biorepository
counts: unrelated adults with multifocal FMD enrolled 2010-2015
quote: The processed DNA samples were batched and transferred to the University of Michigan for GWAS analysis.Between 2010 and 2015, adult subjects with mFMD (Nunrelated = 412) were enrolled with IRB approval in the Cleveland Clinic FMD Biorepository.
note: The quote's span begins with the end of the previous sentence (run together in the XML text). The count is of unrelated subjects, so the biorepository's full enrolment may be slightly larger; 131 had at least one arterial dissection and 28 had SCAD. The 2021 FMD GWAS (PMID:34654805) pools Cleveland Clinic cases with Michigan cases (UM/CCF) and gives no Cleveland-only count in sentences read.

label: Crete Cancer Genetics Program
counts: samples received for OncoArray genotyping (cases and controls)
quote: CCGP Crete Cancer Genetics Program Hospital-based case-control study Greece 366 728 332 681 0 0
note: A row of Supplementary Table 1 of the 2017 BCAC OncoArray paper (doi:10.1038/nature24284), whose columns are 'Samples received for OncoArray genotyping' (controls, cases) then 'Sample size post QC excluding samples previously genotyped' for European ancestry (controls 332, cases 681) and Asian ancestry (0, 0). These are samples sent for genotyping, not the study's own enrolment; no sentence states a total. The PREDICT paper (PMID:37173335, Table 7) lists CCGP with 8 BRCA1, 2 BRCA2 and 387 non-carrier patients (analysed subset). No CCGP design paper was found; one would settle the enrolled numbers.

label: China Cardiovascular Health Study
note: No source read states the study's own enrolled total. The 2014 blood pressure GWAS (PMID:25249183, Table 1) lists two CCHS replication samples, 'Replication 2 CCHS-1 22896' and 'Replication 3 CCHS-2 34142' (analysed samples, table rows, not summed here). The 2012 CAD GWAS (PMID:22751097) says CCHS has been a population-based investigation since 2006 and drew controls from its northern field centres, without a count. The example study (PMID:26250998) gives 27,020 baseline participants (1998-2001) for CCHS and ChinaMUCA combined, which is not CCHS alone and whose dates do not match the 2006 start, so the name may cover more than one survey. A CCHS design paper would settle it.

label: Cross Cancer Institute Prostate Brachytherapy Cohort
counts: men treated with 125I brachytherapy monotherapy who gave saliva DNA
quote: Genomic DNA from 296 men treated with (125)I prostate brachytherapy monotherapy was extracted from saliva samples for this study.
note: The cohort's own 2014 paper (abstract read; full text not on disk); 217 of the 296 had at least 2 years of follow-up. The example study's supplement (PMID:29892016, doi:10.1038/s41588-018-0142-8, table row) lists CCI with 285 cases sent and 270 after QC; the 2019 radiogenomics meta-analysis (PMID:31095341) included 252 CCI-BT patients (analysed subsets).

label: Connecticut Endometrial Cancer Study
counts: incident endometrial cancer cases and population controls enrolled
quote: The study enrolled 668 incident cases and 674 population controls.
note: No source read states the combined total. The 2012 omega-3 paper (PMID:22915050) repeats 668 cases (54.9%) and 674 controls (64.5%) enrolled and analysed 556 cases and 533 controls; the example study (PMID:27409342) repeats 668/674 and used 482 cases and 571 controls in the GWAS (analysed subset).

label: Besta Cerebrovascular Diseases Registry
counts: ischaemic stroke cases genotyped for METASTROKE (analysed subset)
quote: Milano 372 25 74 65 407 European Cross-sectional Illumina 610/660
note: A row of Table 1 of the example study (PMID:23041239, METASTROKE), columns: cases 372, cardioembolic 25, large-vessel 74, small-vessel 65, controls 407; the 407 controls are Italian PROCARDIS participants, not registry members, so they are not recorded as controls here. This is the genotyped subset, not the registry's total enrolment of consecutive stroke patients 2000-2009, which no source read states; the EuroCLOT paper (PMID:23381943) names CEDIR without a count. A Europe PMC search for the registry found no design paper. A CEDIR description would settle it.

label: Central and Eastern European Renal Cell Carcinoma Study
counts: incident renal cell carcinoma cases and hospital controls
quote: In a case-control study of kidney cancer in four central European countries, with 1097 incident cases and 1476 controls, we found an increased risk for self-reported hypertension and for obesity.
note: No source read states the combined total. The same counts are given in PMID:21540858 and PMID:19753122, which adds that DNA was obtained from 987 cases and 1,298 controls. The example study (PMID:22113997) pools CEERCC with other studies (2278 cases, 3719 controls in total).

label: CEFALO
counts: cases and controls interviewed
quote: We conducted interviews, in person, with 352 case patients (participation rate: 83%) and 646 control subjects (participation rate: 71%) and their parents.
note: Main CEFALO results paper; PMID:23652309 gives the same 352 cases and 646 controls. No source read states the combined total. Saliva DNA was genotyped for 245 cases and 489 controls (PMID:26014354; example study PMID:31792337).

label: Color Genomics
counts: clinical cohort sequenced by low-coverage WGS (analysed subset)
quote: The clinical cohort included DNA samples from 11,502 individuals whose healthcare provider had ordered a Color multi-gene panel test (Fig. 1b).
note: An analysed subset from a definition source (PMID:31771638), not the size of Color's whole research cohort, which no source read states. The example study (PMID:32820175) used 1920 breast cancer cases and 17,344 controls, all female, from Color (another subset). A Color cohort description or company statement of consented research participants would settle it.

label: Candidate Gene Association Resource
counts: participants of the nine cohorts in the CARe genotype-phenotype database (approximate)
quote: A database of genotype and phenotype data was created that includes records for approximately 41,000 study participants with approximately 50,000 SNPs from more than 2,000 selected candidate genes.
note: dbGaP description of the MESA CARe substudy, which describes CARe as a whole; the same page says the GWAS covered approximately 8,900 African American participants from ARIC, CARDIA, CFS, JHS and MESA. The CARe design paper (PMID:20400780) says 'more than 40,000 participants' in nine cohorts and a planned GWAS in ~8,000 African Americans (a lower bound, so not recorded).

label: Copenhagen General Population Study
counts: adults enrolled since 2003 (approximate, enrolment ongoing)
quote: The Copenhagen General Population Study Adults (≥20 years) from the Copenhagen area enrolled since 2003 (~160,000)
note: A table row in the 2023 review of Danish biobanks (PMID:36852012, a definition source), footnoted 'Ongoing enrollment'; it may include second-round examinees. Analysed subsets in other sources: 107301 adults enrolled 2003-2015 (PMID:36891075), 94184 with dietary information (PMID:36214322). No CGPS cohort profile was found on Europe PMC; one would settle the baseline total.

label: China Multi-Center Collaborative Study of Cardiovascular Epidemiology 1998
counts: participants aged 35-59 selected by cluster sampling in 1998 (11 clusters)

label: ChooseWell 365

label: Children's Health Study
counts: school children enrolled across all recruitment waves since 1993 (lower bound)

The website timeline says about 3,600 students joined in 1993, 2,100 fourth graders in 1996, over 5,600 kindergarten and first graders in 2002 and over 300 first graders a year later; PMID:20371422 says 5,349 children were enrolled into the 2002-2003 cohort. The website's figure is used as the most recent and inclusive statement.

label: Copenhagen Ischemic Heart Disease Study
counts: IHD patients referred 1991-2009 plus controls from the CGPS

PMID:22698489 (PMC4606982): 5,109 patients referred in 1991 to 2010 and 10,231 controls ascertained as for the CGPS (Table 1 n 15,340). PMID:25406188: patients referred in 1991-2011, of whom 6363 were included with all genotypes. label: Mayo Clinic Center for the Individualized Treatment of Alcoholism Study

The example study PMID:30482948 (PGC alcohol dependence GWAS) gives no count for this study in the text read.

PMID:25809130 (2015) used 302 cases and 676 controls; PMID:39736759 (2024) used 72 cases and 18 controls recruited 2013-2017. A current CLARITY recruitment total would settle it.

An earlier BCAC paper, PMID:21194473 (PMC3046455) Table 1, lists CNIO-BCS with 649 controls and 351 cases included in at least one analysis. The definition source PMID:25390939 and example study PMID:32424353 name the study only in funding and acknowledgements. A CNIO-BCS design paper would settle the enrolled numbers.

counts: patients recruited across all sites by April 2018 (lower bound)

Later papers give analysed subsets only, e.g. PMID:39373623 (2025) included 2,216 stage I-IV patients with recurrence and mortality data. The example study PMID:25472670 used 35 Heidelberg patients. A current recruitment total from the study would update this.

label: Colorectal cancer: Longitudinal, Observational study on Nutritional and lifestyle factors that influence colorectal tumour recurrence, survival and quality of life

PMID:41212533 analysed 1596 stage I-III participants; the example study PMID:29917119 and PMID:30510241 give no COLON-specific count in the text read.

label: Post-Columbian Study of Environmental and Heritable Causes of Breast Cancer
counts: Colombian arm only: cases diagnosed 2011-2017 and controls in the 2024 PRS analysis
quote: In the COLUMBUS-Colombia study, we included 955 breast cancer cases diagnosed from 2011 to 2017, ages 21 to 88 years, and 1,053 controls who did not have first-degree relatives with breast cancer and matched controls with cases by recruiting hospital, education level, socioeconomic status, and local origin data.
note: From PMC11799839 full text, the most recent source. The same paper gives the Mexican arm separately: 'In the COLUMBUS-Mexico study, we included 535 cases diagnosed with breast cancer from 2010 to 2018 at the Social Security Hospital in Mexico City, ages 24 to 89 years, and 887 controls matched by recruiting hospital (11).' No sentence gives a total across arms, so participants is left null and only the Colombian arm is in cases/controls. PMID:25327703 validated in '546 Colombian women with breast cancer and 440 Colombian women without breast cancer'; the example study PMID:31553449 lists COLUMBUS in its Table 1 without a count in the sentences read. These are analysed (genotyped) sets; a COLUMBUS design paper would give recruitment totals.

label: Consortium for the Investigation of Renal Malignancies
counts: registry-identified RCC cases (diagnosed 2009-2015) who consented; controls not counted
quote: Of the 3113 individuals diagnosed with RCC who were invited to participate in CONFIRM, 1424 provided consent.
note: From PMC11393909 full text (2024); 1029 of them were sequenced. No source read gives the number of sibling and partner controls enrolled, the high-risk family participants, or a study total. PMID:34562747 (abstract; full text closed at Cancer Epidemiol) analysed 1064 cases and 724 controls. The Cancer Council Victoria page (web archive, 2022) says recruitment is closed but gives no numbers. The example study PMID:28598434 (RCC GWAS meta-analysis) gives no CONFIRM-specific count in the sentences read.

label: Danish National Patient Register
counts: distinct persons registered at least once, 1977-2012

note: From the registry's profile paper (PMC4655913 full text); the preceding sentence gives the period: 'During 1977–2012, the cumulative Danish population numbered 8,342,199 persons.' The abstract states the same 8,085,603 persons for 1977-2012, with 7,268,857 inpatient, 5,953,405 outpatient and 5,097,300 emergency department contacts (numbers of persons). The register is ongoing, so the count has grown since 2012; the Danish Health Data Authority page was not needed. The example study PMID:3738950 was not consulted for a count.

quote: The present analyses focus on a substantially smaller subsample of the full DNS sample (N = 1332) because the measure of caregiving was added to the DNS protocol during the final year of data collection.

label: Dubbo Osteoporosis Epidemiology Study
counts: men and women aged 60+ recruited 1989-2020 (approximate)

note: An approximate figure from a 2024 analysis paper, covering the study's whole run (1989-2020, including the second recruitment from 2000); its flow chart gives 'N=4,000 Women(2,245),Men(1,760)'. PMID:15727686 (2005) says 'By mid 2003, 2560 subjects aged 60+ have participated in the study' and gives the 1989 eligible population as 1,581 men and 2095 women aged 60 or over. A DOES cohort profile would settle the exact number.

counts: women enrolled 1990-1993 (randomised and non-randomised arms)

The design paper PMID:10340280 abstract gives 501 allocated to HRT and 505 to no treatment in the randomised arm and 219 and 791 in the non-randomised arm. The whole enrolled cohort is recorded since the study is the cohort, not only its randomised arm.

counts: interviewed cases and controls, 2002-2009

No source read states the combined total, so participants is null. The example study PMID:42365137 also says DOVE 'enrolled 1502 ovarian cancer cases ages 35–74 years'. PMID:19240718 used 584 DOVE cases and 716 controls (a genotyped subset).

counts: persons registered with psychiatric treatment

The full text of the 2011 register description (Scand J Public Health, PMID:21775352) or a later iPSYCH/register overview stating the number of persons ever registered would settle it.

label: Danish Pelvic Mass Study
counts: patients with preoperative serum in the ongoing study (as of about 2012)
quote: Serum from 1218 patients in the prospective ongoing pelvic mass study was collected prior to diagnosis.
note: The study is ongoing and no source read gives its total enrolment; this is the largest count seen, from a 2012 diagnostic paper using the study's serum. The definition source PMID:22363532 says 'From September 2004 559 women admitted to the Gynecologic Clinic, Rigshospitalet, Denmark for surgery because of a pelvic mass, were enrolled.' The example study PMID:27418945 says 246 EOC patients were included 2004-2010. A recent overview of the Pelvic Mass Study would settle the number.

counts: colorectal cancer cases and matched controls from the Ontario Familial Colorectal Cancer Registry

note: The design GWAS PMID:17618283 abstract gives the same stage-1 sample: 'we genotyped 99,632 SNPs in 1,257 affected individuals and 1,336 controls from Ontario.' The example study's abstract rounds it to 1,200 cases 'and a similar number' of controls. The GWAS supplement mentions 'the total of 2493 genotyped samples' with 2465 analysed (1239 controls, 1226 cases), apparently a genotyping stage, unclear. No source read states the combined total, so participants is null.

counts: participants enrolled under the BCCR protocol NCT00666731, 2006-2016 (actual enrolment)
quote: "enrollmentInfo":{"count":4945,"type":"ACTUAL"}
note: ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT00666731, official title 'Development and Implementation of The Breast Cancer Collaborative Registry (BCCR)', University of Nebraska, started 2006-10-12 and completed 2016-08-19; enrolment after 2016 continued under iCaRe2 (NCT02012699) and is not counted here. The example study's N=4,219 is the cohort as used in its analysis; PMID:39537796 says a questionnaire was sent to all BDRN participants in current contact, 'just under 4000 participants' (not a number); PMID:38355785 used BDRN N = 2577; PMID:39879180 used 2524 BD cases and 4106 controls from BDRN in the PGC (controls are not BDRN participants). A CEDAR design paper stating the number of individuals enrolled would settle it.

note: PMID:38030128 agrees: '2895 unrelated subjects of Chinese ancestry were selected randomly by their telephone numbers from the Hong Kong population, and invited to undergo a comprehensive assessment in 1995–1996.' These are the samples genotyped for this replication, not necessarily every subject of the study. PMID:25187374 used 474 non-diabetic CUHKS subjects for fasting glucose ('CUHK CUHKS Han Chinese Sequenom MassARRAY 474'). No design paper of the study was read.

label: Chennai Urban Rural Epidemiology Study
counts: adults screened for diabetes in the baseline survey, 2001-2003

note: The same paper says 'In brief, CURES was done on a representative sample of 26001 adults from Chennai city, aged ≥20 years.' and that the diabetic participants (n = 1382) and every tenth participant (n = 2207) formed the follow-up cohort (n = 3589). The 2003 design paper abstract (PMID:14710970) says 'Twenty thousand and one individuals were recruited for the study', which disagrees with the later 26001; the later, achieved figure is recorded. The example study (PMID:15277424) used 600 diabetic subjects.

label: China Pulmonary Thromboembolism Registry Study
counts: eligible patients enrolled, 2009 to 31 December 2019
quote: Up to 31 December 2019, the CURES has enrolled 14,937 eligible patients and collected 1500 blood samples of patients from 100 medical centers in the China PE-DVT network.
note: From the design paper's abstract (full text not on disk). PMID:35242828 analysed 'a total of 7,438 consecutive adult patients with acute PE' included between January 2009 and December 2015. The example GWAS (PMID:37076872) recruited PE cases from 2016 to 2020 (624 in discovery). The registry is ongoing, so the count grows.

label: CVPath Institute Sudden Cardiac Death registry
counts: hearts of sudden-death cases referred January 1995 to December 2015
quote: Between January 1995 and December 2015, CVPath Institute was referred 5262 hearts from cases of unexpected sudden death from the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner of the State of Maryland (OCME-MD).
note: From PMID:34076677. A later paper (PMID:37916415, abstract) gives a different referral count for a similar period: 'From 4327 subjects referred to CVPath by the State of Maryland Office Chief Medical Examiner for sudden death between 1994 and 2015, 2455 cases were randomly selected for genotyping.' The difference is not explained in what was read (possibly different inclusion rules), hence low confidence. The example study (PMID:34039022) genotyped 764 African American subjects. The registry is ongoing; no registry profile stating a total was found.

label: Cleveland Clinic Foundation/Veteran Affairs Medical Center Cohort
counts: AMD cases and controls studied in 2010 (no total stated)
quote: We studied 1037 individuals with AMD subcategorized using AREDS criteria and 370 control subjects without retinal disease.
note: No source read states a single total, so participants is null (summing is not allowed). PMID:20042177 also says '661 patients were obtained from CEI and 376 patients were obtained from the VA' and that 84 controls came from CEI and 286 from the VA; its 1037 'patients' include 132 AREDS Category 1 subjects. In the 2013 AMDGene follow-up (PMID:23455636, Supplementary Table 1) the CCF/VAMC row gives 628 cases and 568 controls ('CCF/VAMC 628 51.1% 64.5% 12.3% 23.2% 568 27.6% 19.'), cases restricted to AREDS groups 3-5. The 2016 example study (PMID:26691988) does not give a per-study count in the text on disk.

note: From the Supplementary Note of PMID:29273806 (TAGC). No single total is stated, so participants is null (summing is not allowed). The same note says 'The 517 controls were selected from the COPACETIC study' for the case-control phase. The earlier DAG GWAS papers were not read.

The definition says enrolment from 2005, the paper says 2006.

note: The only numbers found are the DFCI contribution to PanScan III (PMID:25086665, Supplementary Table 1): 360 cases analysed in stage 1; the QC table gives 'DFCI 405 11 1 2 1 25 5 360' (405 genotyped, 360 after exclusions), and 12 DFCI cases appear in replication group A. These count only the cases the GWAS used, not the whole clinic case series; no description of the full series size was found.

PMID:38728232 says 'In the first follow-up survey in 2013, 38,295 participants completed questionnaires, health examinations, and blood samples collection'. The example study (PMID:23864233) used the baseline 27,009 ('we recruited 87 % (n = 27,009 out of 31,000) of retired employees').

label: Danish HIV Cohort Study
counts: all cohort patients seen 1995-2004
quote: The study population included all 4,025 patients from The Danish HIV Cohort Study seen during the period 1995-2004.
note: The cohort is open and ongoing, so this 2004 count is out of date; the 2009 cohort profile (PMID:18799495) and the 2014 profile update (PMID:25074406) are closed (publisher returned 403) and would give later totals. Other numbers seen are analysis subsets: 4,984 Danish-born HIV-infected individuals 1996-2009 (PMID:22984529); 4168 Danish-born PWH on ART without IDU or HCV, 1995-2021 (PMID:38966335); groups of 871, 704, 379 and 313 patients (PMID:21799935). A web search result mentioned 6,327 PLWH in a cancer study (PMID:37755422), which is also a subset and was not read.

label: Danish National Health Service Register
counts: whole Danish population (no number stated)
note: The register description (PMID:21775348, abstract only on disk) says 'The register covers everyone living in Denmark and data is available from 1990.' but gives no number of people. The full text of PMID:21775348 (Scand J Public Health 2011) might give a count of persons or services.

PMID:27010749 says 'n=2808 breast cancer patients were recruited onto the study (new protocol)', a subset under the revised protocol; PMID:23664318 analysed 1797 women with complete data. The ClinicalTrials.gov record was not on disk.

The example study (PMID:42231601) analysed 1,806 high-confidence DILI cases enrolled 9/2004 to 7/2023. label: European Collaborative Study
counts: cHL cases and controls in the 2012 European GWAS (no total stated)
quote: We conducted a genome-wide association study of 1200 cHL patients and 6417 control subjects, with validation in an independent replication series, to identify common genetic variants associated with total cHL and subtypes defined by tumor EBV status.
note: Cohort aggregation: cases came from five European HL studies. No pooled total of cases plus controls is stated, so participants is null (summing is not allowed). The 2012 paper also says DNA was available for '1238 cHL patients' and '1395 study-specific control subjects', and 'genome-wide data from a total of 6466 control subjects were assembled'. The 2014 meta-analysis (PMID:24920014) describes it differently: 'The European Collaborative Study, presented elsewhere, included 1,241 HL cases aged 13–80 (median age = 33 years) from five European-based HL studies and 5,726 generic controls aged 17–94 (mean age = 62) used in the initial GWAS scan.'

The largest, from the example study, is given here as cases and controls; participants left null because no sentence states the total. The Belfast/Glasgow extension study recruited 696 cases and 561 controls of both sexes (PMID:11040019). The original design paper (the 1992 Nature ACE paper or PMID:1534257 full text) might state the recruited total.

Papers give only the EUDRAGENE cases they used: 19 statin myopathy cases (13 severe) in the example study (PMID:31220337), 19 amoxicillin-clavulanate DILI cases (25 included before QC) in PMID:21570397. The 2020 recruitment statement is taken as the most recent description of the whole sample.

label: Familial Breast Cancer Study

quote: Three thousand nine hundred and sixty breast cancer cases were used in stage 1, of which 3,652 were from cancer genetics clinics in the UK recruited through the Familial Breast Cancer Study (FBCS) and 308 were from oncology clinics in the UK recruited through the Prospective study of Outcomes in Sporadic versus Hereditary breast cancer (POSH) study.
note: No source read states how many index cases the FBCS has recruited since 1995. The example study (PMID:20453838) used 3,652 FBCS cases in stage 1 and, in stage 2, 'the Familial Breast Cancer Study (FBCS), consisting of additional cases ascertained through UK cancer genetics clinics (n = 2,009)'; the two are not summed here. FBCS has no controls of its own (the GWAS used 1958 Birth Cohort and NBS controls). A later FBCS description or the ICR website might give the total recruited.

label: Finnish Colorectal Cancer Predisposition Study
counts: consecutive colorectal cancer patients in the series
quote: To identify susceptibility genes for this common phenotype, we examined familial cases derived from a consecutive series of 1514 Finnish CRC patients.
note: Most recent statement of the size of the consecutive patient series (2013). Earlier: the 1994-1998 collection gave 535 patients in PMID:10829038 plus 'a previous study of 509 patients' (1,044 cases together, as that abstract states). The example study (PMID:21655089) says 'The Helsinki (FCCPS) study ... comprised 988 cases from a population-based collection centred on south-eastern Finland and 864 population controls from the same collection'. The blood-donor controls are not a counted part of the patient series.

label: Finnish Genetic Study of Arrhythmic Events
counts: consecutive autopsy-verified sudden cardiac death victims 1998-2017
quote: The study population is derived from the Fingesture study, which has collected data from 5869 consecutive autopsy-verified SCD victims in Northern Finland (population ≈600 000) between 1998 and 2017.
note: The same 5869 is given in 2024-2025 Fingesture papers (PMID:38476977, PMID:40590619). This counts the SCD victims (cases) only; no source read states the number of acute coronary event survivors used as controls, so the count excludes them. The ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT02075866 (fetched from the v2 API) gives an estimated enrollment count of 8000, a planned figure.

label: FIRE-3
counts: patients with KRAS exon 2 wild-type tumours randomised and treated
quote: Between Jan 23, 2007, and Sept 19, 2012, 592 patients with KRAS exon 2 wild-type tumours were randomly assigned and received treatment (297 in the FOLFIRI plus cetuximab group and 295 in the FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab group).
note: Primary publication of the trial (Lancet Oncology 2014). This is the KRAS exon 2 wild-type intention-to-treat population the definition describes; the full text (closed, not on disk) may also report patients randomised before the protocol was restricted to KRAS wild-type, which are not counted here. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00433927 (v2 API) gives an estimated enrollment count of 568. The example study (PMID:40141198) genotyped 236 FIRE-3 patients (107 bevacizumab, 129 cetuximab).

The HUGR website (hugr.huji.ac.il) did not respond.

counts: no count found

counts: no count found
