At the 2023-2024 wave, 2,350 completed postal questionnaires, 1,519 did tests and 1,388 gave blood. The HAPIEE design paper (PMID:17049075) gives no Czech count in the text read.

label: International Lipid-Based Nutrient Supplements Project-DYAD-Malawi
counts: pregnant women enrolled and randomised from 2011
quote: We enrolled 1391 women with uncomplicated pregnancies
note: Main birth-size trial paper (abstract; the full text was not downloaded). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01239693 (API v2 record) gives actual enrollment 1391, start 2011-02. Their infants are not counted separately in the text read. The example study (PMID:41775864) used 40 iLiNS-DYAD-M children.

label: New Hampshire Birth Cohort Study
counts: women enrolled (more than), with over 1,500 children
quote: Today our study has over 1,500 women and 1,500 children from New Hampshire and Vermont participating in this important study.
note: Website figure is a lower bound and undated. The example study (PMID:27825389) says 'As of May 1, 2016, a total of 1473 participants had enrolled in the NHBCS'; it analysed 1151 women.

label: Shanghai Dapuqiao Aging and Cognition Study
counts: eligible participants of wave 1 (2019)
quote: Data were collected across three examination waves in 2019, 2022, and 2024, with 2287, 1518, and 3554 eligible participants included after exclusions, respectively.
note: The waves are mostly separate cross-sectional samples (only 163 people took part more than once), and no source read gives the number of distinct people across all waves. The catalogue's 'Number of participants' field is 2287, matching wave 1, which is recorded here; wave 3 (2024) had 3554. The example study (PMID:41606232) says the 2019 study 'recruited 2287 adults' aged 60 and older from Dapuqiao Street.

label: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe
counts: people aged 50+ interviewed since 2004 (all waves, 28 countries and Israel)
quote: From 2004 until today, 530,000 in-depth interviews with 140,000 people aged 50 or older from 28 European countries and Israel have been conducted.
note: Website's cumulative figure (undated, current page). The 2013 cohort profile (PMID:23778574) says after four waves 'more than 150 000 interviews have been conducted with about 86 000 respondents aged 50 years and over and their (younger) partners in 19 countries'; superseded by the later count.

label: Harmonized Diagnostic Assessment of Dementia for the Longitudinal Aging Study in India
counts: participants of Wave 2 (follow-up plus refresher sample), 2022-2024
quote: A total of 4635 participants were recruited between 2022 and 2024 from 22 states and union territories of India, accounting for 97.9% of the population in India.
note: Wave 2 design paper. The website (https://lasi-dad.org/about/overview) says 'we recruited a sub-sample of 4,000+ LASI respondents aged 60 and older from 18 states and union territories across the country in Wave 1'. No cumulative count of everyone ever enrolled across both waves was found; Wave 2 comprises Wave 1 follow-ups and a refresher sample.

label: Hokkaido Study on Environment and Children's Health
counts: pregnant women of the Hokkaido cohort only (the larger of the two sub-cohorts)
quote: This cohort consists of 20,926 pregnant women.
note: The study has two cohorts; the 2021 profile update gives them separately and no total: the Hokkaido cohort (20,926 pregnant women, 2003-2012, 37 clinics/hospitals) and the Sapporo cohort ('The subjects included 514 pregnant women who enrolled at 23–35 weeks of gestation and delivered at Toho hospital.'). The number here is the Hokkaido cohort only; no source read states the whole study's total. The Global Exposome catalogue entry also gives 'Number of participants 20926'.

label: GINIplus/LISA North
counts: children of GINIplus and LISA in the Wesel (North) area, as listed by the catalogue
quote: Number of participants 3390
note: Catalogue field (the page's description gives only the whole cohorts: 'In GINIplus, 5,991 healthy full-term newborns of European ancestry were enrolled between 1995 and 1998, in LISA, 3,097 between 1997 and 1999, across four study areas'). Analysed subsets: 2497 children in GINI/LISA North with health and greenness data (PMID:24862831, 'Health and NDVI data for at least one time point were available for 3306 children in GINI/LISA South and 2497 children in GINI/LISA North.') and 2,460 in the ESCAPE analysis (PMID:24149084, Table 1). The Wesel recruitment numbers in the GINIplus and LISA design papers would settle it.

label: Walnuts Smart Snack Dietary Intervention Trial
counts: adolescents randomised
quote: After data collection, 771 participants were equally randomized in two groups (386/385), but because of some exclusions post-randomization, 748 were finally included.
note: Design paper of the trial. Same paper: 748 finally included after post-randomisation exclusions; 270 in the blood/urine subsample. The example study (PMID:35960396) says 'We recruited 771 participants over a 12-month period (2015–2016) in 11 high schools of Barcelona' and analysed 372. The Global Exposome catalogue gives numberOfParticipants 724 (not used).

label: GENOBOX study
counts: children and adolescents in the cohort, as listed in the catalogue
quote: Number of participants 1775
note: Catalogue entry filled by the cohort (data collection 1998 until 2015). PMID:35596598 (2022): 'A sample of 1599 children and adolescents (48.5% males and 70.6% with overweight/obesity) participated in the GENOBOX multicenter case control study, carried out in three Spanish cities: Córdoba, Santiago de Compostela and Zaragoza.' PMID:33171599 analysed 793 children. No source read gives separate case and control totals; no design paper was read.

label: Rio Birth Cohort Study on Environmental Exposure and Childhood Development
counts: pregnant women enrolled in the pilot phase only (135 children born)
quote: A pilot study (PIPA Pilot study) was carried out between September 2017 and August 2018, with 142 pregnant women enrolled in and 135 children born at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro Maternity School [24].
note: Only the pilot's size is stated in anything read. The design paper (PMID:32566487) gives the planned main cohort: 'The estimated population is of 2,500 children.' and the pilot's 142 of 209 invited women. The project website (https://pipaufrj.me.ufrj.br/sobre/) gives no count; a 2025 paper (PMC11906608) also uses only the 2017-2018 pilot. An achieved size for the full cohort would settle it.

label: Programming Research in Obesity, Growth, Environment and Social Stressors
counts: mothers enrolled in pregnancy who gave birth to a live child
quote: A total of 948 mothers were enrolled in pregnancy and gave birth to a live child.
note: From the example study, not a design paper; it counts mother-child pairs with a live birth, not every woman enrolled in pregnancy. The same paper analysed 434 children. The Mount Sinai page (https://mountsinaiexposomics.org/progress/) gives no count; the Global Exposome catalogue gives numberOfParticipants 1140 (API field, not read as text). The PROGRESS design paper would settle the number of women enrolled.

label: Infants' Environmental Health Study
counts: pregnant women enrolled
quote: We enrolled 451 pregnant women from Matina County, Costa Rica, which has large-scale banana production.
note: Baseline paper; the example study (PMID:29847083) agrees: 'A total of 451 women were enrolled in the ISA study.' and analysed 355 mother-child pairs.

label: Multi-Partner Consortium to Expand Dementia Research in Latin America
counts: participants enrolled (retrospective and prospective cohorts) as of 17 August 2024
quote: As of August 17, 2024, a total of 5834 participants had been enrolled in the study (Fig. 1).
note: Genomics paper of ReDLat; 2162 of those had genomic data after QC. The 2021 design paper (PMID:33776890) gives the plan: 'totaling > 4,200 participants, including 2,100 controls, 1,050 AD patients, and 1,050 FTD patients', including US samples. The example study (PMID:42251497) analysed 3941 individuals. No achieved case/control split for all enrolled participants was found.

label: Sustainable plant protection transition: a global health approach
counts: subjects of the 2021 field study, as listed in the catalogue
quote: Number of participants 792
note: Catalogue entry filled by the study; its description says 'In total, samples from over 700 subjects were collected.' The field protocol (PMID:34780516) gives no achieved count; the example study (PMID:37838044, abstract only; publisher page not readable) analysed 128 indoor dust samples. A SPRINT human biomonitoring results paper would confirm.

label: Maule Cohort
counts: adults recruited 2014-2020
quote: The study recruited 9,462 adults aged 35–74 years between 2014 and 2020.
note: Cohort's own catalogue description (the age range stated there, 35-74, differs from the design paper's 38-74). The 2016 design paper (PMID:26847446) gives the plan: 'In this study, we are enrolling and following 10,000 adults aged 38 to 74 years over 10 years.' The example study (PMID:39343441) included 8948 participants in its baseline analyses.

label: Survey on Health, Well-Being, and Aging in Colombia
counts: older adults surveyed (effective surveys) in 244 municipalities
quote: A total of 36,153 older adults were found, of these 23,694 surveys were carried out, for a percentage of national effective response of 66% in 244 municipalities (Table 2).
note: Methodology paper; its abstract: '23,694 surveys were conducted, 17,189 in urban population (72.5%) and 6,505 in rural population.' PMID:27956896 agrees ('23.694 elderly Colombians'). The example study (PMID:31607766) analysed the grip-strength subsample of 4,474.

label: Encuesta Nacional de Situación Nutricional
counts: people interviewed in the 2015 round (44,202 households)
quote: La tercera Encuesta Nacional de Situación Nutricional de Colombia (ENSIN) 2015 es una operación estadística poblacional realizada entre noviembre de 2015 a diciembre de 2016, en la cual, se entrevistaron 151.343 personas de 44.202 hogares en 295 municipios del país.
note: Repeated cross-sectional survey; this is the most recent (2015) round only, and the page gives no counts for the 2005 and 2010 rounds. The example study (PMID:35070447) agrees: 'The ENSIN-2015 included 151,343 people.' and analysed 32,457 participants aged 1 to 64 years with dietary data.

label: Cohorts Consortium of Latin America and the Caribbean
counts: individuals pooled from 32 cohorts at the first datalock (29 March 2020)
quote: At the time of the first datalock, data from 174 180 individuals have been pooled: 171 937 (98.7%) have complete follow-up or were censored (e.g. lost-to follow-up or death by other causes), 578 (0.3%) have had a first non-fatal cardiovascular event and 1665 (1.0%) have experienced a fatal cardiovascular event (Table 1).
note: Cohort profile (2020): 'To date, the CC-LAC is therefore a consortium of 39 cohorts in 13 LAC countries', 32 of them pooled. The 2024 methods paper (PMID:39687239) says 'a combined sample size of >174 000 participants'. The example study (PMID:42724639) describes 'an initial pool of 35 cohorts (n = 147,949...)' and analysed 23,097 adults from 15 cohorts.

label: Ecuador Life
counts: newborns recruited 2006-2009
quote: A total of 2404 newborns were recruited between 2006 and 2009 in a public hospital serving the rural district of Quininde, Esmeraldas Province, in a tropical region of coastal Ecuador.
note: Cohort profile. The example study (PMID:24587469) agrees ('2,404 newborns ... were recruited at the District hospital between November 2005 and December 2009') and analysed 1,697 children with a stool sample at 3 years.

label: Banco Nacional de Tumores Terry Fox
counts: donors recruited 2011-2013, as listed in the catalogue
quote: Number of participants 2065
note: Catalogue field; the entry's description covers donors with cancer, without cancer and survivors recruited 'Entre 2011 y 2013' but gives no count in text. The biobank has taken donors outside that window too: PMID:39264897 used 38 breast cancer donors from 2007-2017, and PMID:40065011 986 patients referred for genetic counselling 2018-2020 whose samples went to the BNTTF. No source read gives the biobank's total number of donors; a BNTTF description paper or the institute's biobank page would settle it.

label: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study
counts: respondents in the 2011-2012 national baseline
quote: The national baseline survey for the study was conducted between June 2011 and March 2012 and involved 17 708 respondents.
note: Cohort profile. Same paper: 'A pilot survey for CHARLS was conducted in two provinces of China in 2008, on 2685 individuals, who were resurveyed in 2012.' and 10257 households at baseline. The CHARLS website (https://charls.pku.edu.cn/en/) gives the planned baseline ('about 10,000 households and 17,500 individuals'). Later refresher samples are not counted; no cumulative count across waves was found.

label: REal-time Assessment of Community Transmission
counts: people consenting to recontact and/or health-data linkage (stated as 'over 3 million')
quote: REACT Cohort is now made up of over 3 million people who have consented to follow-up by providing permission for us to contact them future research and/or to link to their health data.
note: Undated website figure, a lower bound. The definition sources read were abstracts only: PMID:37733993 (REACT-2) 'Overall, 905 991 tests were performed (28.9% response) over 6 rounds of data collection (June 2020-May 2021).'; PMID:36893367 (REACT-1 methods) gives no participant count in its abstract. The example study (PMID:41159539) is a qualitative interview study of REACT Long COVID.

label: 3xG study
counts: children followed in the cohort
quote: Dit gebeurt door onderzoek bij 301 opgroeiende kinderen uit de regio en door verwerking van de ziekte- en sterfteregisters van de drie gemeenten.
note: Study website (Dutch: 'This is done by studying 301 growing children from the region and by processing the disease and mortality registers of the three municipalities.'). PMID:36976969 used a subsample of 125 3xG participants; the example study (PMID:36006149) pools HBM4EU-aligned studies and gives no 3xG enrolment count in the text read. A 3xG design paper would confirm the number recruited at birth.

label: Cohort ’18, Growing Up in Hungary
counts: pregnant women who joined in the prenatal wave (2018-2019)
quote: By the end of this wave of our data collection, 8,287 expectants joined our study.
note: The same page says nearly 400 more mothers joined at the 6-month wave: 'Altogether almost 8,400 children were included in this phase of our research.' The example paper (PMID:37656714) gives the same prenatal count ('8287 women answered the questionnaire in the prenatal wave') and a planned final sample of 8600; the website home page says 'Approximately 9,000 children and their parents participate in the survey.' Later waves: about 5,000 mother-child pairs at 18 months, about 6,000 families at 3 years, about 5,500 children at 5 years.

label: COMmunity-based Behavior and Attitude survey in Tuvalu
counts: adults surveyed in the 2022 wave
quote: The COMmunity-based Behavior and Attitude survey in Tuvalu (COMBAT) collected data between February and May 2022 from 1030 adults (985 with complete data) from Funafuti, the main island, and the other 8 outlying islands [17].
note: COMBAT ran as repeated survey waves (2020, 2022) before becoming a longitudinal cohort in 2025; no source read gives a cumulative count. The 1030 is the 2022 wave only. The 2020 wave size would be in PMID:38810531 (Nutrition 2024, closed; its abstract gives no count). The Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry for the 2025-2029 longitudinal cohort gives 'Number of participants 800' (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/COMBAT), apparently a planned size. Analysed subsets: 849 adults (PMID:40814824), 892 adults (PMID:41667360).

label: São Paulo Western Region Birth Cohort
counts: mother-child pairs enrolled (births April 2012 - March 2014)
quote: A total of 7066 births occurred in the period, and 6207 mother-child pairs who resided in the studied setting were enrolled in the cohort.
note: From the example study's description of the cohort; the cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2021, PMID:33049779, doi:10.1093/ije/dyaa129) is closed and was not read and should confirm the enrolled count. The Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry gives 'Number of participants 3620' (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/ROC), possibly the followed-up subsample. The example study analysed 5268 children.

label: Next Steps
counts: cohort members who ever took part (2004-2023), including the Sweep 4 ethnic minority boost
quote: The total number of cohort members who have ever participated in the study is 16 122, including 352 Black Caribbean and Black African pupils who joined the study at Sweep 4 as part of an ethnic minority boost.
note: Cohort profile (PMID:39540417). Its sweep table gives 15 770 participants at Sweep 1 (2004, age 14) and 7279 at Sweep 9 (2022-23). The example study (PMID:39679959) says 'Data was initially collected in 2004 from a cohort of 15,570 13-year olds.'

label: PROMESA cohort study
counts: children, as the cohort's catalogue entry gives it
quote: Number of participants 506
note: The Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry gives 506 participants without saying whether it is the enrolled count. The protocol (PMID:36662732) gives only the planned size: 'A prospective cohort of 500 children under five are to be followed for 1 year.' (minimum 456, adjusted to 500 for losses). No results paper reporting the achieved enrolment was found in Europe PMC; one would settle it.

label: Butajira Nutrition, Mental Health, and Pregnancy Study
counts: pregnant women enrolled (2017-2019)
quote: Out of the 1,024 women who were enrolled in the study, 196 women exited from the study.
note: The same paper says 'In the BUNMAP Project, a total of 1,860 women were screened and 1,024 of them met the inclusion criteria.' The Global Exposome Cohort Catalogue entry gives 'Number of participants 614' (https://molgeniscatalogue.org/Global%20Exposome%20Cohorts/collections/BUNMAP), unexplained. The example study (PMID:36178051, closed full text; abstract read) says 'we enrolled 492 pregnant females', an aflatoxin sub-study. No cohort profile paper was found.

label: Primeiros Laços
counts: pregnant adolescents randomised (40 intervention, 40 usual care)
quote: Eighty adolescent mothers were included and randomized to receive either Primeiros Laços (intervention group, n = 40) or healthcare as usual (control group, n = 40).
note: Trial results paper. It also says 'From June 2015 to March 2016, one hundred and sixty-nine pregnant youth were assessed for eligibility criteria in a face-to-face interview and 80 youth were included in the study.' The EEG analysis used 31 participants.

label: Golestan Cohort Study
counts: adults aged 40-75 enrolled 2004-2008
quote: Briefly, GCS is a prospective study of 50,045 adults, aged 40–75 years, who were enrolled between 2004 and 2008, from 329 rural and urban areas of the Golestan province in northeast Iran.
note: The cohort profile (PMID:19332502) gives the same total in its tables ('Demographic characteristics of the 50 045 participants and 18 308 non-participants in the GCS (2004–08)'), made up of 10 032 urban participants from Gonbad and 40 013 rural participants from 326 villages, against an accrual goal of 50 000.

label: Norwegian Family Based Life Course Study
counts: individuals in the 1960-2001 censuses with a personal identity number
quote: This comprises in all 6,272,827 individuals.
note: Design paper (PMID:22735991); the sentence refers to 'all Norwegians who participated in the census in 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990 or 2001 and who had received a personal identity number'. The paper presents only the Norway-born, and its abstract says 'In all, 5,266,270 were included.'; 3,564,582 of them could be linked to both parents. The example study (PMID:34650201) analysed 369 464 male conscripts.

label: Chilean COVID-19 Biorepository
counts: adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection enrolled (2020-2021)
quote: In five months, 2262 participants were enrolled, pseudonymized, and sorted by disease severity.
note: Design paper abstract. The results section gives the same total over a longer span ('In 8 months, 2262 participants were enrolled.'). Of them 1866 were volunteers and 381 hospitalised patients; 2057 gave a complete set of biospecimens; 2249 were approached for long COVID follow-up.

label: Million Women Study
counts: women aged 50-64 recruited 1996-2001 (rounded figure as stated)
quote: 1.3 million women aged 50–64 years were recruited into the Million Women Study in 1996–2001.
note: Only rounded figures were found. The study website (https://www.ceu.ox.ac.uk/research/the-million-women-study, cached) says 'Over 1.3 million UK women were recruited into the study between 1996 and 2001 and have been followed for health outcomes ever since.' The 2000 design paper (PMID:11056681) reports recruitment in progress: '800 000 women were recruited between May 1996 and June 1999, and it is planned that an additional 200 000 will be recruited by the year 2000.' The example study analysed 1 244 294 women after exclusions. The website's recruitment page (which may give an exact count) returned 403.

label: Saudi Biobank
counts: participants enrolled to date (lower bound, 'more than 60,000'), recruitment ongoing
quote: With more than 60,000 participants enrolled to date—and a target of 200,000 participants—the Biobank integrates rich datasets, including EHRs, self-reported information, and diverse biospecimens [3].
note: Recruitment is ongoing with a target of 200,000 (also given by the biobanking.org entry). The figure is a lower bound from the 2026 study-design overview; no exact count was found. The example study (PMID:33194979) says 'A total of 5,790 individuals participated in the SNB between 2017 and 2019.', the early survey subset it analysed.

label: Prospective Epidemiological Research Studies in Iran
counts: adults aged 35-70 enrolled at baseline across 18 districts, 2014-2020
quote: Between 2014 and 2020, the PERSIAN Cohort enrolled 170,564 adults across 18 study districts.
note: Biobank design paper (2025). The target was about 180,000 (10,000 per site); 37,334 had completed the first reassessment visit by May 2025. The example study (PMID:42467699) gives a different baseline figure: 'The baseline recruitment phase included 163,770 individuals aged 35–70 years, selected via cluster random sampling from 18 geographically distinct areas across Iran between October 8th, 2014 and March 5th, 2020.' The difference is not explained in either source.

label: Generation Victoria
counts: children and parents/guardians enrolled (Cohort 2020s plus Advance Cohort)
quote: A further 5833 children and 9122 parents/guardians were recruited to the Advance Cohort, bringing the total participants enrolled to 123 516 (49 686 children, 73 830 parents/guardians).
note: Cohort profile (PMID:41844214). Cohort 2020s alone: 'In total, 108 561 participants were enrolled including 43 853 children and 64 708 parents/guardians.' (29.7% of eligible births); 761 had withdrawn. The 2024 protocol (PMID:39754130) projected 45,000-50,000 children plus parents.

label: South Asia Biobank
counts: adults whose data were collected 2018-2022 (as used by the example study)
quote: The data from 149,051 adults ages 18 years and above used for the present study were collected between 2018 and 2022.
note: The 2021 cohort profile (PMID:34143882) reports recruitment up to its pause for COVID-19: 'By March 2020 we recruited a total of 52 853 subjects: 13 954 from Bangladesh, 8620 from South India, 9469 from North India, 5875 from Pakistan and 14 935 from Sri Lanka.' Recruitment evidently continued (244 surveillance sites by the example study, against 118 in the profile), so the later, larger count is recorded; it is the dataset the example study drew on (148,944 analysed), not a statement of total enrolment, and no newer design source was found.

label: Dementias Platform UK
counts: individuals across the 42 cohorts of the DPUK Data Portal (2020)
quote: The Dementias Platform UK Data Portal is a data repository facilitating access to data for 3 370 929 individuals in 42 cohorts.
note: Cohort aggregation; the number is the pooled count of members of the portal's 42 collaborating cohorts in the 2020 Data Portal paper, not people recruited by DPUK itself. Of these cohorts, 24 (n = 1 410 302) had uploaded full or partial datasets and 18 (n = 1 960 627) uploaded per project. By 2024 the portal held more cohorts: the example study (PMID:38506636) says DPUK 'contains > 60 population and clinical cohorts' but gives no pooled count. The DPUK website (dementiasplatform.uk) returned 403 and may give a current total.

label: Iganga-Mayuge Health and Demographic Surveillance Site
counts: population under surveillance (rounded)
quote: The IMHDSS cohort covers a catchment area of 155 km2 with a population of 95 000 individuals and is served by 23 health facilities.
note: An HDSS; the count is the current population under surveillance, a rounded figure. PMID:35427403 (2022) says 'IM-HDSS follows over 95,000 individuals living in about 18,000 households.'; PMID:28799450 (2017) gave 'a total population of approximately 74,000 living in 16,000 households' in 63 villages. The cohort profile (Int J Epidemiol 2020, PMID:32556335, doi:10.1093/ije/dyaa064) is closed and was not read; it may give an exact count and the cumulative number ever registered.

label: HUNT4 70+
counts: inhabitants aged 70+ who took part in HUNT4 70+ (2017-2019)
quote: In HUNT4 70+, all inhabitants aged 70+ were invited (N = 19,403), with 9956 (51.3%) participating (Figure 1).
note: Of these, 5729 took part in the Ageing in Trøndelag follow-up (2021-23), and 5229 dementia-free participants with valid follow-up were analysed. No HUNT4 70+ design paper was read.

label: Coronagenes
note: No source read states how many took part. Read: the archived 'What's Coronagenes?' page and the archived Coronagenes home page (web.archive.org, 2024), the 2020 Institute of Genetics and Cancer news item (recruitment call only), and the example study (PMID:35922517, COVID-19 HGI 2022 update, main text, PMC version and supplementary PDF), which lists Coronagenes only among contributing teams, with no sample size. Europe PMC has no other paper naming Coronagenes. The per-study case/control counts in the COVID-19 HGI supplementary tables (xlsx, not read) or the HGI study list would give the analysed numbers.

label: German National Cohort
counts: men and women aged 19-74 recruited and examined at baseline, 2014-2019
quote: Between 2014 and 2019, a total of 205,415 men and women aged 19–74 years were recruited and examined in 18 study centres in Germany.
note: Cohort design/baseline paper (2022). Of them 56,971 had the intensified (Level 2) programme per the abstract (the results text says 59,971) and 30,861 had whole-body MRI; the target was 200,000. The example study (PMID:37533684) gives 'The NAKO included 204,878 participants aged 20–69 at baseline', a slightly different data release.

label: The Malaysian Cohort
counts: participants recruited 2006-2012
quote: The Malaysian Cohort (TMC) project is a large population-based cohort study that managed to recruit 106,527 participants over a period from the year 2006 until 2012 [23].
note: PMID:29462329 says TMC 'recruited approximately 100 000 Malaysians aged between 35 and 70 y at baseline' and also refers to 'the original 106 527 TMC participants'; 105,391 were selected for that analysis. PMID:34299667 studied 19,343 participants due for follow-up in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.

label: Cancer Prevention Study-3
counts: participants enrolled 2006-2013
quote: In total, 303,682 participants were enrolled.
note: Same paper: 254,650 completed the baseline survey and are 'fully' enrolled; 49,032 are followed for outcomes only. PMID:39150951 repeats 303,682 enrolled, approximately 254,000 completing the baseline questionnaire.

label: Personalized Environment and Genes Study
counts: participants in PEGS Data Freeze 3.1
quote: The PEGS cohort contains 19,445 demographically diverse participants who provided phenotype and exposure data by completing three surveys.
note: Same paper: data from PEGS Data Freeze 3.1 created on 6/27/2023; enrolment is ongoing; 9,449 completed the Health and Exposure Survey, 4,737 were whole-genome sequenced. PMID:36383734 used 9,414 participants (Freeze 1.1).

label: Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project
counts: initial participants with medical history and saliva samples, as analysed in the 2023 paper
quote: The NLGP cohort consists of the initial 2,500 participants for whom medical history and saliva samples were obtained with informed consent under a study protocol approved by the Newfoundland and Labrador Health Research Ethics Board (Ethics Reference #: 2018.243).
note: This is the initial set of participants used in the paper (2,446 passed genotyping QC, 1,807 in the final dataset), not a stated total enrolment. The project FAQ (https://www.nlgenomeproject.ca/faq/) gives only a target: 'While we may enroll up to 10,000 volunteers, enrollment for the NL Genome Project is currently paused as part of a planned ‘data lock’ phase.' The IHCC Cohort Atlas page needs JavaScript and could not be read; a Sequence Bio report or the Atlas entry of the achieved enrolment would settle it.

label: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort
counts: postmenopausal women who joined UKCTOCS
quote: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women’s Cohort (UKLWC) includes the 202,280 postmenopausal women from the general population who joined the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening
note: The Innovative CTU page (https://www.innovative-ctu.ucl.ac.uk/studies/all-studies/u/uklwc/) gives the same 202,280; baseline serum samples come from 189,452 women and serial samples from 50,262 women. The example paper PMID:40067807 says 202,638 postmenopausal women were recruited to the trial between 2001 and 2005 (the number randomised before exclusions); the UKLWC's own figure is used.

label: Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System
counts: residents under surveillance in March 2011
quote: In March 2011, there were 29 970 households with 261 919 residents under surveillance; 49% of these were aged <15 years and 18% were aged <5 years (Figure 2).
note: Open population, so the count is a point-in-time resident population. Same profile: the 2000-2001 census defined a population of 198 063, and the abstract rounds to 260 000 residents. The example paper PMID:41781022 says the KHDSS 'at the time had a population of approximately 309 000 people' (2021-2022, 90,257 households), a later but approximate figure from a non-profile source.

label: Cancer Prevention Study II Nutrition Cohort
counts: CPS-II participants aged 50-74 recruited to the Nutrition Cohort 1992-1993
quote: During the period 1992–1993, 184,194 CPS-II participants 50–74 y of age who resided in 21 states were recruited for participation in the CPS-II Nutrition Cohort.
note: Quote from PMID:38088576 (PFAS case-cohort study, 2023). The design paper PMID:12015775 is readable only as an abstract: 'The cohort includes over 84,000 men and 97,000 women who completed a mailed questionnaire in 1992.' PMID:33578791 (PMC7916573) says the cohort 'enrolled 184,185 men and women residing in 21 states'; PMID:24880342 says 'approximately 184,000 individuals'. The example PMID:33803340 gives 39,239 who gave blood in 1998-2001. The full text of the 1992 design paper would settle 184,185 versus 184,194.

label: Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort
counts: children contributing data from the ECHO cohorts, as of the March 2022 data lock
quote: As of March 4, 2022, the EWC cohorts contributed data from 60,553 children and consented 29,622 children for new EWCP data and biospecimen collection.
note: Counts children only. Same paper: 29,622 children enrolled in the ECHO-Wide Cohort Data Collection Protocol (new data); 36,166 individuals (38,735 pregnancies) were enrolled in the cohorts during pregnancy. The ECHO home page (https://echochildren.org/) as cached gives no participant count. The example paper PMID:40914105 analysed 1,723 and 627 children.

label: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study for the Next Generation
counts: persons enrolled 2011-2016
quote: Results: As of December 31, 2016, we have established a population-based cohort of 115,385 persons (Response rate 44.1%), among whom 55,278 (47.9% of participants) have provided blood and urine samples.
note: Profile paper PMID:30713262. The target population was 261,939 residents aged 40-74; 55,278 gave biospecimens. The example paper PMID:41047337 describes 'a cohort of 52,566 males and 61,539 females' (a later analysis dataset, given by sex only).

label: China Patient-centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events Million Persons Project
counts: participants aged 35-75 enrolled in 31 provinces, 2014-2018
quote: We enrolled 2 660 666 participants aged 35-75 years from 31 provinces between 2014 and 2018 in the cross-sectional China Patient-Centered Evaluative Assessment of Cardiac Events Million Persons Project.
note: From the example study's abstract, not a design paper; enrolment continued after 2018, so this is the count to 2018. The pilot protocol PMID:26729395 planned to screen 0.4 million residents aged 40-75 in four provinces in 2014-2015 and analysed the first 0.1 million. A later cohort profile of the national project would give a more recent total.

label: Africa Centre Demographic Information System
counts: unique individuals who have participated since 2000 (ACDIS and its 2017 expansion, PIP)
quote: Since 2000, 231 179 unique individuals have participated in the cohort, generating >2 million person-years of follow-up.
note: Open population cohort; the cumulative count includes the area added in 2017. Same profile: 'In mid-2018, there were 142 079 individuals in the PIP cohort, of whom 93 074 were members of households in the original ACDIS surveillance area' (102,731 residents and 39,348 non-residents on 1 July 2018). The example paper PMID:27956187: 'Between 2001 and 2014, a cumulative number of 93,903 adults ever resided in the demographic surveillance area.' A point-in-time count may be preferred for consistency with other surveillance systems.

label: LifeGene
counts: participants with information in LifeGene (recruited 2009-2016)
quote: LifeGene startade i september 2009 och innehåller information från totalt 50,437 deltagare.
note: Swedish: 'LifeGene started in September 2009 and contains information from a total of 50,437 participants'; the same page says blood, serum and urine from more than 29,500 participants are stored at KI Biobank. The design paper PMID:21104112 gives only the target of 500,000 and a 5,000-person pilot. The example PMID:39934197 analysed 12 167 participants aged 18-43.

label: SG100K
counts: approximate number of Singapore residents across the four member cohorts in the PRECISE-SG100K dataset
quote: The PRECISE-SG100K resource is a unique multi-ancestry Asian population cohort dataset of ~100,000 Singaporean residents, jointly created by PRECISE, SG100K Institutions and GIS.
note: Approximate (~100,000). Same page: 'The first release of the integrated dataset for 100,000 participants is projected to be released in the first half of 2026', and an intermediate release covered 50,000 participants. No exact pooled count found. The example PMID:41469377 describes only the HELIOS member cohort (10,004 participants) and calls SG100K a 'target 100,000 participants'.

label: South African Population Research Infrastructure Network
counts: individuals under surveillance in the three founding HDSS nodes in 2020
quote: In 2020, the SAPRIN population cohort covered 355000 individuals for whom data on births and deaths, residency status and migration, household asset ownership status, and measures of well-being including employment, education and social protection are updated three times a year.
note: Profile paper PMID:34966919 (Key Features). Its Table 1 gives 297 000 individuals at SAPRIN's start in 2016 and 355 000 at the 2019 first public data release (Agincourt 115 000, DIMAMO 100 000, AHRI 140 000); urban nodes added from 2020 are not included. The example PMID:39282516 says the verbal autopsy dataset covered 'a population of over 250,000' in two provinces for 2012-2019. The SAPRIN website (http://saprin.mrc.ac.za/) as cached gives no count.

label: Lifecourse biological pathways underlying social differences in healthy aging
counts: individuals from 48 cohorts pooled in the flagship multi-cohort analysis of socioeconomic position and mortality (stated as 'over 1.7 million')
quote: Lifepath researchers explored SEP as a risk factor for adult NCDs in a multi-cohort study of over 1.7 million individuals from 48 independent cohorts from the UK, France, Switzerland, Portugal, Italy, the USA, and Australia (7) (Figure 1) (see the section “Health inequalities in cohorts and the underlying mechanisms,” page 18).
note: From the consortium's special report PMID:32478023; the abstract says it 'pooled data on up to 1.7 million participants of longitudinal cohort studies from Europe, USA, and Australia'. The figure is a lower bound ('over'), not exact. The example PMID:28557991 describes the core LIFEPATH consortium of cohorts (CoLaus, Constances, E3N, EPIC-Italy, Epiporto, Gazel, MCCS, SKIPOGH, TILDA, WHIP-retired, Whitehall II) as 'a population of over 500,000 subjects'. label: Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Programme
counts: adult residents enrolled 1985-2001
quote: Between 1985 and 2001, 167 371 adult Vorarlberg residents were enrolled in the VHM&PP Study Cohort after signing an informed consent to store and process personal data (height, weight, smoking and other factors).
note: The analysed cohort in PMID:16234822 was 67447 men and 78484 women ('more than 145 000'). The Me-Can profile PMID:19380371 says 'roughly 176 000 persons participated in the programme' in 1985-2003 (approximate, later, and a different window). The exact 167,371 to 2001 is kept; a VHM&PP cohort description with an exact later total would supersede it.

counts: men and women enrolled 2005-2009
quote: A total of 1 395 174 invitations were mailed and 267 357 participants enrolled.

label: International Health Cohorts Consortium
counts: unique participants across the 69 member cohorts that reported (approximate, summed by the consortium)
quote: A Breakdown of ~33,872,619 unique participants across 69 reporting sites.
note: From the Fig. 1 legend of PMID:40841586; the text says 'Collectively, the cohorts represent ~34 million unique research participants with available data/samples' and the abstract 'We summarize the collective resources of 69 member cohorts, representing over 34 million people.' Also ~12,834,036 participants with genotype data at 41 sites; the Cohort Atlas has 89 cohorts from 43 countries. A consortium of member cohorts rather than a pooled analysis; the example PMID:37337639 is a BMI polygenic score study in several IHCC cohorts and gives no consortium total.
